The Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions have unveiled their final practice reports for Week 5's bout at State Farm Stadium.
For the Cardinals, Walter Nolen and Karson Sharar are both questionable while Jeremiyah Love is good to go.
As for the Lions, four players including Brian Branch have been ruled out.
Full lists for both sides:
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur says nothing really changes in terms of preparation despite a familiar face in former Arizona offensive coordinator Drew Petzing returning to the desert.
“Yes, it’s a good question. People are going to have their narratives probably about it, including us. Drew definitely has his spin on that offense, but it’s the Detroit Lions offense. They’re doing a lot of the stuff that they’ve done in the run game," he said.
"They’re doing a lot of stuff that (Lions QB) Jared’s (Goff) has been really, really successful at — almost at MVP caliber levels and stuff. title: Cardinals Stars, Coaches Reveal What Fans Are Missing About Jacoby Brissett
full_text:
Noise around the Arizona Cardinals and starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett continues to grow louder with each loss.
The 1-3 Cardinals are again projected to fall when they take the field, this time in Week 5 when they play host to the Detroit Lions.
Naturally, as losses mount, attention will turn to the quarterback. Brissett's already accustomed to negative attention after winning a contract standoff with the Cardinals over the summer, one that gave him several more millions of dollars in guarantees with hopes of stabilizing their offense and producing wins.
Brissett, for various reasons, hasn't been able to guide the Cardinals to wins — a similar story to last season — and fans have quickly grown tired of the same old song and dance with him under center.
“None. I won’t say my real answer, but no, none," Brissett said when asked if he pays attention to what's been said about him.
"I could care less to be honest with you. Not in the slightest. It’s part of the gig, right? I’m not shying away from any of that.”
Brissett's time to throw (2.6 seconds) is fifth-fastest in the NFL. The Cardinals are dead last in explosive play rate to begin 2026 and Brissett's average completed air yards is bottom ten in the NFL. Case in point: Arizona's not generating big plays and Brissett's often getting the ball out quickly and close to the line of scrimmage.
As losses mount, expectations of a change at quarterback only strengthen .
However, the Cardinals — even in spite of their slow start — continue to back Brissett.
"I feel so confident with him back there every week," star tight end Trey McBride said at the beginning of the regular season.
For as much noise as Arizona's fan base is generating, people are quick to forget this is the same locker room that voted Brissett a team captain before the regular season.
The 1-3 start, at least internally, hasn't shifted belief from Brissett's teammates.
"Since he stepped in, since Day 1, we have a great relationship off the field. He's one of my better friends on the team. We can talk about anything and I think we both see things the same way and I think Jacoby knows that I'm in his corner and I'm going to do everything I can to make him look good," Michael Wilson told reporters this week.
Often, the biggest question Cardinals fans have: Why Brissett?
Mike LaFleur dove deep into why Brissett's had a major vote of confidence:
"Because he's done really good things. There's a lot of good stuff that he's done. Listen, it's the hardest position in all sports. So when you don't win, it's on the quarterback. When you win, the quarterback gets maybe even more flowers than they deserve. And the truth is, a lot of times, somewhere in between," LaFleur said Friday.
"Let's call it what it is if we're going to be real: if we do finish the job right there [last week] and we score 31 points, no one's talking. But we didn't, and that's part of the business that we signed up [for]. That's why it's so awesome. That's what's so fun about Sundays. That's what's so fun about playing in the NFL is we signed up for this. Coaches, players, everyone, and the quarterbacks understand that.
"And to be a quarterback in this league, you got to have thick skin. And then when things are great and people are telling you [that] you did a great job, hey, you got to turn the page and continue to move forward. So he's a pro. He handles it. He probably hears the noise, but he ignores the noise. He's above the noise. It's not what gets him to play better or anything like that, or prepare any harder. He's just going about it for his teammates, for himself, for his family.
"I got a lot of respect for him and his approach."

title: Cardinals Injury News: Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen Updates vs Lions
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals have ruled out starting safety Andrew Wingard ahead of their Week 5 contest against the Detroit Lions.
Meanwhile, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur gave positive updates for Sunday on running back Jeremiyah Love and defensive lineman Walter Nolen III.
"Right now, trending well. Yeah. It's a maintenance thing with ankles, and you guys see the way he cuts. So I don't know what he's totally feeling. Only he knows, but I mean, he's doing good. He's out there practicing. He's running around, stuff like that," LaFleur said of Love.
LaFleur also confirmed tight end Hunter Long's injury isn't season-ending after landing on injured reserve. Outside linebacker Jordan Burch, who missed two consecutive days due to a personal matter, will be good to go for Sunday.
The Cardinals will reveal official game designations (out, questionable, doubtful) later today after practice.
Love suffered an ankle injury that was different than the one that kept him out of preseason play. Despite managing injuries early in his rookie season, he's still played in every regular season game.
Love, if healthy like projected, will be running behind a Cardinals' offensive line just lost two starters in Paris Johnson Jr. and Isaiah Adams.
Nolen popped on the team's injury report yesterday with a calf injury. It's been a slow start for the former first-round pick, though Nolen seemed to have turned a corner last week in New York.
Arizona's heavily banking on both former top picks to be healthy after suffering a 1-3 start, though LaFleur wasn't into leaning on any positives despite being close in two of those losses.
"Could have, should have, would have. So that doesn't matter in this league. But again, one and three, three and one, four and zero, zero and four, anywhere in between like we are right now — just looking for improvement and trying to get the result this Sunday," he said.
As for the Lions, head coach Dan Campbell called it a tall task for safety Brian Branch to play this Sunday. LaFleur says the game-planning won't change purely based off Branch's availability if he does play.
"It's been five years in a row that we've played Detroit, and he's been a big part of what they've done there. Because he hasn't played this year, you can't overly prepare for him. It's not like they're going to change up their scheme," LaFleur said.
"You're just going to end up grabbing a really good football player if he ends up playing this Sunday. But from a schematic standpoint, there's not really much you're going to change because you don't really know where he's at as a player right now."

title: Cardinals vs Lions Week 5 Expert Picks, Prediction Roundup
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Detroit Lions are set for a Week 5 clash at State Farm Stadium that carries plenty of stakes despite its early-season placement.
Defensive coordinators on both sides of the ball are looking to keep themselves off the hot seat while Arizona and Detroit's offense holds potential to each score 30 points when all cylinders are firing.
A loss would sink the Cardinals to 1-4 on the year while the Lions enter Week 5 with an even 2-2 record.
Week 5 roundup for Cardinals-Lions predictions:
Pete Prisco: "The Lions are playing on the road off a Sunday night loss. They can't stop anybody on defense. But the Cardinals have some defensive issues as well. Look for the Lions to outscore Arizona in a shootout as Jared Goff puts up big numbers. "Pick: Lions 40, Cardinals 31"
Bucky Brooks: "After a hot start in Week 1, the Cardinals certainly have cooled off. They have allowed at least 30 points in each of their last three games. Fortunately, one of the three teams allowing more points per game this season is this week's opponent, the Lions, who have scored and allowed 24-plus points in all four games.
"Simply put, expect plenty of offense (and fantasy points) in this one. The Lions' pick-your-poison unit -- with Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams and Sam LaPorta in tow -- should have no problem rebounding from last week's roller-coaster loss in Carolina. Jacoby Brissett has done some good things, too, notably when targeting Trey McBride and Michael Wilson. The Cardinals must find the end zone to stay with the ever-explosive Lions, but a few too many field goals by the home team will likely put them on the losing end."
This is shaping up to be a fun one at State Farm Stadium, as Week 5 could very well turn into a track meet.
We like the Lions to win that race. DET 30, AZ 24.

title: Cardinals Are Falling Apart: 2 Changes Could Still Save the Season
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are staring the reality of a losing season directly in the face.
Arizona's 1-3 start isn't quite a lost cause, though losses have quickly piled up in the desert, and it's up to head coach Mike LaFleur to make changes before 2026 gets away from him.
“Our focus is (being) 1-0 each and every week so the word change doesn’t — we’re trying to do what we think is best for the week to win a football game. That’s the approach that I take, that (General Manager) Monti (Ossenfort) takes and that this organization takes — the coaches and the players," LaFleur told reporters this week.
"That’s all we’re focused on. I know people want big-picture analysis, but in the world that we try to live in and within our walls where it’s just us and the NFL, it’s week to week and (we) work to be 1-0 each week.”
There's ample opportunity for both sides of the ball to improve ahead of Week 5 . After a quarter of the season, here's one change the Cardinals need to make on each side of the line of scrimmage:
The Cardinals' usage of 13 (one RB, three TE) sets is third in the NFL through four weeks of play, which isn't a surprise given LaFleur's prior experience with the Rams and Sean McVay's love for the hefty packages.
However, Arizona's personnel groupings mostly reside in 11 (three receivers) personnel with that package used on 63% of offensive plays.
LaFleur's usage of 2+TE sets (34%) ranks 16th in the NFL, though that number has to jump for a few reasons.
The Cardinals' offensive line is getting no push upfront. Arizona's run stuff rate (17.8%) ranks in the bottom ten of NFL teams while their 1.1 average yards before contact is in the bottom third of teams. Pass-protection wise, Arizona's 2.6 second average time to throw is third-fastest in the NFL while their ESPN pass-block win rate of just 30% ranks second-worst in the league.
Simply put, the Cardinals are relying far too heavily on running backs making plays of their own accord while they're afforded little time to let passing plays develop.
There's no magic wand to fix these issues, but with two starting offensive linemen out for Week 5 and the next few weeks staring down a gauntlet of a schedule, the Cardinals need to adjust their attack.
Arizona's facing light defensive boxes just 27.9% of the time, which is the third-least in the NFL. Translation: defenses are mostly playing base against the Cardinals and are having success while doing it.
That's where the integration of multi-TE sets comes into play. More heavy bodies will potentially offset some of the losses suffered upfront while giving Arizona more advantageous looks in the run game. Tight ends such as Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins are more than equipped to handle those dual duties.
It's time Arizona embraces going heavier.
It feels like a lifetime ago when Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was in future head coaching conversations thanks to the job done with an undermanned Arizona defense, getting creative with pressure packages and being aggressive towards offenses.
That's changed, drastically, and Rallis now finds himself on the hot seat entering Week 5.
Arizona's defense has allowed 30+ points in three consecutive games. They're bottom ten in yards allowed per contest (351.3) and fourth-worst in points allowed per game (29.3) through four weeks.
The Cardinals opted to fill holes in their defense left by departing starters as opposed to making serious upgrades — which includes their pass rush. Arizona's eight team sacks rank near the middle of the table while their pressure rate (21.1%) ranks in the bottom third.
Their explosive play rate allowed of 7% is also sixth-worst out of all NFL defenses.
Rallis' defenses have typically been at their best when he's sending pressure. That hasn't been the case in 2026, as Arizona's just one of six NFL teams to have a defensive blitz rate of less than 20%.
Half of the Cardinals' sacks have come on blitzes or pressures with five players. Arizona's defense is not nearly talented enough in either the front or backend to rush four and drop seven into coverage.
It feels like Arizona's defense has been more reactionary than aggressive. Yes, there's a talent disparity. No, Rallis doesn't need to turn into an evil genius such as Brian Flores when it comes to dialing up pressure.
The reality is the Cardinals' defense is undermanned. With that, you have two options: Sit back and play exotic coverages and hope offenses will make mistakes — or be the aggressor and force opposing teams to beat you with low percentage/probability plays on a consistent basis.
To Rallis' credit, the Cardinals are sixth in turnovers generated at seven. However, their bend but don't break defense has largely seen too many open receivers and holes afforded for teams to have extensive success on the field.
It's time for Arizona to be more aggressive in their defensive play-calling. Rallis' job may depend on it.

title: Cardinals Hot Seat Rankings: Who’s Under The Most Pressure After a 1-3 Start?
full_text:
We're a quarter of the way through the season, and the Arizona Cardinals have been an unfortunate underperformer with a 1-3 record.
It's not as if the Cardinals have been out-classed through their first four games. A win in Los Angeles started the season off on a positive note while Seattle's blowout loss was a humbling reset for first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. Back-to-back tough losses to San Francisco and New York bring us to present day.
What the rest of the season looks like largely remains to be seen. However, a number of figures within the organization find themselves in discussions daily from the fan base.
Whose seat is hot, and whose is not?
Ossenfort, in his fourth season, has yet to build anything close to a playoff contender. Coaches have come and gone, franchise players have departed, and his draft/free agency classes have yielded a heavy bag of mixed results.
Ossenfort — almost surprisingly — was retained while Jonathan Gannon was fired this past offseason. Injuries again appear to be stalling progress in the desert, though the Cardinals failed to upgrade key positions at edge rusher and right tackle. Those weaknesses are still glaring after four weeks of football.
Patience has run thin on Ossenfort, and if the Cardinals can't turn things around in the final three quarters of the season, it would be a very hard sell to the fan base for him to return for a fifth season.
LaFleur hasn't been without his issues as a rookie head coach. The offense hasn't been able to find explosive plays or counter whatever defenses are doing to stop them on a consistent basis while the defensive side of the ball still remains lackluster — a unit LaFleur doesn't directly oversee but still ultimately is in charge of as a head coach.
Yet we're only four games into LaFleur's tenure, and it's evident the potential he carries as an offensive play-caller once continuity and experience can eventually marry on his side of the ball. Arizona's offense has moved the ball well and quite frankly is a play or two away from being a 3-1 team.
The moral scoreboard doesn't mean anything, but LaFleur's been far from a failure in the infant stages of his career in the desert. His seat isn't anywhere close to warm.
Rallis' leash entering 2026 was already short. The Cardinals interviewed multiple defensive coordinators before being turned down and eventually settled for a fourth season under the play-caller.
There was hope the defense would be different with Gannon's fingerprints removed. That's yet to be the case, as Arizona's allowed 30+ points in three consecutive games. The Cardinals still aren't able to rush the passer and struggle to eliminate a team's top passing weapon on a weekly basis.
Veteran defensive coach Teryl Austin is very much looming as a potential replacement for Rallis, which could happen much sooner than some on the outside anticipate. Unless the Cardinals can turn things around, Rallis being relieved of his duties feels more like when — not if.
The Cardinals engaged in a lengthy contract dispute with Brissett this summer before reaching a number. It was a win for the veteran quarterback — who got one last payday as a starter — while Arizona kept their locker room happy and got a capable veteran passer to run LaFleur's offense.
Thus far, Brissett's been relegated to checking the ball down often and has struggled to find the aforementioned explosive plays. The time missed during his holdout very much impacted his timing/grasp of LaFleur's system and it shows.
Brissett, despite online pitchforks, hasn't been the biggest roadblock for Cardinals success. However, he's proven he isn't capable of taking Arizona's offense to new heights — and as losses pile and patience wears thinner — Brissett is very much on the verge of losing his starting job.

full_text:

Both teams hit the practice field Wednesday for the first time in prep for their clash at State Farm Stadium:
Jeremiyah Love's ankle injury should keep him healthy and ready to go for this week despite his appearance on the report, according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
"No, it shouldn't impact [him]. But again, the best I can just tell you guys is maintenance. Just maintenance throughout the day, and then when we get to Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.

"Look, we know there’s going to be a little bit of kicking the rust off just to get back into all of those, back to the player that he was. It’ll take a minute," said Campbell (h/t Lions On SI ).
"However, he’s an instinctive, aware player and he is a violent player. And so he’s got a knack for the football and his production, even if it’s not what it was in the immediate, as he grows back to that will have an impact, I believe."

On Saturday, the two sides will have the opportunity to make up to two standard practice squad elevations. These could be key in revealing who teams believe will be healthy or unavailable for Sunday.
On game day, a final inactives report is due 90 minutes ahead of game time at State Farm Stadium. With a 1:25 PM kickoff, this report will be due at 11:55 AM on Sunday.

title: Cardinals Update Jeremiyah Love Injury Before Lions Game
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are expecting running back Jeremiyah Love to be available for their Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions after suffering an ankle injury in their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants.
"No, it shouldn't impact [him]. But again, the best I can just tell you guys is maintenance. Just maintenance throughout the day, and then when we get to Sunday," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.
Love was seen on the sideline having his ankle worked on and did not appear on the Cardinals' final drive to potentially win the game in Week 4. He was out-snapped 36-30 by fellow running back Tyler Allgeier.
This ankle injury is different than the one he suffered during preseason play, which kept him out for multiple weeks. He has yet to miss a regular season game.
“He’s been dealing with it for a little bit, but it’s just a management-type thing,” LaFleur said earlier in the week on Monday. “It’s like he tweaks it and then he feels fine, so we’re just trying to manage that. He’s doing a good job with it, too.”
Arizona will reveal their first practice injury report of Week 5 later today. The Cardinals will practice three times this week before designating players as either out, questionable or doubtful on Friday.
Love, just four games in his rookie season, addressed the grueling physicality of playing in the NFL as a rookie after the loss in New York.
"My body sometimes is down, sometimes tired. So it's just managing those things. And coaches know that. This is probably gonna be the longest year of my life," Love said after Week 4.
"I just want to manage that workload. So today just obviously making sure to keep an eye on managing me. But I didn't go out there hurt anything or anything like that. They're doing what they need to do to keep me up so that I can finish the season."
The Cardinals have been insistent on splitting touches between Love and Allgeier to steady the workload of the former number three overall pick .
Love thus far has 55 carries for 223 yards (4.1 YPC) and one touchdown on the ground. As a pass-catcher he has 11 receptions for 36 yards and one receiving touchdown.
The Cardinals are 1-3 on the season and are hoping to avoid a fourth consecutive loss after winning their season-opener against the Los Angeles Chargers.
If he's able to go, the Lions' defense has allowed the most yards and second-most points per game thus far, which opens the door for a big day for Love.

title: Cardinals Surprisingly Stagnant Across Week 5 NFL Power Rankings
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 through four weeks of play, placing them in a precarious spot across NFL power rankings ahead of Week 5.
Conor Orr: "Mike LaFleur was immediate in his response to a question about a quarterback change, which is totally fair. But with a developmental passer on the roster, I do wonder what the 'gotta see him' threshold is for a team that, according to ESPN’s draft slot projector, has a 55% chance of a top-five pick."
Josh Weinfuss described the season in four words: "too many self-inflicted mistakes" which actually might be five words now that we spell them out here.
"The Cardinals are still figuring out life under new coach Mike LaFleur. Following a convincing loss to the Seahawks in Week 2, Arizona has been close in its past two games but couldn't overcome a litany of self-inflicted mistakes," he said.
"Sunday's matchup ended up with a pick-six thrown by QB Jacoby Brissett on fourth-and-goal. The hope in the locker room is that if the Cardinals can minimize those types of mistakes, they can fix the season."
Nick Shook : "I thought I could count on Arizona’s offense to produce at a competitive rate on a weekly basis. The unit did so in two of its first three games and continued to do so on the first two drives against the Giants. Unfortunately, the rut the Cardinals entered (and their failure to find the end zone late) has shaken my confidence in this team.
"For once, the defense did its part to give Arizona a chance -- at least early -- and the offense failed to capitalize. Perhaps this is what I should have expected from the Cardinals all along."
The Cardinals are surprisingly moved up here despite their loss by Frank Schwab, who dove into Jeremiyah Love's usage:
"Love was the third overall pick of the NFL Draft and has looked good (4.1 yards per carry) even though his snaps have been limited. The Cardinals shouldn't be running the third pick into the ground when it's clear they're not a playoff contender, but it's still unusual to hear Love talking about how it has already been a long year when the Cardinals still have 13 games to go."
Staff : "Like the Jets, the Cardinals offered some hope for this season with a Week 1 win. But that victory over the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers looks less impressive each week, and Jacoby Brissett’s three interceptions Sunday weren’t very inspiring."

title: Falcons Get Final Word on Baltimore Ravens QB Lamar Jackson
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will face the Baltimore Ravens without one of the NFL's biggest stars on Sunday night, as quarterback Lamar Jackson has officially been ruled out with an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley will get the start for Baltimore when the two teams meet in Week 6.
Jackson has not practiced this week after suffering the injury during the Ravens' Week 5 victory over the Tennessee Titans. His absence is a significant development for Baltimore, which will have to adjust its offensive approach without its two-time MVP quarterback.
Jackson's ability to create explosive plays as both a passer and runner has been central to Baltimore's offensive identity. Without him, the Ravens will turn to Huntley, who has experience starting games and familiarity with the team's offensive system.
Huntley has a career record of 7-9 as a starter, including a 5-6 record with Baltimore and 2-3 record with the Miami Dolphins. He will make his 12th career start for the Ravens, giving the team an experienced option despite the challenge of replacing Jackson.
Huntley also saw action against Tennessee after Jackson exited with the injury. He completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards without a touchdown or interception, helping Baltimore secure the victory.
The backup quarterback's mobility gives the Ravens another option to execute designed runs and extend plays outside the pocket. Baltimore could lean more heavily on its rushing attack, particularly with Derrick Henry serving as a key component of the offense. Huntley will need to protect the football, make quick decisions, and take advantage of opportunities in the passing game.
For Atlanta, Jackson's absence presents an opportunity to build on its recent success. The Falcons are coming off a convincing 45 -24 victory over the New Orleans Saints and will look to carry that momentum into Sunday night's contest.
Atlanta has historically struggled against Baltimore, holding a 2-5 all time record against the Ravens. Baltimore won the last two meetings, defeating the Falcons 26-16 in December 2018 and earning a 17-9 victory in December 2022.
The Falcons will look to reverse that trend while taking advantage of Baltimore's quarterback situation. Atlanta's defense must remain disciplined against Henry and prevent Huntley from finding a rhythm, particularly if the Ravens attempt to control the game with their running attack.
Jackson's absence changes the complexion of Sunday's matchup, but Baltimore still has playmakers capable of creating problems. The Falcons will need to control the line of scrimmage, limit explosive plays and capitalize on the opportunity to secure another important victory.
The Ravens and Falcons are scheduled to kick off Sunday, October 11, at 8:20 p.m. ET in Atlanta.

title: Falcons Injury Updates ahead of Ravens Clash, Including OL Jake Matthews
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons received encouraging news on the injury front Friday as they completed their final practice before Sunday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. Left tackle Jake Matthews returned to full participation, while several defensive contributors remain questionable for the upcoming contest.
With the Falcons looking to build on their victory over the New Orleans Saints, the availability of several key players could prove important against Baltimore.
Matthews provided the biggest positive development of the day. The veteran offensive tackle suffered a groin injury during Monday night's win over New Orleans , forcing him to leave the game without returning. His availability for Sunday's matchup was initially uncertain after he was listed as a nonparticipant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
However, Matthews made progress throughout the week, participating on a limited basis Thursday before practicing fully on Friday. The improvement puts him in a better position to potentially extend his streak of consecutive NFL starts to 201 games.
Having Matthews available would be a significant boost for Atlanta's offensive line as it prepares to face Baltimore's defense. His experience and consistency at left tackle are valuable assets, particularly when protecting quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
The Falcons also received positive news regarding defensive end Cam Thomas and offensive tackle Michael Jerrell, who were full participants Friday. However, Atlanta still has several defensive injury concerns heading into the weekend.
Defensive end Za'Darius Smith practiced fully despite dealing with a concussion and neck injury. He remains questionable for Sunday night's game, leaving uncertainty surrounding his availability. Smith's potential absence would be notable for a Falcons defensive front that has performed well to begin the season.
Linebacker Divine Deablo and defensive end Samson Ebukam were both limited participants Friday because of hamstring injuries. Both players are listed as questionable against Baltimore.
There is reason for optimism regarding their availability. Deablo and Ebukam also carried questionable designations before Monday night's game against the Saints, but both ultimately played and made contributions in Atlanta's victory.
Meanwhile, linebacker Yasir Abdullah did not participate Friday and is listed as out for Sunday's game because of a hamstring injury. His status presents another concern for Atlanta's defensive depth heading into the matchup.
With the final practice complete, the Falcons will have to monitor their remaining injury situations before Sunday's kickoff. Matthews' progress is an encouraging sign, but the availability of Smith, Deablo, and Ebukam could be equally important as Atlanta prepares for a challenging test against Baltimore.

title: Falcons No. 1 Rush Defense to Face Biggest Test to Date in Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are preparing for one of their biggest defensive challenges of the season when Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens arrive in Atlanta.
Henry has been productive through the first four games of the season, rushing for 374 yards and seven touchdowns on 89 carries. He is averaging 4.2 yards per carry and has added 44 receiving yards on seven catches. Henry is coming off a 73-yard performance against the Tennessee Titans in which he scored a touchdown.
Henry also has a history of success against the Falcons, rushing for 201 yards on 49 carries in two career regular season games against Atlanta. He has yet to score a touchdown in those matchups.
Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich knows the defense will need to be at its best.
“This is a great challenge,” Ulbrich said. “We’ve had some success, not saying it’s been perfect by any means, but we’ve had some success versus the run so far this season.”
The Falcons have the NFL's No. 1 rushing defense by some margin at 48.3 yards per game. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers check in at No. 2 with 72.8 yards per game. They're closer to the No. 7 Cincinnati Bengals than they are the Falcons.
“You want to be the best, you want to play the best,” Ulbrich said. “From that perspective, it’s going to be an amazing challenge.”
Henry's physical style makes him difficult to bring down, but Ulbrich also emphasized the running back's speed.
“Derrick Henry is one of the best, maybe ever, in that way,” Ulbrich said. “Just the physicality, the toughness, and then the speed that you’re not ready for as he runs by you.”
Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels will have a role in trying to slow Henry down, but he knows the defensive line can make the job easier.
“Our D line gets after it, and you never want to slow your defensive line down,” Daniels said. “So that really helps us be able to play off them and just let them go make plays, and we play off of them.”
Ulbrich stressed the importance of Atlanta's tackling fundamentals.
“Population of ball is critical. Stiff-arm defense is critical. A really defined tackling plan is critical,” Ulbrich said.  "Getting to the thigh boards, wrapping, rolling, taking the extra step, putting my body on, and not leaving my feet.”
There aren't many players like Henry who have ever played in the NFL with his combination of size and speed, so it's no surprise this will be a unique challenge for the rookie Daniels.
“I went to school with Ollie Gordon. So that’s the closest I’ve got to Derrick Henry,” Daniels said. “I feel like we’ve gotten closer. I feel like when I first got here, it was kind of everybody figuring out their role, and then I feel like everybody’s figuring out their role. Everybody’s excited for each other.”
The only returning starters on the Falcons' front seven are Brandon Dorlus and Divine Deablo. So it's taken some time to find chemistry. That chemistry could be critical against Baltimore.
For Atlanta, the goal will be to prevent Henry from getting into a rhythm. The Falcons will need disciplined run fits, strong play at the line of scrimmage, and multiple defenders arriving at the football.
If they can limit Henry early and prevent Baltimore from establishing its physical identity, Atlanta will have a much better chance of controlling the game and continuing its defensive progress.

title: Is King Henry Ready to Pass the Crown to Bijan Robinson?
full_text:
It’s starting to seem like a daily occurrence that Bijan Robinson is garnering praise across the NFL.
As the Atlanta Falcons fourth-year running back sits at No. 2 in rushing and scrimmage yards, he’s gotten another bold admission.
This time, from a multi-time rushing leader and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year, “King” Derrick Henry.
“He’s the best in the game right now, he’s doing it all,” Henry discussed Robinson to reporters on Thursday. “I ain’t going to shy away from it. He’s doing a great job, hell of a back.”
Robinson and Henry will be in a running back battle when the Falcons host the Baltimore Ravens at Mercedes-Benz Stadium for Sunday Night Football. Henry may see an increase in touches for Baltimore, which may be without its starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, due to an ankle injury .
Through four games, Robinson has accrued 614 scrimmage yards: 494 rushing, 120 receiving. He’s added five total touchdowns, with one coming on a pass. According to Pro Football Focus, Robinson has broken 17 tackles through four games.
He’s a star in Atlanta’s reinvented attack under new offensive coordinator Tommy Rees .
“Does a great job in the system, then does a great job when the play is not exactly how they want it,” Henry said. “Know how to make guys miss, get vertical – get the most out of the play for sure.”
Henry added that he and Robinson speak on Instagram “here and there.”
Robinson looks to build on a 145-yard rushing and two-touchdown performance in a 45-24 beatdown on NFC South rival New Orleans Saints . Per NFL Next Gen stats, Robinson hit a top speed of 21.78 mph as he sprinted past the New Orleans defense untouched for a 59-yard rushing touchdown on the game’s third play from scrimmage.
Last week, Robinson was also named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his role in the Falcons’ dominating the Green Bay Packers 35-14 on Lambeau Field during Sept. 24’s Thursday Night Football on Sept. 24.
The NFL Top 100 member, ranked third , is on the early NFL MVP watchlist.
Falcons (2-2) versus Ravens (3-1) kicks off at 8:20 p.m. in Atlanta. CBS will stream the game as the Falcons search for their third consecutive win.
Primetime games are Robinson’s forte.
He leads the NFL all-time scrimmage yards average in primetime games , with 145.5, since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. He’s over the likes of Barry Sanders, OJ Simpson, and current Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

title: Falcons RB Brian Robinson Jr. Ready for More as Ravens Loom
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are riding the momentum of their best offensive stretch in a decade, and running back Brian Robinson Jr. played a major role in getting them there.
For the first time since the 2016 Divisional and NFCCG, the Falcons have put up 80 points (40 ppg) across two weeks. pic.twitter.com/qEqddMvitH
Robinson scored three rushing touchdowns in Atlanta’s victory over the New Orleans Saints, finishing with 62 rushing yards on 14 carries. His three touchdowns helped the Falcons establish control early and never look back as the offense continued its impressive turnaround.
Together, Robinson and Bijan Robinson helped Atlanta dominate on the ground. The duo combined for 207 rushing yards and five touchdowns, giving New Orleans few answers for the Falcons’ rushing attack.
“Just staying ahead of the sticks, being super efficient with the run game, and around it,” Robinson said. “I feel like me and B have just been doing a great job of just keeping the run game very efficient, and that obviously helps everything else around it.”
The Falcons have now won consecutive games after a difficult start to the season, and Robinson has been an important part of that turnaround. He has scored four touchdowns over Atlanta’s last two games while helping provide balance alongside Bijan.
Michael Penix Jr.’s recent play has also made the offense more difficult to defend. Penix completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, forcing opposing defenses to respect both sides of Atlanta’s offense.
“Definitely,” Robinson said when asked if the passing game has opened things up on the ground. “I feel like they know they got to respect us. They gotta respect our run game. They got to respect our pass game. So, to leave them guessing, they don’t really know what to expect.”
Despite the offensive explosion, Robinson knows the Falcons cannot spend much time celebrating. The focus has already shifted toward the next challenge.
“We never want to get complacent, man,” Robinson said. “Regardless of what we did last week, after 24 hours, we flush it, and we got a new week ahead of us.”
That mentality will be critical as Atlanta moves forward, Robinson believes.
“Sky’s the limit, man,” Robinson boldly stated. “We can be as good as we want to be, long as guys continue to come in week in or week out and improve.”
The Saints game showed what Atlanta’s offense can look like when the rushing attack and passing game are working together. Now, Robinson and the Falcons have to prove they can carry that momentum into the next game vs Baltimore and continue building on what has been an impressive two week stretch.

title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Scouts Ravens Defense Ahead of Week 5 Showdown
full_text:
Michael Penix Jr. has helped transform the Atlanta Falcons offense since returning to the starting lineup, and his latest challenge will come against a Baltimore Ravens defense he believes has talent at every level.
The Falcons will host the Ravens on Sunday Night Football, with Penix preparing to face a Ravens team ranked 10th in the NFL in total defense, allowing 315.2 yards per game over four weeks.
Penix has been one of the biggest catalysts behind Atlanta's turnaround over the last two weeks. In his two starts, Penix has completed 33 of 45 passes for 479 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while posting a 113.1 passer rating.
The difference has been significant for Atlanta. The Falcons scored just 16 total points and produced 524 yards during the first two games of the season before Penix returned. In the two games since his return, Atlanta has scored 80 points and generated 918 total yards.
Now, Penix will have to keep that momentum going against Baltimore.
“They got some players. They got some ballplayers,” Penix said. “They're a really good team all around, but just talking defensively, I feel like they have guys everywhere.”
Penix believes the Ravens present a difficult matchup because of their depth across the defense.
“Their front is good, and they have backers that are good,” Penix said. “Their defensive backs are as good as, it's hard to find a weak point in their defense.”
Rather than focusing on one individual matchup, Penix emphasized the importance of Atlanta executing its game plan.
“But we’ve got to just lock into our scheme and trust our scheme,” Penix said. “And I know that the coaches, they'll make sure we have all the right things prepared for us so that we can come out and be successful again.”
One player who immediately stands out to Penix is Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith.
“He's a leader. He's the one that makes that whole defense go,” Penix said. “He has a lot of experience, played a lot of football, and he's definitely somebody that keeps them going,”
Then there is Kyle Hamilton, another versatile defender Penix knows will be a major factor.
Hamilton is frequently moved around Baltimore's defense, creating uncertainty for opposing quarterbacks before the snap.
“Yeah, for sure. He's a ball player, as well,” Penix said. “He's going to make plays. We're going to make plays, but we're excited for the challenge.”
The Falcons have gone from struggling to consistently move the football to averaging 40 points per game over their last two contests. Penix has provided stability, efficiency and explosive plays while allowing Atlanta's collection of offensive weapons to operate within Kevin Stefanski's system.
The Ravens will provide a much different test, but Penix appears ready for it.
After two impressive performances to begin his comeback, the Falcons quarterback will now have an opportunity to prove that his resurgence can continue against Baltimore's talented defense.

title: Falcons Get Major National Respect From Colin Cowherd
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have finally entered the national conversation across the NFL, and Colin Cowherd is buying what he's seen from the team through the first four weeks of the season.
In the latest edition of his Week 5 Herd Hierarchy, Cowherd ranked the Falcons No. 8 among the NFL's top teams, a significant sign of respect for a team that has won consecutive games after opening the season 0-2.
Cowherd's biggest reason for believing in Atlanta is the development of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The third-year quarterback has looked increasingly comfortable under head coach Kevin Stefanski, particularly during the Falcons' last two games.
"What you're watching with Atlanta is not a mirage," Cowherd said.
Penix has started the Falcons' last two games and has delivered some of his best football since entering the NFL. In those two starts, he has completed 73 percent of his passes while posting a 113 passer rating.
Cowherd believes the coaching change has played a major role in Penix's emergence.
"Michael Penix broke into this league with a defensive coach," Cowherd said. "Then he gets Kevin Stefanski, who, when Cleveland fired him, interviewed for five jobs in about 45 minutes. He lands in Atlanta with all these weapons."
The results have been clear: the Falcons have scored 80 points in the two games since Penix returned to the lineup.
The Falcons' quarterback completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown in Atlanta's 45-24 Monday Night Football victory over the New Orleans Saints. The performance came one week after he helped lead the Falcons to a convincing victory over the Green Bay Packers.
For Cowherd, the most important part is that Penix is beginning to resemble the quarterback Atlanta believed it was getting when it selected him eighth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft.
"He always threw a beautiful ball, but he didn't have his guy," Cowherd said. "Michael Penix Jr. looked like he did last night and last week, like he did in college."
Penix's emergence has also coincided with the Falcons' offense finding its rhythm. Bijan Robinson has been one of the league's most productive running backs, while Drake London and Kyle Pitts give Penix multiple playmakers in the passing game.
After losing their first two games, the Falcons have responded with consecutive dominant victories. Now, they've entered the national conversation.
Cowherd's No. 8 ranking does not mean Atlanta has proven itself as one of the NFL's elite teams yet. However, it shows the Falcons are beginning to earn legitimate respect.
Atlanta seems to have found what it has been searching for: a confident quarterback and an offense that can make the Falcons a legitimate threat.
Cowherd's No. 8 ranking doesn't mean the Falcons have proven they're one of the NFL's elite teams, but they will have a chance to prove it Sunday night. The Baltimore Ravens come to Atlanta as one of the league's most well-regarded teams, giving Penix and the Falcons their biggest test yet.

title: Falcons No. 1 Rush Defense to Face New Challenge after Big Ravens Trade
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons set out in the offseason to improve their run defense. They overhauled their defensive front in the offseason, partly out of a desire to improve the personnel and partly out of necessity due to players being out.
The results after the first month have been wildly spectacular. New general manager Ian Cunningham traded for two interior linemen in Gervon Dexter and Maason Smith, and the team got bigger at edge after losing Jalen Walker to injury and James Pearce Jr. to suspension.
After the first month of the season, the Falcons not only have the No. 1 rushing defense at 48.3 yards per game, but they'd have to give up 54% more yards per game to even fall to No. 2. They have by far the best run defense.
Atlanta's defensive front is scheduled to take on its toughest test of the season against Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens. Quarterback Lamar Jackson is questionable for Sunday night , but the Ravens' rushing offense is still formidable. They're ranked No. 4 in the NFL at 153.5 yards per game (most of which had Jackson at the helm).
They accomplished the stellar rushing numbers despite being in a jam at center. Baltimore started the season with former Falcons practice squad member Jovaugn Gwyn for the first three games, and then turned to first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane last week against the Titans.
The Ravens were able to manage a 3-1 record against the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, and Titans, but the Falcons' defensive front poses a significantly bigger challenge. The Ravens weren't willing to risk their season on a question mark at center and pulled off a big trade with the Eagles for Pro Bowler Cam Jurgens.
The Ravens sent a fifth and a 2028 second-round pick to the Eagles for Jurgens and a seventh in a rare in-season trade that involves an offensive line starter.
We have agreed to trade C Cam Jurgens and a 2027 7th-round pick to Baltimore in exchange for a 2027 5th-round pick and a 2028 2nd-round pick. pic.twitter.com/8BtXXXtl2K
Jurgens started all four games for the Eagles this year. He was originally a second-round pick out of Nebraska in 2022 by Philadelphia. He's made the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons.
Even if he's not 100% familiar with the Ravens' offense by Sunday, he's still a plug-and-play center who will improve the quality of their line play when they take on the Falcons.
The Panthers' Chuba Hubbard rushed for 53 yards against the Falcons in Week 2. That's the most Atlanta has given up to a running back so far this season. The Ravens will lean heavily on Henry, especially if Jackson is out.
And they just got a big-time player on the offensive line.
The biggest challenge for the Falcons' defensive line just got a little bigger.

title: Falcons Waive Former UGA RB, Sign Former Patriots Draft Pick as Replacement
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are coming off back-to-back weeks of imposing their will on opposing defenses with their running game. Atlanta has the No. 2 rushing offense in the league, powered by Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr.
There hasn't been a lot of room for a third running back through the first four games of the year, but that hasn't stopped them from trying to improve the room with changes.
On Monday, the team announced they had placed popular undrafted free agent running back Cash Jones on waivers and signed former Jam Miller as a replacement.
Miller was selected by the New England Patriots in the seventh round of April's NFL Draft. He rushed 25 times for 92 yards in the preseason for the Patriots, but he didn't make their 53-man roster out of camp.
Miller was a key contributor for the Alabama Crimson Tide across a four-year career. His best season was 2024 when he had 668 yards rushing and seven touchdowns. He also added 16 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.
Jones was considered to have an outside shot at making the Falcons' 53-man roster out of training camp. He was used at running back, wide receiver and on special teams after signing with the Falcons as an undrafted free agent out of Georgia in the spring.
He shined in the Falcon's preseason win over the Indianapolis Colts with seven carries for 41 yards, and he added four catches for 62 yards and a touchdown.
His versatility made him a possibility to make the team. However, the Falcons surprised everyone by keeping just two running backs on the active roster and releasing both Jones and Tyler Goodson. They both re-signed with the team as practice squad players, but Goodson was poached by the Cowboys and signed to their roster.
There's a strong possibility that Jones' time in Atlanta isn't done, and he could rejoin the practice squad in the near future. However, for now, the Falcons are still carrying just three running backs on the team.
The timing of the move is a little ironic for the former SEC stars, as the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs travel to Tuscaloosa on Saturday night to take on the No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide.
The Falcons will take on the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football. It will be their third-straight nationally televised game, and they're hoping to make it a third-straight win.

title: Homecoming or Breakout Party? Inside Falcons LB Harold Perkins Jr.'s Big Night
full_text:
Monday Night Football was a happy homecoming for Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr.
It came at the expense of a sad “Domecoming” for the New Orleans Saints (1-3), as Atlanta (2-2) thrashed the NFC South arch rival 45-24 to spoil the 20th anniversary of the Caesars Superdome reopening after Hurricane Katrina .
“It was a surreal feeling,” said the New Orleans-born Perkins. “I was just trying to do my part and not let my teammates down. I was taking it all in.”
Perkins finished the primetime game tied with cornerback CJ Henderson for a team-high and career-high 10 tackles on the night. He notched his first career sack by getting half credit with safety Xavier Watts as they brought down Saints quarterback Tyler Shough in the backfield. Perkins added a quarterback hit.
Harold Perkins Jr. was everywhere last night, posting 7 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PBU, and 3 stops pic.twitter.com/0Oz3Ykh997
The highly versatile six-round NFL Draft pick out of LSU was also active in pass coverage, breaking up a pass.
“I thought Perk was outstanding,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said of the 6-foot-1, 223-pounder. “Really excited for Perk coming home. I thought he was really good.”
Perkins was just 11 months old when Hurricane Katrina tragically destroyed the city of New Orleans in August 2005. It forced his family to uproot and move to the greater Houston area, settling in Cypress, Texas, where he became a football star at Cypress High School.
Twenty-one years after disaster struck, a “beaucoup” number of Perkins family members watched him play his fourth career NFL game, and first in the Superdome. The Falcons linebacker said that around 30 family members, including his grandmother, were in the building to watch his standout performance.
Some were draped in Falcons gear, while some stayed loyal to their Saints fandom.
“It means a lot, just coming out there, coming back home,” Perkins, 22, said. “Not even just playing the Saints – be able to just be around my family, and they get to see me ball.”
With Perkins leading the way, Atlanta’s defense beleaguered the Saints all night.
New Orleans was held to 320 total yards: 270 passing and 50 rushing.
Shough was sacked twice, but spent the entirety of the game getting chased out of the pocket by the Falcons.
“We were out our top,” Perkins said. That means the Falcons unit was rabid and fierce.
“We played like some savages,” he added.
Per ESPN, Atlanta ranks eighth among the 32 NFL teams in total defense after Monday’s game.
Led by defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich , the Falcons have the league’s top run defense, as was evident in New Orleans.
“Credit our defense as a whole, our coaches for setting us up and putting us in the right positions to win,” Perkins said. “We just went out there and executed.”
The Falcons have a short, six-day turnaround before their next game.
They will finish their three-game primetime run at home against the Baltimore Ravens (3-1) on the Oct. 11 edition of Sunday Night Football.
Baltimore’s two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has an outside chance of playing after spraining his left ankle in the second quarter of the Ravens’ Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson was in a protective walking boot and may miss extra games.
Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will likely start against Atlanta if Jackson isn’t good to go.
Falcons-Ravens is set for an 8:20 p.m. kickoff from Mercedes-Benz Stadium. NBC will televise the game.

title: Ravens Were Fleeced In Cam Jurgens Trade, Longtime Eagles President Contends
full_text:
The Ravens made a significant leap and paid a steep price trading for Philadelphia center Cam Jurgens this week, with longtime Eagles team president Joe Banner speaking for many working for teams around the league in saying Baltimore general manager Eric DeCosta overpaid for the player.
The Ravens were in a pretty dire situation at center, in part due to injuries to fringe players and in part due to their own mismanagement of the position , and it began with not getting an extension done with star center Tyler Linderbaum  well before he became a free agent and ignoring the position despite having  picks in the draft. Jurgens, 27, underwent back/nerve surgery in February 2025, has not been the same player since and Banner, who watched his film closely and was integral in the rise of that franchise along with current Eagles GM Howie Roseman, a former Banner protegee  and former coach Andy Reid, believes Jurgens was losing his grip on a starting guard job with the Eagles.
Therefore, giving up a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 seems quite desperate.
The fact that Jurgens cannot even play this week as he is still in the concussion protocol following a loss to the Rams Sunday, even further speaks to the quirky timing, with Roseman moving on from one of his highest-paid lineman at a time he is already down All-Pro guard Landon Dickerson and with superstar tackle Lane Johnson just retiring. Hence why DeCosta is drawing criticism around the league for this move.
“I think it's hard to disagree with that word,” Banner explained of that "desperation" on “The Daily Flock Show” this week. “It's obviously a very strong word, but I don't think it's an exaggeration or more provocative than it intends to be. That's at least my opinion. I mean, I obviously follow the Eagles as closely as any team in the league. So, at least I have a strong, informed opinion on what they do and who the player is.”
As to who that player is, since the nerve problems created pain up and down his legs that marred his 2025 campaign, there are real questions being asked around the NFL about how he will hold up. The Eagles clearly did not want him snapping the ball regularly despite being a former Pro Bowl center; he was struggling mightily at guard, and, making $16.5M this season with essentially $17.5m guaranteed for next season, Banner believes Roseman was eager to shed this salary despite his line woes.
“The Eagles were really highly motivated to make a trade,” Banner said. “Even with all their problems at the moment (on the line), I mean, I guess I can't prove this, but from talking to people in the building, my impression is that he's about to be benched. You know, he comes in Monday, all of a sudden he's got a concussion. I think they were actually benching him.”
Banner was the president of the Eagles from 2001-2012 and then ran the Browns for two years. He is still very plugged in around the NFL and has always had a strong pulse on the Eagles and has known their owner for quite a long time. He is not one to come off half-cocked and he went back and watched all of Jurgens’s snaps this season again before we chatted.
He knows and understands how Roseman operates as well as anyone and was adamant the Eagles are not waving the white flag on trying to win this season and simply start cashing in good players for draft picks. Banner just thinks it was over-the-top offer they couldn't refuse for a player they saw as steadily on the decline.
“The Eagles are in a real cap problem,” Banner explained. “So getting out of cap is a huge benefit to them. Cap number this year isn't very big but starting next year where it's guaranteed the cap number is very high. You know some people say, ‘Oh it's a great value.’ He's the fourth-highest paid center going forward from today in football. I mean he's not even close at this point in his career to the fourth-best center the league.”
The Ravens are now able to move rookie Vega Ioane back to guard and Jurgens brings leadership, a warrior-mentality and excellent communication skills to a position that was sorely lacking in it in Baltimore and should be a decent upgrade over the likes of Jovaughn Gwyn. That’s if he can return to form at center and stay healthy for a considerable period of time. So, yeah, people around the league are a little baffled.
“You got to the point where you're offering a two for a center who's, you know, really struggled recently and they somehow convince you that's not enough,” Banner exclaimed, “that you need you need to throw more into the pot.”

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Primetime Matchup vs. Falcons
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be back on the road in Week 5 under a national spotlight for the first time this season when they take on the red-hot Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football.
Coming off an injury-riddled victory over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 at home, in which they held on to establish their first winning streak, the Ravens are currently tied for the best record in the AFC North division, right next to the competitive 3-1 Cleveland Browns.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this interconference matchup between these two teams. Here are the top four.
Absent from all three days of practice this week as they prepare for this matchup have been two players who rank among their highest cap hits for the 2026 season. Franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson is dealing with an ankle sprain, and prized offseason addition and star pass rusher Trey Hendrickson is still recovering from finger surgery.
Earlier in the week, head coach Jesse Minter expressed that players of Jackson status and experience could play in a game despite not having practiced all week. As a four-time Pro Bowler and former First Team All Pro, Hendrickson likely falls into that category as well, but following Friday's practice, Minter ruled out both of them .
With the Ravens' first AFC North matchup coming up next week against the Browns, with whom they're currently tied atop the division, risking the long-term health of two of their most pivotal players on the team for a nonconference primetime game doesn't make much sense.
Cornerback Marlon Humphrey, the longest-tenured defensive player, is suffering from both hamstring and calf soft tissue issues, but he was on the practice field on Friday, and Minter expects him to be available.
A week of rest for each would increase the likelihood that they'd be closer to full strength for a game with major implications. Even if the Ravens fall to the Falcons on Sunday and the Browns prevail over the New York Jets, a win in Cleveland in Week 6 would still put them back atop the division standings.
The Ravens are fortunate to not only have one of the best backup quarterbacks in the league in Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley, but he possesses a skill set that is very similar to their starter's, which means the playbook won't be limited. With a full week of reps instead of just being thrust into the starting lineup at halftime like he was last week against the Titans , the former Pro Bowler will be much sharper in the passing game because he'll have had the necessary time on task to get more in tune with top pass catchers, especially two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who has been off to a torrid start to the season.
This will mark Huntley's 17th career regular-season start, but it wouldn't be the first time ever, or even in the last year, that he's been asked to help lead the team to victory against long odds. The former undrafted gem was under center for two of the Ravens' most impressive wins of the 2025 season, both of which came at junctures when they desperately needed to come out on top to keep their playoff hopes alive. Huntley led them to a 30-16 home win over the Chicago Bears in Week 8 to avoid falling to 2-6, and he stepped up again in Week 17 in a 41-24 road win over the Green Bay Packers.
Back in Week 16 of the 2022 season, Huntley picked up his third career win as a starter against the Falcons. That was two offensive coordinators ago, and count first-year play-caller Declan Doyle among the coaches and teammates who have unwavering belief in the seventh-year veteran's ability to answer the call once again and perform at a high level.
"I have a lot of confidence in him to be able to operate the system," Doyle said. "I don't think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all. You're trying to hunt explosives. The standard is still the standard regardless of who's in there and that can't change."
As tough as a blow as not having a two-time league MVP at the helm will be for the Ravens' offense, the side of the ball facing the toughest task in this matchup is their defense. After being the most inept offensive unit in the league with former Ravens backup Cooper Rush under center, the Falcons have fielded the most productive and well-balanced offenses in the league over the past two weeks since 2024 first-rounder Michael Penix Jr. was inserted as the team's starting quarterback.
The third-year signal caller has helped their play-action passing game take flight. Still, their offense begins, ends and is predominantly predicated upon their dominant rushing attack, spearheaded by star running back Bijan Robinson . The two-time Pro Bowler and frontrunner for Offensive Player of the Year is second in the league in rushing yards and yards from scrimmage and is a house-call waiting to happen anytime he touches the ball.
Slowing down Robinson on the ground will be an all-hands-on-deck situation for the Ravens in this game, as tackling in space and maintaining gap integrity will be paramount. Failing to execute either would almost certainly result in a long night for them, and they'd be the third straight team to get embarrassed by the "Dirty Birds" in primetime.
"It is a necessity against guys like Bijan, 11 is needed because he can make 10 miss," safety Kyle Hamilton said. "That 11th guy might be the touchdown-saving tackle, game-saving tackle — whatever it may be — but you have to go in there confident. I think if we run and hit well, we will do what we need to do. And at the end of the day, that is what this game comes down to — a very fundamental approach to this game."
No matter who's been under center for the Ravens through their first four games, the only obstacle, aside from injuries, that has kept them from taking full control, putting opponents away sooner and avoiding late-game theatrics has been themselves. According to NFLpenalties.com, they've been flagged the fourth-most times (39) and have accumulated the fifth-most penalty yardage (329), narrowly behind the Green Bay Packers (344). In Week 4 alone against the Titans , they were flagged a season-high 13 times for a season-high 131 penalty yards.
The bulk of their infractions have been committed by their offense as far too many times; they're having chunk plays and key first-down conversions negated and promising drives are stalled out because of a false start, illegal shift, ineligible man downfield or an unnecessary hold downfield away from the ball carrier. While some growing pains were expected, as the Ravens are in their first year of a new offense under Doyle. His scheme uses a lot of pre-snap motion, heavily utilizes screens and requires skill players to block downfield to turn chunk plays into explosive plays of 20-plus yards.
"You do want to use motions and shifts and cadences as a weapon, and I think when we see our offense really operate, it creates problems," Miner said. "It creates explosives. It creates running lanes [and] it creates angles blocking.
"We need to make sure that we are doing the things with the guys that they are capable of doing, that we are not trying to do too much, that it might not be something that is a one- or two-time thing [and] that it is things that we are working on a lot. Again, I challenge the coaches and myself more than anybody for us to get that right, and we will continue to strive for that."
Defensively, they've been penalized at the most inopportune times and for chunks of yardage and key drive-extending conversions for the opponents, which has prevented them from getting off the field consistently and when it's mattered most, late in games. They needed to keep their composure in coverage, especially on third downs where they're ranked in the middle of the pack in terms of conversion rate (37.5%).

title: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Provides Troubling Injury Updates Ahead Of Sunday's Game
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson and top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson ahead of Sunday night’s game in Atlanta, confirmed what we had been explaining with virtually certain to be the case all week.
Baltimore is without its highest paid players on both side of the ball to face the Falcons who have boasted one of the best offenses and defenses in the NFL the last two weeks since starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returned from his third ACL surgery. However, $19M corner Marlon Humphrey, having another rough season so far, did return to practice after treatment for a calf strain and Minter said Humphrey is expected to face the Falcons.
The Ravens resigned longtime back Snoop Huntley this offseason, even while installing a new and unfamiliar offense with a new coaching staff, and he faces a tall task Sunday behind an offensive line that has a number of issues protecting and run blocking. It will require a comprehensive rethinking of the offensive approach Sunday without Jackson.
Minter praised all the work Jackson is doing behind the scenes to come back from the ankle injury he suffered last weekend as quickly as possible, but this week was always a stretch . Minter said Jackson, a two-time MVP, is “working his tail off” to get back but was noncommittal about what is in store for Week 6 when the Ravens travel to Cleveland.
“I don’t know the specifics of next week,” Minter said.
The Ravens paid a steep price to trade for Eagles center Cam Jurgens this week while he was still in the concussion protocol. He was never really in the mix for Week 5 and was ruled out but Minter said “our hope and expectation is that he’s ready to rock,” in Cleveland.
The Ravens are likely to lean heavily into big defensive fronts to try to mitigate Atlanta’s dominant rushing attack, and Hendrickson is not stout against the run and is being paid top dollar to get to the quarterback. He dealt with a finger issue for a few weeks before the decision was made for a surgical procedure last week, which Minter said would not keep Hendrickson out long. Minter hinted that could come next week.
Humphrey is in the final year of his deal and has battled injuries the last few years. He left Sunday’s game with a calf injury and did not return. He has the highest cap hit in the NFL among all corners and is a favorite of general manager Eric DeCosta, but could be in his final season in Baltimore. With Minter's updates, the specifics of the Ravens' injury report, to be released later Friday, carries little mystery with the rest of the team's starters in line to play.

title: These 4 Individuals Must Step Up Big For Ravens To Upset Falcons Sunday
full_text:
It’s not just who you play, it’s when you play them.
The Ravens may be catching the Falcons at the wrong time, and the Falcons might be catching the Ravens at the right time from a health and personnel and match-up standpoint. That’s how it goes sometimes. Playing any game without Lamar Jackson – as people around the NFL anticipate the Ravens will be – is difficult enough and doing it with another cobbled-together offensive line dealing with injuries only compounds it.
Yes, the Ravens want you to believe that back-up Snoop Huntley has the goods … but this is the same guy they had seen enough of after the 2024 season and moved on from and who had no real market outside of Baltimore save for a few brief-and-cheap dalliances with the Browns and he couldn’t stick in Cleveland. Let’s be real about this situation.
This Sunday night game is going to require some individuals truly standing out, and making an indelible mark on the outcome, or the Ravens will be 3-2 going into Cleveland in Week 6 (which is perfectly fine). The more I study the Falcons and Ravens the more I believe these individuals will have to be truly special Sunday night, and, no, I’m not including the back-up QB in this list because if he tries to be special, and they concoct a game plan for him to attempt to be special it will reflect poorly on all of them.
Here are the four individuals who need to step up:
He’s had a very nice start to the season, but he hasn’t been taking games over and he hasn’t been as disruptive as, say, hybrid defensive back Derwin James at his peak in this system for the Chargers under Jesse Minter. You get the sense Minter has been holding back some with how creative he gets with this unicorn, and that his homecoming in Atlanta might be just the time to create a Hamilton-centric plan.
They need him to be a playmaker in run support with tackling but also maybe trying to punch another ball loose on a jump cut, with Falcons backs Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson dominating the last two weeks. This is a game where he should be all over the line of scrimmage and I also wonder if, with Atlanta young QB Michael Penix still a little skittish coming back from a third ACL surgery, and with top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson not expected to play, if we see intense blitzing – run blitzing and on passing downs – from Hamilton.
“I think if we run and hit well, we will do what we need to do,” Hamilton said Wednesday. “And at the end of the day, that is what this game comes down to — a very fundamental approach to this game. I am excited to see what we do."
Hamilton is blitzing more this season (17% of opposing dropbacks as opposed to 10% last year), but has three pressures on 25 rushes, a 12% rate that is half his career total.
Another Ravens player who is returning to Georgia – Smith played high school ball a few hours from Atlanta and went to UGA – who will want to show out. If Minter does what we expect here and leans into heavy fronts, Smith should be freed to run around and make plays. Dare I say it, I expect to see some 8-man boxes on Sunday night; the Ravens have only played about 5 snaps of 4-3 looks all season.
Atlanta will run the outside zone all night long until or unless it’s stopped ( Bijan averages 7.4/carry in the stretch play ) and the linebackers will have a lot to say about it and this one carries the biggest cap hit of any inside linebacker in the NFL ($33M) and the second-highest salary among all veteran inside backers – and we all know that’s not to make plays on the ball in flight. He’s not getting sacks and passes defensed. He’s here to organize and set a tone and be connective tissue between all three levels of the defense and be a tackling machine.
“Lot of respect for (Bijan Robinson) as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block,” Smith said. “I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game.”
Some looks with four linemen and four linebackers – with Hamilton essentially serving as one – make a lot of sense to me.
We are hesitant to include a rookie on this list but the personnel on the offense is what it is right now. Snoop hooking up with Zay Flowers deep is a silly ask and he has nine completions over 20 yards in his career . The receivers will be doing a lot of blocking, but the back-up QB did connect with the young tight end on some under-center, bootleg plays in the preseason and some quick catch-and-run plays for Hibner in the slot make a lot of sense.
He is a better athlete than highly-paid vet Mark Andrews, and with Durham Smythe now out for the season, and Nick Vannett not as well-rounded as Smythe, there is a runway for Hibner. No Ja’Kobi Lane – another big body who was doing slot work before his injury Week 1 - and a QB who is not going to be pushing it deep. Could see a lot of action underneath and the Ravens badly need YAC; Andrews ain’t that guy and Derrick Henry is somehow second to Flowers on the team in that key metric.
“(Smythe) is such an incredible player, an incredible person and teammate, and he's going to be sorely missed,” Andrews said. “But, we are going to do the best that we can in the tight end room to be ready. [Hibner and rookie Josh Cuevas] have been playing outstanding, just growing each and every game. So we have a lot of trust in them, and it's just going to be all hands-on-deck from us."
I really hope he is playing word games with the Falcons and trying to sell them on a mode of operation that he wouldn’t exactly espouse. Hopefully, he is just gassing up Snoop and trying to send messages to the locker room.
Because if he actually calls this game like he would for Lamar, it will be over at halftime. He needs to lean heavily on run-game coordinator Dwayne Ledford, who coached Atlanta’s offensive line before coming over here, and get creative with perimeter runs and attacking the boundary with speed. Doyle has a minute body of work and is trying to fool the Falcons, surely, when he says the stuff he’s said this week. But just in case, he’s on notice.
He needs to be smart and calculated and conservative with his approach Sunday night.
“I do not think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all,” Doyle said Thursday. “I think regardless of who is in there, you are trying to hunt explosives. I want us to be physical outside, whether that is our first receiver or our seventh receiver that came up from the practice squad. I think that the standard is still the standard regardless of who is in there, and that cannot change.”

title: Ravens Say They Won't Scale Back Offense For Their Back-up QB. They Better Be Bluffing
full_text:
There is some serious mythologizing of Snoop Huntley going on in Owings Mills these days.
The Ravens back-up quarterback, to hear people in The Castle talk about, is one of the premier No. 2 QBs in the NFL, and a trusted piece and an excellent alternative to Lamar Jackson. Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is so head-over-heels about the potential to win a game as a young play caller with a No. 2 QB that he’s threatening to bring a Lamar Jackson game plan into a very difficult game Sunday night in Atlanta .
Good grief. Give me a break.
A year ago these are the same executives who wanted nothing to do with Huntley anymore and believed that thoroughly washed Cooper Rush was an upgrade (Rush is now in Atlanta and “played” two games for the Falcons picking up as the complete mess he was in Baltimore). So spare me the hyperbole and over-the-top compliments. Jackson is almost certain not to play this week and maybe not next week, either , and things are going to be tough for this offense and Doyle better figure that out quickly and make major adjustments.
The combination of Huntley with a makeshift offensive line and one that can’t even really run block for Derrick Henry , is potentially perilous and thinking you can air it out like Jackson was – 10.1 yards/attempt, highest in the NFL – with Huntley (5.9/attempt and very limited as a downfield passer ), is taking people for fools.
“I do not think the mentality of how you want to run the offense changes at all,” Doyle said with a straight face on Thursday. “I think regardless of who is in there, you are trying to hunt explosives.”
The Falcons are getting pressure as readily as any team in the NFL right now, they are doing it without blitzing, and they are facing an incredibly suspect offensive line that is so bad the GM, who created the mess starting with letting elite center Tyler Linderbaum walk as a free agent, just traded a second-round pick for a veteran who hasn’t been the same since back surgery and who the Eagles didn’t even really think was a center anymore .  And Huntley, for all his limitations, is a an acute problem when he is put under any sort of pressure.
Huntley is 7-9 in his career (Jackson covers up a ridiculous amount of roster warts for one of the most overrated GMs in the NFL). Huntley is pretty pedestrian when not pressured _ again this franchise was done with him and so was the rest of the league before Rush crashed out – with a rating of 89.8. One thing Huntley can do when not under duress is complete the lay ups (73% completion percentage).
Everything falls apart when he gets some heat, especially if you can generate that rush without bringing five defenders – which the Falcons do as well as anyone in the NFL.
Huntley has a career rating of 62.0 under pressure, completing just 46.8% of his passes with four TDs and three picks and averaging a scant 4.9 yards per attempt. Yikes. He has a career 84.8 rating against the blitz, so, again, the big problems occur when you get him rattled with four up front. Against this OL, that’s well within reason.
And the idea he is going to attack downfield is taking people for fools. Huntley is 9-for-47 in his career on passes that travel over 20 yards in the air, with four picks and no TDs and a 20-something rating. Going there in a dome with this group around him would be courting disaster. Go for it rook, sitting up there in the press box with your long script of plays. I dare you.
The Falcons will destroy those seven-step drops.
Atlanta leads the NFL generating a 47.3% pressure rate. They have nine more pressures than any team in the league and they are second with 32 QB hits and they are doing all this despite being 29th in blitz rate (around 20%). If Huntley isn't leaning into checkdowns and the ball isn’t coming out very fast and not going not very far, big problems will arise.
