title: The Ravens Must Emphasize These 3 Things To Upset The Falcons
full_text:
The Ravens are underdogs for the first time under rookie head coach Jesse Minter, and rightfully so.
The Falcons board the second-best run game in the NFL – and at 477 yards the last two weeks since Michael Penix Jr. took over at quarterback, it’s really the best (Bijan Robinson is averaging a cool 7.4/carry running outside zone). They are allowing an NFL-best 2.7 yards per carry – a half yard better than the rest of the NFL – and also have the number one pass rush in the league. And they are at home on a Sunday night.
The Ravens’ injury report continues to look quite imposing, from quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) not practicing all week, on down ( there are going to be quite a few absences ) and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle must also navigate a makeshift offensive line for at least another week until new trade acquisition Cam Jurgens is out of the concussion protocol ( a lot about that risky trade is odd ).
It’s a lot to digest and the team is also in its second week back from traveling to another continent to play a football game in Brazil and some around the game believe the impact of that can take hold more acutely in the second week back. Baltimore’s run game is going nowhere with this offensive line right now no matter what Derrick Henry tries, which could spell big problems with backup QB Snoop Huntley not nearly as adept pushing the ball downfield as Jackson is (Lamar is leading the NFL at 10.1 yards/attempt and Huntley is at 5.9/attempt in his career.
Still, the Falcons have not yet proven to be a juggernaut under new coach Kevin Stefanski, the Ravens have a strong understanding of how he likes to operating facing him for years in Cleveland and Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford came over from Atlanta so he should have as good a read on Bijan Robinson as anyone, not that it will matter.
There is a path to win, and it will take the Ravens adhering to these principles:
The Ravens have played just five snaps in a 4-3 look all season. They should double that in the first half Sunday night. They’ve played just 24 snaps in a 3-4. Being in nickel or dime 90% of the time won’t fly against these Dirty Birds, and Minter has to know that .
“I think it is an exciting challenge for us, when you pride yourself on stopping the run,” middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. “Lot of respect for [Bijan Robinson] as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block. I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game. It is about showing up, and obviously the whole world's watching, so showing up and showing out."
Um, maybe a front-eight game. Could line up with Zion Young and Tavius Robinson on the edge, Calais Campbell (a former Falcon) and Nnamdi Madubuike inside (or even a Broderick Washington type), with hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton mugging the line of scrimmage as a de-facto LB, along with linebackers Smith, Trenton Simpson and Teddye Buchanan on the field.
We should see some personnel deployments Sunday that we have not seen prior. This difficult of this assignment dictates it.
So the line is still shaky and do-it-all-blocking tight end Durham Smythe was lost for the season, and we are asking more of a rookie tight ends that was expected. But, it appears both starting tackles – Ronnie Stanley and Roger Rosengarten are good to go. Running behind them has been one of the few things to work for the Ravens lately on the ground, and the perimeter attack will be huge all around Sunday , and extra tackle Carson Vinson should see plenty of the field.
The Falcons are mauling people at the line of scrimmage (72% success rate against the run is nuts) and not devoted a ton of manpower to do so. Ravens have to find a way to swing the math at least a little more in their favor and unbalanced lines and tackle-eligible plays can make that happen.
“For you to be No. 1 in the run game,” Henry explained of the Falcons, “you have to have guys that are willing to go tackle by any means. And it means something to them, from what we see on tape."
Doyle kept going on and on Thursday morning about nothing changing in terms of his overarching offensive goals if he has to play Huntley (he will). Um, that best just be lip service.
“Absolutely, when we put the game plan together, the mindset is still the same,” Doyle opined on Thursday. "We are still trying to stress and attack rules. We are still trying to go after a defense and see if we can pry out bigger plays and be able to move the ball down the field."
This needs to be a scaled -down approach loaded with high-percentage routes and checkdowns everywhere against a team getting a 47% pressure rate without having to blitz (20%, 29th in NFL). Short routes to the outside and trying to crate situations for big YAC is what is required here. Huntley is erratic throwing downfield and doesn't have Jackson's arm; the approach must reflect that.
Henry is already on pace to shatter his 15 receptions last season (seven through four games) and he should get fed some in the air by design – again, to the outside. More bubble screens and passes behind the line of scrimmage might be in order.

title: What The Ravens Thursday Injury Report Reveals About Sunday's Game
full_text:
Ravens coaches continue to claim two-time MVP Lamar Jackson could face the Falcons Sunday, while execs around the NFL wonder if he will even face the Browns in Week 6.
The superstar quarterback did not practice again Thursday with an ankle injury that kept him out of the second-half last week, had him in a walking boot and required an MRI test. Head coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle certainly want Atlanta to wonder who will be at quarterback Sunday night, but trust me, the Falcons are expecting back-up Snoop Huntley for myriad and obvious reasons.
Minter claims the Ravens could take it right up until game time, but having Jackson play this early in the season on an injury like this would run counter to how they have already handled similar situations with star receiver Zay Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley and $30M pass rusher Trey Hendrickson. Jackson, who is essentially in a walk year with no guarantees beyond this season , has traditionally required a week or two to be able to trust his body fully enough to play with lower-grade injuries in the past, and the Ravens offensive line remains under duress (we’ll see if just-acquired center Cam Jurgens can return from a concussion in Week 6 ) and the Falcons have the NFL’s premier pass rush right now.
So, yeah, it will be Huntley at QB, and the Ravens will also almost certainly be without Humphrey (calf) – in a career tailspin for years and injury-prone but carrying the top cap hit of any corner in the NFL and making $19.3M – as well. Hendrickson, also with a significant injury history, has yet to practice since getting a procedure on his finger last week that Minter said would get him back on the field quickly.  Hendrickson was signed to a $30M/year deal after Ravens general manager hid behind Maxx Crosby’s alleged medical issues ( he’s only playing about 95% of the reps for the Raiders ) to bail out of that trade.
Thursday is the last heavy practice day of the week and the participation generally is a strong indicator about Sunday.
Flowers has been limited with an ongoing hamstring injury but he is playing barring some unforeseen setback. The Ravens are trying to navigate left tackle Ronnie Stanley through a painful toe injury and limiting his practice reps but he practiced in full Thursday. Hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton has been nursing a groin injury and was limited Wednesday but practiced full on Thursday and also is in line to play.
Guards John Simpson (groin) and Andrew Vorhees (foot) did not practice Wednesday but returned in a limited capacity on Thursday. Simpson has been playing through this situation all season and started every game. The Ravens would be foolish to move rookie guard Vega Ioane from center . He should remain deployed between those two (on youngster Emery Jones Jr. if he has to fill in) for one more week until Jurgens can likely return.

title: Ravens Trade For Eagles Center Cam Jurgens Deserves Two Grades: We Explain Both
full_text:
The Ravens have known they needed a legitimate starting center option since the February scouting combine when star Tyler Linderbaum had a market far beyond where they wanted to go.
They also had exclusive negotiating rights to Linderbaum for the duration of his rookie contract and failed to get him extended before the 2025 season, when both he and two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson required contract extensions and neither got close. So any window into the Ravens dealing two picks, a fifth in 2027 and a second-round selection in 2028, to take on Eagles lineman Cam Jurgens , who had major back/nerve surgery in February 2025 and has not been the same since, and move him back to his natural position of center has to start there.
Any evaluation of an in-season trade with a general manager as accomplished as the Eagles GM Howie Roseman must factor in the health and current status of the player, and the situation into which Jurgens is being parachuted – bleak with Baltimore’s interior offensive as bad as any in football and getting exploited in the pass rush and unable to sustain any interior rushing presence even for the great and powerful Derrick Henry. It’s a complicated transaction that merits two evaluating grades in real-time given the player’s highly-unusual injury history.
And after having time to speak to two outside general managers about this trade and some former general managers and salary cap guy and some other current NFL personnel executives, it became clear the spectrum to use for setting a standard of what this transaction could realistically offer the Ravens.
There is no way around the fact the Ravens dug themselves an ugly hole here by mismanaging this critical situation – while installing a new offense with a rookie offensive coordinator and with issues across the offensive line beyond just center. Their 30-year-old first-time play caller, Declan Doyle, always needed a proven veteran leader at this position – his mentor Sean Payton told us so this offseason – and the fact they didn’t take their pick of any available in the second round of the draft – before the run on interior OL begun that everyone in the league knew was about to begin – they probably solve this problem far more cheaply than what it’s come to now.
They weren’t fooling anyone pretty budget signings Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn were anything close to starting-caliber players (“They don’t have an NFL center on their roster, they just don’t,” longtime lineman and NFL analyst Brian Baldinger told me this summer), and when those guys got hurt (along with late signing Ethan Pocic who never looked right coming off Achilles surgery) the huge problem became suffocating .
The Ravens’ history is to draft and develop centers and they truly value them, because a lot of people thought Linderbaum went too high in the first place when they took him in the first round. They have resisted paying them top dollar going all the way back to Jason Brown . Holding 11 picks and not addressing this in a draft with myriad options was always odd and taking a hope-and-prayer pass rusher in Zion Young (yes, he can set the edge) struck us as ridiculously odd at the time and plenty of execs around the league agreed.
“You only make this move if you are desperate,” one GM told me, who also noted: "Those guys aren't exactly quick to trade picks that high (second round).
Jurgens has traveled to South America to get treatment for ongoing nerve issues and he gutted through 14 games last season but was in extreme pain and was not good on the field. The issue spread up and down his legs. The Eagles know his medicals better than anyone and were willing to unload him at a time their All-Pro guard, Landon Dickerson, is on IR and all-world tackle, Lane Johnson, just basically retired for mental health reasons. So when they do this, it raises major red flags about the medicals for a player who has a high pain threshold but carries big risks, or “serious medical red flags” as another GM put it:
“Jurgens is still a good player, he is, we have good grades on his film. And it’s a major upgrade to anything Baltimore had there. But … Howie isn’t mailing it in. He’s not tanking. No way Howie does this if he’s convinced this is a starter for him - at center or guard or anywhere - for the rest of that contract.”
Jurgens makes $16.5M this season and is essentially guaranteed $15M of his $17.5M salary for 2027 and carries that same figure for 2028, without such current guarantees.
“What are the Ravens thinking?” said one longtime NFL exec who watches the Eagles closely. “The good, but not really great, Cam, left once he had the back surgery. You don’t see trades like this for interior offensive linemen and this one had back surgery and the tape since then is not the same, including at center.”
Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowl player and replaced a Hall of Fame center in Jason Kelce and learned from him before taking over. He anchored a dominating, Lombardi-trophy winning, offensive line loaded with Alphas. He is a warrior and brings a different profile and resume into that offensive line than anyone else’s, even decorated left tackle Ronnie Stanley.
"At the center position, you really are the voice of the offense out there," offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford said Thursday, hinting strongly at how much having a true vet center matters, as we've said all along.
Jurgens says he feels great this season, it was an ugly situation in Philly (although the one he’s walking into has issues, too), and the Ravens get to move stud rookie Vega Ioane back to guard, where he can maul, and perhaps they will be able to improve in pass protection and run blocking in the interior. Given the price they paid, they must.
Teams were blitzing the A Gap with abandon before Ioane stabilized things Week 4, stunts and twists were gutting them, and there seemed to be very little connective tissue between the center and guards no matter which combination Baltimore tried. Jurgens’s presence and intangibles change that, and they Ravens made big additions to their medical team this offseason and they have to hope they can keep Jurgens as healthy and pain-free as possible but he plays a car-crash position and some wonder if all the years of the Eagles running the “Tush Push” into the ground, literally, has taken years off those linemen.
“They may have just solved their biggest problem,” said one NFL personnel executive. “And if this isn’t their starting center the next three years, they just made it worse.”
But by Week 6, if indeed Jurgens is out of concussion protocol, the Ravens should have a better foundation in the middle of their line than at any point since Linderbaum left and they have to do whatever they can to maintain that as long as possible.
"He isn't a guard, strictly a center,” Baldinger suggested to me after the trade. “It allows Ioane to stay at guard where he can be the next (potential future Hall of Famer Marshal) Yanda."

title: Ravens Georgia Natives Look Forward To Homecomings vs. Falcons
full_text:
Although the Baltimore Ravens will be the visiting team at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday night when they take on the red-hot Atlanta Falcons in primetime, two of their core leaders and best players on the defensive side of the ball will not only feel right at home but will also have a large contingent of supporters in attendance.
Both three-time All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and four-time Pro Bowl inside linebacker Roquan Smith grew up in Georgia and are looking forward to business trip that will double as homecoming for them.
Hamilton hails from Atlanta and attended Marist School, a private Catholic school located in Brookhaven, Georgia. This interconference Battle of the Birds will be a true "full-circle moment" for him, given that his first opportunity to play at the Falcons' home stadium was supposed to be while he was in high school for a state championship game. But Mother Nature had other plans that fateful day.
"That got snowed out, and they moved it to my home stadium my junior year of high school," Hamilton said. "We actually lost that game. It still bugs me. But, yes, it will be cool to play in front of a ton of people that I know, grew up with and have people from Mobile, Alabama — where my dad's side is from — coming up. So, it will be really cool to just see everybody. My family does not have to travel, so that will be easy for them, and hopefully [we will] leave with a win."
Smith is a country boy from Macon County, Ga., which is about a two-hour drive from Atlanta. Unlike Hamilton, who starred at Notre Dame, when it came time to choose where to play at the collegiate level, he opted to stay closer to home and play for the University of Georgia.
While he got to play in some big games on the Falcons' home turf in front of fans as a Bulldog, he has yet to do so as a pro since he got traded to the Ravens during the 2022 season, prior to the Chicago Bears road game in Atlanta in Week 11 of that season. He plans on making the most of this opportunity not only for himself but for the small community that raised him.
"I have my high school football team coming up. I have the rec department coming up. I have like countless family members, countless friends and stuff showing up," Smith said. "It will be pretty sweet, man. [It's] obviously a quick little drive, about two hours, two hours and 20 minutes, and guys [are] coming from the country.
"There will be a heavy 'Macon County Roquan Tribe' out there. I am excited about that, but obviously the mission stays the same. With all the people coming to support, [I] definitely have to show up in a big-time way. That is just going to take me just doing my job, play in and play out, and playing violent."
As two of the central players in the spine of head coach and defensive play-caller Jesse Minter's unit that has underwhelmed and struggled with consistency through the first four weeks, both Hamilton and Smith are determined to take advantage of the opportunity to right the ship under a national spotlight.
The whole world will be watching, and we will be doing what it takes to get the job done," Smith said. "We know that it will be a challenge, but we are all excited for it.
"We are just excited to continue to showcase who we are and just keep building off our positives week in and week out, and building off the negatives as well and not having self-inflicted things.
They both serve as physical tone-setters for the team on that side of the ball and are well aware that any hopes they have of cooling or at least slowing down a 2-2 Falcons team that has looked like a juggernaut and averaged 40 points a game over the past two weeks begin and end with how well they defend First Team All Pro running back Bijan Robinson .
"I think [Robinson] is super talented in everything that he does," Hamilton said. "He is very sudden, very strong, explosive. Obviously, he has the stats to back it up and, you know, there is not a lot like him. So, it is up to us to be where we are supposed to be. I think that is the big thing first and foremost, especially in the run game. Do not get out of your gap, trust guys to come and do their job and I think we will be fine."
The Ravens have particularly struggled when it comes to tackling in space and run defense when it comes to yards given up before contact. They can't afford for either tendency to persist or rear its ugly head against the Falcons because they get steamrolled by one of the hottest and best-balanced teams in the league in primetime.
"I think it is an exciting challenge for us, when you pride yourself on stopping the run," Smith said. "[I have] a lot of respect for [Bijan Robinson] as a runner, their offensive line, their receivers, with their willingness to block. I think it is a great challenge for us. I look at this as a front-seven game. It is about showing up, and obviously the whole world's watching, so showing up and showing out."

title: Ravens Week 4 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Aces Major Test With Flying Colors
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's grind of a 24-18 long-awaited home win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is .500 or better, and they are tied with the Cleveland Browns atop the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookie who was a healthy scratch was undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall is eligible to return from short-term injured reserve after this game, while third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane will remain on it for at least one more week after getting hurt in Week 1. Seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his fourth career start but played his first full game at center after he first slid over from his right guard spot to help close out last week's dramatic win. Not only was Ioane playing out of position, but he was going up against one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league, the Titans' star Jeffery Simmons. He kept Lamar Jackson clean by not allowing a sack, a quarterback hit or even a single pressure on Simmons' 32 pass-rush snaps and held the four-time Pro Bowler without a tackle for loss as well. His overall grade of 75.1 from Pro Football Focus was the fourth-highest mark on the team.
A sampling of Vega Ioane's first game at center. 💪 pic.twitter.com/ZNeBJ8MtGM
"It was pretty solid. I would say, [there were] a lot of mistakes on my end," Ioane said. "I take full responsibility for that. There were a lot of plays where I did not snap the ball at the right time [or] right cadence, things like that. But we have a lot of time to fix that. [I want to just give a] big shoutout to the guys around me, the whole [offensive] line, the receivers, the quarterbacks. They had full trust in me going out there. They have been helping me out throughout the entire game, so big shoutout to them."
Now that the Ravens have traded for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens , they can slide Ioane back over to his natural spot, where he's been the most dominant. However, knowing that the youngster is capable of moving over and playing at a high level is a testament to his versatility and could serve them well if they ever find themselves in a similar pinch in the future.
The second-rounder played nearly 40% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps and had another solid game against the run, where he consistently set a strong edge on early downs and finished with a pair of assisted tackles.
classic zion young pic.twitter.com/a7FgiIX0zh
The fourth-rounder was active for the second time this season, but unlike his uneventful debut, where he didn't log a snap on offense or special teams, he logged 23 snaps and his first career catch and targets. Both of the passes that came his way were from Jackson during the last drive of the first half on back-to-back plays. The first resulted in a 13-yard reception that moved the ball just inside the range of second-year kicker Tyler Loop and the second target was just off the mark on a shallow route.
I don’t know about you guys, but I was starting to get worried about Elijah Sarratt. I’m glad the Ravens finally got him on the field! pic.twitter.com/WKCcXuLkWu
As key as the yardage he picked up on that drive was to set up an M&T Bank Stadium record 64-yard field goal, he committed one of several back-breaking penalties for the offense. Sarratt was flagged for holding while attempting to make a block downfield that negated an impressive 29 yard scramble by Jackson late in the second quarter that would've moved the ball near midfield.
The fourth-rounder recorded multiple new season highs for the second week in a row, playing 37 offensive snaps and hauling in both of his targets for the second week in a row for a career-high 34 receiving yards. His first catch went for a career-long 25-yard catch-and-run that was the result of a masterful play call by offensive coordinator Declan Doyle that got him streaking wide open down the field. His second catch almost went for a first down, as he picked up nine yards to jump-start an early fourth-quarter drive that looked like it was going to end with points had it not stalled out at midfield.
More good scheme by Declan Doyle. Fake screen setup gets the Titans' LB to bite and leave Matt Hibner wide open for a 25 yarder. pic.twitter.com/weIUHZ6AnC
"He is a smart dude, but he's continued just to work and learn and get better in blocking, [and] with anything he's asked to do, he does it, and he does it at a high level," Mark Andrews said. "So, [there's] just a lot of upside with him, and he's going to continue to make big plays and help this team win games."
The fifth-rounder played over 40% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps for the second week in a row, as he has clearly carved out a role in their defense. He recorded a career-high five total, all of which were solos, and he recorded his second career tackle for a loss on a third-down checkdown to a running back one yard behind the line of scrimmage to force a punt. Rivers was also responsible for allowing the touchdown completion to Titans' wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson late in the fourth quarter that made the final score look closer than it actually was and felt for most of the second
The fifth-rounder saw his most extensive playing time of the season thus far for the second week in a row, with 27 combined between offense and special teams, including a season-high 18 on offense and nine on special teams, getting more reps with blocking tight end Durham Smythe lost for the season. He wasn't targeted but recorded his first career tackle on special teams when he ran Titans wide receiver Chimere Dike out of bounds after punt return of 10 yards in the third quarter.
The sixth-round specialist had another strong performance in a game that saw him attempt a career-high six punts and record a career-high 284 punt yards. He was a field-flipping weapon once again, helping the Ravens win the battle of field position by pinning the Titans' offense inside their 20-yard line four times and recording one touchback. He averaged 47.3 yards per punt and a long of 56.
With four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher out recovering from finger surgery, the undrafted free agent got to play his first regular-season snaps on defense after playing exclusively on special teams through the first three weeks. He checked into the game on the Titans' second drive, played 16 snaps and made the most of his first extended opportunity in the fourth quarter on Tennessee's final possession when he recorded his first career sack. After the guard failed to pick him up on a stunt, Burke used his length to dive at the legs of Ward. His 14 snaps on special teams were the most among all rookies and tied for fourth-most on the team.

title: Bills vs. Rams Expert Pick Roundup: Buffalo Faces Uphill Battle in Week 5
full_text:
Week 5 will feature the Buffalo Bills in primetime as they visit the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football .
Buffalo is coming off a frustrating loss to the New England Patriots , and things won't be any easier for them this week. Los Angeles comes into the game with a record of 2-2, but they're still one of the top contenders in the league and were just one game shy of making the Super Bowl in 2025.
A win would do wonders for the Bills' confidence, but can they pull that off? Here's a look at what some of the experts believe will happen as we check out several outlets to see who is favored to win this matchup.
Dan Parr gave his reasoning for picking the Rams, and he was focused on the Buffalo defense being unable to deal with the high-powered Los Angeles offense.
"We saw last week that the Bills have a get-right defense for quarterbacks, with Buffalo allowing Drake Maye to have his best game of the season -- by far -- after a horrendous start to 2026. I’m counting on Matthew Stafford to shake off his struggles (6:6 TD-INT ratio) against a defense that doesn’t appear up to the challenge of covering Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. The Bills rank among the bottom 10 in scoring and total defense, while Los Angeles ranks among the top 10 in both categories," Parr wrote.
Prisco's Pick: Rams 34, Bills 33
"This is one of the best games of the week. The Bills are coming off a tough loss to the Patriots, while the Rams rallied to beat the Eagles. Look for a lot of points in this one as Josh Allen and Matt Stafford have big games. In the end, the Rams will make the plays late to win it," Prisco wrote.
The experts are high on the Rams in this one, and it's easy to see why. Los Angeles hasn't looked like the team we thought they would be, but they played well down the stretch against the Philadelphia Eagles to pull off a big win on the road last week.
Now, they're at home, and they get to face a team that has to travel across the country. Throw in the fact that Buffalo hasn't played exceptionally well over the past two weeks, and it seems like a game they could wind up losing.
There's also the fact that Joe Brady is still a young head coach, and Sean McVay is a Super Bowl winner who knows how to exploit a team's weaknesses. That said, this Rams team doesn't look like the juggernaut we're used to, and the Bills will be focused following their loss to the Pats. That's why I see them pulling off an upset on the road.
Final score: Bills 28, Rams 23

title: Revisiting Huge Josh Allen Performance That Wasn't Enough Last Time Bills Faced Rams
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have certainly been involved in their share of high-scoring games in recent years, and this season has been no exception.
Joe Brady’s team leads the NFL with 127 points after four weeks of play. There was the Week 1 victory at Houston, 36-31. Four days later, the Bills reached the end zone early and often in a 41-31 prime time win over the visiting Detroit Lions.
On Monday night, the Los Angeles Rams will be hosting Josh Allen and company for the third time in five years .
Only the Chicago Bears have gained more total yards per game than Sean McVay’s team, while Buffalo’s offense ranked was ranked sixth in the league in this same category entering Week 5. Brady’s team also leads the NFL in points per game (31.7) this season.
Obviously, there have been a few notable changes for both clubs since these two perennial playoff teams met two years ago at SoFi Stadium. Sean McDermott was still head coach of the Bills. As for the Rams, wide receiver Davante Adams was a member of the New York Jets, and defensive tackle Aaron Donald had retired after the 2023 season.
The last time the (6-6) Rams STUNNED the 10-2 Bills in 2024 🫪 pic.twitter.com/C2EkhoFhT2
In Week 14 of 2024, McVay’s squad outlasted the Bills , 44-42. The clubs combined for 902 yards of total offense, with the Rams owning the slight edge, 457-445. Both clubs played turnover-free football. And while Rams’ quarterback Matthew Stafford was on point with 320 yards through the air (23-of-30) and touchdown tosses to Puka Nacua and Cooper Kupp (now with the Seattle Seahawks), Allen put on quite a show in a losing effort.
The teams were tied 7-7 after 15 minutes of play. Both clubs drove 70 yards for touchdowns in the first quarter. And as it turned out, the Bills would never have the lead in this 86-point shootout. They trailed by 17 points twice in the third quarter and would outscore the Rams, 21-6, in the fourth quarter.
Throwback to one of the most INSANE fantasy performances we’ve ever seen. 🤯🔥 Josh Allen vs. the Rams in 2024: 🎯 342 passing yards 🏈 3 passing TDs 💨 82 rushing yards 🏈 3 rushing TDs 💥 6 TOTAL TDs 📈 51.88 fantasy points The first player in NFL history with 3 passing TDs… https://t.co/eNbOZ8f3Ry pic.twitter.com/rJ7mQWKoUG
As for Allen, he accounted for all of Buffalo’s six touchdowns one way or another. He hit on 22-of-37 throws for 342 yards and three scores. He was the Bills’ leading rusher in attempts (10) and yards (82) and ran for three TDs—all one-year jaunts. Amari Cooper led the team with six receptions, while Khalil Shakir, Mack Hollins (now with the Patriots), and Ty Johnson were on the receiving end of Allen’s touchdown tosses.
One Sunday later, the Bills outlasted Dan Campbell’s club at Ford Field, 48-42. Allen had another huge performance and Buffalo needed all of that to avoid a second straight loss. This Monday evening in Inglewood, he may have to be at his turnover-free best if the club is to avoid back-to-back losses this season.

title: Bills' Week 5 Friday Practice Status for Christian Benford, DJ Moore And More
full_text:
Three Buffalo Bills' starters missed their second consecutive practice on Friday in Orchard Park.
As the Bills prepare for their Monday Night Football road game against the Los Angeles Rams, wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and slot cornerback Dee Alford were not present during the media-viewing portion of practice for the second day in a row (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
While Moore has been fighting through a shoulder injury since midway through the Week 2 win over the Detroit Lions, Oliver and Alford were banged up during the Week 4 loss to the New England Patriots. All three players left the October 4 game early.
Although they're not visibly active during practice, the injured players could still wind up being available on Monday night.
"Our guys are going to prepare," said first-year head coach Joe Brady. "There's going to be guys that might not practice, but you guys know how I am with that, and we're going to do everything we can."
Moore, who has appeared in 91 consecutive games dating back to 2020, is likely doing what it takes to prepare his body for a Week 5 appearance.
"DJ's a competitor," said Brady who spent two years coaching Moore with the Carolina Panthers. "You see the difference with us with DJ out on the football field. I think that that's natural and that's real. He is always going to do, literally, everything he can to be out there, not just for himself, but for his teammates."
Whether it's Moore, Oliver, Alford or all three, the chances of playing increase as a result of the Monday game.
"We also have the luxury of having a full day, an extra day with that. We're gonna give some guys [the chance] all the way through to game day. Knowing that if they give us the best opportunity to win, we're gonna roll with it," said Brady.
Oliver took a hit to the knee area last Sunday, and he exited. He spent the rest of the game in uniform on the sideline sans helmet.
Alford tweaked his ankle, and sounded optimistic when addressing reporters after the game in the locker room.
Although their Week 5 availability is in question, Brady said they were not expected to be long-term issues.
The Bills will need all hands on deck to slow down the Rams' potent passing attack and elite receiving corps. In a positive development, it appears as if starting cornerback Christian Benford is nearing a return after missing the Week 4 loss.
Benford, who suffered a non-contact toe injury during the third quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers on September 27, practiced for the second straight day . He was a non-participant the entire week leading into the Patriots matchup.
With Alford also sidelined and backup nickel Jordan Hancock on Injured Reserve, the Bills are somewhat shorthanded at the position.

title: Three Bold Predictions for Buffalo Bills vs. Los Angeles Rams on Monday
full_text:
All eyes will be on the Buffalo Bills this week as they play in the final game of Week 5 . The Bills will travel to Southern California to take on the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football .
Los Angeles is coming off an impressive win, coming back in the fourth quarter to beat the Philadelphia Eagles. That win moved them to 2-2, which is surprising considering they entered the season as one of the huge favorites to win it all.
Buffalo was also seen as a favorite and while they're 3-1, they haven't looked sharp over the past two games. They still have the talent to defeat any team in the league, including the Rams, and have a far better chance of doing so if these three bold predictions come true.
Here's what the Bills' first injury report of the week looks like.
Through four games, Keon Coleman has been one of the biggest surprises for the Bills . He has 14 receptions for 217 yards and a touchdown, and is coming off his best game of the year. With DJ Moore dealing with a shoulder injury , Coleman stepped up and had 116 yards and a touchdown on six receptions.
He's been earning Josh Allen's trust and that should lead to even more opportunities going forward. In this first bold prediction, Coleman takes advantage of those opportunities and records 100 yards receiving with a touchdown for the second week in a row.
Matthew Stafford is going to be a problem for the Bills since he's one of the more accurate quarterbacks in the NFL. That doesn't mean they can't have some success against him, especially when it comes to the pass rush.
At 38 years old, Stafford isn't the most mobile quarterback, which is one of the reasons he's been sacked six times. That's good news for a Buffalo defense that has seen Greg Rousseau, Deone Walker , and Bradley Chubb all play well. In this bold prediction, all three continue to perform at a high level as each records a sack on Stafford.
During their wins over the Lions and Chargers, the Bills leaned heavily on James Cook as he had 135 yards on the ground in Week 2 and 154 yards in Week 3. Against the Patriots, he had 75 yards, but was still ripping off 6.2 yards per attempt. The problem was that he had just 12 attempts.
Against the Rams, that can't be the case. Cook needs to be a huge part of the game plan and in this final prediction, that's exactly what happens as he runs for more than 150 yards for the second time this season.

title: Bills' Official Week 5 Injury Report: DJ Moore, Ed Oliver Headline 14-Player List
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made three new additions to what is a lengthy Week 5 injury report on Thursday.
Defensive lineman Ed Oliver, slot cornerback Dee Alford and defensive end Landon Jackson are officially dealing with injuries as the Bills prepare for their Monday Night Football road test against the Los Angeles Rams. All three left at some point during the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots.
Alford did not practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue while Oliver also sat out with a knee problem. Jackson, who was seen wearing a knee brace, participated in a limited capacity at the week's first official practice .
There are 14 players listed on the Week 5 practice report, but nine were full participants. It's possible that all 14 wind up being available for the October 12 primetime kickoff.
"I hope to have everybody. We're gonna prepare. If there's guys that aren't playing in this game, I'm going to have the full confidence [in those who are playing]," said first-year head coach Joe Brady .
The fact that the Bills have an extra day for rest and recovery with the game being on Monday has Brady sounding optimistically.
"We're gonna do everything we can. We also have the luxury of having a full day, an extra day with that. We're gonna give some guys [the chance] all the way through to game day. Knowing that if they give us the best opportunity to win, we're gonna roll with it," said Brady prior to Thursday's practice in Orchard Park.
Along with Oliver and Alford, Moore was one of the three non-participants as the practice week kicked off. The wide receiver left the Week 4 loss after reaggravating his AC joint injury while hitting the ground on a catch attempt.
Moore, who has not missed a start since 2020, injured his shoulder in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions. He's been in and out of practice over the last couple weeks as he fights through the issue. He was a limited participant in the days leading up to the October 4 game.
"We owe it to him, if he feels 'hey, I can go out there and I can play at the level I can and I can be there for my teammates,' then we're gonna roll with him because he does make us better out there," said Brady.
Moore has 12 receptions for 178 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's played 132 offensive snaps.
With a Week 7 bye looming, it sounds as if Moore will solider through these next two games .
"I try not to look ahead, but we also do have a bye week in two weeks," siad Brady. "We'll see with where he's at, but he's gonna do everything he can to be ready to rock again this week."
Benford missed the Week 4 game due to a non-contact toe injury that booted him from the September 27 win over the Chargers.
Being that he did not practice at all last week , it's encouraging that he returned to the field in a limited capacity on Thursday. The fact that the Bills haven't placed Benford on Injured Reserve for more roster flexibility is another positive sign that he may be back on Monday night.
Although no injury is the same, it's worth noting that Benford missed one game last December due to a toe issue.
The Bills will practice again on Friday and Saturday with official injury reports to follow.

title: Three Areas Bills Must Exploit vs. Rams on Monday Night Football
full_text:
Despite still leading in the AFC East standings and holding a 3-1 record, the Buffalo Bills are at a bit of a crossroads of their 2026 season under first-year head coach Joe Brady.
After falling short to the previously floundering New England Patriots and quarterback Drake Maye last Sunday at home at Highmark Stadium, Brady and Co. find themselves at a fairly similar juncture as the Bills did just one season ago following a close 23-20 loss to the Patriots at the old stadium across Abbott Road in Orchard Park last October in Week 5.
Following that debacle under former head coach Sean McDermott, Buffalo went on to finish the remainder of the regular season with an 8-4 mark to finish the year second in the AFC East at 12-5, while New England surged forward by winning 11 out of its remaining 12 games to finish the year first in the division with a 14-3 record.
Although fans, players, and coaches didn’t know it at the time, the loss contributed to a seismic shift in the landscape of the division last fall and winter.
And, despite having a chance to rewrite history this season under Brady in their first matchup with the Patriots, the same “smoke detectors” that have been going off all preseason and in the month of September finally sounded the alarm in Western New York this past weekend.
Now, the Bills must quickly right the ship in order to avoid letting one defeat turn into back-to-back losses, which is exactly what happened last fall when Buffalo dropped another game to the Atlanta Falcons on the road immediately after the Patriots’ loss on October 5, 2025.
The game against the Falcons was on ESPN’s Monday Night Football . . . just like Buffalo’s upcoming Week 5 road matchup in Inglewood, California, against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium.
Will the results be different this time around?
For Bills Mafia’s sake—hopefully—but it won’t be easy. There are, however, some chinks in the armor for head coach Sean McVay’s squad, which is led by 2025 MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford.
And, with that in mind, here are three areas that the Bills must exploit in order to be successful in coming away victorious against the Rams across the country on Monday evening.
In spite of all of the early publicity for quarterback Josh Allen and his impressive statistical start to the 2026 season, Bills’ veteran running back James Cook III— last year’s NFL rushing champion —is once again quietly near the top of the leader board for total rushing yards so far this fall.
Trailing only Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker (87 carries/537 yards) and Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson (85 carries/494) at this point of October, Cook (70 carries/421 yards) could easily be atop the list if he would just be given more opportunity.
Twice this season—last week versus New England and in Week 1 against Houston—Cook has failed to top more than 13 carries despite averaging an impressive clip of 6.0 yards per attempt thus far through four games.
Simply put, there’s more to be gleaned from the former Georgia Bulldog, and it’d be prudent for Brady and offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. to get Cook even more involved in the gameplanning moving forward.
And, although the Los Angeles Rams’ defense is quite stout, they’re seemingly more susceptible in the running game than through the air as Los Angeles currently ranks second in the NFL against the pass (145.5 YPG), but just 11th against the run (102 YPG).
Needless to say, Buffalo would be smart to test the waters in the running game first before Allen and Co. start to try and pick apart the sticky secondary on Monday night.
Overall, the Rams’ defense ranks favorably in almost every statistical category. However, one area where they have struggled more than most is in the red zone.
Currently ranked just 14th in the league in red-zone defense after allowing a touchdown rate of 58.3% through four weeks, Los Angeles hasn’t been as strong once opposing teams are able to get inside the 20-yard line.
Luckily for Buffalo, that is an area where the team’s offense has been fairly steady to start this fall, as the Bills currently rank ninth in the NFL with a red-zone touchdown rate of 68.75%.
And, although Allen and the offense were just 2-for-4 on Sunday in the red zone against New England in the loss at Highmark Stadium, it’s still a portion of the field that Buffalo usually succeeds at.
So, if the Bills are going to come away with a win on the West Coast on Monday, then red-zone scoring efficiency will likely play a huge factor in determining the outcome one way or another.
Yes, Los Angeles’ quarterback Matthew Stafford won the NFL’s Most Valuable Player award last season, but that doesn’t mean the 38-year-old, 18-year veteran gunslinger isn’t without his faults.
Despite throwing for 1,189 passing yards and six touchdowns so far, Stafford is also second in the league in interceptions with six. And, he’s also been taken to the ground for six sacks, as well.
Keeping that in mind, it’ll be important for players like outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau and Deone Walker to continue dominating up front on Monday in an attempt to speed things up for Stafford in the passing game.
If they’re successful in getting him off his spot and getting him to throw a bit more erratically, then it’ll be up to players at the second and third levels of the defense to capitalize on any balls that might be left up for grabs in the secondary.
The turnover battle, which Buffalo is struggling mightily with right now, will be critical under the primetime lights at SoFi Stadium.

title: Josh Allen Week 5 Health Update After Only Four Rush Yards in Bills' First Loss
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' quarterback Josh Allen took a hit on his left knee against the Los Angeles Chargers on September 27, but he subsequently avoided a trip to the official Week 4 injury report .
Now, with the Bills preparing for a Week 5 appearance on Monday Night Football, Allen strongly dismissed any idea that the knee is an issue that's ultimately limiting his rushing attempts.
"There's no truth to that. Feeling great," said Allen following Thursday's practice in Orchard Park.
There was some speculation that Allen chose to cut back on his running in the October 4 loss to the New England Patriots as a means of protecting an injured knee . The elite dual threat did not take off to run when the pocket broke down against New England despite multiple opportunities to do so.
Allen carried five times for only four total yards in the 29-26 setback, but the fact that the Bills did not hesitate to call his number in multiple short yardage situations suggests that they weren't concerned about his knee.
It's also worth noting that after being hit on a fourth-quarter carry against the Chargers, Allen proceeded to rush twice more down the stretch in the Week 3 victory. After a one-yard touchdown rush, the quarterback ran for seven yards up the middle out of shotgun formation on his final carry in the 24-16 win.
"I'm not concerned with Josh," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady in the wake of the September 27 incident. "I'd love for him to not take some of the hits. He's a competitor, and I have to take that into consideration with some play calling as well."
We wrote about Brady potentially deciding to dial back Allen in the running game for now.
Although unlikely, one has to wonder if Allen has felt any effects from the offseason foot surgery that had him on crutches for Brady's introductory press conference.
Attempting to avoid the Cleveland Browns' pass rush, Allen broke a bone in his foot in Week 16 last December. He played through the injury the rest of the way, opting for minor surgery not until after the Bills were eliminated.
Including playoffs, Allen has made 141 consecutive starts for the Bills.

title: Four Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 5 Road Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills suffered their first loss of the season in Week 4, falling 29-26 to the New England Patriots. It was a tough outing, and this week isn't going to be any easier.
Buffalo will hit the road in Week 5 and has to travel across the country for a showdown with the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. The Rams are 2-2 and have not looked like the contender everyone knows they can be, but they did seem to find a higher gear in their fourth-quarter win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
The Bills entered the season as a favorite to win the Super Bowl and knocking off the Rams would go a long way toward reminding us all why they're considered elite contenders. For that to happen, they need the following four players, who have a lot to prove, to step up their performance.
Dee Alford recorded an interception in the Week 4 loss to the Patriots, but he managed to put himself in the dog house after the game. Alford made a comment about the defense struggling to communicate due to crowd noise . He was trying to discuss the way sound travels in the stadium and while his words might have been innocent, it led to criticism.
The comment was seen as a complaint and the ordeal made enough noise that defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard decided to call out players who complain about crowd noise, and had some choice words. In addition to the bad PR he recently received, Alford is entering Week 5 with a PFF grade of 42.6 and needs to perform much better as they travel to L.A.
It's worth watching Alford's injury status as the week unfolds. He was absent from Thursday's practice due to an ankle issue.
Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre recently handed out grades for every position group and gave the inside linebackers a C-. He said they both have struggled against the pass and run, while claiming Bernard looks slow and Williams appears confused .
Those aren't flattering descriptions, and even with the coaching staff praising their performance, both need to be at their best against the Rams. If not, Matthew Stafford and Kyren Williams could both have plenty of success.
There's no player on the Bills' roster going into Week 5 with more to prove than second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston. He's struggled through the first four games, earning a PFF grade of 45.6 . Week 4 was easily his worst performance , and Hairston was so frustrated afterward that he avoided the media.
Hairston apologized afterward , which was the right call. Still, he has a huge spotlight on him now and will be out there against an elite Los Angeles passing attack on Monday night. That can be a huge opportunity for him to prove this past game was a fluke, but it could be devastating for his stock if he struggles.

title: Bills' First Week 5 Injury Update: Status for DJ Moore, Christian Benford, Ed Oliver
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were missing a few key pieces when they began practicing for the October 12 primetime road game against the Los Angeles Rams.
Most notably, wide receiver DJ Moore, who is dealing with an AC joint issue , was a non-participant in the week's first practice.
Meanwhile, defensive tackle Ed Oliver and slot cornerback Dee Alford, who were both banged up last time out against the Patriots, were not seen during the media-viewing portion of practice on Thursday ( h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
"Our guys are gonna prepare. There's gonna be guys that might not practice, but you guys know how I am with that," said first-year head coach Joe Brady prior to Thursday's practice . "We're gonna do everything we can. We also have the luxury of having a full day, an extra day with that. We're gonna give some guys [the chance] all the way through to game day. Knowing that if they give us the best opportunity to win, we're gonna roll with it."
Despite banging up his shoulder in Week 2, Moore has maintained his consecutive starts streak that dates back to December 2020. The WR1 reaggravated that injury while hitting the ground against the New England Patriots on October 4.
Moore was limited all last week for practice. The Bills will seemingly handle him with care in an effort to get him ready for game day.
"DJ's a competitor. You see the difference with us with DJ out on the football field. I think that that's natural and that's real. He is always going to do, literally, everything he can to be out there, not just for himself, but for his teammates," said Brady, who coached Moore with the Carolina Panthers in 2020 and 2021.
Benford's presence at Thursday's practice is certainly a positive development considering the starting cornerback did not practice at all during New England Patriots week.
Forced out in the third quarter on September 27, Benford suffered a non-contact toe injury. He was spotted wearing a walking boot in the immediate hours following the Week 3 win. On the sideline in Week 4, he was not wearing anything around the injured area.
With Benford inactive against the Patriots , Maxwell Hairston and second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun were the starters at outside cornerback. It's worth noting that Benford injured a toe last December, and returned after missing one game.
Oliver was ruled questionable to return after tweaking his knee during the third quarter in Week 4, but he never re-entered the game. tweaked his knee came back to the sideline in uniform but sans helmet.
Alford suffered a second-half ankle injury. He was also tabbed questionable to return. Following the 29-26 loss, Alford spoke to reporters in the locker room .
"I'm feeling pretty good. Gotta get an MRI, see how things go. I don't really know too much right now, but I feel good. I'm a warrior, so I'm ready for whatever," said Alford.
According to Brady, neither injury is expected to result in a long-term absence.
Defensive end Landon Jackson injured his knee, but returned to the game for one play wearing a brace. In a positive sign for his Week 5 availability, Jackson was seen participating with the brace on Thursday in Orchard Park.

title: Bills WR Khalil Shakir Surprisingly Leads NFL in Critical Stat
full_text:
Year after year, there’s conversation about the Buffalo Bills’ need for wide receiver help. Despite still looking for a true WR1 they can rely on, the Bills continue to put up elite offensive numbers and one of the key pieces for the past couple of seasons has also been one of the more overlooked players.
Khalil Shakir has led Buffalo in receptions and receiving yardage the past two seasons, but still doesn’t get the credit he deserves. In 2024, Shakir had 76 receptions for 821 yards and in 2025, he had 72 catches for 719 yards.
This season, he’s again being overlooked due to the addition of DJ Moore , as well as the performance of Keon Coleman . Even Dalton Kincaid is getting plenty of attention, while Shakir just quietly goes about his job.
Despite being overshadowed, Shakir enters Week 5 tied for the team lead with 15 catches . He hasn’t made the flashy plays, which is why he’s fourth in yardage, behind Kincaid, Coleman, and Moore, but Shakir is still serving as one of Josh Allen’s most trusted targets.
Shakir is also the one creating the most separation. In fact, he’s not just creating more space than any Buffalo wideout, but through four games, Shakir surprisingly leads the NFL in yards of separation.
According to Gridiron Stats and Info , Shakir is getting roughly 4.5 yards of separation per route. That’s slightly above Jaylen Waddle and Kalif Raymond, who are tied for second with 4.2 yards of separation.
As a slot receiver, Shakir is given a healthy cushion, which Gridiron has at around 7.1 yards. While that seems like a lot, he’s still given less space to operate than both Waddle and Raymond, and is still making the most of his routes.
At this point, the only question is why Shakir isn’t seeing more targets. He does lead the team with 23 targets, but that comes with a caveat. Moore has missed portions of two of their games with a shoulder injury and Coleman is often the WR3, except for when Moore is out.
Shakir hasn’t typically been a red zone weapon and he doesn’t stretch the field, but he’s averaging 11.6 yards per reception. There’s nothing at all wrong with that average, and with him creating plenty of space, it seems he should be featured more often than he has been. Perhaps leaning on him in Week 5 against the Los Angeles Rams will be key, especially since the offense has been in a slump the past two weeks.

title: The Panthers Have a Hidden Advantage That Could Decide the NFC South
full_text:
I really didn't think I'd be talking about the Panthers winning the NFC South four games into the season. After Chicago put 59 points on Carolina in Week 1, I was more worried about how bad things might get if that was what the Panthers were going to look like every week.
Three weeks later, Carolina is 2-2 and coming off a win over Detroit. The Panthers haven't looked anything like that Week 1 team since, and now I'm starting to look at the rest of this season a little differently.
CBS Sports ranked Carolina as the fourth-most vulnerable division leader this week, but something else in there caught my attention. The Panthers are tied for the third-easiest remaining schedule in the NFL.
I don't know if I'd call Carolina's remaining schedule easy. Philadelphia is right there after the bye, and the Panthers still have trips to Green Bay and Pittsburgh. Baltimore and Seattle are still on there, too, and I'm definitely not going to start counting any of those as wins.
But when you look at the rest of it, I can see why the numbers like Carolina's schedule.
The Panthers still play Tampa Bay twice and New Orleans twice. Atlanta comes to Charlotte in Week 18, and Carolina also has Denver, Minnesota, and Cincinnati left. I'm not saying the Panthers should win all of those games, but there aren't many where I'm looking at the schedule and thinking they have no chance.
That's a lot different than how I looked at this schedule before the season.
I think that's what makes this interesting. The Panthers don't have to suddenly become one of the best teams in the NFC to win this division. They just have to be better than Atlanta, New Orleans, and Tampa Bay, and through four games, I don't think that's asking too much.
Atlanta is probably the team I'd worry about the most. Carolina already beat the Falcons 34-3 on the road, but that came with Cooper Rush at quarterback instead of Michael Penix Jr. Atlanta has looked different with Penix back, so I'm not going to look at what happened in Week 2 and assume Carolina is just better than the Falcons.
But that win still counts, and it could become pretty important later. The Panthers have five division games remaining, including Atlanta coming to Charlotte in Week 18. If Carolina can take care of its division games, I'm not sure how many of those tougher games on the schedule it actually has to win.
New Orleans and Tampa Bay haven't exactly scared me through the first month, either. It's still early, and I'm not writing either team off, but I also don't see any reason Carolina should look at those four games and think it can't win them.
The first few games after the bye might tell us a lot. Carolina goes to Philadelphia, comes home for Tampa Bay, and then has to turn around four days later and play at Green Bay. That's probably the part of the remaining schedule I like the least.
Even the Philadelphia game has one thing working in Carolina's favor. The Panthers will have two weeks to prepare, while the Eagles will be coming back from playing Jacksonville in London. I'm not saying that suddenly makes me want to pick Carolina, but having the extra preparation certainly doesn't hurt.
If the Panthers can get through that stretch and stay around the top of the division, that's when I think this schedule gets really interesting. There are going to be games Carolina should have a chance to win, and a lot of what happens in the NFC South is probably going to come down to those five remaining division games anyway.
Maybe I'm getting a little ahead of myself. After Week 1, I was wondering how bad this season could get, and now I'm sitting here looking at the schedule, trying to figure out how Carolina could win the division.
But that's how much the last three weeks have changed things for me. I'm still not ready to tell you the Panthers are going to win the NFC South, and after picking Detroit to beat them Sunday night, maybe I should stay away from predictions for a little while.
I just don't look at this schedule and wonder where Carolina is going to find enough wins anymore.
Now I'm wondering how many they can get.

title: The Panthers Don't Have an Identity — And That Might Be Their Biggest Strength
full_text:
I feel like I've asked the same question about the Panthers every week this season: What exactly is this team?
After Chicago put 59 points on them in Week 1, I thought I knew, and it wasn't good. Then Carolina went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and I started wondering if maybe I overreacted. They lost a game in Cleveland they probably could've won, then came home and beat a Detroit team I didn't think they were going to beat.
So, yeah, I haven't exactly had this team figured out.
I kept waiting for Carolina to show me that one thing it was going to be every week. Maybe the running game would carry the offense. Maybe the defense would be good enough to keep them in games. Maybe Bryce Young would take another step, and Carolina would start throwing it all over the place.
I'm starting to think I've been looking for something that isn't there, and maybe that's not a bad thing.
Look at what the Panthers have already dealt with through four games. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve. Xavier Legette is on IR, Jalen Coker missed the Detroit game, and the offensive line has been moved around because of injuries.
It feels like every week I'm writing about somebody else who isn't going to play, yet Carolina is still 2-2. That's nothing to celebrate by itself, but after watching what happened against Chicago and then seeing the injuries start piling up, I didn't think I'd feel this good about Carolina going into the bye.
The offense is probably the biggest reason I do. Young has thrown for 1,268 yards through four games, and Carolina is averaging more than 400 yards of offense. I thought Young would be better this season, but I definitely didn't expect the Panthers to be doing this offensively.
Sunday night might've been the first time I watched them and thought, maybe this is what this offense is supposed to look like.
Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Chuba Hubbard finally got going with 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns. It wasn't Young having to do everything, and it wasn't Carolina trying to force the running game when it wasn't there.
They just went with what was working.
I've spent four weeks trying to decide if Carolina should be a running team or if it should put everything on Young. Maybe I've been making that more complicated than it needs to be. If Hubbard is running as he did against Detroit, give him the ball, and if Young and McMillan are killing somebody through the air, keep throwing it.
I don't really care how they get there as long as it works.
Dave Canales said this week that the bye gives Carolina a chance to look at some of the things it spent all offseason working on and be willing to move away from the stuff that hasn't worked. I like that because four actual games should matter more than whatever the Panthers thought this team was going to be back in August.
If something isn't working, stop doing it. If something is, do more of it. I know it's not always that simple, but at some point it kind of is.
The defense is where I'm still trying to figure things out. Carolina gave up 59 points and 552 yards to Chicago, turned around and held Atlanta to three points, and then gave up 452 yards to Detroit. Those are three completely different performances, and I still don't know what I'm supposed to do with that.
But I keep going back to the end of the Detroit game. The Lions had a chance to go down the field and win it, and Carolina needed one stop.
Giving up 452 yards is still a problem, and I'm sure that's going to be one of the things Carolina looks at during the bye. But when the game was sitting there at the end Sunday night, the defense made the play it had to make. I'm starting to care more about that than whether everything looks good for four quarters.
Carolina hasn't won the same way twice. The defense carried them against Atlanta, Young has carried the offense at times, and Hubbard finally got going against Detroit. Somehow, the Panthers have also kept finding guys to fill in while the injuries keep piling up.
Maybe I've been waiting for Carolina to show me what kind of team it is when it's already been doing it.
I still don't know how good the Panthers are. Four games aren't enough for me to go that far, especially when I thought they might be terrible after Week 1. But I think I understand them a little better now.
Maybe Carolina's identity isn't one thing. Maybe it's figuring out what works that week and finding a way to win with it.

title: New NFL Mock Draft Spells Doom For 2 Key Panthers Players
full_text:
While the Carolina Panthers are coming off their biggest win of the season, beating the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football and improving to 2-2, the NFL Draft looms large.
Entering the bye week , there's no better time to look towards April and project where the Panthers would look to add to the roster.
After last season, Carolina was aggressive in addressing its pass-rush needs in free agency and added to its offensive line in the NFL Draft by selecting Monroe Freeling with the 19th pick overall.
This 2027 draft class is one of the most highly anticipated classes in years, featuring multiple QB prospects and arguably the best WR prospect ever. As of now, Carolina won't be in the market for either of those positions, but it still could add to the offense.
FOX Sports' Rob Rang dropped his 2027 NFL mock draft on Thursday. In that mock, the Panthers have the same first-round pick as they did in 2026: 19th overall.  With that pick, Rang has Carolina adding to the backfield by selecting the first RB off the board, Jadan Baugh out of Florida.
So far, the best running back in the country so far has been Jadan Baugh. Florida's bell-cow back has carried this offense, posting absurd numbers and improving his draft stock.
Jadan Baugh is one of the best PURE RUNNERS the NFL Draft has seen in a while. Multiple NFL scouts reportedly believe Baugh could “finish” as a Top-15 overall player in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Gators haven’t had a RB prospect like this in a LONG TIME 😳🥶 pic.twitter.com/eTvqB7PwgK
Entering Week 6 of the CFB season, Baugh has totaled 95 carries for 613 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns. That 11-touchdown total came in a four-game stretch, and Baugh's first poor performance of the season came against Missouri.
Baugh is a brickhouse of an RB. Standing 6'1 and weighing north of 225 pounds, Baugh is as physical a runner as they come, using stiff arms and his frame to break tackles and find more yards after contact.
His acceleration for his frame is outstanding. Baugh can break free, turn any play into a track meet, and often win those races downfield to find the end zone. Baugh has runs of 75, 61, and 55 yards this season.
If this happens, then there is no bell cow running back in Carolina, and if there is, it's likely Baugh. Chuba Hubbard has been productive for the Panthers, especially in 2024 when he posted 1195 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns.
However, Hubbard has lost his RB1 spot before, last season, specifically. In 2025, after an injury that sidelined Hubbard for two weeks, Rico Dowdle went berserk, totaling over 200 scrimmage yards in two straight games and leading the backfield for a stretch of the season.
As for Jonathon Brooks, Baugh entering the Carolina backfield means it's curtains for Brooks. After dealing with two ACL tears in his right knee, he is now on IR for a core muscle/groin injury this season.
Carolina clearly believes in Brooks's talent, but if he can't stay on the field, then it doesn't matter. Plus, even if both are healthy, Baugh brings a different element to the backfield than either Hubbard or Brooks does, with his taller, bigger frame.

title: Theres a Dark Side to the Panthers' Sudden Offensive Success
full_text:
Despite the Carolina Panthers starting the season 2-2 and entering their bye week, there's been one aspect of the team that has been nothing short of elite. Carolina's offense has been outstanding, and there are multiple factors behind it.
Bryce Young couldn't have asked for a better start to the season . A long-term, lucrative contract extension has loomed over him throughout the offseason and still does so through four weeks of the season.
Chuba Hubbard has found his groove as a lead back again, averaging 5 yards per carry and totaling 306 rushing yards so far. Both stats rank among the league's top 11.
There's more to it than the individual success of Carolina's core pieces. This offense has been aggressive and efficient, and there's one person who gets the credit for it.
One of the more surprising developments of the offseason, not just for the Panthers but across the NFL, was head coach Dave Canales announcing he would be giving up playcalling duties for the first time in his Carolina tenure.
Canales announced he was relinquishing play-calling at the NFL Scouting Combine, and it seemed to come out of nowhere. The torch was passed onto offensive coordinator Brad Idzik.
Idzik has been with the Panthers since February of 2024, but hasn't called plays in the NFL until this season. Canales was brought in as a head coach because of his play calling in Tampa Bay, so to see him let go of that responsibility initially looked like a bad sign.
Now a month into the season, that couldn't be further from the truth. Canales has shifted to being a team CEO, working with the defense from the sideline, something he couldn't do while calling plays.
The play-calling change has clearly worked; Carolina has the NFL's best passing offense through four weeks and ranks No. 4 in the NFL in both total yards and yards per game. However, offensive success means the Panthers should start looking over their shoulders when it comes to Idzik.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano dropped their NFL Week 5 latest intel and what they're hearing across the league.
One question in the article was whether any coordinators were gaining interest as head-coaching candidates. Fowler brought up Idzik, noting that Carolina's passing offense has jumped from 26th last season to first this season.
Bryce Young's sizable improvement certainly looks good for Idzik's case as head coach. Young leads the NFL in passing yards through four weeks, and has a phenominal 9-2 touchdown to interception ratio.
It may already be safe to say that the Idzik-Young era in Carolina could be a brief one, as the NFL is hiring younger coaches. If that does end up being the case, it will test Young and show just how much of the success thus far is due to Idzik's scheme.
Teams that could look to Idzik after this season, include the 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers, both have struggled on offense.

title: Panthers’ TE Group Has Been Shockingly Good. Here’s Why
full_text:
Just in case it has gone unnoticed, the Carolina Panthers’ offense is alive and extremely well. Granted, Dave Canales’s team has split its first four games. However, the inconsistency that has plagued his team’s offensive attack in recent seasons is slowly becoming a thing of the past.
QB Bryce Young is LOCKED IN on this 32-yard TD pass to Tetairoa McMillan 🔐 pic.twitter.com/ysZ75qAsJk https://t.co/LbCD3a9bAt
Only three teams in the league are averaging more total yards per game than Carolina, which features the NFL’s top-ranked passing game. Quarterback Bryce Young is off to the best start of his young career. He’s already thrown for 1,268 yards and nine scores, and has only turned over the football twice.
Last Sunday night at Charlotte, he and second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan schooled the Detroit Lions’ shorthanded secondary in the team’s 32-26 victory. Young threw for 329 yards and both of his scores went to McMillan, who snared 14 passes for 192 yards. The 2025 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year was targeted a team-high 16 times.
Interesting enough, the Panthers with the second-most targets in the game was veteran tight end Darren Waller. Young threw to him six times and he caught three passes for 36 yards. The tight end position continues to enjoy a revival in Charlotte, and this chart may explain one reason why.
Darren Waller has the highest separation percentage out of all the NFL TEs Tommy Tremble has the 3rd highest https://t.co/A6tLw9oxSv
During the team’s 2-2 start, Waller, Tommy Tremble, and Mitchell Evans have been targeted a combined 41 times. They’ve combined for 30 catches, which has added up to 296 yards and two touchdowns—with Waller catching both of those scoring tosses in the club’s 34-3 rout of the Falcons at Atlanta in Week 2.
In Canales’s first season as the team’s head coach, his tight end saw 86 passes their way. They totaled 60 catches for 595 yards and just three touchdowns. The numbers were up slightly in 2025. A total of 99 targets resulted in 78 receptions for 638 yards and five TDs in 17 regular-season contests.
Last season, the team’s top five leaders in receptions were McMillan (70), running back Rico Dowdle (39), wideouts Xavier Legette (35) and Jalen Coker (33), as well as running back Chuba Hubbard (30). Tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders was sixth with 29 catches. It’s a much smaller sample size but this season, the list is led by McMillan (26), Coker (18), Waller (13), Tremble (11), and Hubbard (10).
Keep in mind that offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is now the play-caller after Canales handed those duties over to him during the offseason. There seems to be a lot more diversity in the Panthers’ passing attack, and the reigning NFC South champions (off this week) look a lot more dangerous these days on the offensive side of the football.
