title: Bengals Injury Report: Dexter Lawrence, More Star Injuries Updated Following Thursday Dolphins Practice
full_text:
Cincinnati went through its Thursday practice ahead of Sunday's road bout against the Miami Dolphins. A bunch of key Bengals are fighting through injury as the bye week comes at a nice time following this game.
Double-digit Bengals players range from slightly hurt to on injured reserve right now. The top two of note are Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin). Chase went limited in an improvement, while Higgins logged another DNP leaving very little chance to play on Sunday without at least limited status on Friday.
Dexter Lawrence (wrist) was limited again as well, but doesn't seem to be taking on any setbacks with his ailment. A bunch of players healed up enough to upgrade from Wednesday.
Check out all of the Thursday statuses below:
DID NOT PRACTICE: Higgins (groin/neck), Kyle Dugger (quad)
LIMITED:  Lawrence (wrist), Bryan Cook (ankle upgraded from DNP), Chase, Dalton Risner (knee),  Swayze Boseman (groin),
FULL: B.J. Hill (Achilles), Jordan Battle (hamstring, upgraded from limited), Barrett Carter (ankle, upgraded), Colbie Young (hamstring upgraded)
Likley not having Dugger this week may be a big test for Cincinnati's safety depth, while Colbie Young's return helps with the equally thin WR depth on the other side.
It's life in the NFL, as coaches like Zac Taylor try to find the best mix of healthy players.
"Start with Troy Walters. I'd start with him. He does a great job developing these guys when their numbers are called. I think our scouting department does a really good job," Taylor said about how his staff adapts to WR injuries and more. "I think we've got a bunch of guys that see the pass game as we do and understand the things that we're looking for. So when they're adding practice squad guys like Tanner Hudson, like Trent Irwin, like the guys that we've added over time that have played for us.
"I think those guys have just stepped up. We've brought the right character guys in here that understand what it's like. I think Joe (Burrow) does a really good job of fitting them in and getting them friendly balls that they can gain some confidence with. And so I think we got a really good track record of developing those guys."
Cincinnati has a light Friday-morning practice before traveling south for the Dolphins battle.

title: Key Bengals Pieces Return to Practice on Thursday Ahead of Dolphins Road Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals got two huge pieces back on the practice field Thursday afternoon as they keep tuning up for the road action against Miami this weekend.
Multiple local media members shot footage of wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and safety Bryan Cook (ankle) in full pads headed out to practice.
The two can be expected limiteds at practice today; their statuses will be released around 4:15 p.m. ET. Cook is fighting through a lower-body issue, while Chase's injury is much more fickle.
It's very rare to see a player suffer a concussion in a Sunday game and play the following Sunday, but if he passes all the tests, he is good to go.
This is the first concussion Chase has ever suffered in the NFL. He has to meet the guidelines laid out below to return to the field.
"Every NFL player diagnosed with a concussion must follow a five-step process before being cleared to fully practice or participate in an NFL game," The NFL rule states. "This process, developed from internationally accepted guidelines, ensures that each player receives consistent treatment.
"Each player and each concussion is unique, and there is no set time frame for return to participation. Team medical staff consider the player's current concussive injury, as well as past exposures and medical history, family history, and future risk in managing a player's care. After a player has progressed through the five-step process and is cleared for full participation by his club physician, he must be seen and separately cleared by an Independent Neurological Consultant (INC), jointly approved by the NFL and NFLPA, who is not affiliated with any NFL club. Until cleared by this independent physician, a player may not return to contact practice or play in an NFL game."
Cincinnati has a few more injured names who did not suit up fully for practice, including Tee Higgins, who looks like a very long shot to play on Sunday as of now, but the positive signs are there for at least a couple of Cincinnati stars getting healthier.
Higgins was on the rehab field but did not work out in full pads.

title: Referee Report: Sunday's White Hat for Bengals vs. Dolphins Holding Down NFL Average
full_text:
While NFL referees are throwing flags at a record pace through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, the white hat on the call for the Cincinnati Bengals vs. Miami Dolphins games on Sunday has one of the lowest counts.
Brad Rogers is in his 10th season as an NFL official and eighth as a head referee.
His first game as a referee also was Zac Taylor’s first as Cincinnati head coach, the 2019 season opener in Seattle, a 21-20 Bengals loss.
The Bengals are 3-3 with Rogers as the referee, with his most recent assignment coming in Week 14 last year in Buffalo, where the Bills won 39-34.
Rogers’ first Bengals game was the wild 37-36 win in Atlanta in 2018 when he was a field judge.
The Dolphins are 1-3 with Rogers.
Brad Rogers and his crew average 12.5 per game. Only Ron Torbert (11.5) and Alex Kemp (12.0) are averaging fewer.
Rogers averaged 13.3 last year, which was the sixth most. He also ranked sixth in 2024 (13.8) and was third in 2023 (12.4).
The league did not reward Rogers with a postseason assignment in either of the last two seasons.
His last postseason game was an AFC Wild-Card contest between the Chiefs and Dolphins in the 2023 season. That was the last time he worked a Miami game.
Rogers’ only other postseason assignment was as a field judge for an AFC Wild-Card game between the Chargers and Patriots in the 2018 season.

title: Celebrating Bengals TE Drew Sample’s 100th Game and 5 Memorable TDs
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals tight end Drew Sample will reach a milestone Sunday when he appears in his 100th game.
“Halfway to Huber,” Sample quipped earlier this week, referring to former punter Kevin Huber’s franchise record of 216.
A 2019 second-round pick, Sample will become the 82nd player in franchise history to hit the 100-game mark, tying Pacman Jones and David Fulcher at exactly 100.
The longest tenured Bengals, Sample was the second draft pick in Zac Taylor’s tenure as head coach. Wednesday, Taylor spent some time reflecting on what he has appreciated most about Sample in his eight seasons.
“Consistency. Dependability,” Taylor said. “His first combine interview with us was a 10 out of 10. You could really see what kind of person you were getting in the room. Especially early on, we wanted to build it with really smart guys that could do a lot of different things for you, and Drew has held up that part of it.
“Consistent special teams player for us over all eight years,” Taylor continued. “He’s played a really valuable role for us on offense. If you just look at the percentage of snaps he’s taken over the years it’s a high, high amount. He’s done a lot of different jobs for us whether it is play tight end, play running back, been a focal point on the punt team over eight years.”
Sample has played 1,095 special teams snaps. Since the the NFL started tracking snap counts in 2013, that ranks eighth among Bengals players behind Shawn Williams (1,673), Clayton Fejedelem (1,454), Vincent Rey (1,394), Kevin Huber (1,370), Akeem Davis-Gaither (1,341), Clark Harris (1,295) and Jordan Evans (1,182).
Offensively, Sample’s statistics are sparse, with 119 receptions for 855 yards and five touchdowns.
The longest reception of Sample’s career came last year in Miami, a 27-yarder.
His longest touchdown was a 22-yarder against Buffalo on Sunday Night Football in 2023, which Taylor referenced in an impressive display of recall after being asked about Sample.
“You look back over 100 games, his touchdown receptions, there’s the story for you,” Taylor said. “What have his touchdown receptions been? None of them we ever thought we would score a touchdown on.
“One was against Buffalo in a seven-man protection where he leaked out and scored on a Sunday night,” Taylor added.
Drew Sample was +1200 to score a touchdown tonight 👀 pic.twitter.com/rw00TTK0RR
That pass from Joe Burrow, who has only thrown two of Sample’s five touchdowns.
Burrow referenced that Buffalo play as well during his Wednesday news conference.
“He was in the protection, a full slide seven-man protection and catching the ball somehow on a scramble drill,” Burrow said. “I think that’s really a microcosm of the evolution of Drew. That’s what we’re going to ask him to do, and everybody knows it. We’re going to put him in to be really good in protection, but when things break down, I think he’s gotten so much better at the second part of a play, understanding spaces and where I’m expecting guys to be in those scramble drills and making himself available.”
Sample’s first career touchdown came in 2020 at Houston, on a pass from Brandon Allen.
“His first one was on lizard against Houston in 2020,” Taylor said. “I think that was the last time we ever ran that play, he ran a flat route for a touchdown. There is your story, 100 games, all the different ways he’s touched the ball for us in the passing game.”
Sample’s most recent score came in last year’s blowout loss at Minnesota, on a pass from Jake Browning.
“One when he was in full-time protection, in 58 protection, home game (against the Raiders),” Taylor said.
What a tremendous touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Drew Sample. It’s the 3rd of the day for Burrow and 1st of the season for Sample. Burrow has been tremendous today playing outside of the pocket and making the most of what the Raiders allow. pic.twitter.com/i9FyooOe9o
The other was in 2023, a home loss to the Steelers.
JAKE FIESTY TO DREW SAMPLE FOR THE TOUCHDOWN 🔥 #WHODEY pic.twitter.com/5PeMP4hcnl
“You can count on him, man,” Burrow said. “As reliable as it gets. He’s going to understand his job as well as everybody else’s job and will work to coordinate and try to get everybody on the same page. He’s a very valuable piece for us.”

title: 3 Biggest Injury Concerns For Browns Heading Into Sunday's Matchup vs. Jets
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are looking for their fourth straight win as they head to MetLife Stadium to take on the New York Jets on Sunday, but a few injury concerns remain.
Cleveland lost two of its defensive tackles in the Browns' Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mason Graham left in the first half and did not return, while Mike Hall also got injured but returned. However, Hall didn't practice all week, raising three injury concerns that could hurt the Browns this weekend.
Graham will not play against the Jets due to an MCL and ankle sprain. The second-year defensive tackle has had a strong start to the season, recording four sacks in his first three games, and the Browns will miss him up the middle.
While the Browns managed to win over the Steelers without Graham for the final three quarters, the Jets now have a week to prepare for his absence, which could hurt the Browns.
Hall left the field on a cart during the Browns' Week 4 game, but he returned and recorded a huge sack on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers late in the third quarter, pushing Pittsburgh out of field goal range and forcing a punt.
Hall's injury didn't seem serious since he returned to play, but he's had almost eight days to recover and still hasn't practiced as of Friday. The Browns have already ruled him out for Week 5.
With Hall and Graham both out, defensive tackle like Adin Huntington will need to step up and take on a larger role than usual.
Sticking with the defensive tackles, the Browns will not have Davis available, as he hasn't played for them this season. The Browns signed Davis to a one-year, $2 million deal this offseason after he spent three years with the 49ers. However, the Browns placed him on injured reserve at the start of the regular season after he suffered a quad injury.
After four games on IR, Davis is eligible to return, and the Browns designated him to return on Tuesday, opening his 21-day practice window. But Cleveland did not add him to the 53-man roster, so he will still miss Sunday.
It seemed like Davis might be able to play, and now the Browns will be without three defensive tackles they expected to play significant roles this season.

title: Pros and Cons of Moving Any of Browns Quarterbacks in 2026
full_text:
At the current moment, the Cleveland Browns have four quarterbacks on the roster.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching in just over a month, it is likely one of them will be moved.
But who does Cleveland get rid of? Here are the pros and cons of moving each quarterback.
While many fans would be happy Deshaun Watson is off the team, the Browns would need a big offer to move their QB1 after his hot start to the season.
Outside of a happier fanbase, moving Watson would probably mean going all in on a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft.
As for the cons, winning and offensive production would likely take a hit at first until the next man up is able to get comfortable in Todd Monken's scheme.
Overall, a Deshaun Watson midseason move is very unlikely.
A potential Shedeur Sanders trade was rumored after New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury.
Since then, those rumors have been shut down, and New York has found their new guy in J.J. McCarthy.
Browns aren't looking to trade Shedeur Sanders, per @RuiterWrongFAN . pic.twitter.com/UB35kUR2Hj
But let's talk about the pros and cons of moving Shedeur.
The only pro of moving Sanders is the potential for a good trade package in return. If Cleveland could get a higher draft pick, it might be worth it. But do draft picks outweigh the numerous cons?
Not only would the fanbase hate Sanders' departure, but the Browns would also mortgage a potential future QB option. Many people aren't realizing that the time currently being spent by Sanders as QB is great time for the raw talent to sit, watch, learn, and develop.
With the way the season has started, it looks like Coach Monken will be at the helm in Cleveland for multiple years. Additionally, with Deshaun Watson being 31 years old and in the final year of his contract, it is crucial that the Browns have a young backup developing now to take over in the near future.
If there's a quarterback that sticks out among the four, it's Dillon Gabriel .
Pros to moving Gabriel would be sending him to a place where he wants to be. Off the field, it has been pretty clearly seen through the media that Gabriel isn't very happy in Cleveland. To be fair, if you had to move to Cleveland from Hawaii during the winter season, you might not be the happiest either.
On the field, Gabriel performed very well in the final preseason game this year against the Patriots. In the first half, he threw for three touchdowns. Basing a trade on recency bias from that game, compared to his poor regular-season action last season, could haul in a better trade package for the Browns.
On the other hand, there are not many cons at all when it comes to moving the former Heisman candidate. The only thing that looks bad on paper is the fact that Cleveland used a third-round pick on Gabriel, just to get rid of him the following year.
Taylen Green is at the bottom because the Browns simply won't move him.
This is because any move to be made would have to be cutting the 2026 sixth-round pick.
Coach Monken has also talked about potentially using Green in specialized sets this season. Clearly, the former Arkansas Razorback is staying with the Browns.

title: Todd Monken Deserves More Credit For Launching Deshaun Watson Career Comeback
full_text:
After the conclusion of Week 1, many called for Deshaun Watson to be removed as the starting quarterback of the Cleveland Browns.
Fast-forward three weeks, and the Browns, still led by Watson, have won three consecutive games with fourth-quarter comebacks involved in each. And while the season opener was incredibly disappointing, it can be forgotten, with the Browns now 3-1 and atop the AFC North standings.
"I think in Todd Monken's mind, there's no week to week, month to month, that whole narrative has dissolved the way Monken wanted it to," - @TonyGrossi on Deshaun Watson's job security as QB1. pic.twitter.com/zMfvcafzkb
While Watson deserves an awful lot of credit, especially considering he now has 855 yards, a near-70% completion rate and six scores through the air, head coach Todd Monken deserves just as much praise and recognition for helping put him in position to succeed.
Watson is beginning to look like the quarterback Cleveland traded for back in 2022.
Watson's time in Cleveland hasn't had the greatest storyline surrounding it. He has been suspended, injured, ridiculed by the media and downright hated by the fanbase at times. Questions were asked heading into the 2026 season about whether or not the three-time Pro Bowler could ever be accepted as the starter.
But after working all offseason to beat out second-year signal caller Shedeur Sanders , he got his opportunity to do just that.
It hasn't always been pretty, but Monken has worked closely with Watson to make sure he can routinely improve and continue to stay under center week after week.
Cleveland columnist Terry Pluto echoed such a sentiment recently, adding that the two worked behind the scenes through tough video sessions to ensure Watson would make changes after the Week 1 disaster class.
"After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson," he wrote on Cleveland.com. "But the week before the game at Tampa, there were some very tough video sessions. I was told it was perhaps some of the 'hardest coaching' he’s had since coming to the Browns."
. @terrypluto credits Deshaun Watson's recent turnaround this season to Todd Monken's "tough love" in film review: "After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson. But the week before the game at Tampa, there were some very tough video sessions. I… pic.twitter.com/C4c7OWV66F
Obviously, such extra attention has worked wonders.
Since throwing for a measly 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception against the Jaguars, Watson has 650 yards, five touchdowns and one interception across the last three games. He has also brought his QBR up to a mark of 58.4, which is 18th in the NFL.
His best outing, a Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he passed for nearly 250 yards and two scores , resulted in high praise from Monken.
"I'm happy for Deshaun," Monken said following the Week 2 win. "I expected improvement and I expect continued improvement. There's a lot of football left in him. He just hasn't played in a while."
Terry Pluto of https://t.co/l4Q3F0Sn4e reveals the turning point behind Deshaun Watson's resurgence, as Todd Monken's tough coaching helped speed up the Browns quarterback's decision-making. "After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson. But the… pic.twitter.com/JbQJrqIEAA
At the time, that somewhat washed over, especially with plenty of other storylines occurring to take the spotlight. Now, though, those words seemed to reflect an important distinction that Monken recognizes: Watson isn't a quarterback who has lost his ability, but rather one who needed time to regain his rhythm and confidence.
Heading into a Week 5 matchup with the New York Jets on the road from MetLife Stadium, a lot of national eyes will be on the Browns.
The big question is: Has this three-game winning streak been a fluke, or is there legitimately something to be excited about in The Land?
And for Watson, he will look to continue silencing the doubts that surround his future in the league. Fortunately, he has Monken and the rest of the team on his side, with the hope that he can continue to lead the team to a fourth straight victory.

title: Browns Officially Without Top Two Defensive Linemen vs. New York Jets
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have some things to figure out as they prepare for the New York Jets ahead of their matchup on Sunday.
Having an extended break in between games was much needed for the Browns, who have been a bit banged up after their big Thursday night win over their division rival , the Pittsburgh Steelers.
During their extra time off, the hopes were that some of their injured players would be able to rehab so that they would be available for their next game. Unfortunately, that won't be the case for two of their top defensive linemen.
#Browns game status for #Jets Davis - out Gabriel - out Graham - out Hall - out T. Jenkins - out Ryan - out Wallace - out
Both Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. suffered injuries in that Thursday night battle last week. That takes us to this week’s practices, where neither player was seen in the open portion of practice.
That led many to believe both will be out for Sunday’s game at New York, which is now a huge blow to their defensive line in need of playmakers with them being officially ruled out.
Here’s who can step up in their absence to help Cleveland get another win:
Collins has been a regular force on defense for the Browns since he arrived in Cleveland. His veteran presence has been much appreciated for their young group of players, and they rally behind his always consistent play on the defensive line.
Last season, Collins saw a career high in sacks at 6.5, even though he missed a few games due to injury. Offseason injuries threatened his availability this season, but it hasn’t seemed to limit him even the slightest so far.
Though four games, Collins has nine total tackles, three solo and six assists, while also tallying one sack. He’s never a sole contributor on this talented Browns defense, but he always plays a role in stopping opposing offenses in all areas of the game.
He’ll be expected to take on a large snap count to guide this thin group against the Jets .
Any time Huntington has been needed for the Browns, he’s been available whether it’s at defensive tackle or rushing the passer off the edge.
In 13 games last season, Huntington made plays as a rotational depth piece, recording 15 tackles and half a sack. Through his first four games this season, he’s already recorded almost as many tackles as he had last season.
His eleven total tackles with one sack playing limited sacks warrant him more playing time, and he will surely get that against the Jets. He could play an even larger role moving forward depending on how long Graham and Hall Jr. 's injuries hold them out.
Since the Browns brought in Williams near the start of the regular season , he’s been needed in all four of Cleveland’s games so far.
Listed as a linebacker, Williams has seen time both rushing off the edge and up the middle on the defensive line. So far this season, Williams already has eleven tackles and one sack after putting up solid numbers with the Dallas Cowboys to start his career.
No matter the position, Williams is a reliable player to plug-and-play, enough to help get the job done against a middle-of-the-pack Jets offense.

title: Shedeur Sanders Shares What He Wants in Life Away from the Browns
full_text:
Shedeur Sanders knows what he wants in a relationship, and he sounds comfortable waiting for it.
During an appearance on Cosmopolitan’s “Blind Date” with Editor-in-Chief Willa Bennett, the Cleveland Browns backup quarterback shared a side of himself fans do not see. The wide-ranging conversation shifted from dating and fashion to family advice, vacations and what makes someone attractive to him.
His answers were mostly playful, but certainly some consistent themes emerged. Sanders values ambition, genuine connections and having a life that feels right to him.
Asked what quality someone absolutely must have to date him, Sanders answered, “They have to be hard-working.”
When Bennett asked what instantly makes someone attractive, his response went beyond appearances.
“I would say their mentality. How do they think about things?”
That led to a conversation about vacations and taking time off . Sanders liked the idea that limited vacation days could make someone appreciate that time more. For him, a getaway means being able to disconnect.
“That’s very important to me because I value vacation time too so it’s time to disconnect.”
Sanders also agreed that a vacation should leave room to relax rather than become a schedule packed with activities. It was refreshing to hear someone whose career revolves around competition wanting an opportunity to slow down.
He also said his approach to dating has been shaped by his father , Coach Prime. Asked about advice that changed how he views relationships, Shedeur pointed to experiences and conversations with his dad.
“Focus on your career and focus on what you have to do,” Coach Prime told him.
He explained that genuine connections can develop when someone takes care of their own responsibilities instead of searching too hard for a relationship.
“I don’t like that. I [prefer] long-term.”
Sanders carried that same outlook into advice for a viewer trying to get the attention of a man absorbed in his career saying, “focus on yours.”
He was also far more lighthearted when discussing first impressions. Asked what he hopes someone notices on a first date, Sanders chose his smile. He also admitted he enjoys being called handsome, giving Bennett an opening to offer the compliment.
There were boundaries, too. When she imagined a second date in Cleveland, Sanders said they would go somewhere together.
“Can’t come to the house yet.”
Asked when that invitation might arrive, he explained, “when I feel the time is right.”
For all the confidence and joking, his most revealing answer may have come when Willa asked about a goal unrelated to football.
“I would say being happy consistently.”

title: Andre Szmyt Shares the Reason the Browns Special Teams Unit Has Found So Much Success
full_text:
For the past decade or so, the Cleveland Browns have been searching for a kicker to fill the shoes, literally, of legendary kicker Phil Dawson.
The 20-year-career finished his career with 215 games, 441 field goals made and 518 extra points . He also kicked over 1,200 kickoffs, marking an incredibly long and reliable career in the NFL.
Fortunately, after years of searching for the next guy to take his spot as a long-term leg in The Land, the front office may have accidentally stumbled into finding one.
In late December 2024, Andre Szmyt was signed to the Browns' practice squad. He was then signed to a future contract in early 2024, before landing on the 53-man roster for the 2025 season.
And since then, he has been the starting kicker for Cleveland , beating out Dustin Hopkins along the way.
Across the last two seasons, Szmyt has locked down a long-term spot as the Browns' go-to leg when needed. While he hasn't yet landed a big contract, mainly because the NFL isn't willing to invest in kickers, he has been incredibly reliable and consistent.
The 28-year-old is knocking through 91.4% of his field goals and 97% of his extra points, with seven makes on kicks over 50 yards.
This season , he is a perfect 100% on both marks. He also made a game-winning 56-yarder against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football, marking yet another memorable moment in his young career.
When asked about what has made him so successful, he shared that the camaraderie with the special teams unit has led to him being so comfortable on the field.
"We're so close. I think that kind of camaraderie we have shows on the field. I mean, I trust those guys with everything," he said when asked about his ability to be confident when out on the field. "I know they're going to do their jobs to the absolute best, and then it kind of allows me to just go out there and play free and not just football, you know, like I know they got me outside the building, too.
"So I love those guys honestly, and I wouldn't be in the position I am without them."
Andre Szmyt opens up about his close relationship with Rex Sunahara and Corey Bojorquez, crediting their trust and camaraderie for helping him play with confidence. "We're so close. I think that kind of camaraderie we have shows on the field. I mean, I trust those guys with… pic.twitter.com/Z7L7KI3gjS
Szmy, Corey Bojorquez and Rex Sunahara have been a trio that has stood out the last few seasons, mainly due to just how consistent they have been.
Sunahara is always right on the money with his snaps, Bojorquez has averaged 40.4 yards per punt across the last five seasons, and Szmyt has done his job with the ball on the turf. That chemistry Smyt mentioned goes a long way, and it has been on full display in each of their productive roles.
While the defense and offense have both undergone plenty of changes, the unit remaining together shows just how important it is to build up a group that is so heavily bonded.
Looking to keep this momentum going and find win No. 4 on the campaign, they and the rest of the squad will return to the gridiron on Sunday, Oct. 11, for a matchup against the New York Jets. The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Why It Works for the Browns to Trade for This Pro-Bowl Running Back
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' fast start to the season puts them in a position to be able to add to the team at the trade deadline.
They have just over one month until the November 10 deadline to decide which areas of the team to address. The favorable schedule in the meantime may increase their urgency to improve the roster.
The Browns’ weakest area on offense has been running the football. Quinshon Judkins has received the bulk of the carries and is averaging just three yards per rush. The running attack will need to improve for the Browns to compete when the weather turns cold and games get meaningful in December.
Tony Pollard would be an intriguing option for the Browns. He currently plays for the 0-4 Tennessee Titans and is on an expiring contract. Pollard is in his age-29 season and has amassed 221 yards with 4.1 yards per carry.
The Browns would upgrade their running back room with the addition of Pollard. They are able to absorb his contract and can get him for mid-round draft picks. The Browns have four fourth-round picks in next year's draft. One of those, plus their fifth-round pick, can be intriguing for a thin Titans team.
Cleveland’s roster no longer needs to rely on mid-to-late-round picks to contribute right away and can afford to lose one of their fourth-round picks. Pollard would come in as a rental player, and if he performs well, then he can be re-signed for cheap as he would be in his age-30 season.
Splitting the carriers with Judkins would make sure each of them are fresh down the stretch. Judkins has struggled to show his burst after a season-ending surgery last year. Pollard has rushed 1,000 yards the past four seasons and is currently on pace to just be shy of the benchmark .
The addition of Pollard can help the running game get going to relieve some pressure off of Deshaun Watson. If the Browns can add a facet to their offense, then maybe they will not need to rely on game-winning drives.
Judkins is a second-year player and should get stronger as the season moves along. He showed flashes in his rookie season that he can be the main guy in the backfield to do all the heavy lifting.
Backup running back Raheim Sanders has shown that he can run the ball hard and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry in limited action. The duo bring a physicality that will not be easy to bring down in cold weather
The Browns have recently signed Jaleel McLaughlin as the team’s third running back. He played one offensive snap and took the ball 28 yards to the end zone. Reinforcements may also be on the way without giving up draft picks.
Dylan Sampson was injured in the first game on a kickoff return. The injury was deemed “significant”, but the Browns have not ruled him out for the season. Sampson could return for the Browns down the stretch and provide a speedy alternative to the power of Judkins.
Andrew Berry values mid-round picks, and now that most of the starters have shown that they deserve to start in the NFL, he can use those picks to build depth to really make the team a contender. Pollard will get a lot of interest from contending teams to bolster the backfield, and the pot could get too big for Berry to want to make the move.
Should they be active or not at the deadline, the Browns have played themselves in a position to seriously consider improving the team for this season.

title: It's Time For the Browns to Move On from This Player
full_text:
Ever since the end of his career-best 2024 season, Jerry Jeudy has not lived up to the Browns hopes.
After finishing with 90 catches, 1,299 yards, and four touchdowns, Jeudy had Browns fans believing he was the team's real number one wide receiver.
However, in the 2025 season, Jeudy's production was basically cut in half. 90 receptions went to 50, 1,229 yards dropped to 602, and four touchdowns dropped to two.
After last season, Jeudy finished second in the entire NFL in drops with 10.
Then came the 2026 NFL Draft . Cleveland used one of their two first-round picks on KC Concepcion, a receiver out of Texas.
Then, they doubled down and used their first second-round pick on Denzel Boston, another receiver out of Washington.
With two additions to the wide receiver room in the draft, it was already being hinted at by the organization that Jeudy was on his way out.
So far in the 2026 season, Jeudy's production on the field has once again decreased.
Through four games, Jeudy has only been targeted a total of eight times. Out of those, he has caught five passes for 62 yards.
As for the rookies, Boston and Concepcion have seen a combined 30 catches through 50 total targets, for 428 yards and two touchdowns.
Not only have the Browns clearly moved on from Jeudy on the depth chart, but also on the field schematically.
Let's say the Browns do actually want to move on. Who could be some teams that are interested?
The first team that comes to mind is in need of some help for their young quarterback trying to avoid "bust allegations"
Outside of Carnell Tate, the Tennessee Titans could use another receiver pretty badly.
As for a potential return, the Browns may want to look into adding a player like Tony Pollard. If not a player, they may do the deal for some late-round picks. As a reminder, the initial Jeudy trade with the Broncos only required the Browns to give up 2024 fifth- and sixth-rounders.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
In the scenario Jeudy wants to go to a contender, the Kansas City Chiefs are always looking to get more help for Patrick Mahomes.
If the Browns want Jeudy out of the AFC as a whole, a trade that has been talked about previously is a receiver swap with the Arizona Cardinals.
Marvin Harrison Jr. is having a similar 2026 season to Jeudy. With only 5 receptions for 85 yards and a touchdown, a change of scenery may be needed for the former number four overall pick.
Regardless of where the Browns receiver ends up, it's clearly time to move on.

title: Deshaun Watson Combats Any Sort of QB Room Drama with Latest Comments
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns quarterback room is facing an unfamiliar problem: they have too many players.
Dillon Gabriel was activated from the injured reserve list yesterday, giving the Browns the next 21 days to make a decision on what to do with their roster. The addition of Gabriel shakes up the room, but Deshaun Watson is not worried.
“Dillon, he’s been around this whole time. He’s been in every meeting. He’s been traveling with us. He’s been on the practice field with us. He’s been communicating, giving suggestions within the offense and different reads,” Watson said about Gabriel returning from injury.
“So DG, man, he’s a great teammate, a better person . It’s good to have him back on the field and see that he’s healthy. All of us in that room, we’re one big group, got one goal and that’s ultimately to win and be successful.”
Watson’s comments show that the team is bought into Todd Monken’s culture, and their main focus is winning. Gabriel returns as Watson is proving that he is the starting quarterback on the team. He is currently backed up by Shedeur Sanders, and Gabriel can challenge for the backup role should they put him on the roster.
Gabriel being with the team while on the injured list means that he has been involved in the installation of Monken’s offense each week. He has been praised for his ability to understand and operate the offense. If he cannot overtake Sanders for the backup role, then he can be listed as the team’s emergency third quarterback on game days.
Taylen Green has been that emergency quarterback and should Gabriel take his spot, then the Browns can activate Green to the roster and use his playmaking skills on gadget plays and short-yardage downs.
Watson has shown that he has the respect of the locker room, as the team has rallied behind him for three-straight game winning drives. They have won their three games as a complete team and the camaraderie has been palpable.
Gabriel has 21 days of practice before the Browns have to decide to promote him to the roster or keep on the injured list for the remainder of the season . Even if he is not on the roster, he has proven that he is a valuable member in the quarterback room and that he can provide positive results for the Browns without being on the field.

title: Ranking the Browns' 5 Biggest Needs Before the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have been one of the biggest surprises of the 2026 NFL season.
Very few people imagined the Browns would be winners in three of their first four games. Even fewer expected to see Deshaun Watson play as well as he has.
With the success, the Browns can actually be buyers at the trade deadline for the first time in a number of years.
Here are five position groups that could use some help.
Over this past offseason, the Browns did a lot of work signing, trading, and drafting different players to improve the offensive line.
Despite all the effort, Cleveland still ranks near the bottom of the league in PFF offensive line rankings at 28th.
Even if the Browns don't want to spend a lot of assests to go get another starter, building the depth of the unit is always in play when Deshaun Watson is taking the snaps.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
The Browns used two top picks on KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in the 2026 NFL Draft.
With that being said, they don't necessarily need another big name to come in. Rather, a better term to use would be a makeover.
Cleveland clearly has their next stars in Concepcion and Boston, so trading a guy like Jerry Jeudy makes too much sense.
As for additions following a Jeudy trade, they could look to sign a veteran receiver who helps develop the young talent.
So far this season, Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams have already proved to be a great duo on the Browns defense.
Outside of them, Easton Mascarenas-Arnold has proved he can hold his own, but behind him is where the depth gets very weak.
It does not need to be a star linebacker, but if Cleveland can get some depth for cheap, they should absolutely look into it
The only reason why the defensive line is so high on this list is due to the recent Mason Graham injury.
While the Browns were able to sack Aaron Rodgers five times against the Steelers without their sack leader, extra help would always be nice.
Very similarly to the linebackers, you do not need a star. However, adding someone to take the weight off Jared Verse's shoulders sounds very nice.
By far, the cornerback room is the biggest place of need for the Browns.
Outside of Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell who has been fighting injury, the Browns have had to rely on Myles Harden a lot.
In week four, the Steelers made it a focal point to target Harden who at times got stuck covering DK Metcalf.
By the end of the game, Pittsburgh targeted Harden a total of seven times. In those attempts, the Steelers were able to generate 4 catches for 117 yards and a touchdown.
If there's a position where the Browns should potentially go after a star, it's the cornerback.

title: 3 Dallas Cowboys Who Should Be Traded After Brutal NFL Week 5 Loss
full_text:
Week 5 was brutal for the Dallas Cowboys . They entered the game heavily-favored against the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who were starting an undrafted free agent at quarterback.
Jalon Daniels, who struggled in his first start against the Green Bay Packers, was sharp against the Cowboys and had no issues with the short week. That loss was frustrating, and it should serve as a harsh reality check.
Despite spending the offseason re-tooling their defense , that side of the ball is actually worse this year than it was last .
A second-round pick in 2023, Luke Schoonmaker has faded from the team's plans this year. He has just three receptions for 30 yards and his time in Dallas is coming to a close.
He wouldn't bring much in a trade, but he's a free agent in 2027 and is unlikely to return. Getting a late-round pick from a team looking for a young tight end could be a win for the Cowboys, but would also be a positive for Schoonmaker. He's shown flashes in the passing game and could benefit from a change of scenery.
James Houston was a breakout star for the Cowboys in 2026, recording 35 tackles and 5.5 sacks while appearing in all 17 games. This year, he's been inactive for two of the five games and has just two total tackles. Houston is a pass-rushing specialist and Dallas could get a Day 3 pick from a team who needs a rotational EDGE.
This isn't a move that will happen just yet, but if the Cowboys continue to struggle, they have to look at players who will no longer be with them in 2027 as trade targets. That's why George Pickens is a name to keep an eye on .
Pickens showed everyone on Thursday night that he's still a difference-maker, with nine receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. Even so, it's still difficult to see Pickens coming back in 2027. There was a time when the Cowboys seemed as though they could extend Pickens, but after trading for Joey Porter Jr. , they have another high-profile free agent who will be the focus in the coming offseason.
Losing Pickens would be tough, but the Cowboys could get a decent pick from a team in need of help at wide receiver and Ryan Flournoy has proven more than capable of being the team's WR2 opposite CeeDee Lamb.

title: Colin Cowherd Blasts Jerry Jones' Cheapness Holding Cowboys Back In Key Area
full_text:
Jerry Jones recently said "There is nothing more dangerous than an old man with money ," letting everyone know he was willing to spend big to help fix his struggling Dallas Cowboys.
Not long after that, he swung a trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , who has yet to sign a new deal, but will need one before the 2027 season . Since last season, Jones has shown he's not only willing to go after big-name players, but he's also willing to hand out massive extensions.
Dallas has signed star players such as Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, Jake Ferguson, DaRon Bland, and Quinnen Williams to extensions over the past few years. They've also come to terms with some of their role players, extending Ryan Flournoy and Brevyn Spann-Ford recently.
While Jones has shown a willingness to pay for players, Colin Cowherd believes he will never win until he decides to pay for a better staff. Cowherd said there's no salary cap on coaches or general managers, yet Jones has decided those were the areas to go cheap.
"In a salary cap league, all right, there's a ceiling, right? There's two places where you can spend all you want, and it doesn't count against the cap. Coaching staffs and front offices, head coaches and GMs. And the Cowboys go cheap on those. Jerry didn't go cheap on his yacht, his helicopter, his stadium, his practice facility. They pay top of the market for quarterbacks, defensive tackles, and wide receivers. He goes cheap on the staff," Cowherd said.
"Jerry will overpay top of the market for players, a yacht, a stadium, a practice facility, and go cheap on the coach. It's like hosting a party in a mansion and going: Who's doing the catering? ... We called Subway" @colincowherd says it's time for Dallas to pay up for a coach pic.twitter.com/RxivQNNSMu
Of course, Jones sees himself as the team's GM, which is why he doesn't go out of his way to pay someone to take over those duties. As for the head coach, Cowherd said the reason Jones won't fork out cash for a premium coach is because those coaches push back.
Cowherd isn't the first to make this claim, with former coaches such as Jason Garrett often being referred to as a "puppet" for Jones. The feeling around current head coach Brian Schottenheimer has been the same.
In 2025, Jones refused to show any interest in some of the hot coaching candidates, including Ben Johnson. Instead, he focused on people he knew, such as Schottenheimer and Kellen Moore.
Schottenheimer, who had been on the Cowboys' staff since 2022, wasn't a popular choice and after 22 games, his hiring feels like a failure. Schottenheimer is now 9-12-1 and they continue to look outmatched week after week.
Cowherd was a huge critic of the Schottenheimer hire, and it's becoming increasingly difficult to find a counterargument to that criticism.

title: George Pickens Defends Helmet-Slamming Moment in Cowboys' Loss to Bucs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of the franchise's more embarrassing losses in recent memory on Thursday night at AT&T Stadium, falling to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 24-16 defeat. Led by undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, Tampa Bay picked up its first win of the season by handling Dallas in a game that was not as close as the final score indicated.
But on a night filled with an unprecedented amount of frustration, even for the Cowboys' standards, no one was more visbily upset than star wide receiver George Pickens.
The Amazon Prime broadcast captured a slow-mo shot of Pickens slamming his helmet into the turf, an image that perfectly captured the mood of every Cowboys player, coach and fan in the building.
In an interview with NFL reporter Josina Anderson after the game, Pickens explained the visible frustration that ensued once he realizes Dallas' hopes of a late comeback were over.
Here's the clip of Pickens slamming his helmet:
George Pickens ready to CRASHOUT 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/zzaTyUGGRU
"I feel like everybody was the same way," Pickens said. "Just disappointed, me most definitely because I'm definitely one of the biggest competitors. So as soon as I seen them intercept the ball, I knew the Bucs was gonna try to run the clock out. That's kind of what they did to start the game. We didn't get the ball into the second quarter, like the third to the second quarter, so I kind of knew they were gonna do that. So my frustration was just, I knew it was over, and I just hate that we had no more time on the clock."
No one is blaming Pickens for the mini outburst. He's also not apologizing for it either, which is understandable given how embarrassing the loss was. Pickens wear his emotions on his sleeve. Cowboys fans should want players that want to win as bad as he does.
While there's little doubt that Pickens and the Cowboys respect every opponent, he didn't sugercoat the fact that it was a game Dallas was supposed to win. As a result, the loss was even more frustrating.
"I feel like we were ready to go. I just feel like you gotta win the games that you're supposed to win," he said. "So whether that's extra detail, or if you are ready to go, then having detail on top of your enthusiasm, on top of your energy, just as if we were playing the Chiefs. And I feel like those couple components of the game of football should be every game. And if you do that every game, then we probably won't have to worry about this."
On a night where CeeDee Lamb found no rhythm before suffering a quad bruise, Pickens stepped up and delivered his best performance of the season thus far.
He finished with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. His late touchdown helped cut it to a one-possession game after making some key catches while Dallas was in hurry-up mode.
The 13 targets tied his career-high total as a Cowboy while the 130 yards marked his sixth 100-yard receiving game since the beginning of last season.
Perhaps, like last year, Pickens is starting to catch fire after building momentum during the first few weeks of the season.

The Dallas Cowboys are coming off of their most embarrassing home loss in recent memory , falling to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers and struggling to show any consistency in all three phases of the game.

The 2027 NFL Draft will be held from Thursday, April 29, through Saturday, May 1, at the National Mall outside of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

title: 5 Players Dallas Cowboys Must Bench To Send Message After Week 5 Embarrassment
full_text:
All losses stink, but the one the Dallas Cowboys had on Thursday night was especially terrible.
The Cowboys allowed an 0-4 team with an undrafted quarterback to come into their building and beat them . It was easily one of the most embarrassing performances we've seen from a Cowboys team in recent memory and that's saying a lot.
With the kind of loss the Cowboys suffered on Thursday, it's time for head coach Brian Schottenheimer to send a message to his players and that should come in the form of benching or temporarily reducing the playing time of some players.
When it comes to Cowboys players who need to be benched, it's DaRon Bland out in front by a country mile and then everyone else because he is so far and away a bigger problem than any player is at their respective position on the entire team.
Bland was putrid once again in Week 5 , with the Cowboys corner giving up a completion rate of 85.7% and a passer rating of 116.1 when targeted and allowed six receptions for 83 yards.
It was a continuation of his awful play that has stretched over two-plus seasons now.
Bland slipped twice in coverage and allowed huge completions. The first went to Tez Johnson for 64 yards, and the other went to Emeka Egbuka, who picked up a first down on a third-and-21. The two receptions ultimately assisted in scores for Tampa Bay.
As if all of that wasn't bad enough, Bland committed a penalty to help the Bucs extend another scoring drive, and he should have had a pick-six in the fourth quarter but just dropped it.
As much as Bland needs to be benched, especially after Cobie Durant comes back, don't hold your breath. Somehow, Jerry Jones still thinks Bland can recover.
"He's got to continue to work to play at the level we expect of him. He's paid because of how he played in the past. One of the things you can always bet on -- one of the surest things -- is when you've seen him do it in the past they can do it again, if they haven't had physical diminishment of their physical skills. And he hasn't," he said to 105.3 The Fan .
From the sounds of it, the Cowboys are still starting Bland because he's getting paid a lot of money, not because of performance. That is a losing strategy.
Ferguson had a crucial drop in the fourth quarter that sealed the loss for Dallas. Dak Prescott threw a pass that went through his hands, bounced off his face mask and landed in the arms of a Bucs defender. Just an inexcusable drop.
We would be more inclined to ignore it but Ferguson has had more struggles beyond that. On top of his shoddy blocking, Ferguson also lost a fumble in Week 3 in Baltimore Ravens territory that proved to be crucial in a three-point loss.
Maybe it's time to give Brevyn Spann-Ford and even Luke Schoonmaker a longer look, at least for one game.
Like Ferguson, Flournoy had a critical dropped that turned into an interception. It happened in the third quarter in Cowboys territory. Prescott's pass hit Flournoy right in his hands and then bounced up into the air a few times before a Bucs defender caught it.
Making matters worse, Tampa Bay flipped that into a touchdown drive five plays later. Flournoy did end up having his best game of the season on Thursday night from a production standpoint, but he had been very quiet the four weeks prior.
Maybe it's time to give offseason standout Camden Brown his first opportunity. At the very least, he should be active over Jonathan Mingo.
Turpin was responsible for one of the three turnovers the Cowboys had in Week 5.
The veteran kick returner was reckless with the ball on a kickoff return and did not protect it well enough. And, sure enough, the ball was knocked loose and recovered by Tampa. The Bucs converted that turnover into a field goal.
Turpin is a great returner, no doubt, but no amount of skill can make that excusable. The Cowboys should send him a message.
Miller said after signing with the Cowboys that the team isn't paying him for what he can do on the football field.
Well, that's good news because Miller hasn't done anything of value. He has zero sacks and just six pressures in five games and he was constantly getting burnt in the run game on Thursday because he just couldn't set the edge.
Miller is only averaging 14.4 snaps per game and he has seen his playing time decline in each of the last three contests. It should decline down to zero in Week 6.

title: Cowboys Should Take Ex-Giants Coach Up On Offer To Help 'Outclassed' Christian Parker
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were supposed to be better on defense in 2026 after making several changes on that side of the ball that included a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker.
But, somehow, the Cowboys might actually be worse than they were last season when they sported the highest points-per-contest average in the league.
Talent has been an issue, but it's not like Parker has had sound game plans, either, and he has no answers to fix the problems Dallas' unit has had going all the way back to Week 1. He is overmatched right now, plain and simple.
One person who has not been shy to express just how bad Parker has looked is former New York Giants defensive coordinator Don "Wink" Martindale, who offered to help Parker out after calling Dallas' play-caller "outclassed" last month.
"I don't wanna be an a******, but he's just being outclassed right now," Martindale said of Parker. "He was in the home opener against the Giants. They gotta stop the run."
"And watching Dallas, that's frustrating. So, Jerry can call me and I'll go help him, but I'm talking about helping the coordinator," Martindale added.
While Cowboys fans are already calling for Parker's head, owner Jerry Jones is not there yet and still has confidence in Parker.
“Premature,” Jones said when asked if Parker's job might be in trouble.
“I do. Yes, I do,” Jones said when asked if he still has confidence in his defensive coordinator. “He’s sitting there taking it on the shoulders, which goes with the territory, but I feel that he’s competent, and the things that he’s trying to do."
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer seemed to be more open to making some kind of change with the coaching staff, but he did not specifically say how.
“Yeah, I'm gonna look at everything. I'll spend [time] trying to figure it out, and getting a chance to step back with these five games and see what we need to improve," Schottenheimer said .
We would venture to guess that if Jerry doesn't want Parker gone, Schotty is not going to fire him.
So, knowing that Parker isn't going anywhere, there are two logical steps: take play-calling duties away from him, which, at that point, the Cowboys might as well just fire him, or they can bring in an experienced defensive coordinator to consult.
Martindale fits the bill as a former defensive coordinator who had a lot of success with the Baltimore Ravens. Martindale also has the experience of being a struggling first-year defensive coordinator after he oversaw a terrible defense with the Denver Broncos in 2010.
Whether it's Martindale or another experienced defensive coach, the Cowboys need another set of eyes and opinions on how to proceed with their putrid defense because the status quo isn't good enough.

title: One Disgusting Stat Sums Up Brian Schottenheimer's Terrible Cowboys Tenure
full_text:
Fans were shocked when the Dallas Cowboys selected Brian Schottenheimer as their new head coach ahead of the 2025 season. Many changed their tunes when they heard him speak, however, as Coach Schotty has a gift for saying the right things.
Five weeks into his second season as the head coach proves that saying the right things doesn't always equal success. When hired, Schottenheimer said he wanted to build " the greatest culture in professional sports ," but after 22 games, he's been the worst coach the organization has seen during Dak Prescott's tenure.
Prescott, who took over in 2016, has faced his own criticism, but he's always been able to win games in the regular season. Under Jason Garrett, Prescott was 40-24, with the Cowboys winning 62.5% of their games. With Mike McCarthy, they had similar success with Dallas going 36-22 when Prescott was healthy under McCarthy.
Schottenheimer has now coached 22 games, all with Prescott, and is 9-12-1. That means he has won just 39% of his games with a quarterback who has historically won 62% of his starts.
Schotty is down to 39% now. Dak has been healthy for all 22 games of the Schottenheimer era. Dallas has won 9 of them. https://t.co/DpOvqrZnJY
One of the reasons Jerry Jones made the surprising decision to hire Schottenheimer was his relationship with Prescott. Schottenheimer spent three years on McCarthy's staff, serving as the offensive coordinator for two of those seasons.
He and Prescott worked well together and the belief was that their offense could pick up where it left off with McCarthy. That has been true for the most part, but as we saw during their loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday, that offense has a tendency to come out flat. They've also been guilty of allowing their opponents to dictate the pace, which happened in their Week 1 loss to the New York Giants as well.
Fingers have been pointed to the defensive side of the ball, and while the defense is terrible, both Garrett and McCarthy found ways to overcome various defensive struggles when Prescott was on the field. For Schottenheimer, that hasn't been the case.
He now enters Week 6 with a record of 1-10 when the offense scores less than 30 points. That shows that the head coach hasn't been able to adapt when the defense struggles, which is why he's been one of the worst hires in recent memory.

title: Jerry Jones Admits Reality of Cowboys' Defensive Issues Is Starting to Set In
full_text:
Before the Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones certainly wasn't thrilled with the overall state of the team's defense.
However, Jerry was also trying his best to keep things positive. For example, he said he wasn't as concerned about DaRon Bland as fans were, and Jones even said after the game that he still has confidence in struggling defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
But Jones changed his tune a bit on Friday, saying that it's "mind-boggling" the numbers the defense has put up over five games.
“Surprising isn’t a big enough word but this is mind boggling that we look back on the stats of our last five games," he said of the defense's issues.
He also realizes that any coat of sugar that is trying to be placed on things in meetings, when coaches point to a handful of things that went wrong and, if fixed, could change the outcome, simply isn't gong to fly with him any longer.
Jones clearly realizes that the Cowboys' defensive woes and losses overall are more than just about a handful of plays in any given game. Rather, it's a systemic issue.
"Every game I've ever been involved in ... you can sit around as a group and say 'but for this play, or this play, or this play,' it's five to six plays usually ... you can say, 'But for those, we would've won that game,'" Jones said on 105.3 The Fan .
"These types of meetings can actually play games with you when you say you can correct those five to six things," Jones added. "You've also got to realize reality is when you plug it up over there, there will be another five-to-six, or seven things that influenced how it goes. You can have an analysis of how the game went and you can basically have a decent attitude.
"That's BS-ing yourself. That's not real. You've got to look at the whole thing and say here we are, we've lost three games, and look at how we're playing. You've got to be hard on yourself. I assure you we're being hard on yourself."
The Cowboys owner said he's pulling no punches in the meetings the team is having to try and figure things out because that's the best way to face problems.
"I don't mind this morning pouring salt in the wound, because that's the constructive thing to do," Jones said . "That's what I've been doing this morning and that's what I'll do all day today. We'll continue to be doing it: giving ourself the roughin' up you have to do when you're performing like this."
While it's good to see things are starting to sink in for Jones, he is not quite all the way where he needs to be.
After all, Jones still thinks DaRon Bland can be the player he was earlier in his career, even though we haven't seen that guy in two seasons and he's looking even worse in 2026.
Jones also isn't even considering making any sweeping changes , he told 105.3 The Fan, even though a shake-up is clearly needed.
"You've got to think more about, now than you do future," he said. "That's not in acquiring talent as much as it is how you address practice this week, how you address how we approach playing Green Bay. Now all of this you say, 'We need better answers,' and, 'We need answers that sound like it could solve it all.' That's just not there, not that answer."
The Cowboys have a coaching issue as much as they have a talent issue at some of their positions on defense. It's hard to have faith in the Cowboys turning things around until at least one of those two things is fixed.

title: Cowboys Defense Ripped as Former Pro Bowler Calls for Quinnen Williams Benching
full_text:
Thursday night was an awful night for the Dallas Cowboys , who suffered a defeat at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It was an embarrassing effort and a historically bad loss for a team that entered the year with championship hopes.
Making the loss sting even more is the fact that the Bucs were starting an undrafted free agent in Jalon Daniels at quarterback. Daniels, who struggled in his first start in Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers, had his way with this defense.
After the game, Dak Prescott said it was "right up there close to embarrassing," but added that he might not use that word. It's hard to find any other word to use , which was what the crew on ESPN's Get Up had to say. Former NFL quarterback Dan Orlovsky even stated that this defense is worse than they were a year ago, which didn't seem possible entering the season.
"This defense is worse this year than it was last year. This defense did everything last night that they couldn't. Four penalties they had to keep drives alive for Tampa Bay," Orlovsky said. "They lost leverage multiple times on a rookie quarterback that the thing he was going to do best was use his legs. Multiple times, the 72-yard run to start the second half is a microcosm because the peaking, the lack of tackling."
Orlovsky then called out the lack of fundamentals, pointing out that veterans such as Rashan Gary, Quinnen Williams, and Kenny Clark all let their team down on Thursday. That belief was echoed by former Pro Bowl safety Donte Whitner, who said Williams is playing like he has velcro sticking him to his blocker. He added that he should "probably be benched at this point."
"Well, schematically, they're penetrating too much. Whenever you bring a run blitz, you want to move sideline to sideline. You want to restrict the space. They're opening up too much lateral space and too much vertical space. And then you see a lack of effort to the football," Whitner said. "You see Quinnen Williams? He's like Velcro. He can't even get off of a block. How much are they paying this guy? And they probably should bench him at this point."
“[The Dallas Cowboys are] a defensive unit that, through five games, is a worse unit than last year.” @danorlovsky7 on the Cowboys' loss to the Buccaneers😬 pic.twitter.com/RRJ9zi3z7F
After five games, Williams has just 15 tackles and one sack for the Cowboys. He signed a three-year, $105.9 million extension before the start of the regular season, poised to be the face of their defense. That hasn't been the case as Williams has failed to make a huge impact.
Asking him to be benched, however, feels excessive. As poorly as he's performed, the fact is that he's still been one of their better defensive linemen. The problems in Dallas go well beyond Williams and considering this unit is worse under Christian Parker than they were under Matt Eberflus, it's clear the problem goes beyond the defensive coaching staff as well.

title: Cowboys Week 5 Report Card Shows Dallas Utter Failure On Both Sides of Football
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys fell to 2-3 on the season after what was nothing short of an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.
The Cowboys were an inconsistent mess on offense , at best, and the defense once again looked like a league-worst unit against an offense led by undrafted rookie quarterback at the helm of an 0-4 team.
After what we've seen through five games, the Cowboys are not a serious football team. The offense has to scratch and claw for everything it gets and the defense is just awful.
If you can stomach it, here's how we graded the Cowboys after their pathetic loss to the Buccaneers in Week 5.
The passing attack started off hot, disappeared, revived in the fourth quarter and then finished off with a turnover to finish the burying of the carcass that was Dallas' offense in Week 5.
Dak Prescott was off badly, and he missed a touchdown chance on a deep ball to CeeDee Lamb, who was wide open down the field before Dak just couldn't get the ball there.
The pass-catchers didn't help Prescott, either, with Jake Ferguson and Ryan Flournoy both having balls bounce off their hands or face mask that turned into interceptions.
As if all that wasn't enough, the Cowboys could not counteract the blitzes Todd Bowles was drawing up, which only made Prescott's job more difficult on a night when he didn't have his best stuff.
The only reason this wasn't a failing grade is because the passing attack was the only reason the Cowboys even had a chance to win the game, even with how bad it was. Somehow, Prescott managed to finish with 316 passing yards, the second-most he's had in a game this season.
It was clear the Cowboys made it a point of emphasis to run behind Tyler Smith early, and it worked. However, that success didn't last long and we began to see the same struggles that Dallas has had on the ground all season long.
Javonte Williams found pay dirt once again, but he also averaged less than four yards per carry and he's averaging 3.7 yards per tote this season.
It looks like it's going to take more than Smith being back to get this part of the Cowboys' offense going.
Joey Porter Jr. was a late scratch because of an illness , so Dallas didn't have its best cornerback. It did, however, have its worst, which is easily DaRon Bland.
Bland slipped on a few occasions, and both were costly. The first led to a 64-yard strike for the Bucs that ultimately set them up for a touchdown, and then he slipped again later in the same quarter and gave up a first down on a third-and-21 play. Tampa Bay managed to turn that drive into a field goal.
Bland had an opportunity to change his and Dallas' fortunes in the fourth quarter with a gift-wrapped pick-six, but he simply dropped it. At this point, it's negligence if Bland is starting in Week 6.
Reddy Steward struggled as well, and the pass-rush once again could not get home to finish with sacks and allowed Jalon Daniels to do his best impression of Houdini on way too many occasions.
If there was a grade worse than an "F," we would give it.
We can just stop at Bucky Irving's 165 yards and one score, but we'll still dive a little deeper.
Irving's 72-yard scamper just never should have happened, as the Cowboys had him dead to rights behind the line of scrimmage, yet he found a way to break through for the big gain that set up a touchdown. A failure to get off blocks caused that one.
The Cowboys failed miserably at setting the edge, and they were not able to plug up holes up the gut. Dallas' run defense once again proved it can't stop a nosebleed.
Special teams, which has been a massive issue this season, was actually the least pathetic group on Thursday night — but there was still a major blunder.
That came when KaVontae Turpin fumbled a kickoff return that the Bucs were able to capitalize on and turn into points via field goal. But, hey, at least there wasn't a blocked field goal again.
Brian Schottenheimer admitted at halftime that he needed to do a better job calling plays, and while there were some adjustments to better handle the blitz, it wasn't good enough overall. Schotty isn't going to get fired, but he should fire himself from play-calling duties and give them to Klayton Adams. Just try something.
As for Christian Parker, he's doing less with more and things are so bad we're actually starting to miss Matt Eberflus. Jerry Jones has expressed confidence in Parker after the Thursday night debacle, but we do not share that belief.

title: Broncos Add Veteran DB—Here's What It Could Mean
full_text:
Entering Week 5's divisional road matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers , the Denver Broncos bit the bullet on Pat Bryant, placing him on injured reserve .
That'll put Bryant out of commission until Week 9, at the soonest. To fill his spot on the 53-man roster, the Broncos promoted veteran wideout Lil'Jordan Humphrey from the practice squad.
The Broncos will be without Bryant for the foreseeable future. As for Week 5, the Broncos will also be missing their two starting cornerbacks — Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss — both of whom were ruled out of action on Friday. Fortunately, the Chargers are also banged up, but the onus will fall on the young Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine to step in and keep the ship afloat alongside veteran nickel corner Ja'Quan McMillian.
With a practice squad spot open, the Broncos worked out eight players on Friday, all of whom were either defensive backs or linebackers. Ultimately, Denver liked what it saw from veteran cornerback Ugo Amadi, signing him to the practice squad.
Amadi joins rookie Brent Austin and the first-year Sean Fresch Jr. as cornerbacks on the practice squad. But Amadi is significantly more experienced than either.
A 2019 fourth-round pick by the Seattle Seahawks, Amadi is now on his seventh NFL team. The 5-foot-9, 201-pound Oregon product has appeared in 85 NFL games, with 17 career starts.
Amadi spent the previous three years with the New Orleans Saints. In 2024, he started five games for the Saints, totaling 65 tackles (52 solo), six tackles for a loss, two sacks, and seven pass break-ups. As you can see, physicality is not an issue for the 29-year-old defensive back.
As a nickel corner, Amadi is one inch shorter than McMillian, but he's nearly 20 pounds heavier. With how much big nickel the Broncos have had to play this season to counter the heavy tight end packages opponents have thrown at them, McMillian's snap share has gone down a little bit.
As the league moves toward this multiple-tight-end trend, it's forcing teams to prioritize bigger, more physical nickel players. Amadi doesn't have great height, but he's physical and can hang in the box.
McMillian is a feisty, physical nickel himself, but he's been neutralized somewhat by opponents' game plans this season. Amadi isn't coming in to replace anyone, but if the Broncos opt to elevate him in the near future — probably not this week — he could be rotated in to help against bigger tight end packages, if needed.
The Broncos have increasingly given No. 3 safety Devon Key more snaps to help counteract the way teams are attacking them with tight ends. It's mostly a run game thing. McMillian is physical enough to hang with most tight ends in coverage, even though he can be outsized height-wise, but when the Broncos are caught in their nickel package and opponents run the ball, that's where having a bit more size in the defensive backfield can be helpful.
Time will tell how Amadi ultimately fits in and whether the Broncos ever elevate him, but it's good to add some experience to cornerback room, especially with Surtain and Moss being injured currently.
In terms of the workouts the Broncos held on Friday, it's worth knowing the names because this team will often circle back to sign players it has worked out, sometimes several weeks in the past.
It's interesting that Denver is keeping an eye on the linebackers available out there currently. With Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad as the starters, the Broncos also have Karene Reid and Jordan Turner on the 53-man roster, with rookie Red Murdock on the practice squad.
The Amadi addition is about more than just depth. The Broncos are facing the reality that Surtain and Moss could miss more than just Week 5, and after Barron, Abrams-Draine, and McMillian, none of their cornerbacks had real NFL experience.
Amadi brings 208 tackles, 22 pass break-ups, a pair of sacks, an interception, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery to the table. He's played for vetearn defensive coordinators like Steve Spagnuolo and Ken Norton Jr., as well as younger coaches like Jonathon Gannon and Brandon Staley, among others.
It's good to have some experienced depth at cornerback as the Broncos roll with the injury punches.

title: Broncos Week 5 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Moss
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's road tilt against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
As expected, the Broncos will be without starting cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss, who went down with ankle and rib injuries, respectively, during last week's loss to San Francisco. They were ruled out after missing practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.
Although it wasn't included on the report, Denver also placed wide receiver Pat Bryant — who suffered an ankle injury of his own in Week 4 — on short-term injured reserve. Bryant will be sidelined for at least the next four games before being eligible to return.
Listed as full practice participants on Friday and given no game designation were defensive end Zach Allen, running back Tyler Badie (foot), defensive lineman DJ Jones, outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring), and tight end Adam Trautman (shoulder).
Friday's #DENvsLAC injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/pkZT6PjAXz pic.twitter.com/4DMyEOpFpt
On the Chargers' side , it's ... much messier. Los Angeles officially ruled out seven players; among them, starting tackle Joe Alt, safety Derwin James, wide receiver Quentin Johnston, and cornerback Donte Jackson. They also listed backup quarterback Trey Lance as doubtful, and five other players (including top WR Ladd McConkey) as questionable.
Beyond this week, the Broncos are expected to get Surtain and Moss back within a few games, as their issues are not considered long-term . RB Jonah Coleman is also eligible to come off IR in Week 7.
Such as they did against the Niners, with Surtain and Moss out of the lineup, the Broncos will turn to reserve cornerbacks Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine to contain a depleted Chargers receiving corps.
Both players held their own in Week 4 and the coaching staff is confident that will persist moving forward.
“They’re savvy players, they both have good football instincts and IQ," head coach Sean Payton said of Barron and Abrams-Draine on Wednesday. "One of the reasons you draft at that position is because it’s hard to find in free agency. So both were ready when they needed to be and that’s encouraging.”
With Bryant absent, Denver could lean more heavily on little-used WRs Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin while attempting to get veteran Courtland Sutton going following a slow start to the year. It, too, is possible — if not probable — that quarterback Bo Nix sprinkles a few additional targets to running back RJ Harvey, who's currently the club's leading pass-catcher.
“Some of it’s the soft zone coverage that went underneath," Payton explained Wednesday. "There are probably five different reasons to the team we played. Certainly, you come away from that game as a coach and you’re like, ‘All right, we have to find more touches for Courtland for “X” amount of receivers, even when they’re in these deeper zones.' We’ll be able to do that, but we start with a mirror right away with ourselves. So we know he can be a factor for… He doesn’t have to be just outside, he can be inside depending on the route.”
