title: Broncos Can’t Afford to Lose These 2 Matchups vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers have been a divisional matchup that Sean Payton and Bo Nix have yet to figure out.
Even with Denver at 2-2, the 0-4 Chargers still have plenty of ways to pull off an upset. The Broncos have plenty of flaws that could have seen them also limp out to an 0-4 start. Thankfully, that's not the case, but it's another example of why L.A. can't be overlooked.
Not only do the Broncos have their fair share of issues, but recent injuries could exacerbate things, and the Chargers have the talent to attack those issues. Denver has to be ready to handle this week's key matchups , especially with the injuries they're dealing with.
Let's break down those matchups to watch in Broncos-Chargers.
McGlinchey wasn't terrible against the San Francisco 49ers, but he wasn't good either. In the first three weeks of the season, he played a bench-worthy brand of football, and if Denver had a viable backup right tackle, maybe it would have happened.
Through four weeks, McGlinchey has been one of the worst tackles in the NFL.
On the flip side, the Chargers have received good showings from their two top edge rushers. Mack and Tuipulotu have combined for 28 pressures, 14 each, with three sacks for the former and one for the latter.
The Chargers also like to flip them around depending on the down and distance, which keeps tackles from getting into a rhythm against the same player.
Left tackle Garett Bolles has been good so far, and there is no reason to expect a drop-off, but Denver needs McGlinchey to step up opposite the All-Pro. If McGlinchey can't hold his own against these two pass rushers, it could make for a long day for Bo Nix and the Broncos' offense, given the quarterback's early struggles with pressure.
With Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss ruled out and likely Riley Moss, too, the Broncos are left with Ja'Quan McMillian, Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine at cornerback. McMillian and Barron lack the ideal size and length, while Abrams-Draine is lighter than you want and not overly physical.
This creates serious concerns against the Chargers' receiving corps, which will look to exploit those limitations.
Quentin Johnston has been ruled out for Week 5 (chest), but he, Tre Harris, and Ladd McConkey (questionable) have 53 combined targets through four games, with 32 catches, 500 yards, and a touchdown. McConkey is small but has taken McMillian to task before; Harris is long and fast, which could create issues for the Broncos' corners.
What could exacerbate the problem is tight end Oronde Gadsden II, given how the Chargers employ him. He can create issues for the Broncos' linebackers and force safety help, which would take away from their ability to shade help toward the boundary corners.
Vance Joseph has his work cut out for him in figuring out how to handle the Chargers' receivers with the cornerbacks at his disposal.

title: Bo Nix Feels He Let Davis Webb Down—Now It's Time to Step Up
full_text:
Bo Nix was disappointed in Sean Payton's decision to take back the offensive play-calling duties this week.
According to Payton, the Denver Broncos' quarterback feels he let his close friend and coach down after Davis Webb lost his play-calling responsibilities after just four games. Nix is not alone in that disappointment.
“Everyone’s a little disappointed because you feel like you let one of your teammates down," Payton said when asked what Nix's reaction to the news was. "That’s the human part of it. That’s our game a little bit in this league."
Nix is aware that, four years into his NFL coaching career, Webb has been on a rocket-ship trajectory, drawing head-coaching interest around the league in each of the past two hiring cycles. If Webb could hit this new offensive coordinator/play-caller job out of the park for Payton, everyone knew that his future as an NFL head coach was secure.
Nix wanted that for his friend, and he certainly didn't want to do anything that would contribute to holding Webb back. That's why the quarterback's disappointment is so understandable.
It's not that Nix is disappointed to be working so directly with Payton again; he's just bummed for what it means for his pal, Webb, especially relative to his NFL coaching stock. The silver lining, though, is that this play-calling shake-up likely means that Webb will be sticking around beyond 2026, even if the Broncos turn things around and meet expectations as a playoff team.
But that's not how Nix and Webb dreamed it up. They were supposed to create some big things together this year, and perhaps send Webb off in style to his first head-coaching gig.
Alas, the NFL decided to structure Denver's first-place schedule in a way that pitted them against the league's four best teams consecutively to start the season. That'd be a tough row to hoe for any coach, let alone a fourth-year guy calling plays for the first time in his career.
The Broncos' offense has been ugly and downright bad at times, but beating two of those teams is more than a moral victory. We're talking about a 2-2 team, after all — not a winless Broncos squad.
It's unfortunate how Denver played in the first four games of this season, but Nix can't afford to dwell on his disappointment. Payton and the Broncos need him to step up and answer the bell this week against the Los Angeles Chargers — and it's not like Webb has gone anywhere.
Webb is still in the meetings and will be on the sidelines with Nix and Broncos quarterbacks coach Logan Kilgore. It's be Payton's familiar voice that Nix hears in his ear now.
In all actuality, Nix stands to be the biggest winner of Payton's decision to take back the play-calling. It wasn't always perfect, but Nix and Payton have conjured a lot of Mile High Magic together.
Some people have theorized that taking back the play-calling was Payton's only alternative to getting Nix back on track because it's not as if the veteran coach could bench his quarterback. But he could bench Webb.
I understand that school of thought, but Nix hasn't been that bad. At the risk of sounding like someone making excuses for the third-year quarterback, he's gone 2-2 against the NFL's very best opponents, passing for 819 and five touchdowns with three interceptions and a lost fumble.
Nix has only completed 60% of his passes, which would be a career-low if he finished there, and that's kind of stupifying, given how many of his targets have been check-downs to running backs. As I wrote earlier this week, he has looked timid as a quarterback, hesitant to push the ball downfield, and seemingly over-focused on ball security instead of making plays.
Payton claims that his decision to take back the play-calling isn't about trying to fix Nix; he did because he believes it's what is best for the Broncos right now.
“No," Payton said on whether this is about fixing Nix. "Bo is the by-product of a lot of things at that position. Hopefully that will be one of the things that can happen, but there are a lot of other things that I think can allow that to happen first.”
Getting the offensive line playing well would go a long way toward helping Nix break out of his funk. He's been under a career-high amount of pressure this season, despite only being sacked five times — the second-fewest in the NFL.
Fielding a viable run game would also help get Nix back on track, and avoid so many third-and-longs. J.K. Dobbins is due for a big game, and he made a lot of hay with Payton as his play-caller last season before his injury.
The truth is, Nix has had a ton of success with Payton as his play-caller, too. We could go through and list all the records Nix owns — and the number of games he's won — but I think fans understand just how prolific his first two seasons were.
Payton believes he has to take back control of the play-calling in order to get the offense back on track and Nix playing like a franchise quarterback. It's unfortunate that it comes at the expense of Webb, but Payton emphasized multiple times at the podium on Thursday that his protege's future is still very, very bright.
"I’m going to go back to what I said earlier relative to his talent," Payton said of Webb. "It’s rare. He’s gifted. It’s all ahead of him, I’m talking about Davis.”
We're going to hear from Webb on Friday. Payton said that Webb "will be fantasitc" at the podium. We're fixin' to find out, as Gary Kubiak was fond of saying.
You feel for Nix and his teammates, but they can't worry about Webb. The Broncos have to focus on righting the ship offensively, and if they can do that this week against the winless Los Angeles Chargers , it'll go a long way toward quieting the noise around this team.
The Chargers may be 0-4, but Nix's only career win against them came late last season when Jim Harbaugh rested Justin Herbert and many of his key starters. The Chargers are desperate, so the Broncos have to treat them no differently than they would if they were 4-0.
L.A. is pretty banged up right now, on both sides of the ball, so Nix has a great opportunity to get his first-ever win at SoFi Stadium and answer the bell for his head coach. Payton's recent decision raised eyebrows around the league, but it also put all the pressure on his shoulders.
If Nix steps up and plays well in L.A., the Broncos will win the game. The pressure on Payton will pop like a balloon, and the Broncos will get to 3-2 in time to host the World Champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football .
Best not to get too far ahead of ourselves, though. Take it by the inch, it's a cinch. By the yard, it gets hard.

title: Mile High Roundtable Delivers Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Chargers
full_text:
Sean Payton is looking for a spark .
Absent one, the Denver Broncos' head coach is bent on striking the match himself.
In a not-too-distant alternate universe, the Broncos could be in the same boat as the Los Angeles Chargers, sitting at 0-4. The Broncos' offense has been that bad, but fortunately, Bo Nix pulled off Bo Nix things, storming back in two of those games to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory.
But as Payton himself said earlier this week , the Broncos have not been playing a "championship" brand of football. They've had to face, literally, the NFL's four best teams in consecutive weeks to open this season, but outside two fourth quarters, the Broncos haven't looked like a team at that level.
Meanwhile, the Chargers are winless and desperate. They're not only a division rival, but they're also a cornered animal likely to bite and scratch without warning and in ways unexpected.
The Broncos can't afford to look past the Chargers, even though tougher games are ahead. Payton has never won at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach, and he's 1-5 against the Chargers.
How will this Broncos-Chargers throwdown shake out? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff envisions this one unfolding. Connect with each writer on X (their handles are linked next to their names).
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 3-1 : It’s easy to pick against the Broncos at the moment, given how they played last week. But after Payton took back play-calling and with the chance to drive a stake in the Chargers’ season, I think Denver finds a spark and doesn’t just eke out a victory. It’ll get downplayed due to the level of competition, and some questions might still persist, but they’ll do what they gotta do.
Pick : Broncos 26, Chargers 19
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 3-1 : If there's going to be a week for the Broncos to have a good start on offense , this is it. The Chargers aren't bad on defense, but they're nowhere near as good as the other teams the Broncos have faced. And with the injury issues the Chargers are dealing with , the Broncos have to capitalize on defense. While it's a legitimate question to ask whether the Broncos can get it done here, I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt here. They find a way.
Pick : Broncos 23, Chargers 17
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 2-2 : Struggles on offense led to Payton taking back the play-calling from first-year coordinator Davis Webb. Something needs to click for the Broncos' offense, regardless of who's calling the plays. A narrow win on the West Coast turns Denver's focus to Sam Darnold's Seattle Seahawks on a short week.
Pick : Broncos 21, Chargers 17
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 2-2 : This has been a dysfunctional week for the Broncos after an abysmal showing against San Francisco. Thankfully, the Broncos are blessed with a struggling and beat-up Chargers team starting four new guys on the offensive line. The Broncos try to stay more balanced on offense, knowing the defense will handle its business. Less pressure on Nix leads to a couple of explosive throws and a good win on the road.

Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 2-2 : In Payton I trust. He may have egg on his face from pulling the plug on the Webb experiment four games into the season, but he's got bigger fish to fry. title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over Chargers at SoFi Stadium
full_text:
Over the first four weeks of the season, the Denver Broncos have faced four teams that are among the favorites to reach the Super Bowl this year. The advanced metrics say Denver's first four opponents are the NFL's four best teams currently.
The theme has been that the Broncos have had sluggish starts, particularly on offense, but find a way to get it together in the second half and, at least twice, produce comeback victories.
While one may not have expected the Broncos to go 4-0 to open the season, fans at least expected them to play well through four quarters, win or lose, given how deep into the playoffs this team got last year. That hasn't happened yet, and the Broncos' first-half struggles on offense are particularly frustrating.
Sean Payton seems frustrated, announcing on Thursday that he's taking back the offensive play-calling from first-year coordinator Davis Webb.
For the first time this season, the Broncos are facing an opponent that is not only struggling, but also a team few, if anyone, expected to be 0-4 to start the season. The Los Angeles Chargers were considered a playoff contender entering 2026, but they haven't looked the part.
It goes without saying that the Broncos can't take anything for granted this week, as they need to come away with a win in this AFC West matchup, especially given that, after the Chargers, they'll face a short-week turnaround with the Seattle Seahawks coming to Mile High on Thursday Night Football.
What will it take to win at SoFi Stadium on Sunday? Let's look at three keys to Denver beating the Chargers and improving to 3-2.
It's no secret that Herbert is off to the worst start of his NFL career. Through the first four games of the season, he's completed 59.7% of his passes with four touchdowns and six interceptions.
Herbert has never had a completion percentage under 65% in his career, so those numbers will likely surprise some people. While he does have weaknesses as a passer, not everything is his fault.
The Chargers face questions about whether Mike McDaniel was the right offensive coordinator for Herbert. Their offensive line is banged up, with both offensive tackles, Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater, expected to miss Sunday's game .
And then there are the receivers. Ladd McConkey is dealing with a foot injury, and Quentin Johnston, who seemed to be coming around last season, has regressed. On the other hand, Tre Harris has been solid with 13 catches for 209 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown.
The Chargers do have a solid tight end in Oronde Gadsden II, who has nine catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. If McConkey doesn't play — and if the same applies to Johnston, who is dealing with an injury of his own — one might expect Gadsden to see more targets.
As for the running game, Omarion Hampton has averaged 4.0 yards per carry and has scored three touchdowns. However, he's fumbled twice, so ball security has been an issue for him.
But regardless of Herbert's play, the Chargers' play-calling, and the injuries on offense, the fact remains that Sean Payton, as Broncos head coach, has yet to beat this opponent when Herbert is in the lineup. Payton is 1-5 against the Chargers since he took over in Denver back in 2023, and the one win came last year to close the 2026 season when Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh opted to rest his starters.
Simply put, the Broncos cannot assume they're going to have their way with Herbert. They need to get it together on defense, even if they won't have Patrick Surtain II this week and may not have Riley Moss, either. The Broncos need to find a way to take advantage of the weaknesses on the Chargers' offense, get a pass rush going, and create turnovers.
The Chargers have 10 turnovers in four games, while their opponents have seven, with the Bills accounting for five of them — and that Buffalo game is the only instance thus far of L.A. winning the turnover battle.
It all adds up to this: The Broncos' defense needs to do its job well and not assume that this will be an easy task. They need to treat Herbert with respect and approach the game as if he's a top quarterback, even if he's not always playing like it right now.
As much as the Chargers have been struggling on offense this season, the Broncos have had their own share of woes. The Broncos have scored just 13 points in the first half through four games. That's not a recipe for success.
It's true that the Broncos have faced a string of quality defenses, as all four opponents they have faced are ranked in the top 10. However, the Broncos have made enough mistakes on offense in the first half that haven't helped matters, from dropped passes to missed reads to poor blocking.
If the Broncos are going to get it together in the first half and put more points on the board, though, this is the game where they need to do it. They are not going against a top defense here — the Chargers rank 20th in defensive DVOA, so while they aren't bad, they're nowhere near as good as the four defenses the Broncos have faced thus far.
Khalil Mack is 35 years old, but he's still getting it done on the field. He has 10 QB pressures and three sacks through four games, so he's still somebody the Broncos must contain, while Tuli Tuipulotu is coming off a strong 2025 season and is off to a good start this season, with eight pressures and two sacks.
It's the secondary that may be the Chargers' defensive weakness, particularly with two players entering Week 5 with injuries. Safety Derwin James and cornerback Donte Jackson are both dealing with hamstring injuries and might not see the field on Sunday.
The Chargers have held opposing running backs to 3.8 yards per carry, so the Broncos will need the passing game to have a good start to take pressure off the running backs. That means Bo Nix and his receivers need to be in sync early and often.
It's a golden opportunity for Payton to have his first game back as the offensive play-caller.
The dropped passes and missed reads have to be cleaned up, and the Broncos need to show they can attack downfield on offense, rather than relying on the screen game and checkdowns too much. The Chargers can bring pressure on defense, but with a defensive backfield that may be depleted, the Broncos must capitalize.
One issue the Chargers have had this season is giving up unfavorable field position to opponents. There have been multiple instances of the Chargers allowing the opponent to get the ball at midfield or in their territory, whether it's through special teams or a turnover.
Against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1, the Chargers had a punt blocked early in the fourth quarter that led to a touchdown. They also had a drive stall late in the fourth quarter, which led to a Cardinals field goal that put the game away.
In Week 2, the Las Vegas Raiders had two drives start at midfield in the first half, one after a missed field goal and the other after they got favorable field position when the Chargers had to punt deep in their own territory, the latter of which led to a touchdown. Late in the game, the Chargers fumbled the ball, and the Raiders recovered at the L.A. 16-yard line, scoring a touchdown after that.
The Bills had a lot of mistakes on offense in the first half of the Week 3 matchup, but they still started the game with the ball on their own 43-yard line after the Chargers gave up a 39-yard kickoff return to Greg Dortch. And early in the fourth quarter, Herbert threw an interception that C.J. Gardner-Johnson returned 41 yards to midfield, setting up a Bills touchdown.
The Seahawks started with the ball on the Chargers' 45-yard line on the first drive of their Week 4 matchup after a Drake Thomas interception. While Sam Darnold threw an interception after that, the Seahawks later got the ball on the Chargers' 31-yard line, after L.A. kicked a field goal, but Derius Davis returned the kickoff 30 yards. title: Broncos Could Catch a Major Break With Chargers' Injury Report
full_text:
The Denver Broncos enter Week 5's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers as banged up as they've been this season.
Still, Denver's Thursday practice report features less than half the number of injured players as L.A.'s does. Let's take a look at how the Week 5 injury report is shaping up, with one more practice day to go before Sunday's action at SoFi Stadium.
Like Allen was on Wednesday, Jones was limited only because the Broncos gave him rest. Jones is not injured.
It's good to see Tillman and Trautman progress from limited to full participants on Thursday. Tillman missed last week's game with his hamstring injury, and the Broncos' defense suffered for it.
Badie is banged up with a foot, but it's good to see that he was a full participant on both days of practice thus far. When it comes to the Broncos' running back room, it's good to see RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins no longer listed on the injury report.
It's not looking good for Surtain, Moss, and Bryant this week. Friday will be the decider for Moss, but he's trending toward not playing.
With Surtain and Bryant, though, we've known since Monday that both are expected to miss Week 5, at the very least, and possibly more time with their respective ankle injuries. Jahdae Barron, Kris Abrams-Draine, and Courtland Sutton will need to step up on Sunday in the absence of this trio of key players.
As you can see, the Chargers are in bad shape. At 0-4, they're literally the walking wounded. The two injuries that could impact this game most are at offensive tackle, as neither Slater nor Alt are expected to play in this game.
Nik Bonitto and Jonah Elliss should be licking their chops over the opportunity for a get-right game against the Chargers. Justin Herbert has been sacked 12 times already, and after being shut out in this department last week by the San Francisco 49ers, the Broncos will be looking to make up for lost time.
The Chargers have several other key players whose Week 5 outlook isn't so good, like James, Jackson, and McConkey, among others. The Chargers are desperate, in more ways than one, so the Broncos will have to be ready to exploit the absence of these key players, and beware the cornered-animal effect of this division rival.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers of Sean Payton Taking Back Play-Calling
full_text:
Sean Payton has taken back the play-calling duties at Denver Broncos HQ.
First-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb had been under heavy scrutiny as the play-caller amid the Broncos' struggles out of the gate. On Wednesday, rumors lit up the NFL that Payton's patience was wearing thin, but he didn't even wait until after this week's road matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers to make the decision.
Payton made the decision to take back the play-calling on Monday. So the ESPN rumors were well-founded after all. On Thursdays, we're supposed to hear from the Broncos' coordinator trio, but instead it was Payton who stepped up to the podium and announced he's taken back the play-calling duties.
"We’ll make a change offensively," Payton said. "I’ll call the plays."
Payton did the best he could to tip his hat at Webb and preserve a semblance of dignity on behalf of his young protege. But it's not just Webb dealing with a dinged PR profile; Payton has plenty of egg on his face, too.
"I want to say this first, and I said it to Davis the other day talking to him. I’ve done this long enough where I know when I have a future head coach, and he’s going to be one," Payton said. "All the things that it’s hard to find will happen. In fact, the same thing to some degree—a little bit different—happened to myself early in my career."
And by the way, if you ever doubted Payton's confidence in his play-calling acumen, after relinquishing them to Webb in the offseason, the veteran coach disabused you that notion when he was asked about the NFL's growing ranks of talented play-callers.
“I think I’m still one of them," Payton said.
With Payton taking back the play sheet, there are some big winners and losers at Broncos HQ. Let's examine.
Amid Nix's early-season struggles, it's easy to forget he's the only quarterback in NFL history to pass for 7,500-plus yards, 50-plus touchdowns, and win 20-plus games through his first two years as a pro. It was unprecedented success, as there have been quarterbacks, like Justin Herbert, who had crazy statistical production out of the gate, but not the wins.
Nix had both. And who was the guy calling the plays and putting the young quarterback in position to achieve such individual success, leading to the Broncos' immense collective success? Payton.
Nobody is perfect. We've critiqued Payton's play-calling at times with Nix as his quarterback. Overall, though, Payton's resume speaks for itself.
Payton's play-calling helped bring the city of New Orleans its one and only World Championship and vaulted Drew Brees into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Payton placed Nix on a similar path to start his career, and although the veteran coach genuinely thought giving Webb the play sheet was the best thing for his young quarterback and the team, the results simply haven't been there.
It's a tough setback for Webb, and I'm sure that Nix feels for his dear friend and coordinator. But he's got to be quietly excited by Payton taking back the play-calling, as Nix has been on pace to produce a career-low season statistically.
In all honesty, Webb is one of the few losers in this equation. But if he has the right mindset, he can take this as a learning experience, grow from it, and become a better coach and play-caller in the future.
I'm sure this was a tough decision for Payton for multiple reasons, not the least of which is how it'll affect Webb's NFL profile as a future head-coaching candidate. That's why Payton led with the head coach stuff in his initial statement.
If Payton's big decision leads to an offensive renaissance for the Broncos, and Nix looks like the quarterback of yore, it'll give owners and front offices around the league even more doubts about Webb's wherewithal as a head-coaching candidate.
But that's only an immediate setback for Webb, relative to the 2027 hiring cycle. If the Broncos go on to meet their playoff expectations, regardless of whether it results in a Super Bowl berth, Webb could still garner head-coaching interest, but more likely, he'll have to wait another year.
That's okay. He's only in Year 4 as an NFL coach, and he's still young at 31. Payton ultimately had to do what he believed was best for the Broncos, not what's best for Webb's NFL resume.
If one of the collateral effects is that this decision keeps Webb in Denver for another year, I'm sure it's a consequence Payton will accept happily, even if his protege isn't quite as thrilled.
Sutton has only caught nine passes for 86 yards through four games. He's on pace to finish the season with under 100 targets, which has never happened with Nix as his quarterback.
Under Payton's play-calling, Sutton produced a career-high 10 touchdowns in 2023 with Russell Wilson as his QB, followed by back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons and his second Pro Bowl selection with Nix.
Sutton would never say it publicly, but he knows his stock just went up.
I say 'loser,' but it could end up being a big win for Engram, too. With Webb as the play-caller, Engram's snap share has risen dramatically since last season because of the coordinator's prioritization of the multiple-tight-end sets.
Engram has been kept in to block at a much higher clip, which has also seen his usage in the passing game climb, too. Unfortunately, though, Nix and the Broncos haven't been able to exploit Engram's increase in playing time with producion on the field.
Last season, Engram finished third on the team in receiving, but he was overall frustrated by the amount of snaps he have up to Adam Trautman. We'll see if Payton chooses to continue the multi-tight-end thing, and I have a sneaking suspicion that he will.
If so, Engram will actually end up being a winner in this big decision. If Payton goes back to the 11 personnel/spread approach he favored last year, Engram might see his playing time decrease.
It's no coincidence that every winner I've mentioned so far is also on my ' Biggest Disappointments at the Quarter Pole ' list. That includes Dobbins, who is also on pace for a career-low-type season.
The Broncos' ground game just hasn't clicked yet, like, at all. The Broncos made the decision to re-sign Dobbins with a 4x raise, and so far, that investment has been squandered.
That's about to change, though, provided Dobbins can stay healthy (knock on wood). He and Payton made magic together last season before the veteran back suffered a foot injury that ended his campaign.
The Broncos returned the same starting five for the third straight year. So why has this offensive line looked orders of magnitude worse than it did the previous two years?
It's the same scheme, the same quarterback, and the same collection of backs. Even Zach Strief remains this team's run game coordinator and ultimate O-line czar.
The only new factor was that Payton wasn't calling the plays. It certainly hasn't helped that Denver has faced, literally, the NFL's four best teams in consecutive weeks to start this season.
That has something to do with the O-line situation, and why it's allowing a career-high level of pressure on Nix. Payton's play-calling should get this unit back on track.
Payton famously advised his wife, Skylene, to draft Waddle in fantasy. Outside of one game, though — Week 2 — Waddle hasn't been much of a fantasy factor, though he did score his first touchdown as a Bronco last week.
In two of Denver's four games, Waddle has totaled two or fewer receptions. That's obviously not what the Broncos had in mind when they relinquished a first- and third-round pick to acquire Waddle and his contract.
Payton now has all the weapons that he's coveted traditionally and that have been hallmarks of his offenses over the years. Sutton gives him the big-bodied X receiver; Engram is the athletic, pass-catching tight end; RJ Harvey is the explosive receiver out of the backfield; and Dobbins is the between-the-tackles grinder.
The only thing missing was the explosive downfield speed demon, and that's exactly what Waddle brings to the table. When we…

title: Broncos' Most Disappointing Players at the Quarter Pole of the Season
full_text:
When the NFL changed the regular-season schedule to 17 games, we lost the ability to perfectly break down the season by four-game quarters.
But as a rule of thumb, I still do it. The Denver Broncos stand at 2-2 at the quarter pole of the 2026 season.
We've seen some epic comebacks and some alarming developments . Overall, though, the Broncos are in exactly the same position they were in at this time last year.
However, a handful of players have been disappointments thus far. The quarter pole is the first pit stop to look back and get a feel for the trajectory the Broncos are on.
Today, we're doing that by looking at the Broncos' biggest disappointments thus far. Note how many of the names on this list are supposed to this team's best players.
That's disappointing, but it also illustrates how much room there is to improve. The Broncos have faced a tough initial schedule, playing the NFL's four best teams to start the season, and once they break through this guantlet, I expect these players to bounce back big through the resistance training they've received.
I don't want to be too hard on Nix because I'm a firm believer in him as a young quarterback, and I remain confident that he'll bounce back. That said, I'd be lying if I didn't say he's been a disappointment this season.
Like all Broncos fans, I expected to see a Year-3 step forward from Nix, but through four games, he's mostly looked like a hesitant rookie, fearful of pushing the ball downfield, and content to take the checkdowns.
It would seem that Sean Payton is equally concerned. Payton took action entering Week 5's road tilt against the Los Angeles Chargers, stepping back into the play-calling process on game day , though offensive coordinator Davis Webb will still be involved and will be the voice Nix hears in his helmet.
Make no mistake; this move is all about getting Nix out of his funk . Yeah, the Broncos' run game has been non-existent, and the offensive line is giving up an unprecedented pressure rate on Nix, but Payton knows that his team will only go so far as this young quarterback can lead them, and the veteran coach is taking a more hands-on approach to ensuring things get back on track.
Color me optimistic that Nix takes some big steps forward this week against the Chargers. He's never won at SoFi Stadium, and he's yet to defeat Justin Herbert head-to-head, which only means Nix is due.
Dobbins is averaging a career-low in yards per carry (3.5). He's been dinged up with a hip injury, though he hasn't missed a full game.
Whether it's the injury, the play-calling, or the offensive line, Dobbins hasn't looked like the confident, savvy runner we saw for 10 games last season. Payton remains adamant that Dobbins is "important" to what Denver is trying to achieve, but it's time for the veteran back to step it up a notch.
In four games, Dobbins has 46 carries for 161 yards. Six of his carries have moved the chains. Beyond that, though, he's been a dud — and after getting a 4x raise this past offseason, that's not good.
A good game for Sutton used to be nine receptions for 86 yards and maybe a touchdown. Alas, he's yet to score through four games and that stat line serves as his total production for the season thus far.
Suffice it to say, the Pro Bowl receiver has been a disappointment thus far. Sutton's effort has been questionable at times, and the typical my-ball mentality fans came to know and love has been absent from his game.
I attribute this to Nix's struggles and the play-calling issues, but with Payton stepping back in on game days, it's time for Sutton to step it up. I believe he will, as soon as this week .
All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles and All-Pro right guard Quinn Meinerz haven't been enough to sustain the Broncos' offensive line as the NFL's top unit this season. Left guard Ben Powers has been okay, but center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been downright bad.
This unit is allowing career-high pressure on Nix, and it's simply not moving opponents off the block in the run game. The Broncos ranked 29th in rushing for a reason. In just about every measurable way, the Broncos' offensive line has been bad this season.
Bolles isn't blameless, as his penalties have popped up as a consistent liability through four games. With Payton's increased involvement, though, this unit should take a big step forward in the second quarter of the season.
Bonitto has exactly one sack through four games. He's off to the slowest start of his career since becoming a starter in 2024.
Although Bonitto has still found ways to impact the game pressure-wise, he's not been able to get home. It's worth mentioning, though, that he had a big strip-sack erased in Week 2 by a Riley Moss penalty.
I don't know if it's the level of competition Bonitto has faced or the absence of John Franklin-Myers next to him on the defensive line, or Jonathon Cooper opposite him on the edge, but Denver's Pro Bowl rush linebacker needs to amp up his game moving into the next few weeks.
Speaking of disappointments, I have to list Cooper's replacement in the starting lineup. Elliss has been ineffectual as a pass rusher and not much better against the run.
Through four games, Elliss has been held without a sack. I'm sure a big part of the explanation is the tough offensive lines he's faced thus far, but the Broncos thought he was ready to be a starter; they were looking for ways to get him on the field more.
But Elliss has been a big disappointment thus far. If he doesn't improve, it wouldn't surprise me to see Que Robinson start eating into his snaps more, much like he did last week against the San Francisco 49ers.
Singleton has missed a lot of tackles, but he's also made a team-high 47. Early this season, he showed a troubling penchant for picking the wrong lanes to fill in run defense, and his overaggression led to missed tackles and big plays by opponents.
Throw in Singleton's scary-bad coverage, and he's been a disappointment thus far. I know most Broncos fans didn't have super high expectations for the soon-to-be 33-year-old linebacker, but I didn't expect him to look as lost as he has at times.
For what it's worth, though, Singleton turned in an encouraging performance last week agains the San Francisco 49ers, though he allowed all of his targets in coverage to be completed. Perhaps it's a sign that he's moving in the right direction, I don't know. But Denver needs him to pick it up.
I don't want to cast Surtain as a liability. He's been far from it. But he's not been great thus far.
In Week 3, Davante Adams burned Surtain up and down the field like he was a rookie again. Surtain seemed poised to bounce back last week before he suffered a lower-leg injury that saw him exit the game early.
Now, Surtain is expected to miss time and is week-to-week, but when he comes back, the Broncos need him to return to a semblance of his Defensive Player of the Year form.
The only impact Mims has made thus far has been a negative one. After getting injured in the season opener, he missed two straight games, and in his return last week, he lost a fumble, which ended up being the momentum-swinging turning point for the 49ers.
Granted, Mims has been held back by multiple injuries, starting in training camp, but when he's been on the field — which has admittedly been few and far between — we haven't seen the high-impact player we know.
With a little luck from the injury bug, though, hopefully Mims can get his groove back. The Broncos are going to need him with Pat Bryant injured and out for the next few weeks .

title: 5 Bold Broncos Predictions That Could Shock the Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers may be 0-4, but the Denver Broncos haven't fared well against them since Sean Payton became the head coach.
Entering this Week 5 matchup with the Chargers, the Broncos are struggling offensively , lacking explosive plays and failing to establish a run game. Sean Payton decided to step in and take on more of a play-calling role on game day, starting with this game against the Chargers.
Payton clearly understands that the Broncos can't afford to overlook the Chargers and lose their second divisional game of the season.
As we all know, fortune favors the bold. If I'm right about this week's bold predictions, the Broncos will walk out of SoFi Stadium at 3-2. Winning cures all.
At some point, Sutton has to make a major appearance. After four weeks of questionable effort, he has 86 yards on nine catches on 21 targets.
Bo Nix has trusted Sutton as his top target through his first two years. With Pat Bryant out, Sutton needs to find a way to get involved. Jaylen Waddle is getting a lot of attention and is still getting open, so Sutton's excuses are nearly out.
But this is the game for the Pro Bowler. Sutton reminds everyone exactly who he is, and produces 100-plus receiving yards.
Nix has been way too quick to hit the check-downs, especially against the San Francisco 49ers. If he keeps that up, Harvey could be poised for a big game, given the injuries the Chargers are dealing with.
Harvey is coming off his season-high 93 yards from scrimmage against the 49ers. Still, the 49ers were healthy last week, but the Chargers are dealing with multiple injuries to their linebackers and secondary.
Watch for Harvey to have a big game at SoFi.
With Patrick Surtain II likely out , Barron will face heavy pressure to perform. Many have already slapped a bust label on him because his play hasn't been great and he's only played sparingly, so this is a prime opportunity.
Against the Chargers' receivers, Barron doesn't have the best matchup, but he has shown a nose for the ball and can snag a pass and take it to the house, which is exactly what happens on Sunday.
Along with Barron's pick-six, the Broncos will snag another interception as their pass rush harasses Justin Herbert all game. The Chargers' offensive line is, once again, beat up, and Denver should be able to win consistently up front without having to blitz.
The Broncos get home at least four times, with Zach Allen picking up a strip-sack that Denver recovers. This defense is a prideful unit, and it has struggled to be consistent and force negative plays.
The Broncos look to this banged-up Chargers offense to correct the narrative.
The Broncos have typically played to their opponent's level, even against struggling teams. The Broncos have also struggled consistently against the Chargers during the Payton era.
But this year, with Denver at 2-2, the enthusiasm around this team has taken a hit. That's about to change.
The Broncos make a big statement before a short week against the Seattle Seahawks, beating the Chargers by at least 17 points.

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are entering a pivotal matchup ahead of their bye week.
With two divisional opponents looming after the Week 6 bye, the Lions have a chance to build some momentum before their break. They take on the Arizona Cardinals Sunday with a chance to get back over .500 before their week off.
Here are 10 thoughts on the Lions' Week 5 battle with the Arizona Cardinals.
The Lions' secondary has really struggled throughout the early part of the season, with D.J. Reed wearing plenty of criticism because of his slow start. Reed was expected to be the team's top shutdown option, but hasn't lived up to expectations through the start of his tenure dating back to last season.
Against a Cardinals offense with some threats on the outside, Reed has a chance to regain some mojo and quiet his critics. If Reed can be consistent in his coverage on the boundary this week, it could go a long way toward the defense rebuilding some momentum heading into the bye week.
Arizona's Trey McBride is one of the top tight ends in the NFL, and he's enjoyed a solid start to the season. Through four games, McBride leads the Cardinals with 33 catches and is second with 242 receiving yards.
Detroit has struggled to cover tight ends throughout the start of the season, allowing 37 catches for 407 yards and six touchdowns through four games. If Kelvin Sheppard can't find an answer, it could be a long afternoon for the defense yet again.
Jack Campbell signed a four-year contract extension prior to the season with the expectation that he would be an anchor for the defense. However, the linebacker hasn't performed at a high enough level through the first quarter of the season.
Campbell has struggled in coverage and hasn't been as impactful against the run after an All-Pro season last year. He's a big part of the team's weekly gameplan as the defensive play-caller, and needs to find his groove quickly amidst the defense's struggles.
Detroit's defense ranks in the bottom-third of the league in many defensive categories, including last in yards allowed, second-to-last in points allowed and last in passing yards per game. In a passing-oriented league, these stats are troubling for a team with aspirations to compete for a title.
Sheppard has had to endure plenty of criticism with these results, and the pressure is on for him to find answers with the bye week looming.
One potential option could be for the Lions to blitz Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The veteran has struggled against the blitz this year, and starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. is out for the season with an injury.
Detroit also could have help coming in the near future. Brian Branch returned to practice Wednesday , and while it's too soon to say he could be back for the team's matchup with the Cardinals, getting him back after the bye seems to be a safe bet.
The Cardinals invested heavily in their run game this offseason, with the most notable addition being the selection of running back Jeremiyah Love out of Notre Dame. Through his first four games, Love has notched 223 rushing yards and one touchdown.
Detroit's run defense has struggled throughout the start of the season, with the lack of a safety presence being a big part of their issues. While the Cardinals have had a lot of success on perimeter runs, the Lions have struggled to defend them.
As a result, Detroit will need their defensive backs to step up in a big way to eliminate what has been a major statistical disadvantage for them through the first four weeks of the season.
The Lions are 0-2 to start the year in road games, and have lost five of their last six away from Ford Field dating back to last season. They won the season finale last year in Chicago, but had losses to Philadelphia, Los Angeles and Minnesota in their road games before that.
Detroit has played each of their first two road games in primetime, and Sunday's will be at 4:25 in Arizona. As they prepare for a second-straight road game prior to the bye, Campbell's team has a chance to generate some positive mojo after a difficult start on the road.
It will be a homecoming for Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing . The Lions hired him this offseason after he had spent the last three years calling the offense for the Cardinals, so Sunday will be the first time he's visited Arizona as a guest since his tenure ended.
Petzing was part of Jonathon Gannon's coaching staff, who was let go after last season and replaced by Mike LaFleur. In his first game against his former team, Petzing could have some tricks up his sleeve.
For the Lions to enter the bye week on a significant high, they need the defense to shed some of their early struggles and put together a complete performance. In the best-case scenario, the defense generates multiple turnovers and Aidan Hutchinson wreaks havoc.
Meanwhile, the offense capitalizes on their chances and converts takeaways into touchdowns. Goff remains efficient and turnover-free, leading to a dominant victory to enter the bye week on a positive note.
It's hard to say the passing defense could get worse, but with McBride's presence the linebacking corps could get thrashed if the scheme isn't on point. The worst-case scenario would be Brissett having a dominant outing, connecting with McBride for big gains to set up touchdowns.
Offensively, the Lions have been conservative albeit turnover free. In this scenario, the turnover bug finally bites them and leads to another insurmountable deficit despite another late push from Goff and company.
For my Week 5 prediction, I'm rolling with Christian Izien to generate his first takeaway of the season. After missing the season-opener, Izien has proven to be a nice addition for the Lions' defense throughout the last three games.
The former Buccaneer has some versatility, and could find his way into an impactful moment by picking off a pass from Brissett in a pivotal point in Sunday's game.

title: Detroit Lions Rule Out Four Against Cardinals, DT Questionable
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official Friday injury designation report, ahead of the their Week 5 road contest against the Arizona Cardinals.
Four players were officially ruled out, as Brian Branch, Rock Ya-Sin, Ben Bartch and Cade Mays were ruled out.
Tyleik Williams, who was limited at practice at times this week, was ruled questionable.
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked at his media session prior to practice on Friday about the possibility Branch and Mays could suit up this week, given they both participated in practice all throughout the week in a limited capacity.
“It's something to think about. Now they'll be here, but you're right it won't be football," said Campbell. "They won't have other teammates around. We're running plays, all that stuff, but they're going to be here continuing to condition, get ready, as football stuff as they can do without it being that with the training staff. And then let's get them going Green Bay week. Let's get them going and then we'll assess.
Hopefully by midweek, we'll have a pretty good idea. We'd love to get them ready to go versus Green Bay, I think, right as after the bye.”
The former NFL tight end fully expects rookie running back Jeremiyah Love to play this week.
“Totally expect him to play and totally expect him to continue to grow like he has every game that he's been in there. He's explosive," said Campbell. "Yeah, we did work, but we also knew he was going early. But certainly looked at him. He's an explosive, dynamic runner. He's got vision, explosiveness, speed, and he's really good out of the backfield and they've just scratched the surface of that. That hadn't even opened it up yet.
"That's coming. So, we know we have to be ready for him. So yeah, we fully expect him to play and be ready to go and be full tilt.”

title: Behind Enemy Lines: Can Lions Contain Cardinals Rookie Running Back?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking to enter their bye week on a high note.
Ahead of the week off, the Lions are traveling to Arizona to take on the Cardinals, who enter Sunday's game with a 1-3 record.
Reporter Donnie Druin covers the Cardinals for Cardinals OnSI . He recently answered five questions from Lions OnSI to preview Sunday's game.
Donnie Druin: That's the golden question here, especially with multiple starters out and a Lions defense that ranks second in sacks. The good news for Arizona is Jacoby Brissett has one of the league's fastest times to throw in the NFL, so the Cardinals naturally get the ball out quickly. I would anticipate plenty of multi-tight end sets to help chip some of Detroit's pass-rushers in hopes of slowing them down and reaching the passer. For what it's worth, the Cardinals are dead-last in explosive plays and Brissett's average yards per intended pass rank near the bottom of the league — I'm not sure either changes on Sunday.
Druin: Cardinals fans are cautiously confident in hopes of a potential upset against Detroit. Arizona fans have often pointed to the Lions' lack of passing defenses, and from my understanding, things aren't exactly great on Detroit's defensive side of the ball either. This is a fairly big game in the eyes of Cardinals fans, as many view this as a final opportunity for the likes of either Jacoby Brissett or defensive coordinator Nick Rallis before serious moves could be made for their respective spots. Fans view this as a track meet in the waiting, and losing to Drew Petzing would sting a little more than a typical loss given his history here.
Druin: All things considered, very good. Love has dealt with injuries, lack of touches and a poor offensive line through his early stint with the Cardinals — though he still manages to make defenders miss and gives fans a few highlights when the ball's in his hands. Arizona doesn't want to overload the rookie and that's understandable, though he's slowly becoming too good not to be consistently involved in the offense. He hasn't been used a ton in the passing game like many projected, though when his number has called, he's delivered.
Druin: Any chance of Arizona winning this game comes in the form of the Cardinals' offense coming alive — which is very possible. It's early in Mike LaFleur's tenure but there's been flashes of the offensive brilliance that made him desirable for Arizona when they hired him. We've yet to see the team's offense truly come alive, and with Detroit's defense entering this matchup as a liability (much like Arizona's), the Cardinals have potential to put up plenty of points. And for what it's worth, the Cardinals are just outside of the top five in defensive turnovers forced, too.
Druin: I do buy that the scoreboard might be broken when the dust settles at State Farm Stadium, though I have the Lions covering the spread on the road. This could be a really fun matchup, but ultimately I think the Cardinals aren't able to pull off a late-game comeback. Give me: DET 30, AZ 24

title: Detroit Lions Injury Updates: Will Brian Branch Play This Week?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will conduct one final practice, before they head out on the road this weekend to square off against the Arizona Cardinals.
Speaking prior to practice, head coach Dan Campbell addressed if safety Brian Branch had a realstic opportunity to play.
Campbell indicated it would be a tall order for Branch to play this week.
"He's looked good for two days," said Campbell. At end of his media session, he also noted center Cade Mays was unlikely to play this week.
The former second-round pick has been limited in practice all this week, as he continues his rehabilitation from an Achilles injury suffered last season.
Detroit's coaching staff wants the talented safety to secure as many reps as possible, so a debut after the bye week is more realistic.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard expressed earlier this week he is looking forward to using Branch as much as possible, when he is eventually cleared from the medical training staff .
“There we go, bring some life into this deal. There we go. There we go. Listen, I don't even know the word for it. I don't. But I mean, how many positions can he play and how fast? I mean, he's a dynamic player. That is an elite player in this league, which we all know guys. I'm not telling you nothing you don't know," said Sheppard. "That is an elite player in this League. But we also got to do right by the player.
"So, just make sure we pick and choose how much, how soon, where, what's best for him right now and  just kind of take that approach to it because I'm ready for him to go all 78, however many we play," Sheppard added further. "The Saints’ game that was 90? Let's go 90, BB. As much of Brian Branch as I could get right now, I want.”
Detroit's secondary is among the worst in the league, as the defense has been prone to give up too many explosive plays. Top wideouts have been feasting on Detroit's undersized cornerbacks.
Christian Izien and Chuck Clark have tried to stabilize the back end, but the defense is in need of a morale boost.
While it is unlikely Branch will play this week, he could debut soon after the Lions Week 6 bye.
Detroit will begin division play in Week 7 after a week off, as they face the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field.

title: Kelvin Sheppard Needs to Clean Up His Act On and Off Field
full_text:
Just when you thought things couldn't get any worse for Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, they did with his tone-deaf press conference Thursday.
Through the first four weeks of the season, the Lions’ defense has been a complete and utter embarrassment. It not only has allowed the second-most points in the league (31.8/game), but it's also surrendered a league-high 1,695 total yards. That figure is just 21 yards shy of the number of yards allowed by the 0-16 2008 Lions over the season's first four games (1,716).
The defense has repeatedly been unable to make crucial stops, and has failed Dan Campbell's squad time and time again in 2026.
Subsequently, Drew Petzing's offense has had to step up more often than not to save the day for the Lions this season. Without the efficiency of Jared Goff through the air and Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground, Detroit would definitely be an under-.500 team – and maybe even winless – through the first quarter of the season.
Yet, Sheppard doesn't see it that way. He admitted as much Thursday when he was asked about whether the offense has carried his unit thus far this season.
“We have a three-phase team here and I firmly believe that,” he told reporters. “And I'm going to stand strong in that belief. And I think that's ultra disrespectful to my unit to say somebody has to carry us. We're going to do our one-third here. Hell or high water. Point blank, period.”
Whether “disrespectful” or not, it's the absolute truth, Kelvin. It might be a tough pill to swallow, but the reality of the situation is that the defense has been so awful that Goff & Co. have had to carry the Lions so far in 2026.
That is hardly a recipe for success for an NFL team, let alone one with Super Bowl aspirations like the Lions. However, facts are facts, and it's time to start accepting them, Kelvin. You are a large part of the problem, and it's time to start taking accountability.
His stubbornness and arrogance reared their ugly heads even further when he was challenged on his heavy reliance on the blitz against Panthers QB Bryce Young in Week 4.
He dialed up the blitz 12 times against Young & Co., and simply, the calls did not work. Young proceeded to complete seven of eight pass attempts against the blitz. And despite the Panthers passer displaying such proficiency, Sheppard refused to adjust. That was a clear-cut misfire from the second-year coordinator , and it cost Detroit dearly in the primetime affair.
So, Sheppard must have admitted he made a grave mistake, right? Not quite. In fact, he did the polar opposite during his weekly media session and conveyed he'd make the same calls again if given the chance.
“Those calls were the right calls,” Sheppard adamantly stated. “Those calls were the right calls, and I’ll leave it at that.”
They clearly weren't, though. Sheppard had a chance to admit his wrongs, and failed to take the opportunity to do so. It was yet another swing-and-miss from the defensive play-caller and one that showcased a glaring lack of self-awareness.
As a whole, he did very little in the press conference to dissuade the notion that he's unfit for the defensive coordinator job. As a matter of fact, he added to my case, and to the case of many others,  that he's in over his head and should be stripped of his duties.
It's been evident since Week 1, to everyone but Sheppard, that his play-calling is extremely flawed and does not work. And the longer he continues to deny that such is the case, the more irreparable damage it will do to Detroit.
Sheppard, however, doesn't seem interested in changing his tune anytime soon. It's all the more reason why Campbell & Co. can ill-afford to spend another week with him leading the defense.
And Sheppard's disastrous presser Thursday should serve as the final nail in the coffin for his tenure in the Motor City.

title: Detroit Lions Jameson Williams Currently Leads NFL in Drops
full_text:
Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams has five drops through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season, tied for the league lead.
Receivers coach Scottie Montgomery has been coaching the former first-round pick tough, and even went so far as to publicly challenge Williams, after he dropped a couple more passes against Carolina Panthers.
The drops were prevalent in the season-opener against the New Orleans Saints. Last year, Williams recorded 12 drops. No other receiver has more drops in the last 21 regular season games (17).
Since Week 1, Williams has seen his productivity steadily increase. Against the Panthers, he secured six receptions for 102 yards.
Speaking with reporters, Williams expressed he tries to play free and move on, if a play is not made.
"Just catching the ball, bringing it in. It’s nothing major, it’s just drops. I just gotta catch the ball," Willams told local reporters. "It’s a long game. With the drops you still can have an excellent game. My biggest thing is trying to minus those things, so I can just go out there and play free, don’t even worry about dropping the ball. Just focus on doing my job the best I could do."
Montgomery expressed this week a player cannot be great in the NFL if they are up and down on a weekly basis.
Related: Receivers Coach Calls Out Detroit Lions WR Jameson Williams
"In the meeting room, on the field, in walkthrough, he's always on you," Williams said about Detroit's receivers coach. "He never lets you take no days, no plays off. He’s just on us. And that’s what he demands out of us. That’s why our room plays the way we play, because we gotta show how much we respect him and how much he does for us and how grateful we are for having him in our room. He's a great guy, been a great guy to me since he took over the receivers room. I got nothing but love for Scottie."
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing indicated Williams has rebounded nicely following errors out on the field.
Despite a couple of drops, Jared Goff was still able to connect with Williams on a 49-yard reception in Week 4.
"The first thing I'm going to evaluate is effort, assignment, energy, and intensity. And I think he's doing a really nice job. Those are the controllables, how hard you play? Do you know what you're doing? Are you doing it as fast and as hard as you possibly can? And I think he's been great," said Petzing. "And then the physical stuff, those are little things that I think, 'Hey, you get 10 plays, I'd love to make all 10.' Sometimes you do, sometimes you don't. You can't let it affect your psyche. And I think he's done a nice job of that."
Williams still sees himself as a big part of the offense and continues to play a big role in the run game, as he and Amon-Ra St. Brown block well for Jahmyr Gibbs.
"He's bounced back and made some really big plays for us. I laugh at the in cut that I think he got his hands on. When that ball got thrown, I'm like, most of the league doesn't even touch that ball. So, he's the type of guy who has the ability to go up and get that," said Petzing. "It's a play I expect him to make, he expects to make. But I also, when it went out, I was like, ‘Woah.’ So, you’ve got to live with a little bit of that. He wants to be challenged in that area, but I do.
"I'm pleased with where he is at and I'm always going to say, 'Hey, can you give us more? Can you make more plays? Can you have a bigger role?' And I think he wants that.”

title: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Arizona Cardinals in Week 5
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions will take on a reeling Arizona Cardinals team which has lost three consecutive games .
After knocking off the L.A. Chargers in Week 1, they have suffered defeats at the hands of the Seattle Seahawks, the San Francisco 49ers and most recently, the N.Y. Giants. And in each of those contests, they've allowed at least 31 points, including 36 points in back-to-back weeks.
So, much like the Lions, it has been far from an optimal start to the season for the Cardinals’ defense.
In fact, while the Lions rank second-to-last in points allowed per game (31.8/game), Arizona ranks 29th (29.3/game).
The Cardinals are led on defense by eight-time Pro Bowler Budda Baker. Baker, an impact safety and two-time first-team All-Pro, is coming off a solid performance against the Giants in which he recorded an interception, two passes defensed and five total tackles.
Detroit offensive coordinator Drew Petzing will certainly have to account for Baker in his gameplan for the week.
Meanwhile, on the offensive side of the ball for Arizona, there is plenty of untapped potential.
Sure, the Cardinals are only presently averaging 21.8 points a game. Yet, offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett's unit features multiple playmakers, including running back Jeremiyah Love, tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Michael Wilson.
Love is dealing with an ankle issue, but is still expected to play in the Week 5 contest. Meanwhile, McBride and Wilson are the go-to targets in the desert for veteran signal-caller Jacoby Brissett.
And there is definitely a chance the aforementioned pass-catchers erupt for big games against Detroit's injury-depleted secondary . Wilson, for one, is coming off two straight performances with a stat line of at least seven catches and 89 yards. He and McBride will unquestionably be big-time tests for the Lions’ cornerbacks group, led by D.J. Reed.
Reed has had a mediocre start to the 2026 campaign. He's earned a 59.3 overall grade from Pro Football Focus , including a PFF coverage mark of 57.5 (57th among 103 qualified cornerbacks).
All in all, Dan Campbell's squad should be able to escape Arizona with a much-needed win. Yet, it won't be easy.
Subsequently, at this present juncture, I'm only willing to give the Lions a 53 percent chance to secure the Week 5 win.

title: Detroit Lions Sign Former Washington Commanders DT to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a practice squad roster decision that should help add depth to the defensive line.
According to multiple reports, former Washington Commanders defensive tackle Jeffrey M'Ba has been inked to Detroit's practice squad.
Since he was designated in the league's International Pathways Program, he is the 17th member of the practice squad.
M'Ba, 27, is a 6-foot-6 defensive tackle who played collegiately at Independence, Auburn, Purdue, and SMU.
He went undrafted in 2026, but was able to land with the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent. M'Ba did not make the Commanders initial 53-man roster coming out of training camp, but returned on their practice squad.
After being cut, M'Ba quickly found his way to Detroit. Tyleik Williams is currently dealing with a foot injury, so added depth could be warranted moving forward at practice.
A native of Libreville, Gabon, he recorded 42 tackles (16 solo), five sacks and 7.5 tackles for loss in his final season with the Mustangs.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard acknowledged the solid play of the defensive line against the Carolina Panthers.
Detroit's defensive line was able to record three sacks and regularly pressured Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.
Unfortunately, the linebackers unit and secondary were not executing at a high level.
"I told them and I told the D-line, 'It's a disservice what we've been doing to you all.' I truly feel like this is the best D-line we've had in my six-year tenure here since I got here in 2021," said Sheppaed. "And we haven't been complementing it well enough on the backend to see the benefits of it and be outright beneficiaries is what they should be with what the D-line is doing, especially Sunday night . They assaulted the pocket all night. They generated pressure all night on the quarterback.
"But as you saw, the quarterback was able to get the ball out with the quick release and get it completed far too many times. So, there are things we've corrected, there are things we've talked about going into another tall task this week against Arizona and (Cardinals Head Coach Mike) LaFleur coming from the LA Rams."

title: Detroit Lions Week 5 Thursday Injury Report: DT Returns to Practice
full_text:
The Detroit Lions continued their preparation for the Arizona Cardinals with a Thursday afternoon practice at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
Defensive tackle Tyleik Williams, who missed the first practice of the week with a foot injury, returned to the playing field. He was considered day-to-day with a foot injury suffered last week.
He expressed following practice that he suffered a bruised foot and feels he should be good to suit up on Sunday afternoon.
Those not spotted, during the period open to local reporters to observe, included offensive guard Ben Bartch and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard shared prior to practice that he did not just want to just provide lip service to address the key issues. The biggest issue facing the defense is the work being done at practice has not translated well to the field.
"So, I get up here and I recap the game before, and I'm going to do the same. But what I'm not going to do is get up here and read off a stat sheet, a stat column, tell you about how we've got to bridge communication, how we've got to do this and that," Sheppard said. "Because at this point, all of it's lip service. Until it starts to show on Sunday, until the evidence starts to show up at the game, it's lip service. What we do here, bridging it to the game, it sounds good, but it's lip service."
Additional Insider Analysis: Cardinals Have Talent, But Lions Can Exploit These Holes
The former NFL linebacker acknowledged the game against the Panthers did not meet the standards and there needed to evidence of change starting to be showcase out on the playing field.
"What I will say is we did not play well enough defensively to help this team win that football game Sunday night at Carolina," said Sheppard. "There were a lot of things in there that we absolutely didn't like that we turned on the tape as a unit on Monday, hashed out, talked about, and the same thing I told them, it's lip service. So there has to be real change. It has to be real evidence of change.
"Whether that's personnel driven, whether that's some things come out, whatever the case is, something has to change."

title: Detroit Lions Receivers Coach Calls Out Jameson Williams
full_text:
Detroit Lion s receivers coach Scottie Montgomery raised eyebrows this week, when he publicly called out Jameson Williams.
The former first-round pick had multiple drops against the Carolina Panthers, including a deep pass early in the game that he should have hauled in.
He was able to finish Week 4 with six receptions for 102 yards, including a 49-yard catch from Jared Goff.
Montgomery expressed Williams needs to refocus in order to become a player that can secure receptions when he is wide-open or in contested situations.
“Every target he had in that game should've been a catch. If it hits you, you gotta catch it," Montgomery told local reporters earlier this week. "You can’t be boom or bust in this league. That is average. We gotta get him completely refocused on making wide-open catches and contested catches."
In training camp this summer, Williams was able to demonstrate improved pass-catching, but it has not translated into the regular season. In the season-opener, Williams had numerous drops against the New Orleans Saints.
Against Carolina, Williams supposedly lost the football in the lights, which resulted in the early drop.
“Yeah, that's a tracking issue. You can lose it in the lights, but when it comes out of the lights, you've got to find it and catch it. Catch the dark spot. We have to make that play. It gives us the ability to go to the next level, and consistency, in every play, is what we really have to work on.”
Williams has regularly stated he wants to be considered among the best in the league, but has fallen short of that standard this season.
"We have to get him completely refocused on making wide-open catches, contested catches. He's doing great in the run game," Montgomery said. "He's doing some things that we really like to see , but we're talking about greatness. We're not just chasing, hey, man, he’s a good player in this league.
"I want him to be among the best, and I think that he has the opportunity to do that if we can clean up some of the things that you're talking about.”

title: Here’s Why Pierre Strong Could Secure Critical Role for Packers vs. Bears
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Following Sunday’s victory at Tampa Bay, Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur was irritated for multiple reasons.
At or near the top of the list were two fumbles in a span of four plays by running backs MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. Lloyd’s fumble dribbled out of bounds. Johnson’s fumble at the goal line was recovered by the Buccaneers. Without the fumble, the Packers might have won comfortably; because of the fumble, they barely beat a winless team with an undrafted rookie quarterback making his NFL debut.
“I think a great teacher’s the bench,” LaFleur said after the game. “If guys don’t start holding onto the ball, they’re going to be sitting on the bench.”
For Sunday’s game against the Chicago Bears, Chris Brooks – who started against the Buccaneers – is out with an ankle injury . In his place will be Pierre Strong, who was promoted from the practice squad on Thursday .
Only LaFleur knows the plan for how he’ll handle the backfield on Sunday. Maybe Lloyd and Johnson will carry the load, with Strong in reserve and playing on special teams. That’s typically what would happen with a player pulled up from the practice squad. Heck, that’s what happened with Strong last season. He was elevated three times for gamedays but didn’t play in any of the games.
On the other hand, if LaFleur was truly serious about using the bench as a teacher, maybe Strong will have a key role against the Bears.
Even now, with his season and Packers debut a couple days away, he’s the team’s most accomplished running back. A fourth-round pick by the Patriots in 2022, he played in 46 games from 2022 through 2024 and had a combined 125 rushes and catches. So, this isn’t some rookie. There should be a trust factor based on his play in the preseason.
“Yeah, P’s done a great job ever since he’s gotten here,” LaFleur said on Friday. “He helps on special teams, as well. I think he’s a natural runner. He’s got experience. He’s been in this league a while now, although he has limited I would say game action. If given the opportunity, I think he’ll be ready to go.”
It’s been a long time since Strong played in a game. He carried the ball five times for the Browns in the final game of the 2024 season. He didn’t make their roster in 2025 and landed on Green Bay’s practice squad, where he spent the entire season.
“Man, I could just thank the Lord,” he said after practice. “Like you said, it was a while but God’s timing is better than everybody’s timing. I’m here now so got to continue to get better.”
As the saying goes, you don’t have to get ready if you stay ready. That’s Strong. He was one of the primary ball-carriers throughout training camp and the preseason. He fell short of a roster spot, though, after the Packers traded for Johnson, but he re-signed to the practice squad.
“Yeah, I come to practice every day ready, training like I’m going to play on Sundays because, being on P-squad, you never really know,” he said. “Last year, I got called up sometimes on Saturdays. On P-squad, you’ve always got to be prepared and be ready to work because that’s your job – being prepared.”
As is typically the case, one man’s pain is another man’s gain. He was excited when told on Thursday that he was going to be promoted to the active roster rather than just elevated from the practice squad.
“Man, it was surreal when I got the call,” he said. “We had just got out of practice. I wasn’t expecting anything. Like I said, I come to work every day practicing like I’m going to play on Sundays. Yeah, man, I’m just happy, man. Grateful, but it’s just getting started. Like I got the call, now I got to stay here.”
Strong gave a glimpse of what he can do in the preseason. He’s got excellent vision, a knack for finding cutback lanes and the speed to take advantage. He had a long kickoff return at Denver in the preseason. While he might not be in the running to return kicks on Sunday, he did have 17 tackles in the kicking game in three seasons – the first of which was in New England alongside Packers special teams coordinator Cam Achord.
So, what will bring to the party against Chicago?
“Man, everything a back can do. Passing, blocking, running,” he said. “Whatever play is called I’m going to execute play by play. Just bring everything I can to win this game.”
Green Bay’s running game could use a jolt. It ranks last in the NFL in rushing yards per game and 31st in rushing yards per carry. The team’s leading rusher, Lloyd, is averaging 2.7 yards per carry. Johnson is averaging 4.0 yards per carry but has fumbled twice.
So, nobody has solidified his role, meaning Strong has a golden opportunity to go from the practice squad to a vital part of the offense.
“We’ll leave that with the coaches,” he said. “We all good backs. We all great backs. We all can take one to the house any given day. So, I’m just going to leave that to the coaches. Whenever my number’s called, I’m going to be ready.”
But what if he gets rolling?
“If I get rolling, I’m rolling,” he said.
You get what you pay for, as the saying goes. Usually. But not always. The NFL salary cap is $301.2 million. A huge percentage of the Packers' allotment will on the sideline vs. Chicago through, for the most part, no fault of anyone.⬇️ https://t.co/XDjeQj5k1B
