title: Jaguars Get Much-Needed Defensive Back News in Latest Week 5 Injury Report
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- While the Jacksonville Jaguars' injury report did not decrease in size on Thursday, they did get some good news.
The Jaguars had safety Eric Murray upgraded from non-participant in Wednesday's practice to limited participation on Thursday. That is a sign of progress as Murray goes through the NFL's concussion protocol, and it does now seem as if there is a chance the Jaguars could have the veteran safety on the field on Sunday vs. the Philadelphia Eagles.
Murray was injured in Week 4's win over the Cincinnati Bengals and missed a good chunk of the second-half, which led to the Jaguars needing to lean on second-year safety Rayuan Lane since Caleb Ransaw was also injured. With Murray's status improving Thursday, it appears the Jaguars might be able to see their secondary be a bit closer to full-strength against the Eagles.
“Eric means a lot to us. Eric is one of the guys you would kind of put him in a classification of he's a coach on the field," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "You guys probably know that from being at practice. He's just really good communicator, knows the ins and outs of the defense and can kind of see problems before they start on the field. He's been great that way all the way through, the entire season last season, the beginning of this season."
Murray is a critical part of the Jaguars' secondary considering he and Jourdan Lewis are amongst the unit's elder statesmen. If the Jaguars do not have Murray on the field, they will likely have to lean on Lane once again, in addition to third-round rookie Jalen Huskey. The Jaguars had Antonio Johnson step in when Murray missed time last year, but Johnson is now a starter.
"Other guys, if they have to step up and do that, I have total confidence that they will, because we've really got a good bunch of communicators back there," Campanile said. "And that's one of the things we're always looking for at that position. A guy who has position flexibility, one. And then two, smart guys,  guys that love to play, that love to learn and obviously, know the ins and outs of all the calls, learn football.”
The list of other limited Jaguars was the same as Wednesday's injury report: offensive tackle Cole Van Lanen (knee), cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring), Jarrian Jones (foot), Jaylon Jones (hamstring), and Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), offensive tackle Anton Harrison (elbow), defensive tackle Davon Hamilton (foot), and defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (groin) were listed as limited.
The Jaguars had two players as full participants for the second day in a row after they had previously been limited throughout the season in running back LeQuint Allen (hip) and wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb).
The Jaguars should have most of these players available in Week 5 against the Eagles in London, though Brown is one player whose status might not be known until much closer to game time on Sunday.

title: 3 Key Areas Jaguars Have an Advantage Over Eagles: Trevor Lawrence and Jalen Hurts
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will need to be at their very best in Week 5 if they want to keep their winning ways going.
The Jaguars have been able to take advantages of mismatches against opponents in recent weeks, especially in Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. But what advantages should the Jaguars attack when it comes to Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles? We break it down below.
This is the one area where I think the Jaguars have a distinct edge over the Eagles. I have believed for a few years now that Trevor Lawrence is the more talented passer than Jalen Hurts, and we have now seen the talent around each passer change enough since then for it to start becoming clearer and clearer. Since Lawrence got the best play-caller of his career in Liam Coen and an improved supporting cast, he has been playing a different sport than Hurts.
As things stand today, Lawrence is No. 8 amongst qualifying quarterbacks in EPA/Play and No. 4 in success rate. Meanwhile, Hurts ranks No. 24 and No. 28 respectively. Hurts has dealt with a bad hand in terms of injuries, but he is coming off several stinkers in a row, while Lawrence just keeps building momentum. For the fifth week in a row, the Jaguars should be entering Sunday with the better quarterback.
The Jaguars' skill players are a major reason they are 3-1right now. The Jaguars have seen all five of their top pass-catchers (Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange, Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Cameron) make big plays, while Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. have led the way for the rushing attack. Compare that to an Eagles offense that is a bit broken right now, and the Jaguars have a big advantage.
While the Jaguars are dealing with some injuries defensively, none of their top-seven skill players have missed practice time this week with injuries. Meanwhile, the Eagles are dealing with injuries to Devonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Dallas Goedert, and Dontayvion Wicks. The Eagles' playmakers are banged up right now, while the Jaguars' are healthy and ready to produce right away.
Week 5 will be a Green Bay Packers reunion of sorts when the Jaguars' defense share the field with the Eagles' offense. In 2024, Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile was the Packers inside linebackers coach/run game coordinator, while Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was an offensive assistant. Fast forward two seasons, and both coaches are now coordinators who are set to play a game of chess against each other.
“Sean's a great football coach. Great guy," Campanile said Wednesday. "I thought he was an extremely hard worker. We were both in there late hours a lot, he's one of the guys you'd see in there. You know what I mean? He's no stranger to hard work. I think he is a really good football coach, super detailed, really bright. Obviously, anybody that's played quarterback that long in the NFL, you have a really good knowledge of the game, and I think he brings that to the offense.”
For as much mutual respect that there is here, though, it is clear that Campanile's unit has the edge. Both coaches are working through some penalties on their respective sides of the football, but Campanile has his unit absolutely humming right now, while Mannion and the Eagles' offense can barely get into neutral. The Jaguars' defense ranks No. 7 in EPA/Play right now despite giving up plenty of yards, and that is due to their ability to force turnovers and prevent points. Meanwhile, the Eagles' offense ranks No. 29 in EPA/Play and No. 30 in success rate.

title: 5 Winners, 4 Losers From Jaguars' First Month of the Season: Rookie and Veteran Risers
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have had quite the first month.
For 14 of the 16 quarters of the season, the Jaguars have been a dominant team that has pushed the opposing teams around. Take away the second half against the Broncos, and there are not many teams better than the Jaguars right now.
But which Jaguars have been the most impressive during the first month of the season? We break it down below with this week's winners and losers.
It is hard to think of many bigger winners than Bhayshul Tuten. According to NextGenInsights, Tuten has reached 15+ mph on 19 of his 60 rushes this season, the most of any player. Nearly half of Tuten's rushing yards (49.9%) have come after a missed tackle this season, the highest share of any player (min. 25 rushes). In short, he is creating a ton of explosive plays and generating his own yards. This is something the Jaguars stressed that they needed from the running back position all offseason, and Tuten has given it to them. He has produced big plays all season long, and he should be only getting better.
Everyone expected Travis Hunter to be a stellar cornerback , but this quickly? Hunter already has become one of the top cornerbacks in football after just playing a month of cornerback full-time. He has already taken massive steps compared to last season, too. According to NextGenStats, Hunter has played 175 defensive snaps through four games this season, already more than his total as a rookie in 2025 (154), while playing 16 offensive snaps after 305 last season. Hunter has aligned as the field cornerback on 74.9% of his defensive snaps this season, up from 44.2% in 2025, and logged a career-high 58 coverage snaps against the Bengals in Week 4.
Emmanuel Pregnon has played every single snap for the Jaguars this season, not something easy to do for a rookie joining a team that went 13-4. Pregnon has had his ups and downs, as any rookie offensive lineman will have, but he has stood out each week with his run-blocking ability. Pregnon has been the Jaguars' most impactful rookie to date, and he is the future at the guard position for the Jaguars moving forward.
There were plenty of questions the Jaguars had to face at the linebacker position this offseason, but Ventrell Miller has helped answer all of them. After losing former All-Pro linebacker Devin Lloyd in free agency, the Jaguars had Miller step into the full-time starting linebacker role for the first time in his career, and he has thrived. He has been one of the NFL's best linebackers against the run (if not the very best) and he has been an impactful blitzer. He has made himself some money this season.
6th round rookies do not often make big impacts on winning teams. It is even more uncommon when that rookie plays the position the team is the strongest at, but that is where the Jaguars are with Josh Cameron. The Baylor product has certified himself as the team's No. 4 receiver, caught two touchdowns in four games, and has turned every single one of his catches into a first-down or a touchdown. He has become a home run Day 3 pick very, very quickly.
Brian Thomas Jr. clearly has a ton of talent and value to the Jaguars' offense, but the lack of production through the first month is jarring. He is averaging a little over 25 yards a game, has only seen a heavy dose of targets in one game, and looks more like a piece of the equation on offense than he looks like a true X-Factor for how they attack each week. Thomas is a good player; too good for just over 100 yards through four weeks.
With Caleb Ransaw placed on injured reserve earlier this week, he is now set to miss 21 of his first 25 possible games in the NFL. He did some good things for the Jaguars at the start of the season, especially as a tackler, but he will now be sidelined for at least a month, if not longer. Ransaw has had some really tough breaks at the start of his NFL career, especially considering how excited the Jaguars were about him as a prospect when they drafted him.
Patrick Mekari did not play in the first four games due to the back injury that landed him on injured reverse, and it does not look like there is much reason for the Jaguars to introduce him back into the starting lineup when he is healthy. Pregnon has played well at left guard for a rookie, and Ezra Cleveland has done enough at the right guard spot for the Jaguars to not muddy up the waters. Mekari has of course done nothing wrong, but the Jaguars do not need guard help, which means he is likely an expensive backup once he returns.
While Travis Hunter has been stellar at cornerback, he has been mostly forgotten on the offensive side of the ball. That makes sense for where the Jaguars are with cornerback injuries and with Hunter's high level of play at cornerback, but nobody could say that Hunter having one catch for eight yards through four games was expected. Hunter is playing great football, but it has been mostly one-sided. That does not take away from his value to the team, but it does change expectations.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars' London Battle vs. Eagles: Trevor Lawrence Keeps Finding Endzone
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the Jacksonville Jaguars to improve to 4-1, they will have to get over the hump against a Philadelphia Eagles team that has had the Jaguars' number in recent years.
The Eagles, of course, are a different team now than when the Jaguars lost road games to them in 2022 and 2024. The Eagles were powerhouses then, while this year's 2-2 Eagles squad seems like it is coming apart at the seams.
“I know that just because you think about—when you're playing an opponent, you naturally just think about the prior games that you've played against them," Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said Wednesday.
"So yeah, I've thought about that I haven’t beat these guys, and they've had some really good teams and we've had some close ones that we've lost. So just excited for another opportunity, because it's the next game though, not because of all that. Like I said last week, I'm like a broken record with you guys. You prepare every week to go win the game regardless of who it is. You don't want to win it more because it's someone in particular. Yeah, we got to put together a good plan.”
So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 5 battle with the Eagles playing out? We break it down below.
Trevor Lawrence, for my money, has been the Jaguars' MVP through the first four games of the season. The Jaguars' franchise passer is playing the best football of his career from an accuracy and decision-making standard, and he has put several wow throws on tape in every single game this season. The Eagles have a great defensive scheme and some good players on that side of the ball even with injuries, so they are no pushover.
With that said, I think Lawrence has a stellar day vs. the Eagles that sees him score four touchdowns: three through the air and one on the ground. Over the Jaguars’ last 12 games (Since Week 11 of 2025), Lawrence has completed 225-of-348 passes (64.7%) for 2,852 yards, 27 touchdowns and a passer rating of 107.6 to pair with 221 yards and five scores on the ground. His 32 total scores lead the NFL over that span, and I think he picks up several more this week. This feels like the type of game that Lawrence could take over from the first drive, and it would be a big step to see him continue his momentum.
The Eagles certainly are facing a lot of changes across the offensive line, plus they are down to their third- and fourth-string running backs. Better running games have tried and failed to get something going against the Jaguars on the ground, but each have failed since the start of the 2025 season; I do not see the Eagles offense in its current form being the offense that flips that script. As a result, I think the Jaguars have another stellar performance against the run.
Last week, the Jaguars held the Bengals to 23 rushing yards, the fourth fewest allowed in franchise history in a single game. The Jaguars have gone 21 straight games not allowing a 75-yard rusher, the fourth longest such streak in the last 50 seasons. The Eagles simply are undermanned when it comes to facing an elite Jaguars' run defense.
The surest sign that things are going a bit wayward for the Eagles is the fact that even the tush push is getting stopped lately. The Eagles got stuffed on a key tush push rep against the Los Angeles Rams last week, and I think the Jaguars are well-equipped to stop the most efficient and effective play in football thanks to their strength in the middle of the defense with their front and linebackers Ventrell Miller and Foyesade Oluokun.
The Rams stop the tush push‼️ 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/7siNXhy8D4
I think the Eagles will go to the well a few times against the Jaguars considering that play is like comfort food to them and, right now, they need something they can rely on. But I also think the Jaguars' run defense is made to stop such efforts, and I think the Jaguars get a few wins against the play Sunday.
The Jaguars have simply had a knack for forcing takeaways under Liam Coen and Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars have three red-zone takeaways in 2026 as well, the most in the NFL. No other team has recorded more than one, while the Jaguars have scored an NFL-leading 38 points off taekaways. They force takeaways and they produce once they get the ball, and I think that happens again this week.
With the way the Eagles offense has taken to their new scheme and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, and with the injuries they are facing across the board, I think this is bound to be a mistake-filled day from Philadelphia's unit and Jalen Hurts. Jacksonville has 13 multiple-takeaway games dating back to Week 1 of last season, and I see No. 14 coming on Sunday.
Arik Armstead was outstanding for the Jaguars in Week 4, and now he will get a chance to do so again with the Eagles on the dockett. The Eagles' days of having a truly elite offensive line seem to be gone, and the departures of Lane Johnson and Cam Jurgens this week, along with GOAT-level offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland this offseason, will play a big role in that. Add in Armstead's momentum, and I think this will be a big week for Armstead.
I would assume the Eagles, like most teams facing the Jaguars, will ditch the run early and proceed to throw a lot of passes. This will give Armstead enough reps against a new-look offensive line that I think he cashes in and records his first two-sack game as a Jaguar. He has heated up with 10 pressures over the last two weeks, and I think he cashes in vs, the Eagles.

title: Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams Star in a Bright Future for the Chiefs' Cornerback Room
full_text:
It was a bit of a surprise when the Kansas City Chiefs traded up to obtain the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, then even more of a surprise when they used that selection on LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane . Immediately, Delane rightfully had sky-high expectations as the new face of the Chiefs' secondary.
Delane was limited throughout the majority of training camp due to a shoulder injury and then played just three snaps (including an interception of Bo Nix) in Weeks 1 and 2 due to an issue with the same shoulder. Even with just two full games under his belt, Delane looks to be worth that draft selection, and he's not alone as a rising star in Kansas City's overhauled cornerback room.
As any Chiefs or Los Angeles Rams fan knows by now, the Chiefs traded away cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Rams this offseason, and Jaylen Watson reunited with McDuffie after leaving for LA in free agency. That left a significant void for the Chiefs to fill at corner.
To begin 2026, veteran cornerback Kristian Fulton was entering the second year of his two-year deal with the Chiefs after a disappointing 2025, and '25 third-round draft pick Nohl Williams was looking to follow his promising rookie campaign with a more consistent workload in his sophomore season.
Delane, Williams and Fulton all hit the ground running .
Highest graded CBs in man coverage this season Mansoor Delane         93.8 Kristian Fulton             92.8 Nohl Williams               91.8 Trent McDuffie            90.9 Travis Hunter               90.3 pic.twitter.com/4Tv5R4kLLU
Delane has been excellent , even when asked to take on difficult coverage responsibilities, as he was asked to do at times against Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. He's also been a missile in run defense, playing with speed and physicality that fits Steve Spagnuolo's defense perfectly.
Mansoor Delane with one of the GREATEST two-play sequences you’ll see from a rook. Registers a TFL on Ashton Jeanty, and follows it up with CLAMPING Brock Bowers. The Chiefs rookie CB NEUTRALIZING some of the NFL’s top weapons 😳🔒 pic.twitter.com/oHzd3YU6qM
Delane has the fifth-highest overall cornerback grade from Pro Football Focus through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, while Fulton lands at No. 11. Williams appears at No. 41 in overall PFF grading but lands at No. 23 with his coverage grade alone.
good player this Mansoor Delane https://t.co/HNmzmM6Pbj pic.twitter.com/XPGheGgX3M
The one area of concern in the Chiefs' cornerback room comes in the slot, where veteran L'Jarius Sneed has provided some value and some tough snaps in his second act with the team. Sneed has the second-worst PFF grade among qualifying cornerbacks (No. 102 of 103), but he's been a positive force against the run and as a blitzer.
Sneed began the season in excellent fashion against the Denver Broncos in Week 1 before being routinely bested by Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs in Week 2. I'll argue that it's a bit too early (and a bit unnecessary) to rush to end the Sneed-reclaimation experiment, but he's certainly struggled more than the team's trio of outside corners to begin the year.
I'd be interested to see Delane get a bit of work in the slot if that would enable Williams and Fulton to hold the outside corner roles in nickel packages, but I'd also understand some hesitance, as Delane's potential value is probably highest as a shutdown outside corner, and he's still acclimating to the NFL game (though you wouldn't know that if you only watched him play).
What other options could the Chiefs have?
Rookie defensive back Jadon Canady was a healthy scratch in Week 4 as safety Chamarri Conner returned to the lineup, while slot corner Kader Kohou remains on the practice squad, so neither Canady nor Kohou seem particularly close to challenging Sneed for those slot corner reps. Versatile DB Chris Roland-Wallace took a season-high 29 defensive snaps against the Raiders, but Sneed has taken more than 72% of the defensive snaps in every game so far this season.
Ultimately, the Chiefs' slot corner position will require more monitoring (and, ideally, better play) in the weeks to come, but the Delane/Williams outside duo—with room for cameos from Fulton this season—appears to be one of the NFL's most promising young pairings.

title: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker Welcomes Potential Tyreek Hill Reunion in Kansas City
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 4-0 start heading into the bye, the front office is actively looking to bolster the roster. Kansas City will likely be without wide receiver Tyquan Thornton for the remainder of the regular season and could miss wide receiver Rashee Rice for some time as well.
KC has been linked to several wideouts, but the most obvious addition could come in the form of a reunion with Tyreek Hill . The speedster is coming off a dislocated knee last season and could make his return to the NFL with the team he started his career with. Rumors have been swirling between Hill and the Chiefs for quite some time. It's the worst-kept secret that Kansas City is showing interest in the 32-year-old. Recently, one of the AFC's biggest stars revealed his thoughts on Hill potentially returning to play for Andy Reid.
In an interview with Yahoo Sports on behalf of Orgain, running back Kenneth Walker III was asked what he thought about Hill potentially rejoining the Chiefs. The NFL's leading rusher is all for bringing "Cheetah" back.
"I've seen his speed. Everybody knows Tyreek Hill is just straight speed, and he's just an athlete in general," Walker said. "And just watching him over the years, I'm like, 'He's one of the best players that really played.' So, it's cool to see that. I think it's cool and it would be a great addition to our team."
Through the first four games of his Chiefs tenure, Walker has truly been an MVP candidate . He's currently sitting at 537 rushing yards with six total touchdowns. Chiefs fans knew he was talented when he signed with the franchise in March, but no one could have expected this level of production.
Part of the reason why Walker believes a reunion with Hill would work, as he later explained in the interview, is that it would make the Chiefs' offense more versatile. Between Patrick Mahomes' arm talent, Walker's dynamic running style , and Hill as a downfield threat, opposing defenses would have a difficult time containing those three players at once. While the backfield is set in Kansas City, the wide receiving corps is far less certain. The aforementioned injuries to Rice and Thornton will hinder KC, leaving the team with Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen, Nikko Remigio, and a potential practice squad elevation for next week's group of wideouts.
There's more at play than Brett Veach simply signing him to a cheap one-year contract, though. Hill is currently battling a civil assault and battery trial in court and has a pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation from the NFL. The Chiefs are already starting to look at other options, including former Chief champion Justin Watson .
Hill is coming off a devastating injury himself and hasn't played in an NFL game in over a year, but he's only two seasons removed from leading the league in receiving yards. If he's even 80% of his old self, he'd be a tremendous help to this offense, and Walker's comments reflect that.

title: Reported Chiefs Interest in WR Reunion Underscores a Harsh Reality
full_text:
Although the Kansas City Chiefs are on a bye week, many folks are still talking about the lone undefeated team left in the AFC. Some of that is for good reason, but there's also a glaring hole on the roster that needs to be addressed at some point.
With wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffering a dislocated ankle in Week 4's win over the Las Vegas Raiders, it'd likely behoove general manager Brett Veach to add another pass catcher. The only issue is that the in-season talent pool doesn't contain many quality options, leaving the franchise in a tough spot.
The most recent bit of Chiefs-related wideout news sums that up pretty perfectly. According to Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star , Veach and Co. are "among several teams" interested in free agent Justin Watson.
The Chiefs are among several teams interested in WR Justin Watson, per source. Watson played for Kansas City from 2022-24 and is a three-time Super Bowl champion, having beaten the Chiefs with the Bucs before being part of their back-to-back title teams.
Watson being the latest name tied to KC emphasizes just how dried up the market is. Barring a trade that would almost surely cost NFL Draft capital, he's right in the thick of the tier of players the team could be vying for. Does a reunion with the three-time Super Bowl champ make any sense? Let's break it down.
They oftentimes come off as buzz phrases in Chiefs circles, but they do matter to the organization and come in handy given the timing of any potential signing once the season's rolling. Veteran experience, familiarity with the scheme, attention to detail, alignment versatility and more all carry significance. Watson checks each and every box there.
Now in his age-30 campaign, Watson has 1,716 regular-season offensive snaps under his belt as a member of the Chiefs and over 500 spanning five other years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans. Thinking from a Thornton-esque perspective regarding the operation of the offense, the former fifth-round pick also possesses proven chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes on vertical passing concepts.
Watson carried a 17.2-yard average depth of target in Kansas City from 2022-2024. He averaged 13.9 yards before the catch per reception and owned an 89.8 passer rating when targeted. According to Pro Football Focus , Watson spent between 63.9% and 68.8% of his time lined up out wide over his three Chiefs seasons. Thornton was at 62.5% in 2025 and is at 70.9% in 2026.
It also doesn't hurt that Watson is a bigger-bodied player than most of the current Chiefs receiver room (6-foot-2, 215 pounds), is a willing and (mostly) capable blocker and can play special teams. Things like that stand out to the coaching staff and front office, for better or worse.
Simply put, Watson just wasn't a very good player during his time with the Chiefs. According to SumerSports , his 50.94% catch rate ranked sixth among all Kansas City wideouts in 2023. The following year, he owned an 0.72 yards per route run figure that was dead last in the group and trailed sixth-place Marquez Valdes-Scantling (0.89) by a decent margin.
The advanced data not being in Watson's favor doesn't stop there. NFL Pro pegs him as posting a -9.8% catch rate over expected in 2022, then a -1.3% mark in 2023 before it spiked to +6.0% in his final Kansas City season. He was worth 17.2 EPA in the latter campaign, but that can't be a reliable expectation baseline for the current year.
Other factors must also be considered, even with Thornton set to miss most or all of this season . What's the latest with Tyreek Hill? The Chiefs have been linked to him at every step over the last few weeks, although his ongoing legal situation muddies those waters quite a bit. Would a Watson addition put that potential acquisition on ice?
What about costing players like second-year man Jalen Royals and rookie Cyrus Allen developmental reps? Is Watson that much better than either option at this stage in his career? So many moving pieces make this far from a no-brainer of a decision.
Now on the wrong side of the aging curve, it's fair to question what Watson has left in the tank. His Texans tenure was virtually silent, but it's also not like he forgot how to function in a Kansas City-style offense after the end of the 2024-25 campaign. As long as there's still some speed, he can execute the same type of role he used to have.
If the Chiefs did sign Watson, this writer doesn't believe head coach Andy Reid and company would be quite as compelled to put him on the field as often as a JuJu Smith-Schuster. Additionally, Watson doesn't carry any off-the-field baggage and isn't recovering from a major injury, so he'd be a more immediate plug-and-play (and keep in the lineup) fit than someone like Hill.
At the end of the day, Watson might just be a more appropriate Thornton replacement than multiple internal options or free agent avenues. Even if he isn't a clear-cut needle-mover, it may not hurt to bring him in and see what he's got as a part-time player. An emphasis should be placed on the part, though, coming with the understanding that the double champion with the Chiefs wouldn't be saving the receiver room.
Again, that's an unfortunate reminder of where things are at. Help could be on the way while still not solving the current problem to the optimal degree.

title: The Chiefs' Pass Rush Has Room to Improve, But It's Probably Been Better Than You Think
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs haven't recorded a sack in three games. At face value, that's an alarming statistic that paints a grim picture of the team's pass rush. After a longer look, there are plenty of reasons to be optimistic that the team's defensive line will be able to put it all together after the bye week.
Using this week off to take a longer look at a few key position groups that will determine where the Chiefs go in the next act of the season, Kansas City's D-line has some work to do, but they have been better than their box score indicates.
First, find the Chiefs in this chart of key pass rush stats. (There's a lot of information for all 32 teams, so we'll break down the important parts next.) Surface-level, what do you see?
Key pass rush stats: pic.twitter.com/uq0LEa6pEK
There's a whole lot of green (which is good) throughout the Chiefs' row, with two dark purple (bad) cells. Why?
In that chart, the Chiefs are No. 6 in the NFL in pressure rate, No. 8 in quick pressure rate, No. 13 in non-blitz pressure rate and No. 8 in average time to pressure. Those are the numbers of a top-10 pass rush unit! Then, the purple boxes.
The Chiefs are No. 31 in sack rate (2.5%) and dead last, No. 32, in pressure-to-sack ratio (5.7%). The KC D-line is creating pressure at a top-10 rate, but they've been one of the worst-finishing teams on those opportunities. Ultimately, I think that paints a relatively positive picture of the pass rush, and it certainly beats the alternative.
Those numbers are supported by other individual stats, like the fact that George Karlaftis was credited with a whopping seven quarterback hits against Kirk Cousins by Pro Football Focus ( a performance supported by a longer look at the film ), giving him a total of 12 quarterback hits this season , despite getting zero sacks out of those hits.
Most QB hits this season, via @PFF George Karlaftis - 12 Greg Rousseau - 12 Dallas Turner - 9 Cameron Thomas - 9 Maxx Crosby - 9 Resulting Sacks Greg Rousseau - 6 Dallas Turner - 6 Maxx Crosby - 3 Cameron Thomas - 2 George Karlaftis - 0 pic.twitter.com/CdsAVfNdmt
Regarding the other defensive ends, rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas has also flashed far beyond his one sack would suggest , while former first-round pick Felix Anudike-Uzomah (lined up over the center in the clip below) has had some of his best reps as a pro throughout the start of this season.
The way R Mason Thomas can accelerate towards the QB is just nuts. pic.twitter.com/ZsjpPTFvY6
Even second-year third-round pick Ashton Gillotte's season benefits from a deep dive into more advanced metrics, as Gillotte's "DIPRA" (defensive impact per rush attempt) is 10th-best in the league through four weeks.
The defensive tackles, particularly superstar veteran Chris Jones and first-round rookie Peter Woods, haven't had a series of game-wrecking moments so far this season, but Woods has shown tremendous physical tools , and Jones has been on the injury report with a calf issue to begin the year. I'm still very optimistic about Woods, and I'll wait a few more weeks before I'm willing to worry about Jones in his age-32 season.
Defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga has been a positive force against the run, and second-year lineman Omarr Norman-Lott is still on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list due to his ongoing recovery from last season's torn ACL.
Yes, the Chiefs' pass rush still needs to turn pressures and hits into sacks, but they appear to have the players to get to the quarterback; that's a much better problem than the issues they had last season.

title: How Does the Chiefs' Wide Receiver Room Stack Up at the Bye?
full_text:
On Sunday in Las Vegas, the Kansas City Chiefs' offense felt like it was hitting its stride, particularly in the deep passing game. Explosive plays had returned both on the ground and through the air, giving the Chiefs multiple ways to burn opposing defenses. Then, on one of those deep completions, wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a serious ankle injury, ending Thornton's two-touchdown, 111-yard day on a somber, season-threatening note.
For now, the Chiefs will at least be without Thornton for the foreseeable future , while Rashee Rice also exited the Raiders game with a tweaked hamstring. Even if the Chiefs do complete the much-speculated reunion with Tyreek Hill , he reportedly wouldn't be ready to return to the field until November . So, how will the offense adjust in the meantime?
Every *catchable* target for Worthy through 4 weeks. *Two route-pass location miscues not included, plus final pass vs LV + Best in open space & on the move (crossers and crossers) - 15/19 balls were caught against the body, double underhand - Rarely working back to the ball pic.twitter.com/d5x7D51rCf
Even as fan sentiment regarding third-year first-round wide receiver Xavier Worthy has shifted from excitement to frustration, the 23-year-old speedster is still the Chiefs' best chance to create explosive plays from the wide receiver position .
Yes, he's had his struggles with the deep ball. No, he hasn't yet found a way to turn his record-breaking speed into consistent NFL production. Yes, he still has a skillset that doesn't exist elsewhere on the roster (or many places throughout the NFL).
Worthy has already consistently been the Chiefs' most-used wide receiver by snap count (now at 80% of the offensive reps through four games), and the Chiefs' coaching staff has the benefit of an extra week to review Worthy's strengths and weaknesses while retooling the receiver room. For better or for worse, Worthy is even more important to the Chiefs now than he was before the season began.
Cyrus Allen target on third down.. like the idea of using him on possible M2M reps. Go get the DE’s hands down on a quick pass tho. pic.twitter.com/3Jbg3cqvkC
Elsewhere, Kansas City has no choice but to bring at least one of their most recent wide receiver draft picks into the fold. Second-year fourth-round pick Jalen Royals has played 60 offensive snaps through four games, with 38 of those reps coming in Vegas. Royals didn't take an offensive snap in Week 1 and has just three catches on the season, but he has been the team's No. 4 receiver so far.
Rookie fifth-round pick Cyrus Allen was the recipient of a massive amount of training camp hype , but he's taken only 10 snaps so far in the regular season —fewer offensive reps than defensive tackle/occasional fullback Khyiris Tonga.
Even with Allen's preseason hype, it always made more sense for him to be a late-season climber after he becomes more familiar with the offense and as the coaches and quarterback develop more trust in him. Now, however, the once-long runway could be shortening. If the Chiefs truly believe in Allen's skillset, the Chiefs' thinning receiver room needs playmakers wherever they can be found.

title: Will the Chiefs' Offensive Line Stabilize After the Bye Week?
full_text:
In some instances, an early Week 5 bye could be an unwelcome arrival for an NFL team, particularly for an undefeated squad with the type of momentum that only comes with four consecutive wins. For the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs, however, it might be exactly the right time for the sake of their uncertain offensive line.
While we use this bye week to evaluate a few key position groups for the current No. 1 seed in the AFC, you may not expect too much concern for the only unbeaten team in the conference.
Still, offensive line uncertainty has been one of the defining storylines of the Chiefs' strong start. How will the group come together after the bye week? That's the team's biggest issue to solve before they host the Los Angeles Chargers on October 18.
Starting left tackle Josh Simmons has missed the first four games of the season with a bulging disc, an injury the team only publicly defined on September 30 . Starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched for the Chiefs' Week 4 showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly due to a " coaching decision ."
Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has held up at left tackle in Simmons' absence, while veteran backup Mike Caliendo got the left guard reps in Las Vegas. Right tackle Jaylon Moore has had his ups and downs, leaving an interesting question for the Chiefs to answer— Benson or Moore at right tackle? —when Simmons returns.
Even All-Pro center Creed Humphrey has had some issues to begin the year, tossing some bad snaps and starting the year on pace to have career-low grades from Pro Football Focus .
To be fair, across an array of offensive line metrics , evaluation of the Chiefs' performance varies —a frequent phenomenon due to the variety of often-subjective ways O-lines are evaluated . Still, with such uncertainty at left tackle, it's seemed apparent that the unit has not yet fully gelled to be as solid as the sum of its parts.
Pass block grade of offensive linemen in true pass sets only Mahomes/Trevor good What happened to the Broncos' OL?? pic.twitter.com/DQCqy3lTpE
The Chiefs bolstered their depth on the O-line just before roster cutdowns, trading for veteran lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the New York Giants and undrafted rookie tackle Diego Pounds from the Baltimore Ravens.
Ezeudu has taken five offensive snaps for the Chiefs, while Pounds has been inactive through the Chiefs' first four games. Pounds remains an intriguing developmental tackle prospect, but his future on the field appears to be some time away. Ezeudu is on a one-year deal and provides short-term versatility at guard or tackle, though either Benson or Moore would clearly be the team's backup swing tackle when Simmons returns.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Assessing the Landscape at Bye Week
full_text:
Somehow, we're simultaneously about a month through the 2026 NFL season already but still have several months to go before we truly find out who some teams are. Don't get it twisted — multiple pretenders have already managed to stand out, but the cream of the crop won't be made obvious for quite some time.
Sitting at 4-0 on the year, the Kansas City Chiefs' hope is for them to be categorized as the latter once the postseason rolls around. That'll take continued impact from general manager Brett Veach's rookie and sophomore classes, which have presented both positive and negative value to this point.
At the bye week, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott isn't included due to him currently being on the physically unable to perform list .
There's no derailing the Nohl Williams hype train, even after an afternoon and evening in which the second-year cornerback got flagged for a pair of costly penalties . He remains a promising young building block in the secondary, forming a two-man show with rookie Mansoor Delane that could terrorize opposing offenses for years to come.
Second-round pick R Mason Thomas has bounced back from some rough moments in the last couple of weeks, flashing rare bend and quickness as a pass rusher on the outside. According to Pro Football Focus , he set a new career high with five Week 4 pressures. Late first-rounder Peter Woods may have just turned in his worst performance to date, although the interior lineman was also reportedly banged up at some point in the contest.
The real X-factor here might be Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson. While he earned a respectable 16 offensive snaps on Sunday, he only got one touch. Perhaps if Kenneth Walker III's workload dwindles a bit coming out of the bye, the Nebraska product will get his time to shine .
With left tackle Josh Simmons still working his way through a back injury , the Kahlil Benson roller coaster keeps on running in Kansas City. His level of play has undoubtedly slipped, but he was surprisingly fine in Week 4 considering he had a fill-in next to him at left guard and, per TruMedia , the Chiefs trailed only the Houston Texans in throws relative to the sticks on average.
An ankle dislocation for wideout Tyquan Thornton might just earn sophomore Jalen Royals some more snaps, but only if an external acquisition isn't made and the coaching staff deems the former Utah State standout worthy of the reps. Another member of the 2025 NFL Draft class, defensive end Ashton Gillotte has received more than a 40% workload share in three consecutive weeks and had a season-high three quarterback hurries in his last performance.
Bryson Eason , as promised, finds himself getting bumped up after being activated for the second week in a row. He could just as easily come back down given the restrictions capping him at three practice squad elevations per season. For now, he's worth keeping an eye on.
The only people who truly know when Simmons is coming back seem to be Simmons himself and those within the building at 1 Arrowhead Drive. Heck, there may not even be a solidified plan. Kansas City certainly hasn't done itself many favors with how it's handled the injury situation to one of its more polarizing youngsters, but all it'd take is a post-bye return for just about everyone to probably sweep that under the rug.
Late-round draft selection Cyrus Allen was the flavor of the summer in Chiefs circles; the Thornton injury will bring that buzz back around for the fall. Elsewhere on offense, tight end Jake Briningstool is still an occasional sighting on the field. Running back Brashard Smith is a special-teamer through and through . Barring injury, cornerback Jadon Canady is stuck in the same boat.
This is where things get a little interesting. Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa isn't in the huddle much on defense, but could forcing a fumble on special teams be the launching pad he needs for an increased overall role? Undrafted free agent Xavier Nwankpa helped seal the deal against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 by picking off a pass on his only defensive snap. It doesn't get much more efficient than that.
Nothing much to see here, truthfully. Both tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn have made routine appearances on the game-day inactives list in recent weeks. Seventh-round quarterback Garrett Nussmeier always carries an outside shot to get on the field, although it'd take a catastrophic stretch of injuries to both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields for that to happen as the emergency third signal-caller.

title: Kenneth Walker Has Been Incredible, But Emmett Johnson's Time May Be Coming Soon
full_text:
Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has been one of the best players in all of football and is firmly on track to be in the Offensive Player of the Year conversation in his first campaign with the Chiefs.
The only downside of Walker's 2026 so far? He's taken a whopping 99 touches through four games, putting him on pace for 420 touches this season. During his four years with the Seattle Seahawks, Walker recorded 255, 248, 199 and 252 regular season touches, respectively. It's still a compliment to note that Walker has been too dominant to take off the field, but with a long-term view of the Chiefs' season, another back will need to spell Walker at some point.
During the Chiefs' bye week, we'll be taking a closer look at a few key position groups to see how they've stacked up to preseason expectations and where they could improve after the bye. However, for the Chiefs' running backs, "improvement" seems almost impossible.
Walker has been darn near perfect through four games, and his impact on the Chiefs' offense has been remarkably evident. From his ability to be the "easy button" for Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes to his home run-hitting ability out of the backfield , Walker has exceeded even the most optimistic offseason expectations. Now, can the Chiefs keep Walker fresh enough to stay that consistent late into the year?
Outside of Kansas City, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson may be flying under the radar. He has 16 carries for 56 yards and five catches for 74—not quite enough to be added in most fantasy football leagues. However, Johnson's highlights have been about as impressive as anyone's.
Emmett Johnson has some MOVES 😮‍💨 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/yEWu90SL7G
Even while currently standing in Walker's shadow, I'm confident that Johnson would have been the best running back in KC's 2025 backfield, and probably by a large margin.
Emmett Johnson is 1 of 5 RBs with 10+ missed tackles forced (MTFs) The 4 other RBs have 40+ touches each. Emmett Johnson has 10 MTFs on just 14 touches. Absurd.
Through four games, Walker has taken 75% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps (196) while Johnson has taken 26% (69). That's the 13th-most offensive snaps on the team for Johnson, and his role should only grow from there.
As long as Johnson is trusted by the coaching staff—and if he wasn't, I don't think the team would have parted ways with Emari Demercado during roster cuts—his workload should increase during the Chiefs' midseason grind as the team tries to spare Walker from a few hits while trying to keep him in top form for a postseason run similar to what he did for the Seahawks en route to his Super Bowl MVP award in February.
Even without significant statistical output so far, Johnson is dynamic enough that Walker can leave the field without allowing opposing defenses to let their guard down on the running game.
The only potential "negative" for the Chiefs' running back room so far would come in the evaluation of second-year seventh-round pick Brashard Smith. (Even then, "negative" is probably too strong.) Smith has taken only six offensive snaps this season, catching one pass but taking zero carries.
The optimistic case for Smith is that he's firmly behind one superstar back and one extremely promising rookie. On the other hand, Smith saw the field sparingly last season, recording just 44 carries (with 26 coming in the team's two games against the Las Vegas Raiders) in 2025. Smith's speed is still a unique enough trait that he should be worth keeping an eye on as the season unfolds, but he's more of a special teamer and injury insurance until further notice.

title: Three Things Andy Reid and the Chiefs Need to Correct Going Into the Bye
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are one of two NFL teams on bye this week, giving Andy Reid's group some additional rest after its strong 4-0 start. KC could certainly use the break after its grueling rivalry win over the Raiders this past Sunday.
While the Chiefs don't have a blemish on their record yet, there's always room for improvement. Certain aspects on both sides of the ball could be cleaned up as the squad gears up for a 13-week stretch without another break. Let's take a look at three things Kansas City needs to improve upon during the bye.
The biggest storyline for the Chiefs offense this year has been Kenneth Walker III , who's been better than anyone could have imagined in his first year donning the red and gold. He leads the league in rushing yards early on and is a serious candidate for AFC Offensive Player of the Year.
However, another encouraging factor is how Patrick Mahomes looks in his return from ACL surgery. He looks every bit like the Hall of Fame signal-caller he was before his rocky 2025 campaign. Mahomes will really get put to the test over the next few weeks as Kansas City's wide receiving corps battles injuries. Breakout candidate Tyquan Thornton ended his career day versus the Raiders in heartbreaking fashion , dislocating his ankle and potentially missing the remainder of the regular season. Earlier in the contest, WR1 Rashee Rice also exited with a hamstring strain that could sideline him for some time.
Thornton was one of Kansas City's two downfield threats, which means Xavier Worthy will have to step up in his absence. The third-year wideout has been shaky thus far but recorded a season-high 71 yards last game, including a 41-yard catch that could have gone for a touchdown had Mahomes not slightly underthrown the ball.
⏰⏰ @XavierWorthy https://t.co/bBmZo8b23u
Regardless of whether Rice's hamstring is long-term, Kansas City's deep passing attack will face a major challenge without Thornton in the mix. Walker's emergence on the ground could help open things up downfield with Eric Bieniemy's increased usage of play action.
I want to preface this by saying the pass rush came alive in the second half against Vegas. The defensive front finally started to generate pressure after halftime, which ultimately contributed to Kansas City's late stops. With that being said, the defensive line needs to see tangible results sooner rather than later. The Chiefs have yet to log a sack since the opening victory over Denver, going more than 190 minutes without getting to the opposing quarterback.
Despite having the immobile Kirk Cousins wrapped up multiple times this past weekend, the pass rush still failed to capitalize on its opportunities. George Karlaftis was the star of the show as he finished with 11 quarterback pressures, tied for the most in a game all year, yet even his fourth-quarter sack was wiped away by a penalty.
Simply put, KC needs more from pass rushers like Chris Jones, Felix Anudike-Uzomah, and rookie R Mason Thomas. Finishing with a goose egg in the sack column every week isn't a sustainable formula for success.
As if the Chiefs needed any more drama along the offensive line this year with Josh Simmons' bulging disc in his back, another issue surfaced on the left side of the trenches before Sunday's victory. Kingsley Suamataia was unexpectedly benched at left guard for Mike Caliendo due to a "coaching decision" which Coach Reid refused to clarify in his postgame presser.
Andy Reid addressing the benching of Kingsley Suamataia.  “That is between Kingsley and I.”
Entering the bye, there are now two spots on Mahomes' blind side that are completely uncertain heading into Week 6. That's obviously not ideal for your superstar quarterback who underwent a grueling rehab process this offseason.
Mahomes took a lot of rough hits from the Raiders' front four, and Chiefs fans surely don't want to envision another scenario where something goes awry with his lower body. Things won't get any easier when Kansas City faces a dominant edge-rusher duo in Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu next weekend. There have to be corrections made in the film room during this extended rest period. And obviously, having one of Simmons and/or Suamataia back on the field wouldn't hurt.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Would a Tyreek Hill Reunion Be Good or Bad for the 2026 Chiefs?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are undefeated heading into their early Week 5 bye, but the team has issues to solve on both sides of the ball, particularly after the loss of Tyquan Thornton .
How will the Chiefs manage the wide receiver position? That's where we'll begin in this week's Chiefs On SI mailbag , where we take your questions from @chiefs_kcsn on Twitter/X and @jbbrisco.com on Bluesky .
Would a Tyreek Hill reunion help or hurt this team? We all know how long it takes new WRs to learn the system. - @dandykstra.bsky.social
Unsurprisingly, most of this week's questions revolved around the possibility of a reunion between the Chiefs and wide receiver Tyreek Hill.
I say this as someone who was lukewarm on the idea of a Hill reunion this offseason: I don't see the downside at this point.
Even if Thornton returns late in the year , the Chiefs need more speed at receiver right now. Perhaps Rashee Rice is able to return from his hamstring injury after the bye, but Rice would be leading a receiver room with Xavier Worthy and a pair of unknowns. Second-year receiver Jalen Royals has played 60 offensive snaps through four games, while rookie Cyrus Allen has played 10. Special teamer Nikko Remigio hasn't taken an offensive snap yet this season.
The point about "new" wide receivers is another vote in Hill's favor. Sure, it's been years since he was last in Kansas City, but he'd return as a player familiar with Andy Reid's offense and Patrick Mahomes' passes. I think he would have a much shorter ramp-up period than most of the other receiver names being tossed around as potential trade targets.
Tyquan Thornton is the first WR Mahomes has had deep ball chemistry with since 2021. How big of an issue is it if Worthy suddenly has to be the deep ball guy again? I'm concerned Kenneth Walker will now get more and more attention week after week (plus wear/tear), and we could have a diminished ability to make teams pay for it. - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
The closing worry in this question does give me a bit of concern. Kenneth Walker's outrageous impact on the offense is multiplied by the way it should force defenses to respect Kansas City's run game, while the rejuvenated explosive passing game can keep defenses from devoting all of their attention to Walker. The explosive plays must continue for the Chiefs, and that's one reason I think the Hill reunion makes so much sense.
Worthy was always on track to have a large role in this offense, but I do think the Thornton injury is the official end of any possibility that Worthy will be phased into a significantly smaller role. However the Chiefs try to utilize him now, Worthy will need to have his best year yet for the Chiefs' offense to remain as explosive as it's been through the first four weeks.
What is most to blame for the lack of a pass rush? Drafting? Chris Jones (age/contract)? Young guys still learning? - @lmackshry5
I think there are a few good answers to this question, and none of them should be particularly alarming just yet.
This defense was always going to have its fair share of growing pains this season; Peter Woods and R Mason Thomas have played roughly half of the team's defensive snaps in the first four games of their young careers. Thomas has stood out in a hugely positive way with his explosion off the edge, but I do think it's fair to acknowledge that he will continue to grow as the season goes on.
Chris Jones has been a bit underwhelming to start the year, but he's been demanding plenty of attention from opposing offenses while remaining on the injury report with a calf ailment. I'm holding off on a significant judgment on Jones until later in the year—perhaps the bye week also arrives at a good time for him.
No sacks in three weeks is certainly not ideal, but I think the pass rush has been a bit better than their box score indicates. I still expect growth from the unit later in the season, but if it stagnates at this level, it would put even more pressure on the Chiefs' secondary down the stretch.
What are the biggest impediments to a perfect season as of this moment? - @hokius.fromthehawkseye.com
Football. Football itself is the biggest impediment. I haven't even seriously considered the possibility that the Chiefs (or 49ers or Vikings) will go undefeated this season. I don't think the Colts are particularly good, and the Chiefs squeaked by them in overtime in a primetime game at Arrowhead.
Kansas City will go to the Seahawks and Broncos in Weeks 7 and 8, then later go on the road for the Bills, Rams and Bengals before hosting the Patriots and 49ers in late November through December. The highest mark of regular season success the Chiefs should be shooting for is the No. 1 seed in the AFC. The sport is too inherently wild and parity-filled for me to imagine anyone going 17-0 anytime soon.
How many games does a Chiefs team made up of 53 Khyiris Tonga clones win? Is there a player on the Chiefs you could clone that would win more? - @SirHunkzAlot
This is an incredible question, and one that I've actually considered before. Khyiris Tonga is a fun nominee, but I think speed is too important in this exercise. Even at age 37, six or seven Travis Kelces could probably block long enough for quarterback-Kelce to find pass-catching-Kelce down the field. Kenneth Walker might be the best answer, but we've now seen rookie Emmett Johnson make plays on offense and on special teams; either of those running backs could create some havoc... but I'm not sure any of those iterations are winning any games against a proper 53-man squad.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Chargers' Week 5 Matchup vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are not dead yet, but their 2026 season is barely breathing. Justin Herbert and the Chargers showed that they still have fight left in them in the second half of their week four battle in Seattle against the Seahawks. There is a path forward for them to save their season but it all starts against the Denver Broncos at SoFi Stadium.
Los Angeles has been off to a rough start to 2026. Expectations entering the season were sky high and their struggles on the offensive side of the ball have been shocking to everyone around the NFL. If the Chargers have any hope of saving their season, it starts with the offense finding its identity.
Entering into the week five matchup against the Denver Broncos, the Chargers are dealing with a substantial amount of injuries and nearly their entire starting offensive line is out. As they try to fight to stay alive in 2026, let's dive into some of the key storylines of this game that I will be closely watching on game day.
The Los Angeles Chargers lost three out five starting offensive linemen in week four against the Seahawks and left guard Trevor Penning was already the fifth option at left guard looking back to training camp. The Chargers hope to activate Branson Taylor from injured reserve for this game but even if he returns to the lineup, they will still be sending out at least two rookies and potentially up to four to face the Denver Broncos.
The lack of experience and time on task will absolutely affect the play calling and available play calls for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. A limited play sheet may be the best-case scenario for the offense to catch their breath and find a groove. The Chargers started moving the ball against the Seahawks in the second half of week four by keeping it relatively simple.
The Broncos run defense is giving up 4.1 yards per carry and are second to last in the NFL in defensive epa against the run. The Chargers enter Sunday down multiple receivers on top of the offensive line injuries, establishing the run is an absolute must for Mike McDaniel.
If the Chargers can establish the run, it will help the inexperienced offensive line face a very good front seven from the Broncos but it should also open up the play action passing attack and help Tre' Harris and whichever receiver is left available to play. Mike McDaniel has to nail the game plan to help out this offensive line.
The Chargers offensive weapons in the passing game outside of Ladd McConkey have been inconsistent. Harris and Johnston both came up clutch in the comeback attempt against Seattle and someone needs to carry that energy and momentum forward.
Johnston and Brenen Thompson are already ruled out for this week and McConkey may not play either which leaves Harris, Marquez Valdez-Scantling and Derius Davis as the only healthy receivers. Practice squad call ups for Greg Jennings and Theo Wease Jr are likely and tight end Oronde Gadsden should be involved as well.
The Chargers are leading the NFL in false start penalties and have consistently shot themselves in the foot with negative plays from either penalties or just from negative results. Mike McDaniel has not yet dramatically altered his play calling to adjust to the struggles. The offensive line that will be trotting out his Sunday should force his hand.
The Chargers will be facing the Broncos missing a significant chunk of their starting lineup and even if some of them play through injuries, they will have had limited to no practice all week. Complex plays and curveball snap counts should be dialed back.

title: Devastating Chargers Injury Updates Ask the Question: What Are They Even Doing?

And this came on the heels of Jim Harbaugh admitting that, part of the reason his 0-4 team looks so unprepared, is that because they mishandled the training camp and preseason work.
That mishandling aimed at potentially keeping the roster healthy hasn’t even worked, either.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Tre' Harris, Keaton Mitchell Among Players Who Could Shine in Week 5
full_text:
Week 5 brings some interesting choices for fantasy managers when it comes to the Los Angeles Chargers playmakers.
With the Denver Broncos up next, managers will need to think carefully about which players have the best opportunity to deliver and which ones could leave them disappointed.
Tre’ Harris is an intriguing option for fantasy managers looking for a receiver who could provide value beyond the more familiar names in the offense.
His physical playing style gives him the ability to compete for contested catches, and an opportunity to earn a larger share of the passing game could make him an interesting choice against Denver.
Harris is still developing his role, so expecting a massive performance would be premature. However, managers in deeper leagues may find him worth a look. Especially if the offense creates more opportunities for him to get involved. His potential makes him a player to watch as the season progresses.
Keaton Mitchell brings an explosive element to the running game that makes him an appealing fantasy option. His speed allows him to create opportunities that might not be available to a more traditional running back. The former Ravens running back has gotten a surprise amount of playing time. Splitting carries with Omarion Hamptoin who is the main starter.
Mitchell received the most carries he’s seen all season with 10. He also has the ability to receive which is crucial for managers wanting an all around back.
#Chargers Week 4 RB Usage - Keaton Mitchell: 38% snaps, 10 carries, 13 routes, 6 targets (63 yds) - Kimani Vidal: 37% snaps, 5 carries, 14 routes, 3 targets (36 yds, TD) - Omarion Hampton: 32% snaps, 9 carries, 9 routes, 2 targets (53 yds, TD) Absolute nightmare for fantasy
Oronde Gadsden is a name fantasy managers should keep in mind when evaluating their options at tight end. His athletic ability gives the offense another way to create mismatches, and his potential as a pass catcher makes him an interesting option.
With Njoku and Kolar out for multiple games, Gadsden is a week-to-week flex option. He will always have upside when these two are gone, based on the fact that he is now the starter.
Justin Herbert is talented enough to make almost any matchup interesting, but fantasy managers should still consider the circumstances before automatically placing him in their starting lineup. Denver presents a challenging opponent, and if the passing game struggles to find its rhythm, Herbert could have a harder time reaching the production managers expect from him.
According to CBS Sports, Herbert has yet to reach a game above 14 points. The key is less turnovers and more redzone opportunities that are cashed in.
Managers who have another quarterback performing consistently well should compare their options before making a final decision. Herbert is not someone to dismiss entirely, but this matchup deserves careful consideration.
Justin Herbert's stats on deep passes this season, per @PFF : • 2 for 10 • 3 INTs • 9.2 passer rating pic.twitter.com/BkYAmx76bO
Omarion Hampton has the talent to become a valuable fantasy running back, but his weekly production depends on how effectively he can turn his opportunities into yardage.
When a running back’s workload is difficult to predict, it becomes harder for fantasy managers to trust him in a starting role. Hampton has the physical tools to make an impact, yet Mitchell and Vidal getting more reps each game makes him harder to trust.
With a physical matchup ahead and less reps, Hampton could be staring down a rough performance fantasy wise.
Quentin Johnston has the ability to make explosive plays, but that does not always translate into dependable fantasy production. His value can fluctuate depending on how frequently he gets targeted and whether he can turn those opportunities into meaningful yardage.
For fantasy managers, that inconsistency can make him a difficult player to trust when a safer option is available. Johnston remains capable of delivering a strong performance, particularly if he connects on a big play, but relying on that outcome carries risk. You should evaluate the other receivers on your roster before committing to him, especially if you need a dependable floor rather than a high-variance performance.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Rumors Finally Loop in Chargers, Jim Harbaugh
full_text:
Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers feel like perhaps the most obvious sell candidate at the upcoming NFL trade deadline.
Harbaugh’s Chargers have fully faceplanted over the first month of the season and have yet to win a game. Historically and statistically speaking, the season is over.
Naturally, this means looking at the Chargers as sellers. The Mike McDaniel experiment was a flop and Harbaugh and his coaching staff sit on hot seats.
With aging veterans like Khalil Mack, Denzel Perryman and even Derwin James, one could see why contenders around the NFL might give the Chargers a ring about a trade or two before the deadline.
Whether the Chargers actually want to play ball on trades is another story, though, with some around the NFL finally commenting on the situation.
The Chargers don’t usually go wild with trade deadline moves under Joe Hortiz. Last year, though, they went and got Odafe Oweh to boost the defense. That was a time of need, though, whereas this year is a disaster.
According to Fox Sports’ Eric Williams , one NFL executive said this week that there’s no expectation that the Chargers will trade away assets at the deadline.
Williams spoke with someone else who went into the why of things.
"Harbaugh has been fairly loyal to players he’s helped acquire, and I don’t think the personnel department is any different," one scout told Williams. "[Khalil] Mack just needs to retire after the season. Quentin showed inconsistent hands coming out and similar vibes to why Mike Williams wasn’t a long-term player, either.”
Sort of a weird one from the scout there. If Mack needs to retire, he might want a shot at a Super Bowl somewhere first, right?
Regardless, another executive told Ralph Vacchiano that things could certainly go the other direction, calling the Chargers the team “the most likely team to pull the plug” if things keep going poorly.
We’ll see if Hortiz and the Chargers want to build for the future if they’re sitting on an 0-6 mark by the bye, or even 0-8. And if that’s the case, the do right by the players reputation for Harbaugh could very well mean trading away some guys like Mack to a contender.
Either way, this certainly won’t be the last time the Chargers come up in NFL trade deadline rumors now that the ball is rolling on a lost season.

title: Chargers and Jim Harbaugh Each Receive Unflattering Review at NFL Quarter Pole
full_text:
These are trying times for head coach Jim Harbaugh and the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers. And this Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium, the team will try, try again for its first victory of the season. Sean Payton’s Denver Broncos will be in town, and both of these clubs are coming off road losses to NFC West teams.
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off Thursday night at AT&T Stadium as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first victory of the season by knocking off the Dallas Cowboys, 24-16. Earlier this week, Mike Jones of The Athletic had plenty of thoughts on the first four weeks of the season. And Harbaugh and the Chargers were the subject of two topics.
THE SEAHAWKS DEFENSE FORCES THE GAME-WINNING FUMBLE 😤 Former Charger Uchenna Nwosu gets to Justin Herbert and gets the strip sack 💪 Seattle moves to 3-1 while Los Angeles falls to 0-4. pic.twitter.com/8T8dj0Ilel
When it came to the biggest disappointment of the NFL’s 107th campaign, the Bolts got the nod. “Winless through four weeks,” explained Jones, “ the Chargers look completely lost and in no shape to contend for a third straight playoff berth under Jim Harbaugh. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel should have helped quarterback Justin Herbert reach another level while arming him with a highly creative attack. Instead, Herbert appears to have regressed, and it’s hard to find a bright spot on that side of the ball.”
The Chargers’ offense has produced just seven touchdowns in four games, and only three teams in the league have scored fewer points (67). Herbert has been sacked 12 times, thrown six interceptions lost one of his four fumbles. But the disappointing showing by the team this year has not been all of the offense.
“Los Angeles’ defense has played nearly as poorly,” added Jones. “Rather than finally getting over the first-round playoff hump, the Chargers could hit the reset button once again this offseason, if not sooner.”
But wait, there’s more. According to Jones, Harbaugh has turned in the season’s worst coaching job after four weeks of action. “As noted above, McDaniel isn’t solely responsible for Los Angeles’ struggles. The Chargers have hampered their efforts by committing 38 penalties (4th-most) and turning the ball over 10 times (tied for the league high). After each disjointed performance, Harbaugh and his players appear equally miffed over their struggles.”
There’s a chance this week for the Chargers to snap their seven-game overall losing streak—which dates back to last season and includes the 16-3 playoff loss to the Patriots—by knocking off the up-and-down Broncos at SoFi Stadium this weekend for the third straight year. They last faced Payton’s team in Week 18 at Denver last season and Harbaugh sat Herbert and other starters in a 19-3 loss.
It’s been a disastrous season to date for a team that has reached the playoffs each of the past two seasons, and there have been very few positives to date. Of course, this remains a “never-say-never” NFL these days.

title: Justin Herbert is in Trouble: Non-Chargers Fans Wouldn’t Be Able to Name 1 Starting OL
full_text:
Pray for Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. Cross the fingers. Whatever. Just send the guy some good luck and vibes.
The Chargers enter Week 5 with an injury report 18 players long . One of those is starting star offensive tackle Joe Alt, who is out at least one week with a new injury. The other starting tackle? Rashawn Slater was spotted on crutches after a loss one week ago.
Just fire up the trade candidates talk already, really.

title: Chargers Week 5 Mailbag: Hypothetical Path Forward, Seats Getting Warm, Future Focus
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4 and their roster has been brutalized by injuries. The Chargers personnel have been hot and cold with their performances and how they are grading out on gameday. They host the Denver Broncos at home in week five as they look for their first win and look to find any hope moving forward.
Fans and the media have clearly started the process of looking forward for the Chargers with the odds stacked against them for the remainder of the 2026. Trade scenarios are already being floated for Chargers star players and seats may be getting warm on the Chargers' sideline. This week's mailbag focuses on some of those forward looking hypothetical scenarios.
From JH^3 (@777onlinegamer on X): Two part question looking to the future. 1) Assuming the Chargers miss the playoffs and Jim Harbaugh is back but current struggles continue, what's the best path forward?
If the Chargers season continues on its downward spiral there will be massive questions to answer. The manner in which the season continues and wraps up will be the biggest factor in how the organization moves forward. The Chargers special teams unit is currently dead last in the NFL in terms of EPA per play and a change at special teams coordinator would be an easy and expected scapegoat-style change.
Chris O'Leary's defense has largely been the only reason the Chargers have been relatively competitive in the past two weeks and seem to be trending in the right direction. The offense is the question mark. The Chargers made a sizeable investment in Mike McDaniel but something is obviously off.
If the struggles lead to the Chargers and Mike McDaniel going their separate ways, the first call should be to former Chargers offensive line coach and run game coordinator Frank Smith. Smith served as Mike McDaniel's non-play-calling offensive coordinator in Miami the past three seasons and is currently the assistant head coach for the 4-0 Minnesota Vikings.
Smith would make sense because the offense would not necessarily have to change but someone familiar to the Chargers, Justin Herbert and who is getting a top of the line look at running a team side-by-side with Kevin O'Connell could be the perfect blend the Chargers offense would need without tearing it down to the studs. The largest contracts and investments that the Chargers have in the offense would be hard to move on from until after the 2027 season, so a teardown after 2026 seems unlikely.
I also believe, the with the current struggles of the roster, Joe Hortiz's seat could get very warm by season's end. The Chargers ownership usually gives a long runway to general managers but the offensive line woes that has plagued this team during the entirety of his tenure may be unforgiveable.
If the Chargers choose to move in a different direction, it has to be someone with an analytics background and a proactive philosophy to contract negotiations. The 49ers and Eagles are the teams that immediately come to mind. For continuity, 49ers assistant general manager Brian Hampton is the name I would have at the top of my list. He comes with a background in analytics, something that the current front office has seemingly gutted and actually worked with Jim Harbaugh during his time in San Francisco focusing on salary cap and contract negotiations.
Second part of the question from JH^3 2) Who do we target in the draft and free agency in 2027?
This is a broad and early topic but I will give two areas of focus. The Chargers have to look to upgrade their offensive line, they simply can't afford to narrow their focus to find scheme fits who could work if the world aligns perfectly in order to get value from the interior of their offensive line. Perennial all-pro guard Quenton Nelson is an unrestricted free agent next offseason and the Chargers should back up the Brinks truck even if the contract does not yield surplus value, they have to do something to change the interior.
The draft has a handful of promising interior guard prospects that could be available on the second day of the draft or they could target former teammate of Justin Herbert, Cowboys guard TJ Bass and let him battle it out with whoever is left standing from Branson Taylor and Jake Slaughter.
The Chargers need a difference-making wide receiver. Luckily, the 2027 draft class has at least five outside downfield threats that could be projected to go in the first round, possibly more. Depending on where the Chargers end up picking a wide receiver or potentially a cornerback would make a ton of sense in the first round based on needs and how the draft class is shaping up.
From Chargers Lead (@ChargersLead on X): Which of the three (Hortiz, Harbaugh, McDaniel) is most to blame? What do you think the likelihood of seeing an in-season firing is?
This may be a cliche answer but in terms of the Chargers struggles, the general manager, head coach and offensive coordinator all share in the blame significantly. Mike McDaniel has been a successful play caller and play designer but something went dramatically wrong in the initial install and implementation of the offense.
Jim Harbaugh instituted a new and lighter offseason training program designed to get the team to the season healthy. This lighter training camp may have set the offense back weeks and they coaching staff may have missed the opportunity to identify true weaknesses until it was too late.
Joe Hortiz uses the Baltimore Ravens philosophical approach to guards and focuses on gaining surplus value on interior offensive line contracts. Unfortunately this approach and drafting only one option, Branson Taylor, to potentially develop in the sixth round of the 2025 draft left the cupboard bare in terms of in-house options to fill roles. This approach has yielded disastrous results.
Justin Herbert is yet again one of the most pressured and hit quarterbacks in the NFL. Now, the Chargers are staring at a reality in which they will be starting three or four rookies against the Denver Broncos in week five.
In terms of an in-season coaching change, if the Chargers still do not have a win by the trade deadline, it has to be an unfortunate reality. But, it is worth noting, Chargers ownership does not want to make mid-season moves, it took the team flat out giving up on national television against the Raiders on Thursday Night Football for a change to be made in-season.
