title: A Realistic Scenario and Path for the Los Angeles Chargers to Save Their Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have started their season 0-4 and have looked lost on offense as they try to find their identity. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been grappling with the team's struggles with the many moving parts of his offense. The 1992 Chargers started 0-4 and made the playoffs that season, the 2026 Chargers will look to follow the same path.
Los Angeles entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations and playoff expectations, to say the season has been a shocking disappointment thus far is a deep understatement. The Chargers defense has been performing well and showing up on game day, specifically in the past two weeks. The offense finally showed signs of life and fight in the second half of their week four loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
The Chargers enter week five at a crossroads. They could have easily folded against the Seahawks when Sam Darnold and Seattle's offense marched down the field to open the second half and go up 27-6. Instead, Justin Herbert and the Chargers, aided by penalties from Seattle, fought and clawed their way back into the game. The run game started landing heavy punches and Herbert seemed to lean on scrambling to make plays.
Chargers fans have seen what happens when the team is out of breath and gives up. It led to the dismissal of the previous coaching staff and general manager following a loss on Thursday night football to the Las Vegas Raiders. LA welcomes the Denver Broncos to SoFi Stadium in week five and with their massive list of injuries they will have a choice to make, come out swinging with everything they have like their season depends on it, or fold.
If Justin Herbert and the makeshift offensive line manage to take down the Denver Broncos and show they are not ready to lie down and die just yet, there is a realistic path forward for them to save their season and even potentially make the playoffs. Obviously, time is not on their side but lets take a look at the landscape across the AFC.
The Chargers find themselves in a tough spot but entering week five, there are five teams remaining in the NFL that are winless, four of them are in the AFC. The Chargers have three of the winless teams on their upcoming schedule and additionally will face the New York Jets who have only one win on the season.
Los Angeles has lost to three good teams so far to start this season but what once looked like a schedule of doom, has now become more manageable if they can figure out their offense. The Chargers face the Broncos in week five and the Chiefs in week six before their bye in week seven. The bye couldn't come at a better time given their injuries but it is also an opportunity to regroup before the final stretch of ten games.
In the Chargers final ten games they will face the currently winless Texans, Buccaneers and Dolphins. The Jets and Patriots are both struggling with their own issues as well as being AFC opponents. If Los Angeles can get their first win of the 2026 season against Denver, who are struggling on offense themselves, it could be the beginning of a turnaround for Los Angeles.
The Broncos are taking a more collaborative play-calling approach this week with HC Sean Payton having an increased role in the process and OC Davis Webb continuing with a significant game-planning and game-day role, per sources. Denver is looking to spark its offense ahead of… pic.twitter.com/6y2jHZTaYn
The Week 5 battle will truly be a battle of who can manage their injuries the best. The Broncos will be without wide receiver Pat Bryant as well as top cornerback Pat Surtain II and most likely number two cornerback Riley Moss will be out as well.
We asked @AdamSchefter for an injury update on Pat Surtain, Riley Moss, and Pat Bryant. "I don't expect any of them to play this week. My guess is we'll see certainly Surtain [on IR], quite possibly Bryant, and I would guess not Riley Moss." #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/qCgkJuS4oS
Assuming the Chargers can snag their first win against the Broncos in week five and in theory take care of four out five of the perceived winnable games down the road, they would be searching for five more wins on the season.
The Chargers face the Chiefs two times as well as the Broncos and Raiders down the road. They will also face off against the Rams, Ravens and 49ers. Of those eight matchups, can Los Angeles sneak five wins to get to 10-7 on the season? It is possible if they manage to get back on track.

title: Chargers Week 5 Injury Report: Latest Updates, Practice Status and Replacement Options
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers limped back to LA after dropping their fourth straight to the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field in Week 4. The Chargers were already banged up heading into the game against Seattle but it got significantly worse by the end of the game.
The Chargers are the subject of several sports jokes and sayings. The term "Chargering" is now common knowledge among NFL media as a term used to describe the Chargers magical ability to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory. Now it seems that the Chargers curse is becoming more widely known and accepted.
The Chargers curse refers more to the high volume of injuries at key positions the Chargers seem to face on a consistent basis. The 2025 season became a train wreck on the offensive line when the Chargers lost both of their top tackles for the season and had a revolving door at the positions the entire season.
This offseason, newly signed center Tyler Biadasz suffered a season-ending knee injury during training camp. Entering Week 4, the Chargers were already down to their fifth option at left guard and ended up losing both tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt on top of left guard Trevor Penning to injury. The final offensive line that finished out the game consisted of four rookies and the original starting right guard Cole Strange. Curse or no curse, the results are devastating.
The Chargers may be getting some reinforcements this week before they face off against the Broncos. The team opened the practice window for offensive lineman Branson Taylor and fullback/tight end Scott Matlock, both of whom started the season on injured reserve. If Taylor is healthy, he should be rushed to the starting lineup with guard Kayode Awosika still not practicing, guard Trevor Penning in concussion protocol and both Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt already ruled out.
wednesday's injury report for week 5 vs DEN pic.twitter.com/1xgJcHuFUy
One of the more positive developments is that tight end Charlie Kolar returned to practice in a limited fashion after undergoing forearm surgery after an injury suffered in Week 2. If Kolar is able to play, his blocking will greatly help the gameplan for a pair of inexperienced tackles, presumably Branson Taylor and rookie Travis Burke.
The Chargers skill position groups on both sides of the ball will be tested this week with three out of four of the top wide receivers and cornerbacks carrying an injury designation to start the week. With an inexperienced offensive line and receiving options banged up, establishing the run will be critical for the Chargers if they are going to have a chance Sunday.
Due to the significant injuries, the Chargers may use multiple practice squad elevations to fill out the game day roster. It will be worth noting who is able to log full practices as the week continues.

title: Ranking Chargers Trade Candidates If LA Starts Fire Sale
full_text:
The NFL is a league where the roster churning never stops, even during the season when teams are taking form and showing off the efforts of the offseason. While this has a positive connotation, the Chargers' 2026 season is indicative of the Bolts' 2026 offseason, an offseason filled with half measures and unrighted confidence.
With this, the Chargers are 0-4 and seemingly ready to move on from valuable assets in hopes of creating a brighter future for a team that was seemingly ready to make a run in 2026. Who are some of the players the Chargers can move on from and get trade value?
Khalil Mack is the most obvious player on the Chargers who should be traded to another team before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. A team that is in a position to compete and possibly make a run to the Super Bowl. Mack has been in the league since 2014 and has never won a playoff game.
He is by all means an NFL legend, and he deserves--in what is likely his last season in the NFL--to have a chance to make it far in the postseason. He is still playing at a high level, even at age 35. It would be hard to see Mack wearing another uniform in 2026 , but for the Chargers, it makes no sense to keep him around during a failed season. Get your trade value and do right by one of your all-time great defenders.
Current Contract Left: 1-year, $18 million
Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Third Round Selection + 2028 Sixth Round Selection
Denzel Perryman , like Mack, is one of the Chargers' great leaders and long-time defenders. He is not expected to play much longer in the NFL as he is a 34-year-old thumping linebacker who is already not known for his premier sideline-to-sideline abilities.
Perryman can bring a much-needed thumping presence and leadership to a defense that is in need of such a skill set. Even with Perryman being the Chargers'  "oldest" draft pick, it makes no sense to keep him around one last year, especially with other LBs on the roster, like Marlowe Wax, who can take on the role.
Current Contract Left: 1-year, $2.3 million
Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Seventh Round Pick / Late Round Pick Swap
Trey Pipkins III is currently on injured reserve and will be needed as soon as he returns from injury, considering the Chargers are expected to play their Week 5 game against a strong Denver Broncos defense with an offensive line that can consist of 3 rookies, a second-year Day 3 offensive tackle and one of the worst guards in the NFL.
Even with the need for Pipkins III, he brings obvious trade value to any team that needs offensive linemen. He has guard/tackle versatility while being a strong leader with a little bit of playoff experience.
Current Contract Left: 2-years, $10.15 million
Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Fifth Round Pick
Derwin James Jr. is the heart and soul of the Chargers' defense. He has been this since his arrival in 2018 as the Bolts' first-round pick. James Jr. has been a constant hellraiser for opposing offenses, striking fear into QBs and receivers alike.
That said, he is now 30 years old and is likely looking for a team that can actually make a playoff run and sees a real Super Bowl future. Trading James Jr. seems very unlikely given his brand-new contract extension, but weirder things have happened in the NFL.
Current Contract Left: 4-years, $100.2 million
Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Second Round Selection + 2028 Fifth Round Selection
Quentin Johnston is the player that seemingly every Chargers fan wants to trade away to another team, given his expectation as a first-round pick never really panning out, coupled with the constant drop issues and lack of explosive games.
Johnston has been very quiet in the 2026 NFL season, doing so after signing his fifth-year option, giving him one more season after 2026 with the team. Even with that, a team that wants to take a chance on a 6'4 athletic receiver can call the Chargers and make an offer to send him to whichever team is interested. This trade would allow the Bolts to play some of their younger receivers while giving the headache of Johnston to another franchise.
Current Contract Left: 2-years, 22.51 million
Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Fifth Round Selection

title: Rams Midweek Report: Searching for Consistency, Myles Garrett Update, Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
A big theme this week for the Los Angeles Rams has been whether they can find some consistency . The Rams have the No. 2 offense and No. 2 defense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit. They have a top-five offense but are just 19th in points per game. They have a top-5 offense, but are just 19th in points per game.
If the Rams are going to become the team that many expected coming into the season, they need to find consistency. This is a team that’s been penalized 21 times over the last two weeks, the most in a two-game stretch under head coach Sean McVay. They have a -5 turnover differential through four games, which is tied for 28th in the NFL. Untimely turnovers, penalties, and special teams gaffes have been a recurring problem for this team.
“I'm interested to see how we can play cleaner football,” said McVay on Monday. “We have to play better. We have to consistently do it in all three phases and we have to earn the right to play better quality football. We have to all coach better too.”
The Rams are doing things that we aren’t accustomed to seeing from a McVay-coached team. That’s what makes the penalties and untimely mistakes so baffling at times . McVay can become pass-happy at times, but over 100 pass attempts in a two-game stretch is unheard of even for him. Sunday marked the first time since 2012 that Stafford had 50 or more attempts in back-to-back games.
Through four weeks, Matthew Stafford has an EPA per pass of -0.01. At this time last year, it was 0.15. Stafford starting the season slowly is nothing unusual, but his mistakes have cost the Rams in big moments or put them in difficult positions.
“Definitely room for improvement. There have been some really bright moments and some stuff I'm really proud of and stuff that I definitely wish I could take back to help us be in a better position to win games,” said Stafford. “I want to do everything I can to put our team in the best position to succeed. I've done that sometimes this year and other times I have not. I want to make sure that I do that at a more consistent clip moving forward.”
Given that teams no longer play their starters in the preseason, there is some belief that it can take those first three or four weeks for starters to get up to speed. The Rams have now played four games. There are no more excuses.
Coming into the season, this was a team with high expectations, and they have yet to really play up to that level. A lot of that is because of the lack of consistency. After coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Rams seemed to find something. They’ll have a chance on Monday night to show whether they can carry that over or if it was just another flash in the pan.
"It's that time of the year where you're establishing your identity both schematically and the mentality that you play with," said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. "There are things that we can do to take care of stuff that we can control so that's been an area of emphasis for us, especially this week."
Prior to the season, the Rams placed a pair of offensive linemen in Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on injured reserve. Trost injured his hamstring in the first preseason game and Dedich managed a hand injury all summer. With the Rams having played four games, both players are eligible to come off of injured reserve . However, it doesn’t appear as if the Rams are in any rush to do so.
“Those guys, they could,” said McVay. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point.”
It makes sense for the Rams to hold off for now, as both players are depth pieces and not immediate starters. The Rams only have eight injured reserve return designations to use and they are already set to use two on Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson. There’s a chance one or both are activated at some point, but given the current health of the offensive line, the Rams are waiting.
McVay was asked on Thursday whether Garrett will return to practice after his four-week injured reserve window. Monday night will mark Garrett’s fourth game that he’s missed and he’ll be eligible to return.
“I'm not sure yet,” said McVay. “I know that the rehab is progressing well. He's looked good in the meetings.”
The Rams’ head coach had previously mentioned that he would have more of an update, but that was not the case on Thursday. With that said, based on reports that exist , the Rams remain hopeful that Garrett will return next week, but Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders is more realistic. Garrett had a six-week timeline, which would have put him on track to return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers, but that was more of a worst-case scenario. Garrett has been progressing ahead of that.
Prior to Sunday’s game against the Eagles, the Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve . Just when Ferguson was starting to have a positive impact on the offense and become a featured piece, a medial ankle sprain has forced him to miss time.
Ferguson will have to miss four games, which would put his return in Week 8 against the Chargers. Based on what McVay said on the Coach McVay Show this week with JB Long, it doesn’t seem like Ferguson will miss any more time beyond that.
“He’ll be back. He’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” McVay said.
I wouldn’t expect the Rams to be active at the trade deadline. That doesn’t mean they won’t make a move, but it would be very difficult for them to do anything significant. It’s possible the Rams will see Myles Garrett’s return and getting Terrance Ferguson back as in-season additions.
There are a few things to note here. The Rams currently only have around $981,000 in cap space. That’s by far the lowest in the NFL. It would be nearly impossible for them to take on another contract at that number. TThe Rams also don’t have a lot of draft capital to send away. They don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. If they moved that second-round pick, they wouldn’t select until the fourth round. Additionally, they don’t have a second-round pick in 2028. While the Rams could use a third wide receiver, it just isn’t something that will be in the cards.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams will beat the Bills on Monday night . The Bills are dealing with injuries in the secondary, which will provide the Rams an opportunity to get something going in the passing game. However, the Bills are coming off of a loss last week and will be ready to play a clean game.
A loss to the Bills isn’t the worst thing. That would put the Rams at 2-3 with two of their three losses against AFC opponents. The Rams can ‘get right’ against the Cardinals in Week 6 and then the schedule lightens up. It’s possible the Rams could rattle off six straight wins before playing the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 13. A Week 14 matchup against the 49ers will then provide an opportunity to avenge their loss in Week 1.
The Rams signed Eric Kendricks this week, which came as a bit of a surprise. While some have speculated that Kendricks is a special teams addition, it may have been more than that. Some of Kendricks’ early role may come on special teams. The Rams have already used two of Eli Neal’s three roster elevations. Grant Stuard is also dealing with an injury this week.
However, at 34, Kendricks likely wouldn’t have signed on simply to play special teams. He’s beyond that point of his career. His addition will give the Rams some flexibility to manage Nate Landman’s injury if needed, while also allowing Kendricks to rotate in alongside Omar Speights. He may have a bigger role once he settles in.

On Friday, several players had their designations upgraded. Defensive lineman Aaron Donald was limited on Thursday, but was a full participant on Friday. The same can be said about tight end Colby Parkinson. The Rams will be glad to have both players back against the Bills.

title: 5 Keys to Victory for the Rams Against the Bills in Week 5
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to host the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on Monday Night Football in Week 5. With a win, the Rams could get above .500 for the first time this season . Over the first month, the Rams have been scrapping to get by, and Monday night will provide a good test against a team many consider to be a Super Bowl contender. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams to beat the Bills.
Under Joe Brady, the Buffalo Bills have had their most successful run game under Josh Allen. James Cook has a 52.9 percent rushing success rate. Cook’s 11.4 percent explosive run rate is also the highest in the NFL.
For the Rams defense to operate the way it wants to, stopping the run is key. It’s something that they didn’t do in Week 1. However, over the last three weeks, they’ve been much better. Their -0.2 EPA per rush allowed in that span ranks sixth in the NFL. The Rams need to be able to contain James Cook and limit the explosive runs. That will also limit what the Bills can do in the passing game with their tight ends in heavy personnel.
Last week, Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley to have at least 10 carries and 10 receptions in a game. The Rams have struggled to find a third wide receiver in the offense with Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. It’s possible that Williams can be that third option in the passing game.
The Bills could provide another opportunity to get Williams involved. Defensively, the Bills have allowed the third-most targets to running backs with 21 receptions. Their 162 receiving yards allowed to running backs are the seventh-most and they’ve allowed three receiving touchdowns. This is an area where Williams showed last week that he can be a threat in this area, and the Rams may need him to contribute again.
For as solid as the Bills have been at tackle in the past, that hasn’t been the case this year. Dion Dawkins allowed a seven percent pressure rate last year and that’s up to 12 percent in 2026. For the most part, Dawkins has struggled this season.
#Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas's bull-rush puts five-time Pro Bowl LT Dion Dawkins on the ground. pic.twitter.com/8Wu10Z0Tle
This is a matchup that the Rams will have to win if they’re going to have a chance in this game. Byron Young has one of the highest pressure rates at 18.8 percent among edge rushers. That ranks 10th in the NFL. He also ranks eighth with 18 pressures. Without Myles Garrett, the Rams need Young to continue taking over games as he did last week.
The Bills have struggled at cornerback this season as they’ve dealt with some injuries. However, it’s also just not a position group that’s played well. The Rams should have the advantage here throughout the game. Puka Nacua returned from injury last week, but the Rams will also need Davante Adams to play like he did in Weeks 2 and 3.
If the Rams can get Adams isolated against Maxwell Hairston a few times, that’s a matchup they can take advantage of and find success with. Romeo Doubs scored two touchdowns against Hairston last week. The Rams haven’t gotten the connection between Stafford and Adams going in the red zone yet this season. Monday night could provide an opportunity.
When in doubt, attack Maxwell Hairston. He’s been horrible Bench him. Put in Kani Walker pic.twitter.com/MW1ELJHLKq
For as much as fans will want the Rams to play man coverage, that’s simply not something they can do against Josh Allen. Allen has the ability to scramble for large gains, which are effective against man. Against man coverage, Allen has a 0.36 EPA per play, which is the sixth-best in the NFL. Against zone coverage, that drops by more than half to 0.17.
This isn’t to say that the Rams should stay away from man coverage altogether. However, Chris Shula will need to mix up his coverages and do so selectively. He’ll need to pick his spots and do the same when he opts to blitz. This will be a good test for Shula and the defense, who haven’t faced a true challenge since playing the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

title: Matchups the Rams Must Win to Beat the Bills on Monday Night Football
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in what should be one of the best games of the week. When these two teams have gotten together in the past, it usually comes down to a dramatic finish. Two of the last three games have been decided by three points or less. Here are three matchups that could decide the game between the Rams and Bills.
This season, the Rams have averaged 1.5 yards before contact in the run game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL. However, when Deone Walker is on the field for the Bills, teams have averaged 0.1 yards before contact compared to 1.8 when he’s not on the field. Walker has been a key piece on the Bills’ defense, and they are much better when he’s on the field. On all plays, the Bills average 5.2 yards per play compared to 6.2 when he’s off it.
Deone Walker lol I'm not fully convinced he knows what he's doing on a down-to-down basis... but this dude is massive and athletic lol some straight freakazoid reps pic.twitter.com/WM4b45MrHY
If the Rams are going to get the most out of Matthew Stafford on Monday, they need to be able to remain balanced in the run game. They also need to protect the pocket. That starts with Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, and Kevin Dotson against Walker. Walker’s 20 impact plays rank third in the NFL among interior defensive linemen.
It’s no secret that the weakness of the Rams’ defense is at linebacker. The Bills utilize heavy tight end sets more than any other team in the NFL. This season, the Bills have utilized 12 personnel on 20 percent of their offensive snaps and 13 personnel on 26 percent of their offensive snaps. Out of 12 personnel, the Bills rank third with 0.31 offensive EPA per play.
While Dalton Kincaid may not be a featured piece of the Bills’ offense, when he gets involved, he can be successful in the pass game. The Bills could have a huge matchup advantage here with Kincaid against Omar Speights, who can struggle in coverage. Speights has allowed 1.51 yards per coverage snap this season, which ranks as the eighth-most in the NFL. Both of the Rams’ linebackers are better in the run game.
The Rams will need to be ready on the offensive line as the Bills have the personnel up front to take over a game. Despite having to throw more than 100 times over the last two weeks, the Rams have done well from a protection standpoint. The Rams held one of the better pass rushes in the NFL in check two weeks ago against the Denver Broncos. The Bills will provide another challenge.
NFL sack leaders through Week 4 Greg Rousseau        6.0 Dallas Turner            5.5 T.J. Watt                      4.5 Will Anderson Jr.     4.5 Mason Graham       4.0 pic.twitter.com/IcCI3R05IF
This season, the Bills have a 45.8 percent pressure rate, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. It’s a group led by Greg Rousseau. His 24 pressures rank fourth in the NFL, despite him facing the sixth-most double teams. He also leads the NFL with six sacks. Warren McClendon has been good, but he certainly has his deficiencies.

title: Rams vs. Bills Week 5 Preview: Prediction, Matchups and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Coming into this game, the Rams are 2-2 after beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, 24-20, and coming back from 10 points down in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game of the season, falling to the New England Patriots, 29-26.
Through the first four games of the season, the Rams have yet to truly find their identity. Matthew Stafford has been inconsistent and special teams remain an issue.Already two games behind in the NFC West, the Rams can’t afford to fall much further behind.
For as inconsistent as the Rams have been, the Bills have had their moments as well. They turned the ball over five times against the Los Angeles Chargers and somehow managed to win. The Bills’ defense has struggled early on, and Drake Maye had his first strong game of the season after not playing well in the first three games.
If there was ever a chance for the Rams to get it right on offense, it’s this game against the Bills. The Bills rank 26th in pass defense EPA per play. Additionally, their 48.2 percent pass defense success rate ranks 30th. This is a team that has struggled to stop opposing passing attacks. While the Rams will be without Terrance Ferguson, this could be a game for Stafford, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua to take over.
Hairston has allowed just eight receptions on 19 targets this season, which is an improvement over his rookie season. However, last week, he struggled against Romeo Doubs on the outside. Doubs had six receptions for 58 yards and two touchdowns. Both of Doubs’ touchdowns came against Hairston.
Maxwell Hairston is having TROUBLE today against Romeo Doubs. Hairston’s holding penalty on 3rd gives NE a fresh set of downs inside the five. Then gets beat by Doubs again for another TD… NE retakes the lead 21-17 #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/HsmMHCS8zI
It’s no secret that the Rams and Bills like to use multiple tight ends. The Bills’ offense has a 49.2 percent success rate and 15.6 percent explosive play rate with multiple tight ends. However, the Rams’ defense has allowed a 33.8 percent success rate against multiple tight ends and just four explosive plays, according to NFL Pro. The Rams are susceptible at linebacker with Nate Landman and Omar Speights. Both players will need to play well on Monday Night.
In the first game of the season against the Houston Texans, Dalton Kincaid had five receptions for 130 yards. He followed that performance with seven receptions for 95 yards and a touchdown the following week. When the Bills’ offense is at its best, Kincaid is heavily involved. Landman and Speights can be exploited in coverage and Kincaid will be a difficult challenge.
Whenever the Rams and Bills get together, it’s usually a good game. The two teams put on a show in 2024 with the Rams winning 44-42. In 2020, the Rams nearly came back to win, but fell short 35-32. With both teams needing a win, Monday night should be no different. The big question here is which team will get out of its own way. There’s an opportunity for the offense to get going against the Bills’ secondary, but can Stafford and Co. be trusted not to make a costly mistake? With the Bills coming off of a loss, the Rams get a more focused Buffalo team and come up just short. Bills 30, Rams 27

title: Rams Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Key Starters Who Could Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will hope to get multiple starters back in Week 5 as they get set to take on the Buffalo Bills. After missing Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson against the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are hopeful that all three will be back for Monday night’s game.
"The expectation is that as long as they progress accordingly then they'll be ready to go," said head coach Sean McVay. "I want to see how Jaylen feels. We'll get a little shoulder harness out there, [see] how he's going to be able to block destruct. Colby is really progressing in a very positive direction. We'll be smart with the kind of reps that he takes. Then like I mentioned to you guys with Aaron, [we'll] see how his back responds. Everything is trended in the right direction.”
On the initial injury report, Donald, Parkinson, and Watson were all listed as limited participants on Monday. Donald was a surprise addition to the injury report last week after head coach Sean McVay said that he had a sore back after the game. The Rams erred on the side of caution by resting Donald last week, and the team was able to get a win without him. All indications are that Donald could play on Monday night .
Additionally, the Rams will hope to get Parkinson back after he was inactive last week with an AC sprain in his shoulder. The Rams will certainly welcome Parkinson back as they look to get back to 13 personnel this week. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at their highest rate since Week 5 of last season.
Jaylen Watson also missed last week after dislocating his shoulder in the loss to the Broncos. Getting Watson back before facing a good Bills offense would be a huge boost for the defense. The Rams will look to ramp up Donald, Parkinson, and Watson as the week progresses.
Also on the injury report were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), edge rusher Josaiah Stewart (groin), safety Quentin Lake (hip), linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder), and wide receiver Davante Adams (rest). None of them participated in practice on Thursday.
According to The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, Lake’s injury is minor, and he was heavily iced after Sunday’s game. Landman has been on the injury report the last three weeks and has played. Stewart showed up on the injury report toward the end of last week and managed to play on Sunday. Still, he’ll be one to monitor.
"He's so tough. He pushed through it," said McVay. "He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good. We're just being smart with him."
Not practicing today will be DB Quentin Lake (hip), LB Grant Stuard (hamstring), OLB Josaiah Stewart (groin), ILB Nate Landman (shoulder) and WR Davante Adams (veteran rest day). Lake's injury is minor, Sean McVay said. Lake had it pretty iced up after the game on Sunday.
McVay mentioned that wide receiver Konata Mumpfield had a rotator cuff contusion during his Monday press conference. Mumpfield was a full participant on Thursday.
On the Bills’ side, the Rams will be monitoring the availability of wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver, and cornerback Dee Alford. All three did not practice on Thursday. Additionally, defensive lineman Landon Jackson and cornerback Christian Benford were limited.
The Rams will certainly hope to be as close to full strength as possible heading into Monday night’s matchup against the Bills. While they managed to overcome several key absences against the Eagles, doing so against the Bills will present a more difficult challenge. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson trending in the right direction, the Rams could be getting some much-needed reinforcements at an important point in their season.

title: How to Watch Rams vs. Bills in Week 5 (Start Time, TV Channel, What to Watch For)
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium. After beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are 2-2 and back at .500. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game in their new stadium, falling 29-26 to the New England Patriots.
Prior to losing to the Patriots , the Bills looked like an unstoppable force. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers the week before despite turning the ball over five times. Heading into Week 5, the Bills rank fourth overall in total DVOA.
The Rams were staring a 1-3 record in the face before overcoming a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter. If they’re going to win at home against the Bills in primetime, they’ll need to find a way to be much more consistent.
For the second time this season, the Rams will play at home on Monday Night Football. They played the New York Giants in Week 2, snapping a five-game losing streak on Monday Night Football. The Rams last played the Bills in primetime to open the 2022 season and lost, 31-10.
Fans should expect plenty of penalties in this game. Scott Novak's crew is now responsible for the two games with the highest combined penalty totals this season. Last week, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers combined for 30 penalties for 280 yards. In Week 2, the Green Bay Packers and New York Jets combined for 27 penalties for 280 yards.
Bills-Rams MNF uniform matchup is set. Appreciate Buffalo going white pants against the royal-heavy Rams.  Best possible primary outcome for this one. pic.twitter.com/ZYOisQaFw5
The Rams and Bills have played some dramatic games in the past. When these two teams met in 2024, the Rams won 44-42 after the Bills nearly erased a 38-21 fourth-quarter deficit. The Rams almost came back from a 28-3 deficit in 2020, but lost 35-32. Back in 2012, Sam Bradford found Brandon Gibson with under a minute left to win 15-12. In the all-time series, the Bills lead 9-6 and have won three of the last four.
Over the past few seasons, Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen have been two of the most prolific quarterbacks in the NFL. They’ve met three times in the regular season, with Allen leading the head-to-head, 2-1. On Monday night, each player has an opportunity to reach a different milestone.
With a win on Monday Night Football, Josh Allen can become the fourth quarterback all-time with at least 100 wins, including the postseason, in his first nine seasons. He can also tie for the third-most regular season wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine seasons. Only Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes have more. Additionally, if Matthew Stafford throws a touchdown pass, he can surpass Ben Roethlisberger for the sixth-most touchdown passes, including the postseason, all-time. With three touchdown passes, he can become the first player in NFL history with at least 150 touchdown passes with two franchises.
This season, the Rams and Bills have used three-tight-end sets at the highest rates in the NFL. The Rams lead the NFL in 13 personnel usage at 31 percent. Meanwhile, the Bills are right behind them at 20 percent. Additionally, The Bills also frequently utilize 12 personnel, featuring two tight ends. Tight ends play a huge role in both offenses, making their usage something to watch on Monday night.

title: Rams' Penalty Problems Are Real, but the Numbers Tell a Bigger Story
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Denver Broncos in Week 3, they were penalized 13 times for 91 yards. It was the most accepted penalties against the Rams in a game since Week 4 of 2020. Last week against the Eagles, the Rams were penalized eight times for 100 yards. The 21 accepted penalties for 191 yards against the Rams are their most over a two-game stretch during Sean McVay's tenure as head coach.
The recent uptick in penalties by the Rams is simply uncharacteristic of a Sean McVay-led team. Throughout the McVay era, the Rams have struggled to score in the red zone at times due to questionable play-calling. This season, the Rams have had to settle for field goals because of penalties.
“The things that really chapped me that I think are a reflection of an undisciplined team are the pre-snap, the procedural things,” said McVay this week. “Those are the things that we can control with focus and concentration. They'll happen from time to time, but we have to minimize those situationally whether that's jumping offsides offensively, things like that, even making decisions where there's no discrepancy on.”
The past 2 weeks, 21 accepted penalties against the Rams measured 191 yards. Both figures are the most in consecutive games in 10 season under Sean McVay, a span of time in which discipline has been a hallmark. I just looked through them all, a few things to note: *Penalties…
In Week 3 against the Broncos, the Rams had to settle for field goals after an offensive pass interference penalty on Davante Adams and a hold on Steve Avila.
Last week, the Rams settled for field goals after a holding penalty on Davis Allen. According to Warren Sharp of Sharp Football Analytics , red-zone holding is up 38 percent, second only to 2019. After taking over at the Eagles’ 38-yard line, a seven-yard run from Williams was called back because of a questionable illegal blindside block.
BLINDSIDE BLOCK…on Puka Nacua?! What happened to the beautiful game of football… pic.twitter.com/RjcsS1MepO
However, this isn’t only happening to the Rams. This season, there have been the most red zone penalties per game by offenses in NFL history according to Sharp. More than 56.55 percent of red zone flags are on offense, which is up from 48 percent. There have also been the most penalties on third and fourth downs in the second half of games in NFL history.
For as frustrating as some of the penalties have been at times, context is important. This season, the relationship between the NFL players, league, and its officials has hit a breaking point. This week, the NFL suspended two officials for their on-field behavior . The 2026 season has seen the most flags in over a decade.
Penalties are certainly up for the Rams, but that’s also the case around the league. Despite the Rams being penalized more, they are still only tied for the 10th-most penalties per game with five other teams, and there are eight teams between 7.5 and 8.0 penalties per game. They have lost 0.15 EPA per play due to penalties, which is the 11th-worst in the NFL. With that said, the Rams still have a net penalty count of -11, which is the fourth-worst.
Penalty Impact so far this year (Somehow another Vikings defense stat) pic.twitter.com/0DByDipxfG
This is a case where multiple things can be true at the same time. Penalties are up around the NFL as a whole. Comparatively speaking, the Rams are also committing more penalties and ranking higher than they have in the past. The Rams have also been on the wrong side of some of the 50-50 calls, most notably the defensive pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace at the end of the game against the Broncos.
Throughout McVay’s tenure, the Rams have generally been one of the more disciplined teams in the NFL. It’s part of what makes the more recent uptick so jarring. Some of the increase can be attributed to the league-wide trend, but the Rams are also to blame. McVay has made it clear that those are mistakes that they need to clean up.
The league-wide trend of more penalties being called certainly adds some context, but it doesn't completely excuse the Rams' lack of discipline over the last two weeks. There are still things that they can control. If the Rams are going to reach their ceiling as a Super Bowl contender, they can't continue allowing self-inflicted mistakes to take points off the board.

title: Kyren Williams Gives the Rams an Answer to Their WR3 Problem
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams needed a third wide receiver to step up on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, it was running back Kyren Williams who made his presence felt in the passing game. Williams had 10 receptions for 67 yards and became a legitimate receiving threat. Given his success in Week 4 and the offense's continued injuries at tight end, the Rams may need Williams to remain in that role going forward.
If one thing has become increasingly clear with the Rams’ offense, it is how they are lacking a consistent and reliable third wide receiver . Puka Nacua and Davante Adams have combined for 36 catches for 589 yards, while all other wide receivers on the Rams’ roster have combined for 10 catches for 151 yards.
Early in Sean McVay’s tenure with the Rams, the offense consistently featured a running back in the passing game. It certainly helped that the running back at the time was Todd Gurley, but that element has been missing from the Rams’ offense since 2018.
In 2017, Gurley led all Rams players with 64 catches, and his 788 receiving yards trailed only Cooper Kupp. The next season, Gurley was the team’s third receiver with 59 catches for 580 yards. Robert Woods and Brandin Cooks led the wide receivers, while Josh Reynolds was the third option with just 29 receptions for 402 yards.
The Rams entered the season with the idea that they would make 13 personnel their identity on offense. Through the first three weeks, that had been the case. However, with injuries to Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson, the Rams ran the highest percentage of their offense out of 11 personnel since Week 5 of last season.
Despite the increased usage of 11 personnel, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, and Tutu Atwell each had just one catch, and none finished with more than 10 receiving yards. Meanwhile, Kyren Williams had 10 catches for 67 yards. Williams became the first Rams player with 10 receptions and 10 carries in a game since Gurley in Week 15 of 2018.
He also became the first player in the NFL this season with 10 receptions and 10 carries in a game. Williams joined Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs as the only players to achieve that feat since 2024. Williams is the first player since Breece Hall in 2023 to have 15 or more rushing attempts for at least 80 yards to go with 10 receptions for at least 65 yards in the same game. That’s something that Gurley only did once in his career in the Rams’ 27-23 win over the Tennessee Titans in 2017.
If the Rams are forced to continue utilizing 11 personnel, they need a third option outside of Nacua and Adams to get involved in the passing game. For the Rams to be successful, they may need to continue throwing the ball to Williams.
While he may not be a standard receiving back, he’s shown that it’s something that he can do successfully. Among running backs with at least 35 routes this season, Williams’ 1.77 yards per route run ranks sixth. He’s also third in receiving yards per game.
Williams is doing all that without having plays designed for him. Only four percent of Williams’ targets have been designed, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL. However, last week showed what Williams can do when he is a focal point. Against the Eagles, Williams was the first read on 14.5 percent of the team’s targets, which was up from 8.6 percent in the first three weeks.
Williams certainly isn't the same type of player that Gurley was. However, his improvement in the passing game presents an opportunity to bring back an element of the offense that made McVay’s early teams so dangerous. It’s also an area where Blake Corum has struggled. With the Rams struggling to find production from their wide receiver depth, Williams has shown that he can help fill that void.
Williams may not be a traditional receiving back, but he’s proven that he can at least be effective when he gets involved. He already has 21 receptions for 173 yards this season. If he continues at that pace, he’ll finish at 89 receptions for 730 yards. It’s highly unlikely he hits those numbers, but it’s a testament to his early-season success as a pass-catcher.
When the Rams needed a spark on Sunday against the Eagles, they were able to lean on Williams, which also opened things up for Nacua in the passing game. Williams has demonstrated that he can be a reliable option when given opportunities.It's now up to McVay to determine how much of that production can become a consistent part of the offense until the Rams are healthy enough to get back to what they do best.

title: Rams Special Teams Analysis: What's Going Wrong and How to Fix It
full_text:
Through the first four weeks of the 2026 season, the Los Angeles Rams have struggled on special teams . In 2010, the San Diego Chargers went 9-7 and missed the playoffs because of poor special teams play. Much like the Rams this year, they also started the season 2-2.
The Chargers opened that season with a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, in part because of a 94-yard punt return touchdown by Dexter McCluster. In Week 3, the Chargers gave up a 101-yard kickoff return for a touchdown to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chargers gave up a second kickoff return for a touchdown in the fourth quarter, losing by seven.
That 2010 Chargers team is infamous for having the No. 1 defense and No. 1 offense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit. Through four weeks, the Rams have the No. 2 offense and No. 2 defense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit.If they don’t fix their special teams, the Rams could be heading down a similarly disappointing path.
According to DVOA, the Rams’ special teams unit ranks 32nd at -14.5 percent. The next four teams ahead of them have a combined record of 0-16. In every game this season, the Rams have had some sort of special teams error. Against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Rams allowed a 45-yard kickoff return to open the second half. It didn’t take long for the 49ers to score a touchdown and take control of the game.
While the Rams beat the New York Giants in Week 2, Ethan Evans opened with a 38-yard punt and Harison Mevis missed a 43-yard field goal. Xavier Smith also bobbled the opening kickoff of the second half and Tanner Ingle took a 15-yard penalty on a kick return.
Against the Denver Broncos, Smith again made poor decisions in the return game. Additionally, Evans shanked a re-kick, and the Rams allowed a 28-yard return to give the Broncos a short field. Neither of the Broncos’ two touchdown drives in the third quarter went more than 52 yards.
Special teams almost cost the Rams last week as well. The Rams allowed a 41-yard punt return to set the Philadelphia Eagles up in the red zone. In the same game, Harrison Mevis missed a 48-yard field goal and had a kickoff go out of bounds.
To the Rams’ credit, they are actively trying to address the issues . Head coach Sean McVay recognizes that changes need to be made. Even though the Rams beat the Eagles on Sunday, McVay addressed the special teams issues.
“We need better,” said McVay on Monday. “As it relates to the return game, you have to do a good job of holding up and doing better on some of the perimeter play. I thought we fielded the ball clean. The conditions were unique, but we have to be able to get some more production out of that. Obviously, I would have loved for us to have made that field goal kick, and then the long punt return is not good. We have to do a better job of casting a net, being able to tackle.”
The Rams cut punt returner Xavier Smith last week and also moved on from Tanner Ingle. Both players had been responsible for key special teams errors in the past. The Rams also signed Maximus Pulley off of the Eagles’ practice squad who is a good special teams player. This week, they signed linebacker Eric Kendricks. Still, the changes are only scratching the surface.
According to DVOA, the Rams’ field goal unit ranks 28th at -4.0 percent. Only the Steelers, 49ers, Dolphins, and Falcons are worse. Their kickoff unit ranks 28th as well at -2.1 percent. Mevis’ longest field goal this season is 48 yards. He’s one of just six kickers without a make over 50 yards. The Rams have lost 0.17 EPA per kick from Mevis, ranking 26th in the NFL.
NFL Kicker Rankings through Week 4 pic.twitter.com/5QLmQMWsLY
It would be one thing if Mevis was missing long field goals, but the Rams don’t appear to trust his leg from range. Mevis is 4-for-6 in his career from beyond 45 yards. The Rams have actively passed up kicking 52-yard field goals and taken delay-of-game penalties to punt. Last week, the Rams went for it on 4th-and-8 instead of allowing Mevis to kick a 53-yard field goal.
This isn’t to say that the Rams should go back to Joshua Karty, but Mevis is just 1-for-3 from 48 yards in his career. From 45+, Karty was 3-for-4. That’s not necessarily an argument for Karty, but rather an illustration of Mevis’ inconsistencies from range. His miss on Sunday against the Eagles was so far left, it didn’t hit the kicking net behind the goal posts.
MEVIS' KICK IS NO GOOD ❌ #NFL #Rams #RamsHouse #Eagles #FlyEaglesFly #LARvsPHI pic.twitter.com/Wbs5Wcu2vP
The lack of confidence in his kicker has forced McVay to become more aggressive, which might be a good thing. At the same time, you have to have a kicker that can make it from range in today’s NFL.
Inside of 45 yards, Mevis has been reliable. However, some are mistaking being reliable for being good when it comes to Mevis. Given Karty’s inconsistencies, Mevis being 46-for-46 on extra points is a good thing.
With that said, 20-of-26 attempts in his career have been inside of 45 yards. He’s 19-for-20 on those attempts. From 45+, Mevis is 4-for-6 with a 66.7 percent make-rate. The NFL average from 45+ is 73.4 percent. In today’s NFL when two first downs can essentially put an offense in potential field goal range, the Rams need a kicker who is consistent inside of 45, but also has the leg to hit from deep.
The Rams don’t necessarily need to replace Mevis, but last year they brought in competition for Karty and they should be looking to do the same now. Tanner Brown was signed by the Rams as a rookie, but didn’t make it through the preseason. He was 29-for-32 in the UFL last year, missing one field goal from inside of 50 yards. Brown also had makes from 60 and 63 yards.
The Rams previously signed Tanner Brown as a UDFA and he didn't make it out of the preseason. Hit bombs from 60 and 63 last year in the UFL. Gotta say he's at least worth a look, right? https://t.co/8R527iZptS
The Rams made a change at punt returner with Alex Bachman last week after cutting Smith. It was a much-needed change, but it’s hard to say that it was the answer. Replacing Smith with Bachman wasn’t a solution, but rather a band-aid.
DVOA currently has the Rams’ kick return unit ranked 32nd at -6.4 percent and their punt return unit ranked 27th at -2.2 percent. Their average starting field position at the 26.8-yard line ranks 29th in the NFL. Rams’ opponents are averaging starting field position about 5.6 yards better than the Rams. That difference ranks 27th.

We’ll see how this improves without Smith over the next four weeks, but it feels like the Rams still need to do more here. However, the bar remains very low at “simply catch the ball and make good decisions.” Bachman did that last week and likely will remain in that spot until he shows that he can’t be trusted.
If there is another spot that the Rams make a change, it wouldn’t be surprising to see it come at punter. The Rams rank 30th in punting DVOA at -3.4 percent. For every good punt that Evans has, he follows it up with one that puts the defense in a bad spot.
Evans’ seat is, at the very least, getting warm . Special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone called out his inconsistencies last week.
“We need to get more consistency from the punter,” said Ventrone. “Ethan can do a better job being able to elevate the ball and match hang times and distance at a greater rate. We have to do a better job in his position.”
The big return last week against the Eagles was more on the punt coverage unit than it was Evans’ punt. Evans actually did a good job getting the punt along the sideline and his coverage unit was in position to make a play on the returner. Both the punter and coverage unit can be better.

title: Multiple Doctors Believe Rams WR Puka Nacua Is at Risk of Re-Injury
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams just got wide receiver Puka Nacua back last week after missing the previous two games with what the team described as a hip/groin injury.. Nacua looked good in his return with nine catches for 125 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles. However, according to multiple doctors, Nacua could be at risk for re-injury.
On Wednesday, Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio noted that Nacua has been dealing with a pre-hernia. While it isn’t a hernia right now, it could develop into one.
“The question becomes whether the rest has allowed the weakness/strain in the affected area of the hip/groin to improve sufficiently to prevent a hernia from developing,” said Florio. “If it ever does, there’s only one way to fix it.”
The one way to fix it would be surgery, and the Rams will hope it doesn’t come to that point. A typical recovery from a hernia surgery would be 4-6 weeks and Nacua would almost certainly land on injured reserve if that were to be the case. After resting Nacua for the past two weeks, the Rams are banking on that helping the issue long-term.
However, there is some risk with Nacua, especially with his physical style of play. Toward the end of training camp, Nacua was h eld out due to a psoas injury in his groin. Following the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers, Nacua felt discomfort during the following week of practice and didn’t return until last week..
Despite the Rams erring on the side of caution with Nacua, some doctors seem to believe it’s only a matter of when, not if, Nacua re-aggravates the injury.
Dr. Jeff Mueller on Twitter noted that there is some re-injury risk.
“My guess with Puka is that this sling suffered enough trauma to require rehab but not to a full extent of requiring sports hernia surgery,” said Mueller. “In that scenario, their hope is that the traumatized tissue scars over/heals enough to where it doesn’t rip any further. However, this does place enough reinjury risk where if he twists sharply and it does rip the tissue more, it could push him into a situation where it causes a true sports hernia.”
Puka Nacua Q: It’s some speculation on our part but we know for sure that Puka has dealt with Groin and Hip Flexor muscle injuries since August with a condition currently labeled as “pre-hernia”. Sports Hernia injuries involve the groin, abdominal and hip flexor musculature.… https://t.co/vYhWttjNjS pic.twitter.com/r40i6k8EkJ
Throughout the offseason, the Rams have erred on the side of caution with several of their star players, Nacua included. If they are able to avoid surgery and a longer absence, that’s obviously ideal.
Still, this is a similar approach that the Rams took with Myles Garrett. The Rams held out Garrett for much of training camp, hoping that the swelling in his knee would go down. Garrett’s knee didn’t respond as the team had hoped and he had one of the worst games of his career in Week 1 against the 49ers because he wasn’t able to feel like himself.Had Garrett simply gotten surgery in the offseason, the team may have been able to avoid that situation altogether.
It appears to be a similar situation here with Nacua. With the Rams being in the middle of the season, they obviously want to avoid the surgery if they can. However, they could be delaying the inevitable.
“This is a matter of when, not if. Best case scenario, he makes it the entire season and ends up having sports hernia repair surgery (likely by Dr. William Meyers) in the off-season,” said Dr. Jesse Morse. “Every time he lifts his leg, pushes his foot down to cut and get off the line, he is stressing this tissue. Every time he reaches out over his head for a ball that is higher than usual, this currently damaged tissue is going to be stressed further.”
Morse noted that if Nacua were to suffer a significant setback, the surgery would be moved up significantly and would take about six weeks to return.
Puka Nacua In my opinion, this is matter of when, not if Best case scenario, he makes it the entire season and ends up having sports hernia repair surgery (likely by Dr. William Meyers) in the off-season. Every time he lifts his leg, pushes his foot down to cut and get off… https://t.co/C6oTmuokV8
Nacua looked good in his return, but his physical style of play will always leave him susceptible to injury. When Nacua spoke to the media last week, he said he felt good. Still, as Florio said, “Nacua has been dealing with the symptoms of the kind of weakness in the structures that can allow a hernia to form. It hasn’t yet, and that may simply be a matter of luck.”
For now, the Rams will hope that the two weeks of rest were enough time for Nacua’s injury to heal. His performance against the Eagles was certainly encouraging, but it doesn’t necessarily mean the issue is behind him. The Rams avoided the worst-case scenario, but the risk of a significant setback may not be going away anytime soon.

title: 3 Key Raiders Players To Watch Against Patriots
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders head east for their first of two East Coast trips this season to face the New England Patriots, coming off a big road win against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills.
The Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they have a chance to prove that they are a legitimate team early in the 2026 season. If Las Vegas is to beat the defending AFC champions on their home turf, they’ll need these three players to shine in Foxboro. Here are three key Raiders players to watch on Sunday.
Earlier this week, I wrote a story on how the Raiders have viewed the former undrafted free agent. The former 3-star recruit was once stuck in a deep pass-catcher room at Michigan State and, years later, is finally making his presence known on an NFL team. White has a chance to have a productive day against a Patriots cornerback room missing Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis.
White has been making big plays this season, and it is evident in how he attacks the football. This week, look for White to be targeted a handful of times this week as quarterback Kirk Cousins looks to take advantage of an injured New England defensive backfield.
After missing a game against the New Orleans Saints with a concussion, Stukes returned to the field last week and seemed everywhere, using his athleticism and coverage skills on the back end to fly to the football, nearly picking off Patrick Mahomes at one point. This week, he has a chance to make Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffer when attacking downfield.
Maye is tied for third in the NFL in deep-ball percentage (15.4%), and opposing defenses are exploiting that strength this season. This week seems like another opportunity for Stukes to secure his second interception of the season and force Maye into the short and intermediate; exactly what the Raiders will want.
Walker’s versatility should come into play this week, and I think he is due for a monster game at the second level. This is his chance to be used effectively as a pass rusher, drop him into coverage if the deep ball is unavailable for Maye and the Patriots, and make stops in the run game against running backs like Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson.
Look for Walker to be a big part of defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s game plan as the Raiders look to shut down offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, Maye, and the rest of New England’s offense.

title: 3 Uncontrollables That Could Decide Raiders’ Fate on Sunday
full_text:
PROVIDENCE, RI.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) arrived last night from the desert and are ready to take on the AFC’s reigning Super Bowl representative in what has become a major clash.
The Raiders have a chance to flip the script this season with a win, and if they played this game ten times, I would expect them to win five.
After a significant film study, I already provided three keys to a Raiders victory. Still, in today’s article, I want to go in a different direction and discuss three uncontrollables - things they don’t automatically control - and how they will impact this game.
The Raiders' sophomore running back was tailor-made for the Klint Kubiak system. The Kubiak wide-zone rushing attack is exactly where the Patriots have been struggling this season. He is battling an injury, and while he is expected to play, that isn’t 100%.
Klint Kubiak confirmed he traveled with the team here, but his health could still be a factor. Kubiak addressed it. He said of Jeanty, “He's going to do his best to go."
Some have been critical of Jeanty after a breakout Week 1 performance against the Dolphins, and Kubiak was asked about Jeanty's production and whether he's had a nagging injury since before the first game that sent his teammates to the ground in prayer.
"I don't. I think he's been doing a great job. And again, he's a leader on our team. He's a guy we're counting on. I couldn't be more happy with Ashton [Jeanty]. We got to keep getting him and the entire offense playing better every week. But no, I don't think so."
The New England Patriots' secondary is anemic with injuries, and the Raiders are coming in with a high-flying aerial attack led by 15-year veteran Kirk Cousins.
So how does Kubiak prepare with no idea who is playing in the defensive backfield for the Patriots?
He made it sound like business as usual.
"Yeah, you just worry about yourself and worry about our guys getting better and it’s the NFL, injuries happen and the next guy steps up."
With Jalen Nailor out and Dont’e Thornton not yet back, more pressure rests on Cody White and rookie Malik Benson at WR. Kubiak doesn’t see it as a problem, and I agree.
"They've been challenged all year, and that's no different this week."
Keep in mind the "Rule of Five." The game is considered over if the Las Vegas Raiders win this key statistical battle. This rule involves sacks and turnovers.
For example, if the Raiders achieve three sacks while allowing two, they have a net score of plus one. If they force four turnovers and allow only one, their score improves to plus three.
In total, a plus-four score for the day would be achieved. The Raiders aim to accomplish a plus-five ratio in every game. On average, teams that attain the Rule of Five win 91 percent of their NFL games.
In a game as close as this one, the Rule of Five becomes an even bigger narrative. The 2026 Raiders have already "shocked" NFL executives , and they just might do it again on Sunday.

title: Raiders' Injury Report Solidifies Plan Ahead of Patriots Matchup
full_text:
On Friday, the Las Vegas Raiders finished up their final practice ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the New England Patriots. The Raiders are looking to get back on track after losing for the first time this season last Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Las Vegas' upcoming game against the Patriots is another early test for a Raiders team that significantly improved over the offseason. After starting 3-1, Sunday is yet another game in a month-long stretch of challenging outings for the Raiders.
Las Vegas has worked hard in practice this week to correct the mistakes that cost them last week. The Patriots will enter Sunday's matchup minus several critical players, but Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak knows they will still present a formidable challenge to his still-developing team.
"Very well coached, high effort. Take the ball away. Just a very impressive defense, and that's obviously going back two years, and have a ton of respect for what they do schematically and how hard they play," Kubiak said on Friday.
Spencer Burford, Cody White, and Trey Zuhn were listed on the injury report as limited participants on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday/in each of this week's practices. All three will play on Sunday. All three players are contributors Las Vegas is counting on in their road matchup against New England.
Dareke Young, Brock Bowers, Dont'e Thornton, Jackson Powers-Johnson, and Folorunso Fatukasi were listed on the injury report throughout the week. Each player is expected to play on Sunday. Las Vegas' offense needs all the help it can get to start fast and finish strong on Sunday.
Running back Ashton Jeanty was listed on the injury report throughout the week. The second-year back was a full participant on Wednesday, a limited participant on Thursday, and did not practice on Friday. Jeanty was officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game.
Wide receiver Jalen Nailor missed Friday's practice, completing a week of missed practices. He will miss Sunday's game. Although Thornton practiced during the week, Kubiak announced on Friday morning that Thornton will not be activated for Sunday's game . He and Zuhn will be out.
Jeanty's availability and overall health are worth monitoring. Jeanty suffered an ankle injury shortly before the first game of the regular season and had limited time off between the injury and the Raiders' Week 1 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.
Jeanty had a solid debut, registering over 100 total yards. However, since then, Las Vegas' ground game has struggled. Jeanty's injury undoubtedly has impacted the Raiders' offense, in addition to opposing defenses going all out to stop Jeanty.
Still, Kubiak explained on Friday that he does not believe Jeanty's health has affected the ground game. Kubiak noted that Jeanty has done the best he can since returning from injury, and that many teams around the league, such as the Patriots, are dealing with injury-related issues.
“I think he's been doing a great job. And again, he's a leader on our team. He's a guy we're counting on. I couldn't be more happy with Ashton [Jeanty]. We got to keep getting him and the entire offense playing better every week. But no, I don't think so,” Kubiak said on Friday, following the team’s final practice of the week.
Sunday could be another step forward for Las Vegas. A 4-1 start to the season would be much more than expected. Las Vegas faces the Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams over the next few weeks. Entering the season, many would have understandably expected them to lose all three.
If they win even one of those three games, they'll still be ahead of schedule. Including Sunday, two of Las Vegas' next three games are at home. If the Raiders beat the Patriots, that would give them even more breathing room as a team that is still gelling overall.
No game is too big for the Raiders; they're talented enough and well-coached enough to win. As always, Sunday will come down to Las Vegas' ability to execute at a high level while minimizing costly mistakes. Hopefully, last Sunday showed the team their potential when they play sound football.

title: Hondo’s Film Study: 3 Keys to Raiders Victory After Reviewing Patriots
full_text:
PROVIDENCE, RI.—The Las Vegas Raiders will arrive later today in New England to take on the Patriots (2-2), the reigning Super Bowl representative of the AFC, in what is sure to be a terrific football game.
The Raiders have an opportunity that was just a few short months ago thought unthinkable: win this game and flip the script from rebuild to playoff contender.
The aforementioned Raiders rebuild has been handled brilliantly by GM John Spytek and Klint Kubiak, but that doesn’t mean a Silver and Black win on Sunday against the Patriots wouldn’t be considered an upset.
The way Klint Kubiak has coached, his staff has led, and risk has been calculated from 2026 to now screams first-year coach. In fact, it calls back to the old-school days when the Raiders had a schematic advantage every week because of the man in charge.
Outside of last week versus Andy Reid, Kubiak has outcoached the previous three head coaches, embarrassing them easily, and even with Reid, neither man outdid the other.
But Kubiak is highly intelligent, and he knows how critical these three areas are.
The Las Vegas Raiders will not waver from Klint Kubiak’s iron-jawed commitment to running the football. Kubiak earned his head-coaching job because, as an offensive coordinator, he built his resume on that commitment.
Every game this season, teams have stacked the box to stop the Raiders' run game. Sunday will be no exception. The Raiders must maintain that commitment and punish the Patriots with their wide zone attack, which the Patriots struggle with.
Let me explain in more detail.
The Mike Vrabel-led Patriots' struggles defending outside runs play right into the hands of Klint Kubiak and his outside zone offense.
The Patriots' run struggles on defense stem from thin depth along the defensive front and edge-setting issues.
​Patriots' opponents have exploited their unproven, younger edge rushers the same way Kubiak will, using perimeter sweeps and outside zone plays to stretch the field and wear down the front seven as the game progresses. For the Patriots, Kubiak will serve up their biggest defensive kryptonite on a platter.
But other issues remain for the reigning AFC champs, including inconsistent second-level tackling by linebackers (not named Spillane) and safeties, which have allowed ball carriers to turn short outside gains into bigger, explosive runs.
OC Andrew Janocko wasn’t going to give away any part of the game plan, and who would expect that? But he reiterated the importance of getting the run game going for the Silver and Black.
"I think we just have to pay attention to our details. Starting with ourselves, what we're asking of the players, how we're attacking each plan, what we are attacking each game plan. Then, presenting a great plan to the players, allowing them to be detailed so they can go out, play fast, and attack it. That's what we're looking forward to doing."
The Patriots have a very good defense led by former Raider MLB Robert Spillane, who never wanted to leave Las Vegas. But they are very thin in many areas, similar to the Raiders.
As thin as both teams are, neither team can afford injuries. I don't expect WR Jalen Nailor to play for the Raiders, and while that loss is significant, it's manageable against this Patriots defense.
That said, watch both teams' health, as one key injury could flip the switch either way.
Last week, I told you that the Raiders were not good enough to beat the Chiefs, and themselves. Ultimately, the Chiefs made mistakes, and so did the Raiders, but the Chiefs were good enough to beat themselves and the Silver and Black.
This Sunday, the Raiders' opponent isn’t as good as the Chiefs. But the Raiders still can't beat themselves and the Patriots.
Mistakes will ultimately determine the winner in such a close game. DC Robbie Leonard knows this and must keep the Raiders focused on fundamentals. He explained.
"It always comes back to fundamentals and execution, especially in the critical moments. That they felt the reality of what you preach every day, of being locked in, regardless of the environment and how loud it is. A call can't save you. It comes down to fundamentals and taking the ball away and playing blocks the right way, releasing blocks, being on the same page in coverage."

title: Two Potential Additions Raiders Could Target in Trade Market
full_text:
Heading into the season, the Las Vegas Raiders were expected to be sellers at the trade deadline, with Maxx Crosby a popular candidate to move.
However, the Raiders have jumped out to a 3-1 start, with wins over the Dolphins, Chargers, and Saints, who have a combined record of 1-11. So, those wins could be viewed as a fluke. Las Vegas faced its first true test in Week 4 against the Kansas City Chiefs , and even in a loss, the Raiders looked the part. Las Vegas pushed Kansas City to the brink in a 30-27 loss .
It's only been four weeks , but Las Vegas looks like a legitimate playoff contender. We'll learn a lot about this team in the next few weeks, with a daunting stretch ahead. The NFL trade deadline isn't until Nov. 10, but some teams are already trending toward a lost season. That has culminated in several players rumored to be on the block. With that in mind, here are players the Raiders could target as they look to enhance their chances of competing in meaningful games down the stretch.
After posting 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns in his rookie year, the former 2024 first-round pick has been on a downward trajectory. Through four games this season, Harrison Jr. has accumulated five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown.
Harrison Jr. has been phased out of the Arizona Cardinals' offense, as he's the fourth-leading pass catcher on the team behind Michael Wilson, Trey McBride, and Kendrick Bourne. Things have run their course in Arizona for the Ohio State product. The talent is still there, which is why coughing up a third- or fourth-round pick is well worth it for the Raiders to improve the wide receiver corps. A change of scenery could unlock Harrison Jr.
Acquiring the Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver will come at a steep price, as Thomas Jr. recorded 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns during his rookie campaign. The talent is evident.
It would likely take a first- or second-round pick to pry Thomas Jr. from the Jaguars. A first-round pick may be too rich, but if Jacksonville is willing to move the 24-year-old wide receiver for a second-round pick, general manager John Spytek should seriously consider pulling the trigger if that opportunity presents itself. Again, it's early in the season, and so much can change in the coming weeks, but Thomas Jr. has also fallen in the pecking order in the pass-catching department.
I understand that Las Vegas didn't want to be too aggressive in the offseason and overspend at certain positions, but reaching the playoffs is a legitimate possibility for the Silver and Black. The Raiders lack a true WR1. Tre Tucker leads all wide receivers on the roster with 15 receptions for 233 yards and one touchdown. However, 119 of those yards came against the Los Angeles Chargers. Tucker is the only wide receiver on the team with more than five receptions and 64 yards.
Acquiring Harrison Jr. or Thomas Jr. would give Las Vegas a potential legitimate WR1 in 2026 and give Fernando Mendoza a weapon moving forward. Trading for a young receiver isn't a win-now, all-in move. It's also a way to build the franchise's foundation at a discount.
