title: 5 Vikings Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Saints in Week 5 After Friday's Injury Report
full_text:
On Sunday, the Vikings will face off against the Saints in a game that could create huge momentum for the Purple and Gold. A win would extend the winning streak to five games , while suffering their first loss would start their Week 6 bye on a low note.
The Vikings can have a maximum of 48 players active on game day, which means at least five individuals will need to be inactive against the Saints. Choosing which players to sit on Sunday could be the difference between a victory and a defeat.
Minnesota's inactive players won't be announced until a few hours before this weekend's game, but by looking at the injury report and the previous inactive players, five Vikings are more likely to sit out than others against the Saints in Week 5.
Minnesota's starting left tackle is on the injury report with a concussion and hasn't practiced all week. Christian Darrisaw was declared out on Friday afternoon (h/t Vikings), and Ryan Van Demark is expected to get the start at LT in New Orleans.
Final #Vikings Week 5 injury report OUT: Christian Darrisaw and Chuck Demmings QUESTIONABLE: Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, Michael Jurgens*, Brian O’Neill and Ben Yurosek* *Currently in 21-day return to practice window pic.twitter.com/TLCCJUfUFF
Although Van Demark doesn't offer the same kind of pass protection as Darrisaw, he is a quality run blocker. He earned a 75 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus this season and should be used to open holes for running backs while Darrisaw misses at least one game.
Like Darrisaw, Chuck Demmings is on the injury report this week. A hamstring injury prevented him from fully participating in practice this week, and he was declared out on Friday and will not play against New Orleans.
Demmings has played 26 total snaps for the Vikings this season, with only two of those coming on defense. Minnesota shouldn't have much trouble filling his role, especially on special teams. However, it will be great when the young defensive back returns to gain more experience on the field.
Defensive lineman Elijah Williams has been inactive for all four of the Vikings' games this season, and that trend likely won't stop in Week 5. Although he has experience from last season, playing 42 defensive snaps, Minnesota has enough depth and talent at the position to keep him inactive.
Besides, there are already players who are fighting for snaps on the defensive line. Rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange need that experience to continue their development Jalen Redmond, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, and Levi Drake Rodriguez hold down the trenches to allow the younger players time to adjust to the NFL.
This is another case where a player has been inactive all season. Jakobe Thomas ended the preseason with an ankle injury, and Minnesota hasn't rushed him back. But he hasn't appeared on the Vikings' injury report with that injury leading into any of the team's regular-season games, which means it shouldn't be an issue going forward.
Thomas was a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, so the Purple and Gold will want to get him on the field eventually. However, there is absolutely no reason to throw him into Brian Flores's complicated defense until he is ready to be a contributor.
Max Brosmer will technically be inactive, but he will dress for Week 5 against the Saints. He will act as the emergency third quarterback if something happens to Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz in that game and neither can continue.
By naming him the third quarterback, he receives an inactive designation and will not count against the roster limit for Week 5. If Brosmer has to enter the game, something very bad is happening in New Orleans.

title: Vikings Week 5: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for vs. Saints on Sunday  (Underrated Rivalry Continues)
full_text:
Your 4-0 Vikings head south this weekend to chase a perfect 5-0 record as they prepare to enter their bye week. In their way? A chippy Saints team led by head coach Kellen Moore and quarterback Tyler Shough.
Despite their record, facing the 1-3 Saints won’t exactly be a vacation to the French Quarter, as Shough has thrown for an impressive 1,203 yards and nine touchdowns to start the season.
The Vikings' defense will certainly need to keep up their patented aggression to limit Shough’s effectiveness, but the biggest story may be on the opposing side of the ball.
Here’s what to watch as the Vikings fight to remain perfect in 2026 against an opponent with whom they share quite a history.
If recent trends continue, the matchup between the Vikings and Saints may just be one of the more entertaining games of the weekend.
In fact, the two squads have built quite the rivalry over the years, despite being non-divisional foes on opposite sides of the country. Although Minnesota holds a dominant 25-13 all-time series lead, the two squads have had some incredible matchups over the last two decades.
Of course, there’s the 2009 NFC Championship/Bountygate scandal that we choose to ignore whenever possible, the Minneapolis Miracle in the 2017 divisional round, a Vikings OT walkoff Wild Card round win in 2019, Alvin Kamara’s six rushing touchdowns against the Vikings in 2020, and the peak of “Dobbs-sanity” as Josh Dobbs defeated the Saints in Minnesota in the last battle between the two teams.
Throwback to the last time the Vikings and Saints faced off in 2023 as Josh Dobbs plays lights out in his first start for the Vikings. - 268 passing yards - 1 passing TD - 1 sack taken - 101.1 passer rating - 44 rushing yards - 1 rushing TD Vikings win 27-19 pic.twitter.com/SYJUh1tED7
Needless to say, there’s not much love between these two franchises in recent years.
Drew Brees’s induction into the Saints’ Ring of Honor at halftime on Sunday adds extra fuel for Vikings fans in the stands who saw him win a Super Bowl with New Orleans after the controversial 2009 conference championship.
We started to see glimpses of what the Vikings’ pass game could look like at the end of Week 4’s matchup against Miami, and we’ll need to see the next steps in that marriage between coach and QB this weekend. Head coach Kevin O’Connell and quarterback Kyler Murray are clearly working through the difficult task of blending two completely different passing philosophies, and it has not always been perfect.
The Vikings are currently dead last in the NFL with 156 passing yards per game (h/t: ESPN ).  While it would be unfair to expect Murray to suddenly become Sam Darnold or Kirk Cousins and turn into a pure pocket passer, the team needs the passing offense to get on track if it wants to contend.
Luckily, we saw glimpses of what this could look like last week, as O’Connell began implementing more shotgun and quick-game concepts. Minnesota’s offense could start to take key strides this weekend if that trend continues.
Justin Jefferson was listed as a limited participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday and told the media he plans to play Sunday, barring any setbacks with his left ankle. Jefferson’s return in front of his hometown crowd could give the passing offense a much-needed boost, especially if he takes the field with fellow Louisiana legend and mentor Odell Beckham Jr.
Entering the bye week at 5-0 would be a major accomplishment for the Vikings, especially given how inconsistent their offense has been at the start of the season. With their schedule getting tougher, every win they can stack now gives them an additional buffer for a challenging November-through-December stretch.
The bye week also gives them chances to address concerns along the offensive line , the running back room, and in the passing game, regardless of Sunday’s outcome. If the Vikings use the bye week to retool and recover, they may be set up for a successful run through the gauntlet portion of their schedule that starts in November.
Being 5-0 on the break just happens to be the best possible circumstance.

title: Under-the-Radar CB Is Clearly Vikings' Best Offseason Addition One Month Into 2026 Season
full_text:
It's hard to believe that the first month of the 2026 NFL season is behind us , but here we are. The Vikings—against all odds—have an unblemished 4-0 record to show for their early efforts, and though there is room for improvement (looking at the offense), the Purple and Gold have given fans enough reason to believe that the best is yet to come.
Staying perfect won't be easy, but Minnesota can remain one of the NFL's top teams if its best contributors keep producing, which includes first-time Vikings. While some fresh faces (like Jauan Jennings) are struggling, others have thrived in the first month of action, setting the stage for what should be a promising rest-of-season performance.
That includes one under-the-radar defender who's quietly become a key cog in Brian Flores's defensive machine.
Isaiah Rodgers and Byron Murphy Jr. were always going to enter the 2026 season as the Vikings' top cornerback options, but they needed more depth than just Zemaiah Vaughn behind them. That's why, before using a fifth-round pick on rookie CB Chuck Demmings, Minnesota signed former undrafted free agent James Pierre to a two-year, $8.5 million contract in March .
The Florida Atlantic product was looking for a fresh start after playing 95 games (13 starts) across two stints with the Steelers, splitting his time almost evenly between defense (1,309 snaps) and special teams (1,359 snaps). Pierre amassed 102 solo tackles (1.1 per game), five forced fumbles and four interceptions during that stretch, which included a pick in each of the last three campaigns.
Pierre wasn't a household name, but his 87.4 Pro Football Focus coverage grade with the Steelers last season provided a glimpse of what he could do. Fortunately, the Vikings' free-agent signing picked up where he left off, as proven by his stats from the first four games:
James Pierre after 4 games
Defensive snaps (in coverage)
Sure, Pierre's sample size isn't the biggest at a glance, but his 75 coverage snaps rank third among Vikings CBs, trailing only Murphy (155) and Rodgers (154), and he's only been targeted 10 times.
It's clear that Flores & Co. have found a way to maximize Pierre's skills without needing to constantly have him on the field, which could be smart in the long run. Having the 30-year-old veteran more rested later in the year could let the Vikings use him more often while saving Murphy and Rodgers's energy for the postseason.
Pierre will have one more opportunity to build on his strong start to the 2026 season when the Vikings visit New Orleans to take on the 1-3 Saints this weekend .
The Saints average the fourth-most passing yards per game (278.5) on an NFL-leading 45.0 attempts, which means Pierre (and the rest of the Vikings' secondary) should have plenty of chances to make plays. New Orleans' offensive line is a work in progress and has already allowed QB Tyler Shough to be sacked 12 times (T-3rd-most), and the pressure has also led to three interceptions (T-9th-most).
In other words, Pierre has a busy Week 5 ahead. If he stays the course and keeps his foot on the gas, it could be another productive day in coverage, adding to the case that he's been the Vikings' best offseason addition and may deserve an expanded role as the season continues.

title: 3 Bold Predictions as Vikings Battle Saints for a 5-0 Start (Kyler Murray Remains Clean in the Big Easy)
full_text:
The Vikings head south to New Orleans this weekend to take on the 1-3 Saints, who are coming off a 45-24 home loss to their division rival Falcons.
The Saints are a feistier team than their record may suggest, and the Vikings have not always had the best of times in the Big Easy. Still, the opportunity to enter the bye week 5-0 means Sunday afternoon's contest is too important to downplay.
As the action nears, here are my three bold predictions as the Vikings fight to remain undefeated against the Saints in Week 5.
Admit it. Every Vikings fan has imagined themselves lining up at quarterback in the Superdome on Jan. 24, 2010, with a chance to get the team in range for a game-winning field goal to advance to the Super Bowl.
The reality of Brett Favre’s interception across his body (h/t: NFL) in that exact scenario has left a traumatic scar on generations of Vikings fans, including Kyler Murray, who wasted no time ingratiating himself with the fanbase when he signed in March, saying he cried “real tears” after Favre’s brutal NFC Championship interception .
Murray now has the chance to suit up for the team he grew up rooting for, in that same stadium. I predict he'll make sure history doesn't repeat itself. With the offense’s new focus on smart, safe football, I see Murray avoiding unnecessary risks.
Mark me down for a zero-turnover game from QB1 on Sunday.
After a relatively quiet two-sack performance (h/t: NFL) by the Vikings defense in Week 4, Sunday seems like a great chance to go all out before the bye week. The Vikings’ defense leads the NFL with 16 sacks so far this season, while the Saints offense is tied for third in total sacks allowed at 12.
Dallas Turner stays hot 🔥 MIAvsMIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mL27DhWl9A
The Vikings have been attacking opposing QBs at an astounding rate, and Saints QB Tyler Shough may be the perfect target. Although he’s 27, he has yet to play a full season’s worth of games in the NFL.
Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores will be looking to play mind games with Shough and Saints head coach Kellen Moore.  Shough is currently third in the league in passing yards with 1,203 through four games, for an average of just over 300 yards per game. Taking him down will be essential to slowing down the Saints' passing attack.
This may be my boldest take of the week, as neither Justin Jefferson nor the newly signed Odell Beckham Jr. is guaranteed to play this weekend . Jefferson was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday and Thursday's practices after missing last week with an ankle injury. While his status is uncertain, he made it clear he intends to play on Sunday, barring any setbacks (h/t: ESPN’ s Kevin Seifert).
Beckham is currently on the team’s practice squad, but head coach Kevin O’Connell emphasized Wednesday that he has no concerns about his ability to be ready for an elevation on Sunday, referencing his signing and immediate use with the Rams in 2021 .
Kevin O’Connell says he’s confident Odell Beckham can be ready to impact the game Sunday if he is elevated. pic.twitter.com/gaGMvvc5UF
I'm confident one or both of the former LSU Tigers will take the field for their return home, and O’Connell will find a way to get at least one of them into the end zone. So far, Jefferson’s only pro game in New Orleans came on Christmas in 2020, when fans were not even allowed to attend.
Sunday marks his first chance to play in front of his home crowd in his career, and I feel like he’s about to put on a show.

title: One Thought on All 11 Vikings Offensive Starters One Month Into the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Vikings are a perfect 4-0 a quarter of the way through the NFL season , but it hasn't all been smooth sailing. While the defense and special teams units have pulled their weight and more, the Vikings' offense is still figuring things out.
Things looked a little crisper on offense last week against Miami, but there's still plenty of room to grow moving forward. Now that one month of action has provided a sufficient sample size, here are my thoughts on every Vikings offensive starter four games into the schedule .
The bad news is that Kyler Murray's start with the Vikings hasn't been especially pretty. He's 30th in QBR, 24th in completion percentage, and—we'll save you the time—bottom 10 in most other passing metrics too.
The good news, though, is that each game has been an improvement over the last. Murray has gone from 11 snaps and the ugliest interception human eyes have witnessed, to simply finishing the game against Tampa Bay, to looking somewhat decent against Miami. By Week 12, the Vikings should have a potential MVP at this rate.
Since Jordan Mason's Week 1 injury, Aaron Jones Sr. has been the sole source of the Vikings' offensive production for the most part. Ahead of the season, some writers—including this one—had written Jones off a bit as an aging back who had seen his production drop in three straight seasons.
While those things still remain true, he's actually single-handedly carried the load in the Minnesota backfield this season with 297 yards. He'll get a bit of a break after the bye when Mason returns, but Jones kept this offensive train from completely derailing.
Outside of a scorching hot Week 1 performance with eight catches for 92 yards and two scores, Justin Jefferson has logged just five catches since. He missed the majority of the past two games with injury and slogged through a Chicago monsoon in Week 2, so there's no reason for alarm.
The Vikings' best player should be back in action soon and has been the only bright spot in the receiver room thus far.
Jordan Addison is tracking to fall short of his incredible rookie season numbers for the third straight season, and it's getting hard to get a good read on him. He's got 11 catches for 163 yards this year, and barring a huge outburst the rest of the season, he will again post mediocre numbers for a player many believe to be one of the best WR2's in the NFL.
Obviously, quarterback issues from last year have dragged on into 2026, so Addison's modest production may come with a bit of an asterisk.
Head coach Kevin O'Connell can point to Jennings' work in the run game (h/t Bring Me The Sports ' Will Ragatz) all he wants, but it's hard to look at the big ticket free agent with just two catches and say that things haven't been disappointing.
Again, quarterback play hasn't done him any favors, but Jauan Jennings really needs a few big catches in the coming weeks to show some proof of concept here.
T.J. Hockenson leads all Vikings receivers in most every statistic after a monster 13-catch, 119-yard performance in Week 4. It appears that Murray has found a friend, and that should be welcome news for Hockenson, who took a pay cut and chopped a year off his deal to stay in Minnesota this season. One game does not make a season, though, and we'll see if his connection with Murray is real.
Christian Darrisaw's evaluation never really wavers season-to-season: when he's healthy (he's usually not), he's very good (elite even). The left tackle has yet to play a full season in his six-year career, and after suffering a concussion last week, that may be the case again in 2026.
It's unfortunate for a player who could and should be top-five at his position.
Donovan Jackson was playing some of his best ball before tearing his meniscus last Sunday. He had allowed just two pressures heading into the game, but he will now miss the remainder of the year in what could be a huge loss up front. We'll see what new starter Joe Huber has this week .
After a full summer of worry and panic about the non-center center, Blake Brandel has actually been mostly fine. His snaps have been steady for the most part, and his 76.2 pass-blocking grade with Pro Football Focus ranks fifth among centers. Good enough for me.
Will Fries definitely suffers from 'Kirk Cousins Syndrome': he's been a decent enough player, but his huge contract puts a big magnifying glass on his play. At the time of his signing, Fries was getting paid like a top-10 guard in the NFL. He hasn't been truly awful, but he's probably only played up to the level of maybe a top-30 guard instead, and that's hard to be content with given his deal.
Captain and fan-favorite Brian O'Neill is back with a new extension. He was playing well until Miami's Chop Robinson came to town in Week 4, notching eight pressures and a sack. While that didn't all fall on O'Neill's shoulders, let's hope that game was more of an anomaly than a sign of things to come.

title: The Case for Why Justin Jefferson Should Play vs. the Saints in Week 5
full_text:
The Vikings head to New Orleans this weekend to face the Saints for a Week 5 face-off . The two NFC teams are on opposite paths: the Vikings aim to enter their bye week 5-0, while the Saints hope to avoid a brutal 1-4 start to the season.
It's safe to say the stakes are high for both teams. The Vikings, though, are hoping their X-factor will be available to help them on Sunday: star receiver and St. Rose, LA native Justin Jefferson.
Jefferson, who injured his ankle early in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, was limited in practice to start the week after missing all of Week 4. This progress is certainly a welcome relief for Vikings fans everywhere, but it doesn’t guarantee he'll play this weekend.
Despite any potential concerns out there, here's why I think Jefferson should , and ultimately will, take the field in New Orleans on Sunday.
Let me start by making one thing abundantly clear: Jefferson and the Vikings should not risk putting him on the field if there are any serious concerns about his ankle.
The good news so far is that it seems unlikely. Jefferson hoped to return in the Week 3 game against the Buccaneers, where the injury first occurred, and stood on the sideline with his helmet on after spending time in the blue medical tent. Ultimately, he would head to the locker room for additional testing that determined he had sprained his left ankle.
The team played it safe in Week 4, holding Jefferson out of practices and last Sunday’s game against the Dolphins, but his limited participation in practice to start this week shows he’s making positive strides (h/t: Vikings).
If there were serious concerns about the stability of Jefferson's ankle, he likely wouldn't even be practicing on a limited basis. The 27-year-old wideout stated after practice that the ankle “feels good now” and that he hopes to “rock and roll” on Sunday (h/t: Bring Me The Sports ' Will Ragatz).
Justin Jefferson on his ankle injury against the Bucs: "Like 4 or 5 people tackled me on that play. Big Vita Vea, 300 pounds, he kinda landed on my leg a little bit." "It feels good now. Hopefully, Sunday, being able to rock and roll." pic.twitter.com/eodlc4aiqm
The Vikings' passing game has been less than stellar to start the 2026 season, and Jefferson has played fewer than 20 total snaps with new starting quarterback Kyler Murray after both have left games with injuries.
Jordan Addison was held out of Wednesday’s practice with a hamstring injury, and while he seems like he'll be good to play Sunday, there's no guarantee he’ll be at 100%. Jauan Jennings is next on the depth chart, but he has yet to prove himself reliable this season , with only two receptions for nine yards over three games.
Jefferson’s inclusion in the passing game opens opportunities that simply aren’t there otherwise for him and his fellow wideouts. The Vikings will also face a much tougher slate of opponents in the coming weeks.
After the Saints, they’ll head to their bye before hosting the Colts. Then things get challenging: the Vikings will play the Lions (twice), Bills, Packers, 49ers, Falcons, Panthers and  Patriots between Nov. 1 and Dec. 20.
If the Vikings’ passing offense is going to reach its full potential, Jefferson and Murray will need every possible rep to be at their best before the toughest stretch of the schedule. The Vikings are a very good team , but they need their offense in sync if they want to be true contenders.
If Jefferson is cleared to play on Sunday, I don’t see many things preventing him from suiting up in front of his hometown crowd.

title: 3 Biggest Vikings Concerns Heading Into Week 5 (OL Injuries Among Top Worries)
full_text:
Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season is in full swing , marking another opportunity for the 4-0 Minnesota Vikings to put their undefeated streak on the line. Their next challenge comes Sunday when the New Orleans Saints—who are coming off back-to-back losses—welcome the Vikings to Caesars Superdome, marking the Purple and Gold's final game before their Week 6 bye.
A perfect start to the year has left Minnesota fans with plenty to celebrate, but it would be absurd to think the Vikings are without issues. Head coach Kevin O'Connell and his coaching staff still have a long way to go to unlock the team's full potential , and they can take a step closer to accomplishing that by improving in key areas before it's too late.
That said, here are three of the biggest concerns surrounding the Vikings ahead of Sunday's afternoon contest.
The Vikings' win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 4 came at a price, as the offensive line lost two key contributors. Left guard Donovan Jackson tore his meniscus, likely ending his 2026 campaign , while left tackle Christian Darrisaw is currently in concussion protocol , and time will tell how quickly he clears the five-step process.
Being without any O-line starter would be a challenge, but missing both left-side star blockers could make it harder for the Vikings to move the ball on Sunday. According to Pro Football Focus , Darrisaw has the 14th-best pass-block grade (76.9) among 69 offensive tackles this season and has allowed pressure on 2.3% of offensive snaps compared to 3.8% in 2025.
As for Jackson, he's been among the Vikings' most consistent offensive linemen this season. Although he's been solid at opening run lanes like last year, he's made major improvements in pass protection, with his grade rising from 65.7 to 77.2 after allowing only two pressures across 100 passing downs.
Sunday is almost here, so the Vikings need to have a next-man-up mentality, regardless of how devastating the injury losses are. That said, Joe Huber and Ryan Van Demark will likely start in place of Jackson and Darrisaw, respectively, with Michael Jurgens' potential return adding more help to the interior .
It's safe to say that Aaron Jones Sr. has been one of the hard-working Vikings this season.
Despite this being Year 10 in the league, the veteran running back has been tasked with averaging a career-high 18 carries per game, which includes averaging 20 in the last three outings. It's great to see Jones thrive and occasionally spark the Vikings' inconsistent offense. But it's also fair to say that overworking a 31-year-old RB might not be the best idea for Minnesota's long-term aspirations.
Unfortunately, the team's less-than-ideal backup running back situation has left O'Connell & Co. with no choice but to use Jones as a bell-cow rusher.
With Jordan Mason still on injured reserve, the Vikings have used veteran DeeJay Dallas and rookie Demond Claiborne to support Jones with little success. Claiborne has been one of the most disappointing members of Minnesota's 2026 draft class , averaging just 2.2 yards on six carries. Meanwhile, Dallas has only seen three carries for 10 yards and has been detrimental in pass protection, as evidenced by his putrid 17.8 pass-block grade on PFF .
Former Saints RB Audric Estime was signed to the practice squad last week, but it remains to be seen if he's ready to face his former team. Assuming he isn't, Vikings fans can expect to see a lot of Jones against the Saints' run defense, which allows 147.8 rushing yards per game (30th) and 5.1 yards per carry (30th), at least until Claiborne and Dallas prove to be more than warm bodies.
Remember when Jauan Jennings was signed back in May? The Vikings were optimistic that the former 49ers playmaker could slot in as the No. 3 wide receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, potentially giving the Purple and Gold one of the best wideout trios in the NFC, if not the entire league, on paper.
Fast-forward to now, and it's fair to wonder if the Vikings are dealing with some buyer's remorse .
If you haven't noticed Jennings on the field through the first quarter of the season, you likely aren't the only one. The Cowan, TN native looks rather pedestrian with only two catches for nine receiving yards on four targets.
The Vikings' quarterback room has a putrid 16.7 passer rating when targeting him, worse than if the ball were thrown into the ground every play (39.6). His 31.0 run-block grade is another example of his shortcomings , making it hard to feel optimistic about his outlook.
With Jefferson still recovering from an ankle injury and Addison missing Wednesday's practice with a hamstring issue (h/t Vikings), Minnesota might need Jennings to finally wake up this weekend.
The veteran receiver tallied five catches for 89 yards and a touchdown in his last visit to New Orleans in Week 2 of the 2026 season, offering hope that he can replicate that performance on Sunday afternoon.
Otherwise, the Vikings will need to rethink whether and how Jennings fits into their offensive plans going forward.

title: 3 Vikings Coaching Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell vs. the Saints in Week 5
full_text:
It's Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and it brings plenty of potential changes for the Vikings to make in their quest to move to 5-0 ahead of their bye. The Vikings will take their talents down to New Orleans for a matchup with the Saints on Sunday, but they have a few things to take care of first .
After a rash of injuries and several roster moves over the last week, here's how I would handle the game plan if I were in head coach Kevin O'Connell's shoes in the Big Easy this weekend.
It's certainly not flashy, but starting the undrafted free agent from 2025 is probably the best path forward for the Vikings—at least for now. Joe Huber came in for the injured Donovan Jackson last week against Miami and should get the start at left guard this week against New Orleans after a decent performance.
After playing 71 snaps, O'Connell wasn't shy to praise his young lineman in the win.
"Joe’s a good young player that we’ve been really excited about since we first brought him on as an undrafted free agent last year,” said O’Connell. “He’s been able to be versatile to have a game-day role at three spots when called upon. It happened to be left guard yesterday. I thought he had some really good snaps."
Trading for a quality offensive lineman midseason is nearly impossible, and any free agent guard who has even looked at a football in the last year was scooped up by the Packers last week. Luckily, the Vikings have a bye after facing the Saints and can fully evaluate the position then. But if Huber again plays solidly this week, it would be tough to take him out of the lineup in favor of an outside hire.
Much was made about Kyler Murray's odd fit with Minnesota before he even took a snap. Before joining the Vikings, Murray spent 85% of his time in shotgun with the Cardinals , a stark contrast to O'Connell's much tamer 53% rate since becoming the head man in Minnesota (h/t NFL Next Gen Stats and ESPN ).
It shouldn't come as too much of a surprise, then, that Murray's best game so far was when O'Connell opted to operate out of shotgun 54 times in the win over Miami—his most since taking over in 2022.
The Vikings initially hoped to blend O'Connell's under-center preferences with Murray's comfort working out of the gun in some sort of a happy medium. It may already be time, though, that O'Connell just admits his new quarterback is clearly better with what he knows.
With the offense struggling, opportunities for growth and experimentation are dwindling, and O'Connell should probably put aside his ego and recognize that his preferred offense isn't what's best for the team right now.
The Vikings turned heads when they added Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad this week.
After getting released by the Giants without registering a catch, the Vikings were quick to make the call to reunite Beckham with his former offensive coordinator from their L.A. Rams days. O'Connell has basically already admitted that Beckham could be elevated for Sunday's game, saying the wideout has familiarity with the scheme.
So, yeah, sure, let's see what the old guy's got left.
Expectations should be low, but it's not like the bottom of the wide receiver depth chart is producing much either. Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price have combined for just three catches through four games, so the bar isn't especially high to clear. If Beckham can get some meaningful production from the WR4 spot, this odd, fun, weird signing will look good in the eyes of many.
If not, well, it drew a few more eyes to the team for a couple of weeks.

title: Predicting How Patriots Perform vs. Raiders in Week 5: Can They Overcome Injuries?
full_text:
The New England Patriots will be celebrating their 2001 Super Bowl team , as well as Hall of Fame kicker Adam Vinatieri, this week at Gillette Stadium. They'll also play host to the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders as they look to win back-to-back games for the first time since last year's postseason.
These Raiders aren't the slouch that some might have expected before the season. They rattled off three wins to open up the year, and hung close with the Kansas City Chiefs a week ago. Kirk Cousins, Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers make up a pretty solid offensive trio that has given teams fits.
"They turn what would be a 5-yard gain into 15-yard gains because of his ability to see that quickly," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "So, it’s a great challenge, it’s a new opponent, and somebody that we have to really invest a lot of time in."
Ahead of Week 5, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
It was a fantastic bounce-back showing for the Patriots in Buffalo a week ago , but as it stands right now, that's a one-off. The Patriots — and Drake Maye — will need to start stacking those types of games together to really get back into the groove we saw a season ago.
Sure, his offense is banged up ( Mack Hollins won't play after suffering a calf injury ) and the running game hasn't been as consistent that you might have hoped. But Maye will need to look the part for the world to start taking him seriously again. If he can avoid the strong pass rush that's led by Maxx Crosby, Maye and this offense should start to look "normal" again.
A.J. Brown remains out for at least one more game, and Hollins won't be able to go after missing all three of the team's practices. So that leaves the Patriots' wide receivers down to Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams (with Kyle Dixon, Chandler Brayboy and Cameron Dorner on the practice squad). Doubs, who caught two touchdowns a week ago, has a big opportunity to become that "WR1" and rectify a slower-than-expected start to his first New England season.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 26, Raiders 14
Coming into the game, the Raiders do have the better record. But let's now cloud our judgement and get ahead of ourselves. This is a game that the Patriots should come out on top. If Maye plays like he can, plus a banged up defense gets some timely plays, this should be just another one of those games that New England can celebrate.
If you are reading this, there is a non-zero chance the Patriots will need you to suit up at cornerback on Sunday. New England’s top players at the position, Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, have both been ruled out for the game. Depth rookies Channing Canada and Karon Prunty have also been ruled out, while backup Charles Woods is marked as questionable to play.
That leaves Marcus Jones as the sole guarantee to play corner on Sunday from New England’s 53-man roster. The team also has a pair of practice squad options in Kindle Vildor and Al’Zillion Hamilton, who signed with the Patriots on Tuesday. With Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (who is utilized more similarly to an oversized receiver as a true tight end) coming to town, the New England secondary will have a tall task ahead.
X-Factor: CB Kindle Vildor
Yes, I predict a practice squad player to be the x-factor for the Patriots this weekend. With New England down Gonzalez , Davis, Canada, Prunty and possibly Woods, SOMEBODY is going to have to cover Bowers. So, with Jones standing eight inches shorter than the star tight end, and Hamilton having been signed just a handful of days ago, Vildor will play a substantial role in slowing down the Las Vegas pass offense.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 30, Raiders 27
Although the Patriots defense may struggle due to its countless injuries, the offense finally found its groove last week. New England put up 29 points a week ago against the Buffalo Bills. Maye returned to his 2025 self, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors . The Patriots offense must go shot-for-shot with the Raiders, which it should do with relative ease. New England comes out on top by three after a game-winner from kicker Andy Borregales.

title: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson Gives Positive Update on Playing Status
full_text:
FOXBORO — Late in the New England Patriots' 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills, Rhamondre Stevenson got banged up and would exit the game on the final drive. Stevenson would be a limited participant throughout practice the week following, another injury the Patriots wouldn't be able to afford.
So as the team looks ahead to the challenge of the Las Vegas Raiders, Stevenson gave reporters a positive update for if he'll suit up or not.
"Feeling great. Ready to go," Stevenson told reporters in front of his locker on Friday. "I just got rolled up on. It was really just a little scare I had. Just really making sure I was good, honestly."
The Patriots officially listed Stevenson as questionable with a knee injury, one of seven players to enter the game with a questionable designation. But Stevenson has his sights set on playing. He's been solid — not mind-blowing — four games into the season (44 carries, 163 yards, one touchdown), but his hard running style helps set up the rest of the Patriots offense looking to stack positive weeks together.
"I've just been recovering during days like (where I'm limited). Got on the field, I ran," he said. "Ran around yesterday, and I was full go today, so I'm feeling good."
Mike Vrabel didn't rule out the possibility of Stevenson playing against the Raiders — "Not out yet. Not out as of yet," the head coach said at his weekly Friday availability.
Stevenson says that there's a heavy emphasis every week on the run game, but this week can be critical considering some of the injuries to the wide receiver room. Mack Hollins was ruled out with a calf injury he suffered in Week 4.
But it's a tough challenge against a Raiders front that includes both edge rusher Maxx Crosby and linebacker Nakobe Dean.
"Staying on the field as long as we can, keeping our defense off the field, staying ahead of the sticks," Stevenson said. "That's gonna be key."
If Stevenson wouldn't be able to go, that will mean a larger dose of snaps for TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner (with a potential practice squad elevation for Lan Larison, who was elevated back in Week 1). And while nothing is set in stone just yet, it feels like it's safe to assume Stevenson will remain in the starting lineup.
"Obviously we haven't arrived yet, still a ton of work to be done," Stevenson admitted. "But I think we've progressed a little bit in that area last week out there."

title: Patriots Promote Veteran Safety Who 'Loves' Special Teams Role
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots entered this week with a pair of open roster spots . One of those was filled up when the team promoted safety Mike Brown from the practice squad to the 53-man roster.
Brown, who was a game day elevation for each of the last two weeks , signed with the Patriots as a free agent this offseason. In the two games that he's played in this season , he's recorded 12 defensive snaps and 42 special teams snaps. Brown has two tackles this season.
Earlier in the spring, Brown was repping as the team's third safety. He then fell down the depth chart a bit, but latched onto special teams. He was released during roster cuts in August, but rejoined the team with the practice squad.
Now, he'll be given a larger opportunity to show why the team signed him to a one-year deal.
"When you think about football, you can never be where you want to be," Brown told Patriots On SI. "I'm thankful. It's part of the journey, and I'm happy to be a part of the roster now."
Brown's promotion comes after a wave of injuries hit the Patriots secondary . Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty were all ruled out for this week's game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Charles Woods was spotted on the injury report with a shoulder injury, and the Patriots lost special teams ace Dell Pettus to an ankle injury earlier in the year.
There's a lot of moving pieces for the Patriots this week, but adding Brown to a more solidified role on the active roster should help some of the bleeding. He'll likely join Brenden Schooler, who Mike Vrabel said is ready to make his season debut after starting the year on the non-football injury list.
"He's a core special teams player, personal protector on the punt team and backup safety," Vrabel said of Brown and why the team chose to elevate him. "So, going to need him eventually."
Brown will become a regular on a special teams unit that's been solid to begin the season. It's part of his bread and butter as a player, and a part of his game that Brown takes a lot of pride in.
"I enjoy it. I mean, I wouldn't have a job without it," Brown said. "You got to embrace it. That's the way I feed my family. So I love it if it loves me."
This week will be tough for the Patriots, as they face a Raiders team who relies a lot on Brock Bowers' production. The superstar tight end has the ability to change a game, and so the Patriots' secondary will need to key in on him. Brown might not get a large dose of snaps in the defensive huddle, but all the safeties (Kevin Byard, Craig Woodson, Jaylen Reed) will be asked on to do a lot .
"Brock Bowers is unique," Brown said. "He's a big body, but he's almost like a receiver, so he can create a lot of matchup conflicts. I would say they like to run the ball, so you got to be keyed in to stopping the run and taking away the players they want to get the ball to.
"But Brock's a really good player. It's kind of weird watching him because he's so big, but he's a receiver, so it's like a very, very skilled player."

title: Patriots Suffer Major Blow Ahead of Tough Raiders Matchup
full_text:
FOXBORO — For the second-straight week, the New England Patriots will have their best defensive player on the field.
Christian Gonzalez was absent from the team's third and final practice this week as they prepare to host the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Gonzalez was a non-participant the first two practices with a shoulder injury, the same injury that held him out of the team's 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills in Week 4.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, Mike Vrabel shared that Gonzalez won't suit up ths week against Kirk Cousins and the Raiders offense.
"Put the next guy in there," Vrabel said. "Elevate who's ever available. All we got on the roster."
The 24-year-old cornerback, who signed a record-breaking contract extension ahead of the season opener , has been one of the best players in football when healthy. But he's been banged up a lot since arriving in the NFL in 2023, and will now miss his 19th career game.
Without him, the Patriots would typically lean on Carlton Davis to step up. But Davis is dealing with a neck injury and has also missed all three practices. Channing Canada (hamstring), Charles Woods (shoulder) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) were also all on the injury report, making this group of cornerbacks as slim as you can get. Both Canada and Prunty were ruled out as well.
Only Marcus Jones and practice squad players Kindle Vildor and Al'Zillion Hamilton practiced in all three sessions, and could be tasked with much more important roles if the top-half of the depth chart isn't able to go. Vildor will likely be elevated to the game day roster for the second-straight week.
"He's a veteran who's played a lot of football," Vrabel said. "I don't think the moment's too big for him. He just jumped in there last week and was ready to go."
But it will be a tough test regardless of who's healthy. The Raiders have gotten good play out of their veteran quarterback, and when you add in the energy brought by new head coach Klint Kubiak, they're a tough out.
"They have a lot of chemistry," defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr said Thursday. "Obviously, Klint and Kirk being in Minnesota together, they definitely know each other well. You can tell that from Week 1 there wasn’t really any slow growth. They hit it. They hit the field running. They’re doing a great job with their big skill and they’re dialing up some good plays to their skill."
The Patriots have been banged up in recent weeks, and losing Gonzalez for another game is just another wound to try and recover from. They've placed more players on IR this year (17) than they did all of last season.
"Nothing is more important than the health of the football team," Vrabel sai this week. "We clearly see that and understand that. So, there's a fine line that we wage between practicing, having speed at practice, having pads at practice, but also making sure that we are doing everything that we can to avoid injuries in practice.
"Then obviously when you go to the game, there are just some things that you can't avoid."
The Patriots also ruled out wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) and fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle/knee).

title: Patriots Coaches Remember 2001 Super Bowl Team Ahead of 25th Anniversary Celebration
full_text:
FOXBORO — Ahead of the New England Patriots ' Week 5 home game against the Las Vegas Raiders, a ceremony for the team's first Super Bowl championship will take place.
Celebrating the 25th anniversary of the now-iconic 2001 team, plus giving Adam Vinatieri his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime and wearing the Pat Patriot red throwback uniforms, is a love letter to the region as they dip themselves into a pool of nostalgia.
Nobody on this current Patriots team was in the league when that team hoisted the Lombardi Trophy following a 20-17 upset of the St. Louis Rams. Some of them, like Kevin Byard, vaguely remember that team as a young kid, seeing Tom Brady take over for the injured Drew Bledsoe and lead his team through the playoffs.
Andy Borregales grew up admiring Vinatieri and his pressure-packed kicks , but was too young to ever cross paths with him on the football field. Sure, Hunter Henry and Marcus Jones played for Bill Belichick during their Patriots careers, but they were still more than a decade away from entering the NFL.
But they still aren't experts. So far, Mike Vrabel has yet to show any of his old highlights to his current players.
"I was eight years old, so I wasn't fully just like into NFL football just yet," Byard said about his memories of that 2001 season. "I've been a football historian ever since I was young. I was watching NFL Films, NFL Network, stuff like that. So I've definitely been tapped in."
So it's up to the New England coaching staff to sit around and look back on that first championship team. Vrabel, a star linebacker that recorded three sacks and nine pass breakups that season after signing as a free agent, has his photo up right outside the Patriots locker room. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels was a first-time NFL coach during that 2001 season, working as a personnel assistant.
Those two have lasting legacies in New England. Vrabel got into the face of Kurt Warner as Rams quarterback — the leader of the "Greatest Show on Turf" — threw a pick-six to Ty Law. McDaniels would eventually become the team's offensive coordinator three different times.
"I'll see those guys on Saturday. I'll see those guys for a quick dinner," Vrabel said Wednesday. "But it's exciting that there are so many guys that want to come back, and it was a special year for everybody involved."
It's making McDaniels feel a bit old as he looks back on his long coaching tenure.
"Boy I was young, and I just think that team embodied all the right things," McDaniels said. "Kind of fought through some early season adversity with the Drew situation and in the injury, and had a lot of new players getting used to each other and familiar with one another, and how to play together. ... 5-5 after 10 games, and then, as happens often in this league, kind of figure out how we had to win.
"...Just super fond memories for me to start my career in the NFL, just watching that happen and being a little fly on the wall and seeing how it operate and how those guys ended up buying into the way we had to win. And then watching them complete the mission down in New Orleans was really cool."
The team is set to have a number of alumni return to Foxboro for the game . On Friday, Matt Chatham, Bobby Hamilton, Marty Moore, Otis Smith and offensive line coach Dante Scarnecchia are taking part in a youth football clinic. The Patriots social team posted an old video of the team celebrating the AFC Divisional game, the Tuck Rule game in the snow against the Raiders, in preparation.
It's becoming a big thing this week at Gillette Stadium.
Other coaches on staff weren't in New England when the Patriots ended up winning the game. Special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer grew up playing quarterback and as a Dallas Cowboys fan, so he wasn't really pulling for the underdog Patriots in that game.
"It was a hell of a game, and I do remember watching it and it was fun to watch," Springer said. "And that kind of started the reign of the wins and me hating the Patriots at the time."
Others, who have extensive coaching backgrounds in New England, appreciate what the Patriots have established in the region. But Doug Marrone has fonder memories of a different era.
"I've always had a great deal of respect," offensive line coach Doug Marrone , who has experience coaching at Coast Guard, Northeastern and Boston College, said — going on to share personal memories about Patriots Hall of Fame lineman John Hannah. "We've studied New England in almost every place where I've been. Respect and acknowledging how hard it is to do what they did, having been in this profession is probably the thing that sticks with me the most."
There was an enduring message for the young McDaniels to learn from that Patriots team, and it's one he wants to carry over into his coaching philosophy 25 years later.
"There's a way to win and everybody can't do it the same way," he said. "I think if you're not too proud to acknowledge what your strengths and weaknesses are, you can figure that out eventually. ... That was a great example of a team that really understand what the phrase complementary football meant."

title: Patriots Get Fantastic News on A.J. Brown's Health
full_text:
FOXBORO — It's been a long few weeks for the New England Patriots without their top wide receiver, but the return of A.J. Brown could be on the immediate horizo n.
Brown, who suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, was spotted in the Patriots locker room for the second-straight day on Thursday. Brown walked into the locker room with cleats on with no apparent limp, and had a slight tape job on his right ankle.
The 29-year-old appeared to be in good spirits at his locker, chatting with Drake Maye and Mack Hollins as he untied his cleats . He also took time to chat with some reporters as the rest of his teammates headed out to practice.
That alone, Brown's energy and lack of limp, should be a good sign for Brown as he plans to be activated off of injured reserve. After being placed on IR after the season opener , the Patriots were set to have Brown miss at least four games.
Reports also mentioned that he could end up missing six games, but based on how Brown is looking, his timetable could end up being on the shorter end of that.
A.J. Brown just walked into the locker room with cleats on. Once again, no limp. Had a small tape job on his right ankle.
Brown still has to miss the Patriots' Week 5 battle against the Las Vegas Raiders, and the team is only focused on that game right now.
"He won't be out there today, I can promise you that because he's not eligible," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "I can only speak to what I know for today."
The Patriots receivers getting banged up in recent weeks only makes this potential return that much bigger. Mack Hollins, who immediately stepped up after Brown's injury in Seattle, suffered a calf injury in Week 4 and has yet to practice this week.
Once both those guys are healthy, this group can finally attack the season like they did during the kickoff game. Before Brown got hurt, the Patriots looked like they were on their way to beat the Seahawks. Instead, Maye threw three interceptions in the fourth quarter post-injury and left the Patriots in a 0-1 hole.
"Excited to get A.J. back here in a little bit, and hopefully Mack can get back here as soon as possible," Efton Chism III said this week. "We love our room, we love our team."
Chism has stepped up without Brown on the field, a good sign for the depth that this wide receiver possesses. But getting the WR1 back in the fold — where a budding chemistry with Maye was built in traning camp — can help unlock a Patriots offense that's had a bit of trouble at times this season.

title: Patriots Safety Duo Getting More Comfortable Each Week
full_text:
FOXBORO — On Wednesday, both of the New England Patriots ' starting safeties spoke to reporters at their lockers. They spoke about carrying over confidence from game to game, preparing for the Las Vegas Raiders offense they'll be facing on Sunday and clinching the win last week with an interception.
But for Kevin Byard and Craig Woodson, both of them have begun to form a deep bond on the field as they man the last line of the Patriots' defensive backfield. Through three games together, they've combined for 19 tackles, three pass breakups and Woodson's interception put the 29-26 win in Buffalo on ice .
Despite Woodson missing one game with a shoulder injury, he's starting to get more and more comfortable playing alongside the veteran Byard — and vice versa.
"We definitely have chemistry," Woodson told Patriots On SI. "I think for us, we talk all the time and we see a lot of things the same, so I think it makes us play faster."
Woodson shined as a rookie a year ago , and now he's being given an otherworldly mentor in Byard, who led the NFL in interceptions a season ago. Byard, a captain in his first season with New England, has continued to earn the respect of his young counterpart.
And that feeling is mutual. Getting Woodson back only helped a Patriots defense that started the year off strong. That was evident in how the team responded from their Week 3 drubbing in Jacksonville.
"It was awesome," Byard said. "Obviously Craig is another player that we trust on that can go out there and make plays. I think for what we both bring, just being versatile as far as our disguise and different things that we can do. ... It was good to have him back for sure."
The Raiders lean on their tight ends a lot. Both Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer have been big parts of how they've gotten off to a 3-1 start this season, and having bigger bodies on the field could put some additional pressure on the safeties. It's helped Kirk Cousins soldify himself back as a starting quarterback and have the Raiders thickly in the AFC conversaton four weeks in.
"I can't say enough about them," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "Really, Brock is a receiver. That's impressive — what he does at his size, the speed, the route craft, and being able to catch at the catch point. He's like a big slot receiver. He has downfield speed, he runs outward breaking routes, he runs routes like a receiver, but then also he's got the ability to double guys up inside.
"I think that Mike has really turned into a complete tight end, and everything that I think people that looked at him coming out of the draft envisioned."
How are both Woodson and Byard embracing that challenging? Head on.
"You kind of have to be good with your keys, read run/pass," Woodson said. "I think we'll get a plan together, get going and stick to that."
"We've done a good job up until this point, but this is going to be probably the biggest challenge up to this point," Byard said.

title: Why Patriots WR Efton Chism Isn't Satisfied With Breakout Performance
full_text:
FOXBORO — Efton Chism III was the talk of New England last weekend. The second-year wide receiver made two impressive catches in the Patriots' 29-26 win against the Buffalo Bills, the second one being a one-handed, game-winning touchdown .
Now Chism, who was on the receiving end of a large media scrum in front of his locker before Wednesday's practice, wants to build on what he put on the field last game in Western New York.
"For me, it’s just reset," Chism said. "The good, the bad, whatever it is, it’s getting back to my work and our work as a team. Try to stack another one."
After A.J. Brown got hurt in the season opener, it opened the door for Mack Hollins to get more snaps. Hollins became the Patriots' top target until a calf injury forced him out of the Week 4 win. That's why Chism was on the field for his touchdown, and why if Hollins isn't able to play against the Las Vegas Raiders this week , the 24-year-old might end up with a larger workload.
"You never know when you're gonna get those opportunites," Chism said. "Excited to get A.J. back here in a little bit, and hopefully Mack can get back here as soon as possible. We love our room, we love our team."
Chism has shown that his hands — whether he's using both of them or just one — are solid and he's starting to build that chemistry with Drake Maye as the year progress. Right now, he's tallying four receptions for 41 yards and that one touchdown in a reserve role. That could easily change in the next few games .
Above Chism on the depth chart is Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams — though it appears Chism has surpassed Williams in terms of snaps played. While Williams ' speed is a nice addition to the offense, there really isn't a part of the offense that easily lends itself to getting the ball into his hands.
We've now seen how Chism can perform under pressure, and it will only allow him to get on the field more. Hollins is working towards getting back on the field for Week 5, though he didn't participate in the Patriots ' first practice.
Chism's teammates have seen his process and if his output in Buffalo didn't impress you, maybe the quotes from his quarterback will.
"Yeah, it's been awesome. Seeing Chiz just come in and be the same guy," Maye said. "He's been doing a lot of the little things that I think were just showing up.
"He comes in every day, enjoys trying to see my side of things, asks questions and tries to get on the same page, and that's what ends up happening. You start seeing the results."

title: Patriots Week 5 Injury Report: Offensive Starter Returns, Top CBs Remain Out
full_text:
FOXBORO — It was not a great day attendance-wise for the New England Patriots for their first practice of the week. Eight players, including several starters, didn't suit up as the 2-2 Patriots turn ahead to the Las Vegas Raiders.
Two of the their best defensive players — Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore — missed last week's win over the Buffalo Bills. Were they ready to go for Wednesday?
"I don’t expect Gonzo to be back out there today. Christian (Barmore) may do some things," Mike Vrabel shared before practice kicked off.
The initial injury report felt like a CVS receipt after one day. On Thursday, it got a little bit better. Here are all the Patriots dealing with injuries ahead of their Week 5 game against the Raiders.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle/knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (calf)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (shoulder)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (neck)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (hamstring)
S Brenden Schooler - NFI list
And looking to the other side, here are all the Raiders banged up on their first injury report of the week:
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (concussion)
Rhamondre Stevenson got banged up in the final moments of the Bills win, and it's bled into this week of practice. The sixth-year veteran was limited on Wednesday with a knee injury and wasn't spotted during the media-available portion of the practice.
On Thursday, he suited up in pads while reporters were in the locker room. Stevenson remained limited on the injury report, but the fact that he returned is a good sign for if he'll play on Sunday.
"There's a chance he can play. There's just no chance that he'll practice (Wednesday," Vrabel said.
If Stevenson isn't able to play, the team has TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner on the active roster, and Lan Larison on the practice squad. They also hosted free agent Jamaal Williams on a visit earlier in the week.
Gonzalez , Davis, Prunty and Canada were all absent from practice, leaving the Patriots with just four healthy cornerbacks. Marcus Jones, Charles Woods (who was limited with a stinger he suffered last week), Kindle Vildor and Al'Zillion Hamilton — who signed to the practice squad yesterday — were the only ones repping in positional drills.
Although the Raiders don't have a very deep receiver room (Tre Tucker has the most receptions out of any receiver with 15), their tight end duo of Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer is how the passing game makes its money.
We'll have a better understanding of this group moving throughout the week, but seeing how banged up it is right now, it could be a tad concerning. Canada missed last week, and Prunty — who didn't look injured in Buffalo — walked into the locker room with a sleeve on his left leg. This will be the biggest storyline of the week for New England.
On Thursday, Canada returned to the field in a limited capacity. He offers special teams versatility, but it might be another missed game for him. The Patriots did add some depth in the secondary, promoting safety Mike Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Brown had a large role on special teams against the Bills.
After four weeks, players who have been on injured reserve to open up the season are able to return to the practice field. Now that Week 5 is approaching, does the team plan to activate any of them this week?
"I just think that with the uncertainty here, that probably won’t happen," Vrabel said. "I wouldn’t anticipate that happening. Those guys have all worked really hard to get back, and it’s just where the situation is with the roster and trying to figure out what we need to do. So, we’ll probably not start those guys practicing."
The Patriots currently have offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, linebacker Khalil Jacobs and punter Bryce Baringer all on IR that are able to return. They also have edge rusher Harold Landry (physically unable to perform) and safety Brenden Schooler (non-football injury list) both able to play, though Schooler appears much further along to return than Landry.
There are still two open roster spots on the active roster after the Patriots placed edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins on IR and released edge rusher Jose Ramirez.

title: Patriots Get Worrisome News on Practice Field, Especially at Cornerback
full_text:
FOXBORO — Banged up would certainly be one way to describe how the New England Patriots looked at their first practice of the week. As they took the field to prep for the Las Vegas Raiders, they were missing eight players — half of them at one positions.
Christian Gonzalez, who continues to deal with a shoulder injury that kept him out of last week's win over Buffalo, remained on the sideline. Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were also missing. Canada was a late scratch from last week after suffering a hamstring injury.
Prunty didn't appear to get banged up in the team's 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills last week , but did walk into the locker room late during media availability and was sporting a sleeve on his left leg.
The Patriots were also without Rhamondre Stevenson, Mack Hollins, Reggie Gilliam and Morgan Moses. Christian Barmore, who missed last week with a shoulder injury, returned.
Long story short, it was another shorthanded day from Foxboro. Gonzalez's absence is something to monitor this week, as the team's top defensive player has consistently dealt with injuries throughout his young career.
As a rookie in 2023, he missed 13 with a torn labrum before missing one the next season with a concussion. Gonzalez also injured his hamstring last summer, forcing him to sit out the first three games of the season. If Gonzalez misses this week , it will be his second-straight game missed, and 19th game missed since being drafted.
Certainly there was some cornerbacks dressed, right? The Patriots had exactly three of them practicing, and one of them hasn't even been on the team for a full 24 hours.
The three were Marcus Jones, and practice squaders Kindle Vildor and Al'Zillion Hamilton. Jones is a mainstay and will continue to be that way. Vildor, who was elevated to the game day roster last weekend, worked as the CB2, while the rookie Hamilton took part in his first practice since signing with the team on Tuesday .
Next week, the Patriots play host to the Raiders — who aren't that deep at receiver. So while that might be good news, the pair of tight ends that the Raiders utilize (Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer) are a major factor in the passing game.
The Raiders are also sitting pretty at 3-1, one of the biggest surprises in the NFL to this point in the season. A lot of that comes from how they've operated offensively. If the foursome of Gonzalez, Davis, Prunty and Canada all can't go, that could be an issue.
"The (Raiders) offense really stays committed to what they want to do, which is run the football to find their playmakers," Mike Vrabel said prior to practice. "They've got a great group of big skill players, and I think Kirk (Cousins) has done a great job of understanding when to throw the ball, when to keep the ball down the field and when to get it to guys that are uncovered underneath."
New England's first injury report of the week will be announced later today.

title: Saints DC Doesn't Hold Back in Response to Troy Aikman
full_text:
New Orleans Saints defensive coordinator Brandon Staley pushed back Thursday against criticism from ESPN analyst Troy Aikman , who said during a 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons that Staley "didn't have any answers" for Atlanta's rushing attack.
The Saints (1-3) surrendered five rushing touchdowns and 205 yards on the ground while playing without linebacker Kaden Elliss and edge rushers Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings . Staley acknowledged his responsibility for the outcome, but stated the comments bothered him "because they're not true."
“I did hear those comments, and I have no idea what he’s talking about.” #Saints DC Brandon Staley addresses Troy Aikman’s comments from Monday Night’s broadcast. pic.twitter.com/mukvaI6DMO
Bijan Robinson had 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns while Brian Robinson had 14 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns.
"It was a tough night for us, and certainly, I'm responsible. I'm calling the defense, but we've got a great group of guys," Staley said. "No one defended that runner last year better than us. He's a hell of a player. But our group defended him twice last year better than anyone through his time in the NFL."
Staley said he had heard Aikman's comments but had "no idea" what he was talking about as he alluded to how the Saints held Bijan Robinson to just 33 and 70 yards in both meetings last season.
With 2:43 left in the third quarter of the "Monday Night Football" broadcast, Aikman weighed in, highlighting missing personnel up front.
"Brandon Staley, he just simply doesn't have any answers. And I think he knew it when we talked to him coming in," Aikman said. "I think he knew. He didn't tell us, but the guys that are out ... their big edge rushers and guys who can play the run and set the edge, they're not on the field, and they just don't have that star defender that can erase mistakes for other people.
"This was a matchup issue coming into this game, and it's proven true."
Aikman also criticized the team's effort on Atlanta's fifth rushing touchdown and the third by Brian Robinson, noting that players were "standing around watching the play, missed tackles, just bad football."
Addressing the defensive breakdown, Staley noted that Bijan Robinson's 59-yard run on the third play was a "shock to everybody," but defended his unit's overall effort.
"There were plenty of good moments in there in the first half, but after that possession, it was really up and down," Staley said. "We did not play a good game after that fourth-down penalty. We never got our rhythm back as a defense. And that's what stood out to me. And that's why I say it was very uncharacteristic of us because, since I've been here, we've been very steady. But that game got away from us."
"Our guys have played the right way," Staley added regarding effort. "And mainly that's assignment, technique, effort, all in one. I think the other night, we were missing two out of the three. Our effort was there."
"We're focusing on Minnesota, learning the tough lessons from the other night," Staley said as the Saints prepare to host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. "We've got the right guys to bounce back."

title: Kellen Moore and Saints Have a Serious Problem After Falcons Humiliation
full_text:
Before the season, the New Orleans Saints had high expectations after a strong finish to the 2025 season and with one of the best young quarterbacks in the league, Tyler Shough .
However, the second season of the Kellen Moore era has not gotten off to the start the organization wanted. After a 1-1 start featuring an upset win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2, the Saints have lost their last two games—falling in a fourth-quarter collapse to the Las Vegas Raiders and getting blown out by the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football.
The loss to Atlanta has seemingly broken the dam. It was an embarrassing 45-24 loss on a night commemorating the 20th anniversary of Domecoming. TV networks, the city, the franchise and the league designated the game as a celebration of the night that rebirthed New Orleans.
Then, the Saints laid an egg in front of 73,000 fans, with former players such as Drew Brees and Steve Gleason and members of the 2006 team watching by a national audience.
What is going on with the Saints?
Slow starts remain a defining flaw of the Moore era for the Saints.
In 2025, New Orleans was outscored 122-29 in the first quarter. This minus-93 differential routinely forced the team to play from behind, despite second-half improvements after Shough took over at quarterback.
The issue persists in 2026. A Week 3 touchdown pass from Shough to Juwan Johnson against Las Vegas provided the Saints with a 6-3 first-quarter lead—their first under Moore and their first since Dec. 8, 2024, ending a 23-game drought.
However, the momentum proved brief. Against Atlanta on Monday night, New Orleans fell behind 24-7 at halftime following an early Falcons touchdown, a quick three-and-out, and a lone second-quarter score, ultimately losing 45-24.
Moore noted postgame that the team has tried various approaches to resolve the issue but has not yet found a solution.
"We have tried a number of different things," Moore said. "Obviously, we have to solve this. We have to find a way."
Dating back to 2025, the Saints continue to struggle early, leaving them constantly playing catch-up.
The Saints' secondary entered the season with legitimate questions, and four games have done little to provide answers.
New Orleans has talent on the back end, but the unit has struggled to prevent explosive plays and has compounded those mistakes with penalties, missed tackles and breakdowns at critical moments. Those issues were on full display against Atlanta, when Michael Penix Jr. needed only 20 attempts to throw for 223 yards and a touchdown. He averaged 11.2 yards per attempt and completed 75% of his passes despite Atlanta leaning heavily on its running game.
Cornerbacks Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley had particularly difficult nights. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF) data, Riley allowed four receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown as the nearest defender, while McKinstry allowed two catches for 60 yards and committed two penalties. They finished with overall PFF grades of 28.0 and 29.5, respectively.
The problems extend well beyond one game.
Through four games, McKinstry has been targeted 22 times, allowing 13 receptions for 209 yards and one touchdown. He has surrendered four first downs while forcing four incompletions.
Riley has faced 21 targets, allowing 11 receptions for 142 yards and three touchdowns. He has allowed three first downs and forced three incompletions. The three touchdowns allowed are particularly concerning considering Riley has been targeted only 21 times.
The Saints haven't received much better production from their safeties.
Jonas Sanker has been targeted 19 times and allowed 17 receptions for 161 yards and a touchdown. He has yet to force an incompletion or allow a first down, according to PFF's charting.
Veteran Justin Reid has also struggled to consistently hold up in coverage. Opposing quarterbacks have completed 13 of 15 passes for 111 yards and a touchdown when targeting him. Like Sanker, Reid has not recorded a forced incompletion or allowed a first down through four games.
Combined, McKinstry, Riley, Sanker, Reid and Julian Blackmon have surrendered 57 receptions on 79 targets for 657 yards with seven touchdowns and only one interception. That is a 70.1% completion rate, with the five defensive backs combining for only seven forced incompletions.
If there is one defensive problem that should concern the Saints even more than their secondary, it's their inability to stop the run.
The warning signs were already there before Monday night. New Orleans entered Week 4 allowing 128.7 rushing yards per game, 27th in the NFL. Atlanta then turned that weakness into a full-blown disaster.
The Falcons rushed for 205 yards and five touchdowns on 35 carries, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt. Bijan Robinson accounted for 145 yards and two touchdowns, while Brian Robinson Jr. added 62 yards and three scores.
Worse, the Saints were overwhelmed immediately.
Bijan Robinson ripped off a 59-yard touchdown on Atlanta's third offensive play, setting the tone for an evening in which New Orleans never found an answer. The Falcons didn't need deception or a complicated offensive formula. They repeatedly attacked a defensive front that couldn't maintain its gaps or consistently finish tackles.
And this wasn't an isolated performance. New Orleans has now allowed 165, 108, 113 and 205 rushing yards through its first four games. That's 591 yards overall, an average of nearly 147.8 yards per game, which is 30th out of 32 teams in the NFL. The only two teams that have a worse rushing defense than the Saints are the Dallas Cowboys and NFC South rival Carolina Panthers .
There is a difference between losing games and losing the fanbase. Moore may be dangerously close to the latter.
Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Falcons felt like more than another defeat for a Saints team that has fallen to 1-3. New Orleans was embarrassed at home by its biggest rival on a night meant to celebrate the 20th anniversary of Domecoming, and the frustration inside the Caesars Superdome was impossible to ignore.
Fans can tolerate a rebuilding team. They can understand injuries, growing pains and a young roster making mistakes. Who Dat Nation can tolerate a close loss where the Saints fight until the final whistle, especially given the key injuries the team faced entering the game.
What becomes much harder to accept is a team consistently looking unprepared, undisciplined or incapable of matching its opponent's intensity.
That's where Moore's problem begins.
Moore was hired to give the Saints a new direction after years of stagnation. Instead, the results are beginning to look painfully familiar.
Four games should not determine a coach's future, particularly one overseeing a roster with obvious deficiencies. But patience around Moore could disappear quickly if performances like Monday's continue, especially since everyone, from the city of New Orleans to the NFL and television networks, designated that night for New Orleans to celebrate one of the city's and franchise's greatest moments.
This loss is something that they will not forget, and given their reactions across social media , it has not been pretty.
Saints fans aren't simply asking for wins right now. They're looking for evidence that the franchise is actually headed somewhere.
Against Atlanta, they didn't get much of it.

title: Saints Get Torched on Social Media After Disastrous Falcons Loss
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints picked the worst possible night to deliver their ugliest performance of the season.
With the franchise commemorating the 20th anniversary of its emotional return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina, the Saints were dominated by their biggest rival, falling 45-24 to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night.
And Saints fans were not shy about expressing their frustration afterward.
The Falcons rushed for a dominant 205 yards after Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson ran roughshod over the Saints’ depleted and fatigued defense.
Bijan Robinson spearheaded the ground attack with 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns, delivering explosive plays throughout the night. Meanwhile, Brian Robinson provided a powerful complementary punch, finishing with 14 carries for 62 yards and finding the end zone three times to anchor Atlanta's physical offensive showing.
