title: Steelers Get Good and Bad Injury News With Two Starters
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers received both positive and negative injury news ahead of their Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts.
According to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, safety DeShon Elliott is set to have his 21-day practice window opened on October 8 while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
McCarthy added that Elliott will initially register as a limited participant in practice.
On the flip side, McCarthy also told reporters that wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. is slated to miss multiple weeks with his foot injury, which has lingered for most of the season up to this point and has now been aggravated.
McCarthy noted that the team is still evaluating his roster position in light of that news, likely meaning that a stint on IR is a possibility.
Pittman Jr. missed Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots as a result of the injury, though he returned in Week 3 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals and also played in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns.
The veteran was seen with his foot propped up on a scooter in the locker room on October 7, however, which was a sign that his injury situation had worsened.
It's still up in the air as to whether or not Elliott will be activated from IR this week and thus miss just the minimum of four games.
Being active vs. Indianapolis does feel ambitious, though it doesn't appear as though that possibility can be completely ruled out just yet.
The Steelers have a clear need in their secondary, and adding a proven starter like Elliott back into the mix (whenever the time comes) next to Jaquan Brisker at safety would allow the team to further limit Rayshawn Jenkins' playing time while also not putting too much pressure on rookie Robert Spears-Jennings to go out and perform on defense.
As for Pittman Jr., his absence will open up more opportunities for Germie Bernard over the next handful of weeks.
The second-round pick logged 45 snaps against the Patriots when Pittman Jr. was out and played that exact number over the next two weeks combined (per Pro Football Focus ), so he should be in for quite the jump in reps.
DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson would still seem to profile as Pittsburgh's top-two options at the receiver position for the time being, however.

title: Seahawks, 49ers Release Final Injury Report With Key Game Statuses
full_text:
Yesterday provided some drama, in the form of two stars missing practice . So now, both the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks are providing their final word on who will be available and who won’t be on Sunday, at least until the hours before kickoff. Let’s run it down and get a sense of what this weekend might hold in store for us.
Opening up with the Seahawks, the big relief was the lack of any game status for Leonard Williams (ankle), which means he is good to go. I won’t pretend that he’s 100%, but this is about the best you could hope for after yesterday’s missed practice. Also in the clear is Ty Okada (hamstring), Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle) , and Tyrice Knight (ankle).
In fact, the only players who are unknown at the moment are George Holani (ribs) and Irv Charles (knee), both questionable. Based on what we’ve seen from George recently, he’s clearly not all there, but the team desperately needs running backs. Charles being questionable already is a great sign, and I look for him to inject life into this special teams unit.
The players declared out were Zach Charbonnet (knee) , Chazz Surratt (calf), and Julian Neal (hamstring). Charbonnet was declared unavailable this week days ago, Surratt got injured in practice last week, and Neal is a new addition to the injury ranks. Given where we were less than 24 hours ago, this is a great spot for the Seattle Seahawks.
San Francisco has a mixed report today. Starting with the good, Mike Evans (ribs) has no game designation and will be playing. Like Leonard, I won’t suggest he’s fully healthy. In fact, he’s probably in a lot of pain. But he’s toughing it out. Kaelon Black (illness), Jaden Dugger (shoulder), and Romello Height (hand) are good as well.
The things we don’t yet know concern two defenders that the 49ers are counting on this weekend. Upton Stout (shoulder) and Mykel Williams (knee) are questionable. My understanding is that Stout didn’t practice today, so I’m expecting Stout to sit and Williams to go. We’ll probably find out 90 minutes before kickoff, but that’s my current read.
The bad is mostly straightforward. Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Kyle Juszczyk (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle) and James Thompson (ankle) are out, as they were assumed to be earlier this week. Just because it was known doesn’t make it any less devastating, of course, as the 49ers are missing a lot of pieces they were counting on to win games like this.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About 49ers vs. Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The last time the San Francisco 49ers lost a football game, it was at Lumen Field in the 2025 NFC Divisional Playoffs. The Seattle Seahawks rolled to a 41-6 win, then knocked off the Los Angeles Rams and the New England Patriots on the way to winning Super Bowl LX .
Kyle Shanahan’s club is one of three teams that have not lost a game this season. The 49ers are ranked seventh in the league in both total offense and total defense, and only the Buffalo Bills had scored more points in the first four weeks of the season. The Seahawks have allowed the fewest total yard and passing yards per game in the NFL.
But how’s this for an oddity? While the Niners were handed their lunch at Seattle in the 2025 playoffs, Shanahan’s team has won its last four regular-season games at Lumen Field.
Rashid Shaheed with a 95 YARD KICKOFF TOUCHDOWN WITHIN 13 SECONDS 🏈🤯 49ers 0-7 Seahawks pic.twitter.com/Kv65759t5c
The franchises first met in 1976 during the Seahawks’ debut season in the NFL. Seattle was placed in the NFC West that year, then moved to the AFC West a year later where the team remained until realignment in 2002.
Including three postseason encounters, the ‘Hawks own a 33-24 overall lead in the series, including a 31-20 mark since ’02. A year ago, the clubs met three times for the second time in four seasons.
In Week 1 at Lumen Field, Seahawks’ quarterback lost a fumble in the closing minute deep in Niners’ territory and San Francisco held on for a 17-13 win. In the teams’ regular season finale at Levi’s Stadium, Seattle’s defense was the difference in a 13-3 victory. Two weeks later in the divisional round, Rashid Shaheed returned the opening kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown, Macdonald’s club opened up a 17-0 first-quarter lead and Seattle coasted to a stunning 41-6 victory.
Simply put, the Niners have not allowed a sack during their unbeaten start. Led by Leonard Williams (3.0) and Derick Hall (2.0), Seattle has totaled 11.0 sacks in four outings—the seventh-most in the league. The ‘Hawks have totaled two-plus QB traps in each game, and comes off a season-high four sacks in the 30-23 win over the Chargers.
Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has only played nine quarters of football this season, and has thrown a combined six touchdown passes the last two weeks. However, he has also served up three interceptions, including a pick-six vs. Washington. Last Sunday vs. the Chargers, his first pass attempt of the afternoon was intercepted.
Emanuel Wilson's first TD as a Seahawk! 🔥 @LACvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RVKrkhoLku
In three games vs. the Seahawks a season ago, including the 41-6 playoff loss at Seattle, Shanahan’s team scored a total of 26 points. The 49ers averaged 264.3 total yards per game and their offense managed only two touchdowns, both in the Week 1 win at Seattle. The Niners gave up a half-dozen sacks and turned over the football six times.
While Super Bowl LX Kenneth Walker III is busy leading the league in rushing for the Chiefs, running back Emanuel Wilson leads the Seahawks with 53 carries and 190 yards, and has scored two total TDs. Jadarian Price (on IR) and George Holani have combined for 50 attempts and 189 yards on the ground, and neither has reached the end zone.

title: 5 Score Predictions for 49ers vs. Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready for their Week 5 matchup as they host the San Francisco 49ers for their second NFC West contest of the season.
The Seahawks are 1-0 in the division after beating the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2, while the Niners come into the contest 2-0 in the NFC West and 4-0 overall.
Some members of the Seattle Seahawks On SI staff predicted the outcome for the game and explained their reasoning.
The last two times the Niners faced the Seahawks, they scored a total of nine points and didn't score a touchdown in either contest. The challenge for Seattle's defense on Sunday is not only slowing Christian McCaffrey, but harassing Brock Purdy. San Francisco has not given up a sack during its 4-0 start. The 'Hawks will settle for five field goals and one touchdown and hand Kyle Shanahan's club their first loss of the season.
This is going to be a close game either way. I think the Seahawks are going to struggle running the ball in this one, which is what leads to the loss. This game could be very reminiscent of the Washington Commanders matchup back in Week 3. The Seahawks give up an early score and are forced to come from behind by abandoning the run and going through the air. While Jaxon Smith-Njigba helps the Seahawks' cause, the Niners have enough playmakers on offense to get it done.
This will be a tough one as both the Seahawks and 49ers are top 10 in points scored on offense as well as points surrendered on defense. Fans will remember Seattle torching the Niners in the playoffs last year, but this game is going to be much closer than that. Being at home, the Seahawks have the edge.
The Seahawks have their toughest test of the season with the 49ers. Luckily, the 49ers have their toughest test of the season too. San Francisco will allow its first sack of the season to Seattle and allow three total sacks, led by DeMarcus Lawrence and Nick Emmanwori. Sam Darnold might be the biggest surprise and find ways to get the ball to JSN for a big game.
Mike Macdonald's defense has a good handle on the 49ers offense and their lack of a speed threat to take the top off the defense means you can keep them in a box close to the line of scrimmage. The Seahawks offense struggles to run the ball but Darnold makes enough plays to win.

title: Why the Seahawks Could Give 49ers' Brock Purdy a Rough Performance
full_text:
Week 5 will be a huge opportunity for many teams this season. For the Seattle Seahawks (3-1), it’s an opportunity for them to make a statement win against an NFC West Divisional opponent as they host the San Francisco 49ers (4-0) on Sunday. The 49ers already got a statement win over a divisional opponent after defeating the heavily favored Los Angeles Rams 27-7 on Thursday Night Football in Week 1.
​Seattle takes on a dangerous San Francisco team that is not only a legitimate Super Bowl contender, despite the countless injuries, but also has league MVP-caliber performances from quarterback Brock Purdy. The 49ers have taken down some great teams with tough defenses, but Purdy’s bad luck against the Seahawks could continue in Week 5.
​ The 49ers go into Week 5 without their starting fullback Kyle Juszczyk . This likely forces San Francisco to go into the game utilizing a 12-personnel, which is one running back and two tight ends. One of the key aspects of the 49ers’ offense is motions and the usage of their fullback in the run game and passing game. San Francisco’s offense could be too predictable for the Seahawks, which might be a problem for Purdy.
​In the last four games versus the Seahawks , including the 41-6 Divisional Round win for Seattle this past January, Purdy completed 69.2% for only an average of 175.8 yards, three touchdowns, five interceptions and eight sacks. The Seahawks know how to get Purdy to throw interceptions and suppress him in a limited offense.
​Seattle is 3-1 in the last four games where its defense has held Purdy to under 160 passing yards. The Seahawks are coming into this deep with the league’s top-ranked passing offense (144.8) thanks to their ability to take away the deep passing game.
While cornerback Riq Woolen has been a great player for the Philadelphia Eagles’ defense, but Josh Jobe fits the Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense’s philosophies and schemes more. Seattle is also seeing Pro-Bowl caliber performances from cornerback Devon Witherspoon and safety Julian Love .
​Seattle has sacked Purdy eight times in the last four games. The Seahawks are coming off their best pass-rushing game of the season in the 30-23 Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , where they accounted for four sacks and nine tackles for loss. The Seahawks tormented Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert with 10 quarterback hits and still had some rough moments because of penalties.
​The 49ers haven’t allowed a sack through the first four games of the season. The Denver Broncos weren’t able to sack Purdy, but Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen accounted for three quarterback hits. San Francisco also faced an unmotivated and jet-lagged Rams defense. Even if the Seahawks can’t sack Purdy in the backfield because of his ability to escape the pressure, the Seahawks have the linebacker and defensive backs to defend the short-to-mid-range passing game.
​The Seahawks are coming off two games where they wanted to play better, encountered a defensive players-only meeting , and they heard all of the noise from the 49ers coming into this matchup. The Dark Side Defense will be motivated to bring down a 49ers team they are familiar with and know the weaknesses of.

title: Sam Darnold Has a Big Opportunity This Week vs 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have a pretty clear Plan A on offense. They want to run the ball, get into favorable third downs, and have Sam Darnold hit throws off play action. It’s a formula that won them a lot of games last season, including the super bowl. But right now, they need to find a Plan B, because I doubt that formula is going to produce success.
We all know how bad things are in the backfield for the Seahawks right now . At the moment, you have Emanuel Wilson starting, a limited back who doesn’t fit the offensive scheme. Behind him is George Holani, similarly limited and clearly playing injured. Then, Velus Jones Jr, who isn’t really a running back. Robert Henry Jr, who just got here a few days ago.
On top of that dismal lineup, the run blocking hasn’t been particularly strong so far this season. We saw some improvements against the Chargers, but there’s not much for these backs to work with. Anthony Bradford is missed, and the lack of a true fullback is a problem. So being run-first right now is a recipe for running into a brick wall and ending up in third and long.
So, what do the Seahawks do? You get aggressive, let Sam Darnold sling it , and try to hit bigger plays. This week’s opponent, the San Francisco 49ers, can be had through the air. They have one of the worst pass rushes in football with Nick Bosa on the sideline, and are down at least one defensive back starter. The opportunity will be there.
Furthermore, so far this year, opposing defenses have been mostly happy to stack the box and play the run aggressively, believing that the quarterback (be it Drew Lock or Sam Darnold) won’t be able to punish it. I believe the 49ers will probably do it as well. At some point, you have to punish it. They did last season. We need more of that.
If (when) Sam Darnold pushes for a contract extension this offseason in the range of $55 to $60 million a year, I’m going to think about games like this one. A divisional game, with first place at stake, where Sam can’t just game-manage his way to a victory. A game where his ability to hit big plays and make crucial throws to put points up will likely determine the result.
I can pay $30 to $35 million a year to a solid quarterback who needs a clean process and structure to win games. But to climb up to the top of the market? I want to see you win when you need to put the team on your back. And this weekend feels like a ‘put the team on your back’ opportunity for Sam Darnold. Succeed with a high volume of pass attempts.
He’d done it before. Last year’s NFC Championship Game is the most obvious example, a game where most of the team didn’t perform up to standard but Darnold did. But we need to see it more, especially against division rivals. If turnovers happen, then so be it . I want to see a confident quarterback this weekend, willing to make big throws.

title: 3 Bold Predictions For Seahawks vs. 49ers in Week 5
full_text:
Week 5 provides the Seattle Seahawks with an excellent opportunity. They're set to host the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers , who are one of the final three unbeaten teams in the 2026 season.
They're also an NFC West rival and are currently leading the division with the 3-1 Seahawks looking up at them in the standings. Getting a win would be huge since it would not only hand the Niners a loss, but it would give them the head-to-head tiebreaker, meaning they would be the leaders in the division.
It won't be easy, but the Seahawks know how to defeat the 49ers, having done so twice last year, including once in the playoffs. Their chances of securing that win become much greater, especially if these three bold predictions come true.
Despite being rivals, there are some strong ties between the Seahawks and 49ers. That includes Sam Darnold, who played for San Francisco during the 2023 season. Seattle offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is also a former Niner, employed as an assistant coach from 2019 to 2025 before taking his new role with the Seahawks.
Their familiarity with the 49ers will help them as Fleury and Darnold enter this one with a strong game plan. In this bold prediction, that leads to a strong showing with Darnold tossing 300 yards against his former team.
Julian Love was off to a hot start this season, with interceptions in each of the first two games. A calf injury kept him out in Week 3, but he was back in Week 4 and had five tackles and a pass defense. If the Seahawks are going to win this one, they will need Love to step up and that's what he does in this prediction. Not only does he get another interception, but he helps out his offense by recording his first pick-six of the year.
During the win against the Chargers, Jaxon Smith-Njigba had an "off" game. He finished with five receptions for 76 yards, which is nothing to scoff at, but for him, it was subpar . It was not only the first game where JSN didn't top 100 yards this season, but it was also the first where he didn't score a touchdown. In this final bold prediction, he makes up for that by recording at least 100 yards receiving while scoring two touchdowns.

title: Seahawks Injury Report Gives Cause for Concern on Both Sides
full_text:
After what looked like a fairly straightforward and clear injury picture for both teams this Sunday, Thursday brought some plot twists. The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers will both be sweating out the final reports tomorrow after Thursday exposed some serious issues. So, who is in danger of missing Sunday’s crucial affair?
There were only two DNPs today for the Seahawks, and one of them was Chazz Surratt (calf), so at first it didn't look so bad. But Leonard Williams (ankle) was the other, after practicing some yesterday, which makes one wonder if he’ll be available for this week. Remember, Friday is typically a lighter day, so Thursday tends to be the key practice day.
Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Irv Charles (knee) remained limited on their trek back to the roster. George Holani (ribs) and Nehemiah Pritchett (ankle) are still there too. Joining them are Julian Neal (hamstring) and Ernest Jones IV on a rest day. Not ideal, but the signs are good for them to be at least available against the 49ers.
Tyrice Knight (ankle) graduated to full practice, as did Beau Stephens (knee) and the previously resting Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Patrick O’Connell (thumb) and Ty Okada (hamstring) remained full participants. It’s not bad overall, but Big Cat’s absence looms massive. Hopefully, this is a move to account for a Thursday game the following week.
The alarm bell for the 49ers was Mike Evans (ribs) missing practice, although it seems to be more a question of pain mitigation, and he plans to play. Not that there’s anything good about your top receiver being in so much pain he can’t practice. Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Kyle Juszczyk (knee), Marques Sigle (ankle) and James Thompson (ankle) all remain out too.
Mykel Williams (knee) is still limited and on track to make his season debut. The good news for San Fran, however, is Upton Stout (shoulder) getting in some work, putting him on a decent track to play. A crucial player in their secondary, Stout was one of the big question marks yesterday. The rest is fairly simple.
Dre Greenlaw , Christian McCaffrey , and Trent Williams returned from rest days to practice in full, Kaelon Black (illness) is feeling well enough to get back on the field, and Jaden Dugger (shoulder) and Romello Height (hand) remain at full blast. Expect all of them to play on Sunday. As it turns out, we can’t have a completely drama-free week at practice.

title: 5 Burning Questions on Seahawks Trade Target Tony Pollard
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are linked to several veteran running backs on the trade market ahead of next month's deadline.
Among those players is Tennessee Titans veteran Tony Pollard, who has 54 carries for 221 yards and a touchdown through the first four games of the season. Pollard has run for over 1,000 yards in each of the last four years and could be what the Seahawks are looking for.
To learn more about Pollard, we spoke with Tennessee Titans On SI publisher Lane Mills.
Not at all. He's in the final year of his contract. Pollard does what the Titans ask of him, but he looks like the odd man out in the midst of their rebuild. It's seemed like a matter of time that Tennessee parts ways with him for a while now.
Pollard is at his best in a passing offense as an early-down back. He's not someone to throw in on a crucial third or fourth and medium, but he can reliably collect a few yards and sees the field well as a veteran.
In turn, Pollard's biggest weakness is in short-gain scenarios when defenses are expecting the run. He's not as explosive as he used to be, and Brian Daboll has struggled to make good use of him when the offense needs a big pickup. Pollard can't fully be "that guy" anymore.
Pollard is a leader, and embraces his role as a veteran. I spoke to him a few weeks ago about his role in the Titans' backfield. He embraced splitting snaps with Tyjae Spears, and shared some of the advice he passed on to rookie RB Nick Singleton. That kind of positive mindset is hugely undervalued for a player in his position.
Absolutely. Especially with Emanuel Wilson already in place , Pollard would make perfect sense as a complimentary back in Seattle's offense. Something like 10 carries for 40 yards, and he'd shine.

title: Seahawks' Defense on Verge of Greatness After Players-Only Meeting
full_text:
Week 4 against the winless Los Angeles Chargers should’ve been a get-right game for the Seattle Seahawks. While the Seahawks won convincingly 30-23, they shot themselves in the foot to do it . Between the countless penalties and dumb mistakes, it allowed the Chargers to push for a potential game-winning final drive.
​The game was saved thanks to a strip-sack from former Charger and starting edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu. Seattle is preparing for a huge divisional matchup against the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). The Dark Side Defense can’t afford making penalties and dumb mistakes to give the 49ers’ talented offense more chances. The Seahawks’ defensive players are taking every chance they get to improve with a players-only meeting on defense.
​Veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed told the media that the Seahawks’ defensive leaders called a defensive players-only meeting. The meeting’s purpose was to eliminate plays that could become penalties or anything that could give the 49ers life. Linebacker Ernest Jones IV, defensive tackle Leonard Williams, safety Julian Love and Reed were the ones who called for the meeting.
There are worse reasons for teams to hold player-only meetings. The Seahawks are still one of the top teams in the league despite the ugly loss to the Washington Commanders. Seattle is fifth in the league in points allowed per game (18.3). Its defense is also first in passing yards allowed per game (144.8), total yards allowed per game (246.8) and first in tackles for loss (28).
​10 of the Seahawks’ 14 penalties were on the defense or the special teams’ defending unit . A good portion of those penalties didn’t need to be called by Scott Novak and his officiating crew, who had a questionable performance of judging plays, but the Seahawks can’t give any reasons why they need to be flagged. Edge rusher Derick Hall’s late hit and nickel Nick Emmanwori’s unnecessary roughness are two types of penalties that the defensive leaders want to shed.
​The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense arguably played some of its worst performances through the first few weeks of the season. Giving up 27 points to the Commanders’ short passing scheme wasn’t good. The Seahawks’ mistakes resulting in penalties weren’t a good substitute either. This player-only meeting should not only bring the defenders more focus, but also more determination to strive for perfection.
​This defense is among the best in the league in nearly all major statistics and they haven’t been fully healthy. There is a great chance that starting free safety Ty Okada will make his first appearance this season after missing four games with a calf injury.
Williams, Love and Jones are playing at a Pro Bowl caliber level . Emmanwori is 100% healthy and is being utilized at every major defensive area of the field. The Seahawks haven’t even seen the best out of cornerback Devon Witherspoon and defensive tackle Byron Murphy II yet.
​Seattle’s defense has to be ready for its toughest test yet. It will face a 49ers offense that is tied for second in the league in points per game (30.5), the offensive line hasn’t given up a sack yet and quarterback Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level.
The Seahawks will be the toughest test for the 49ers and the game will be in Lumen Field. This game will be a battle of juggernauts and the Seahawks’ player-only meeting might have been their get-right moment.

title: 5 Seahawks RB Predictions for Week 5 vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will employ several running backs for their game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5.
With Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still working his way back from a torn ACL, the running back room has had to adapt every week throughout the season. The team signed Robert Henry Jr. off of the Washington Commanders practice squad to join George Holani, Emanuel Wilson and Velus Jones Jr. on the roster.
Here's a look at how each available running back could perform against the Niners.
As someone who is on the physically unable to perform list, Charbonnet is officially eligible to return to the field in Week 5 against the Niners. That doesn't necessarily mean he will be playing, however.
Charbonnet was a limited participant on the injury report this week, which puts his status up in the air for the game. The fact that the Seahawks signed another running back suggests that he may not be ready quite yet to make a return. Given that the team also has a game on Thursday Night Football in Week 6 against the Denver Broncos, the team might be looking to preserve him for that game.
Prediction: Charbonnet is not placed on the 53-man roster
Wilson crushed it as the lead back in the team's Week 4 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. He ran the ball 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown, while catching three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. Wilson proved that he can be the top option in the offense, and it is a role he could easily have against the Niners as well.
San Francisco has a much more challenging defensive front than Los Angeles, so there will be a fair set of challenges going into the week. Wilson is currently Seattle's best running back, so the team should be handing the ball to him frequently.
Prediction: Wilson gets 15-20 carries and scores a touchdown.
Like the aforementioned Charbonnet, Holani was on the injury report this week with a rib injury. Holani has consistently been the team's backup running back throughout the season, accruing a couple of carries in each of the team's first four games. In Holani's most effective game this season, he caught five passes for 48 yards against the Washington Commanders in Week 3.
During that game, the Seahawks found themselves trailing for most of the contest. This is likely where Holani fits best, and if he were to have a larger role in the game, it would possibly be because the team is trailing. The Seahawks hope that this isn't the case, but if they were to fall behind against the 49ers, expect Holani to be catching passes out of the backfield.
Prediction: Holani plays, but only gets around five carries for 10-15 yards.
Jones was signed to the active roster after Jaden Price was placed on injured reserve just ahead of the team's Week 4 contest against the Chargers. Jones has been elevated from the practice squad twice already this season, and the team would have only had one more chance to do so. This meant it was time to bring him back onto the active roster.
In three games so far this season, Jones has been mostly a special teams player. He did appear in two snaps on offense, but special teams has been where the team has asked him to perform. This is what he should be expected to do during this matchup as well.
Prediction: Jones gets special teams snaps, but doesn't play on offense.
The Seahawks signed Henry from the Commanders' practice squad earlier in the week, hoping he would give the team some depth. The 2026 undrafted free agent out of UTSA ran the ball 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown during three games in the preseason. He did not make the team's 53-man roster but was brought back onto the practice squad.
It remains to be seen if Henry will even be active for the game, especially because he does not have much knowledge of the playbook. He's doing the best he can to make himself available, but if he were to be active, he likely won't have a very large role against the 49ers.
Prediction: Henry is inactive for his first game with the Seahawks.

title: How 49ers Can Take Advantage of Malik Mustapha Starting
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are going to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline. However, there is one player who might end up being worth selling if the price is right. Malik Mustapha has not played much in the new Raheem Morris defense after being a two-year starter for the 49ers.
The 49ers could trade the safety with starting experience if the price is right at the trade deadline.
Mustapha is a former fourth-rounder, drafted 125th overall. However, that did not stop him from seeing the field in a significant way as a rookie. Mustapha started in Week 4 and did not look back. He started 12 games in his rookie season and added 72 tackles.
Unfortunately, he tore his ACL in Week 18 of his rookie season. Mustapha missed the first six weeks of the 2025 season as he recovered from the injury. However, once he was healthy, the team started to bench rookie Marques Sigle to get Mustapha back into a full-time role.
Despite 22 starts in his first two seasons, new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris has not been as interested in getting him on the field. Mustapha missed some time in training camp, and it opened the door for Sigle to start in Week 1.
Sigle has an ankle injury , but will return in a few weeks. This could give Mustapha a chance to prove that he is valuable on the trade market in a short-term starting stint.
On one hand, the 49ers are a team with too many injuries and not enough depth. Trading a starter-caliber player, even if Sigle returns, could be unwise.
The other thought is that the team acquiring Mustapha will be adding him at a time when they have a year and a half of team control on his rookie contract. He is young and is a two-year starter.
The combination of experience, youth, team control, and a cost-effective deal would probably net more on the trade market than some would expect.
The 49ers could find a way to spin Mustapha into a player at a different position of need. They could also recoup draft capital. Given the top-heavy state of the roster and the age of some of their stars, it would not be a bad idea to try to add a few extra draft picks.
It will be interesting to see how the 49ers handle Mustapha.

title: Why the 49ers Will Beat the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The Seahawks destroyed the 49ers the past two times these teams played each other, but both are decidedly different teams now.
Those 49ers had Jauan Jennings and Ricky Pearsall as their starting wide receivers. Pearsall had a PCL injury that rendered him practically useless -- not his fault, at least he played -- and Jennings got shut down both times. He caught six passes for 58 yards and no touchdowns total in both games.
This tandem's complete lack of speed allowed the Seahawks' defensive backs to attack the line of scrimmage and smother the short passes and the run game. This explains why the 49ers scored no touchdowns and reached the red zone only once in those two games against Seattle.
These 49ers have Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel as their starting wide receivers. Samuel seems completely rejuvenated, running harder than ever, he's still explosive and has scored three touchdowns in four games.
And Evans is a huge upgrade over Jennings. That's because Evans is a future Hall of Famer, and defenses must respect his size, catch radius, vertical ability and red-zone prowess. So, even when he's limited by a rib injury, as he is this week, he still alters coverages before the snap because defenses are scared of him. His mere presence on the field provides the 49ers with a schematic advantage.
Meanwhile, last season's Seahawks had Kenneth Walker, one of the best running backs in the NFL, and Klint Kubiak, one of the best offensive play callers in the league. This season's Seahawks don't have Walker anymore -- he's on the Chiefs. His replacements -- Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price -- both are injured, and neither will play on Sunday.
As a result, these Seahawks are one-dimensional on offense. And their new play caller, Brian Fleury, never has called plays before this season. And he's having trouble establishing anyone other than reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba as a legitimate weapon. That's why the Seahawks offense stinks on third down this season.
Sam Darnold is a good quarterback when he can complement a strong running game, but he can't do that this season. Now, he's the focal point of Seattle's offense, and he's turnover-prone when he's under pressure.
That's why the 49ers will beat the Seahawks on Sunday. They have a better quarterback than Seattle, a better offensive play caller than Seattle, and a more balanced offense than Seattle. And while the Seahawks have a great defense, the 49ers' defense is really good in its own right.
This will be a grim, violent, low-scoring game that will come down to field goals.

title: Mike Evans Has Revealed His True Importance to the 49ers Since Rib Injury
full_text:
Even if he is 33 years old and no longer in his prime, the San Francisco 49ers having Mike Evans on their roster is a sight to behold.
It always felt like he was going to stay with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers his whole career. But he chose to join San Francisco for less money .
Already, upon hearing that, his motivation is clearly about winning and not about the digits increasing in his checking account. But financial deals aside, Evans has shown in a completely different way what a future first-ballot Hall of Famer wide receiver adds to the locker room.
The 49ers, at least in the Kyle Shanahan era, have had their fair share of injury problems. In some cases, players play through the pain, but it's extremely rare for someone to do so and still excel.
Evans embodies the latter. He said that his injury felt like he was stabbed, yet he suited up and delivered arguably his best game with San Francisco so far. Five receptions for 76 yards against a step-up Denver Broncos team was a very good effort.
But there was little chance Evans wasn't going to play in that game. General manager John Lynch shared this week just how determined the wide receiver was to take the field.
“I remember first time in the locker room going down there – you always want to hear it for yourself – and I said, ‘Mike, good news, we’ll have you for Seattle,’” Lynch recalled on KNBR . “And he said, ‘No, I’m playing this week.’ And he said it in a way like he’s playing this week.”
And that speaks volumes. He fits the Kyle Shanahan mould of a player who is not only tough but also intensely focused on winning football matches.
Evans signed a three-year deal in free agency, but even if he's around for just one, the 49ers are incredibly lucky to have a player with his tangible achievements, as well as the drive and willingness to produce at all costs.
Actions speak far louder than words, and Evans has shown exactly what he's willing to put on the line for this team.
I'm no doctor but I advocated for him to be rested , but upon seeing his actions from the last week, it would be far from surprising seeing him gear up for the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5 and deliver yet another good performance,

title: The One Brock Purdy Stat That Could Give the 49ers an Edge vs. Seattle
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers facing the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5 presents their biggest challenge of the season so far.
The 49ers are 4-0 so far, with two wins against the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos, teams who reached the AFC and NFC Championship last season.
That's a resounding positive. Now the next big test against the Seahawks is just around the corner - the very team that defeated San Francisco in both the regular season and in the playoffs last season.
Seattle went on to win the Super Bowl. In the game against the 49ers, you could feel the game slipping away from San Francisco after the Seahawks scored a touchdown following the opening punt.
So let's be honest, they represent a huge test. They have a great team in all three phases and heading to Lumen Field is always recognized as one of the most hostile environments in the league. A victory against Seattle shows they are truly a Super Bowl contender.
There is one Brock Purdy statistic that should favor the 49ers heading into this game though.
Since becoming the 49ers' starting quarterback, Purdy has never lost a regular-season road game against Seattle. The stat suggests complete dominance over a divisional rival, and when needed, he has found ways to get the job done in these crucial matchups.
Last season provided a perfect example. Granted, it came in Week 1, when neither team had fully found its footing, but Purdy still stepped up to lead the 49ers to victory. He was later diagnosed with turf toe, making his performance all the more respectable.
So far this season, Purdy is playing like an MVP-caliber quarterback . He's elevated his game to an even higher standard and is making it look effortless. His ridiculous 2026 stat line so far speaks for itself.
Compared to last season, when the offensive line was lacking, it now appears to be the best it has ever been. Purdy should have more time in the pocket and, overall, be in a much better position to perform than he was when the 49ers were knocked out.
A win against Seattle would justify the hype surrounding the 49ers' season prospects this year . A defeat wouldn't ruin those expectations completely, but it would indicate that they're still there or thereabouts, which was ultimately what was expected heading into the season. They just need results to go their way.

title: 5 Biggest Questions Facing 49ers Against Seahawks
full_text:
With the San Francisco 49ers sitting at 4-0, they now face their biggest test of the season with a road matchup against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. What are the biggest questions the 49ers have to answer in Week 5?
The 49ers essentially have two receivers on their current roster. Mike Evans has 213 receiving yards. Deebo Samuel has 185 receiving yards. Demarcus Robinson is next with 84 yards, and he is on the IR.
Jordan Watkins currently has 60 yards, while Khadarel Hodge has 18. They need somebody to step up.
The 49ers' interior offensive line has been one of the most impressive revelations of the season. However, they are going to see a much tougher test with the Seattle Seahawks. Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams have typically had their way with this group.
Still, Connor Colby and Dominick Puni look much improved from last season . Do they hold up?
Last season it was notable that the defensive coordinator Robert Saleh did not have Lenoir move from his outside spot to follow Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Raheem Morris said that Lenoir will not follow him everywhere, but noted that they have the ability to move Lenoir around more often than they did in recent years.
The Seahawks can move Smith-Njigba around and get him away from Lenoir, but we could see more of Lenoir in the slot this week than in past years?
Morris did not draft Mykel Williams, so it will be interesting to see how he aligns in the 49ers new defense. Williams is an edge rusher, but did most of his damage along the interior last year. Morris runs more five-man fronts than Saleh did last year. So, Williams can be a five-technique as an interior base end more than we saw as a rookie.
Do we see a more versatile Williams in this defense?
The 49ers' loss of Kyle Juszczyk is magnified by the reality that Jake Tonges is hurt and the team does not have a quality third wide receiver. They have their stars at receivers, tight end, and running back. The fifth skill player is almost always going to be a weak link at the moment. How do the 49ers fix that issue?

title: One 49ers Offensive Player Who Could Make the Difference Against Seattle
full_text:
Last year, the San Francisco 49ers' biggest struggle against the Seattle Seahawks was on offense.
Scoring points against Seattle’s vaunted defense was nearly impossible in the last two matchups. However, the 49ers should have an easier time scoring against them in Week 5.
The 49ers are clicking on all cylinders this season. They’re riding quite a bit of momentum into Seattle this Sunday. One of the reasons for that is thanks to Deebo Samuel .
He’s been sensational for the 49ers in his second stint with the team. Mike Evans will be seen as a significant factor in why the 49ers are better against the Seahawks’ defense , but Samuel will be the difference-maker on offense.
Two things were lacking from the 49ers’ offense last year — explosive plays and physicality. That was desperately missed in the last two games against the Seahawks.
Samuel has brought that back to the 49ers. He's the ultimate tone setter. If you want a player to create contact and impose their will, Samuel is that guy on offense for the 49ers.
“He's a special player with the ball in his hand, and you're always looking for those,” said offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak. “The way he's punishing the defense when he touches the football, it has an effect. So, it's our job to keep getting him the ball and find ways to involve him in the game plan.”
He’s like the Dre Greenlaw of the offense, but without the penalty risk. That’s how he makes his impact, and it’s going to be desperately needed against Seattle’s physical defense.
The 49ers’ offense was bullied by the Seahawks last year. That won’t be the case. Samuel will not allow it, and he’ll make it clear on his very first touch in the game.
I think Samuel will total over 100 yards in this game and register a touchdown. He’s looked as strong and as fast as he did three years ago. This is his time to showcase it.
I’m sure Kyle Shanahan will want Samuel featured, especially since Evans is still nursing a rib injury. The last thing he wants is for Evans to worsen it in this game, especially knowing this will be a very aggressive game.
This matchup is perfectly suited for Samuel and George Kittle. But Samuel will be the gas that ignites and sustains the flame for the 49ers’ offense. They have to feed off him.
And maybe Samuel doesn’t eclipse 100 receiving yards, or even total yards, but his impact in getting the entire offense revved up off some plays will be more than enough to help them make it a competitive game.

title: 49ers’ 2025 Draft Class Raises Major Concerns
full_text:
At the quarter mark of the 2026 season, it is always a good time to look back at the rookie draft class and see how they look adjusting to the NFL. However, the 2025 draft class is just as interesting, and their second season should see a strong leap.
Unfortunately for the 49ers, the early returns from the 49ers' 2025 class are more about big questions than players taking leaps, although they do have some progression candidates.
The 49ers' first draft pick was Mykel Williams. He has not taken a snap yet in 2026 after tearing his ACL in Week 9 of his rookie season. Williams is expected to debut in Week 6. Still, over a year and a quarter into his NFL career, he is still a complete unknown.
Alfred Collins got better as his rookie season went. He was expected to jump into a bigger role on a reshuffled defensive line in 2026. However, he tore his Achilles right before Week 1 started. He is an unknown until 2027.
Nick Martin was active for seven games as a rookie and played 15 defensive snaps along with 74 special teams snaps. He has been on the IR in 2026 and has not taken a snap.
Upton Stout is the first 49ers pick to be a hit. He has started for San Francisco the past two seasons and is progressing in the new Raheem Morris defense.
CJ West was a depth option as a rookie, struggled early into Year 2, and then got hurt. He should be back this season but brings plenty of questions.
Jordan Watkins has four catches for 86 yards in his NFL career. Injuries are starting to force him onto the field in his second season.
Jordan James has four rushes for 15 yards and was promptly beaten out by third-round rookie Kaelon Black.
Marques Sigle has been a breakout starter in his second year after getting benched as a rookie.
Kurtis Rourke has been on the practice squad.
Connor Colby has taken a big step forward and looks like a competent left guard after being benched as a rookie.
Then, there is Junior Bergen, who is not on the team.
They found three starters from this draft class, which is not bad. However, the top three picks are major question marks, and four of the picks look like they will not contribute much in the next year or more.

title: 49ers Have 7 Intriguing Trade Options From Division Rival
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 this season, and with a new coaching staff, the 2026 season is more about rebuilding than competing. While the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers are in their division, the two teams could end up being great trade partners for each other.
On Arizona’s side, they do not want to give a rival their best players. On the flip side, if they turn the picks they get from San Francisco into players who beat them in the future, the trades will be gifts that keep on giving.
If the 49ers and Cardinals come together on a deal, these seven players are worth keeping an eye on.
The Cardinals are starting to realize that the former top five pick needs a change of scenery. While giving the 49ers this type of talent would hurt, he could also end up burning San Francisco as well. The 49ers need a receiver , and Harrison could grow under Mike Evans' wing.
The 49ers are very familiar with Bourne. This would cost a late pick swap or a conditional draft pick. Still, if the 49ers are desperate at receiver, it makes sense.
The Cardinals have said that they do not plan to trade Sweat, who still has a couple of years on his contract. However, the right price could get them to change their stance. Sweat had 12 sacks last year, but just one so far this season.
Browning is in the last year of his contract with the Cardinals. He is in an edge rusher rotation and has four sacks in 27 games since being traded to the Cardinals. Browning fits the scheme of Morris in that he can play off of the ball or put his hand down and rush. He would also not cost much.
Collins is another player with linebacker/edge rusher hybrid ability. He has been with the Cardinals for all six NFL seasons but is in the last year of his deal. Recouping something would be a win .
Stills starts for the Cardinals, but is in the last year of his contract. The team has other young defensive linemen who can take his snaps. He would immediately come in and start for the 49ers next to Osa Odighizuwa.
Billings is a run-defending nose tackle. This is exactly what the 49ers need. If Arizona wants to give a rental to the 49ers for a late-round pick, this is an excellent fit.

title: Mykel Williams Sends Strong Message Ahead of 49ers Return
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' former 11th overall pick Mykel Williams tore his ACL once he was starting to get into a groove during his rookie season. Now, Williams is about a week away from returning to the NFL to start his 2026 season.
He told reporters that he is going crazy in anticipation of getting back on the field.
“I’m going crazy; I'm losing my mind,” joked Williams . “Nah, I'm playing, but I'm ready to go. I'm excited to play ball. I miss playing ball. It's been damn near a year since I played, so I just want to get back on the field.”
"I'm going crazy. I'm losing my mind." Do you think Mykel Williams wants to get back on the field? 😅 pic.twitter.com/IPbCBY7lwW
Williams is on the PUP and can return in Week 6. The 49ers already opened his practice window, signaling they expect him to be on the field at the earliest date he can return.
When the 49ers drafted Williams in the 2025 NFL Draft, the expectation was for him to get off to a slow start. He is a younger player with limited experience at Georgia. His upside was high, but his prospect profile signaled a raw player, especially as a pass rusher.
So, it was not a surprise to see that he had just 19 pressures and one sack on 385 total snaps and 245 pass-rush snaps. He did add 12 run stops on 133 run defense snaps. Still, he had three pressures in his last game, and his first sack came in Week 6. He was playing better when he got hurt.
Now, the question is how he will fit into the new defensive scheme. Williams typically played the edge on run downs, then would slide inside on pass-rush downs under Robert Saleh.
However, Raheem Morris runs more five-man fronts, and it could push Williams inside as more of a 5-technique defensive end. Williams being able to slide inside and outside makes rookie linebacker Jaden Dugger more valuable as well.
Dugger has 100 defensive snaps this year, with 48 being on the edge.
So, the 49ers can align Dugger as a third linebacker in 4-3 base looks. Then, they can slide Williams inside, have rookie Romello Height stand up, and slide Dugger down to be their two outside linebackers in a 3-4 look.
Even if Williams is not providing massive production, his value on the field will be seen immediately. The 49ers defense has been strong already, but could be getting much better.

title: 4 Reasons 49ers Will Be Much Better Against Seahawks
full_text:
No team pummeled the San Francisco 49ers more last year than the Seattle Seahawks.
The 49ers stood no chance in their last two matchups against them. It was downright embarrassing, and that could happen again when they square off on Sunday in Week 5 .
However, I don’t think that will be the case. The 49ers will be much better against the Seahawks this time around, and there are four reasons for that. Let’s dive into what those four reasons are.
Without question, the 49ers’ offensive line has been the best unit in the NFL. They proved that last week against the Denver Broncos, who are one of the best defensive fronts in the league.
I fully expect them to hold their own much better against the Seahawks this year. They are easily still the best defensive line in football, but the 49ers’ offensive line is as well.
They won’t be mauled from start to finish as they were in their last two matchups. I’m sure they will have their fits throughout the game, but pure domination should be out of the question.
The last two games against the Seahawks were when the 49ers missed Brandon Aiyuk. No one could separate or carve out a soft spot in Seattle’s defense for Purdy to throw to.
That’s all changed with Mike Evans and George Kittle in the fold. Yes, Evans won’t be fully fit, but he’ll still have a major impact in this game. So will Kittle, even though he played in one of the last two games in a 13-3 loss.
Deebo Samuel will help as well. He’s not going to make an impact as a pure receiver, but his dynamic gives the 49ers an explosive and aggressive ability they didn’t have the last two times.
You can make the case that Purdy is playing better in this four-game stretch than in any stretch of his career. He’s been sharp, even though he did cool off against Denver last week.
Still, it’s hard to deny how comfortable and composed he looks on almost every drop back. He’s also not trying to force chunk plays as often, which has led to him getting pressured a bunch.
The Seahawks will be a big test for Purdy to see how much he’s ascended this year, but Purdy is also the best quarterback Seattle’s defense has faced thus far. It’s going to be an exciting matchup.
There’s no way the Seahawks would’ve been as incredible on offense in the divisional playoff game if the 49ers had Fred Warner out there. His presence alone is all the 49ers needed on defense.
Obviously, having Dre Greenlaw back is sweet, and Nick Bosa would be phenomenal to have back as well, but Warner is the first and foremost important player they need.
It’s not just what he does against the run and pass, but as a leader. He gets his guys situated in the right spot to execute the play call. His impact is second to none, and it will be felt immediately in this game.

title: Buccaneers Rookie Quarterback Makes NFL History With Cowboys Win
full_text:
It took awhile, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally have their first win of the season.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. They did it with undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels under center, who is filling in for QB Baker Mayfield as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.
Daniels played well against the Cowboys, completing 76% of his passes for 178 yards and a touchdown. But he also made history when he beat Dallas at AT&T Stadium, and it's a record that will never be broken.
Per FOX Sports' Greg Auman, Daniels is the only quarterback outside of the NFL's strike year in 1987 to ever defeat the Dallas Cowboys in a regular season football game.
Tampa Bay’s Jalon Daniels is the first undrafted rookie QB ever to beat the Cowboys, aside from a strike game with replacement players in 1987.
That stat makes sense — UDFA rookies rarely ever start football games anyway. Daniels is the first UDFA rookie to start for a team before Week 4 since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. There have been just 10 UDFA rookie quarterbacks to start a game since 2013 — of those 10, one of them was Kendall Hinton, a wide receiver who had to play emergency QB.
Daniels has done a decent job filling in for Mayfield so far. Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards, and on top of that, he's rushed for  87 yards on 16 carries.
Daniels is set to start another game two Sundays from now against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. With Mayfield already looking to come back from his dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have one more week to show his worth and cement himself as Tampa Bay's backup for the foreseeable future when the Steelers come to Tampa Bay.
The Bucs and Daniels will play the Steelers on Oct. 18. The Bucs have alternated wins and losses against the Steelers since 2002, so maybe Daniels will help continue that trend two Sundays from now.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Who They're Planning to Start at Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
It took a while, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers officially got their first win on Thursday night.
Tampa Bay bested the Cowboys 24-16 to move to 1-4 on the year. There's still a lot of work to do and things to clean up, but Tampa Bay ran the ball exceptionally well and the defense showed up in a big way to help secure the victory.
The first win of the season didn't come with starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, though. It came with backup quarterback Jalon Daniels under center, who executed the offense well and took care of the football to help Tampa Bay win. Daniels is now 1-1 as a starter in Tampa Bay — but with a long week off and the Pittsburgh Steelers coming two Sundays from now, will he get to play a third game?
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Friday after the win, and he revealed who the Bucs are planning to go with against the Steelers — for now.
Bowles confirmed to the media that while he still needs to see what Mayfield looks like and how he can grip the football after the stitches in his thumb were removed, he's planning on going with Daniels against the Steelers at the moment.
"Right now, we plan on starting Jalon Daniels against the Steelers," Bowles said.
Todd Bowles says that he’ll see what Baker Mayfield looks like when he comes in and how he’s able to grip the ball, but the team is planning on starting Jalon Daniels again against the Steelers
Starting two games and appearing at the end of one, Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards. Daniels has also been a significant threat on the ground, already amassing 87 yards on 16 carries.
Despite Daniels being the plan for Week 6, it will be interesting to see if Mayfield begins to practice or has an outside shot at playing against Pittsburgh. Mayfield has been campaigning to play the game, per NFL insider James Palmer, and if the medical staff thinks he can grip the football well enough, Bowles may be faced with the decision to rest Mayfield or to let him get back in after the team has gotten its first win of the season.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
Mayfield has started three games for Tampa Bay and has thrown for 615 yards on 96 attempts with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
The Bucs have the rest of the week off before preparing for the Steelers, who they'll play on Oct. 18. That's plenty of time for Mayfield to recover, but it's also plenty of time for the Bucs to continue game planning with Daniels and the skill set he has as he goes into what is currently set to be his third NFL start.

title: Grading the Buccaneers' Week 5 Win Against the Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first win of the season, and it was in primetime against the Dallas Cowboys.
There was a great level of execution on the defensive and offensive sides of the ball. Let's go over our grades for the Bucs in their 24-16 win.
It was an overall very solid night for Jalon Daniels. He took what the Dallas defense gave him and didn't make any real mistakes, to the tune of 19/25 passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. He had seven carries on the ground for 23 yards.
The running game was the largest reason the Bucs won this matchup and it was by far the best thing the Bucs offense has produced this season.
Bucky Irving finished the day with 23 touches for 175 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns. Irving also had the eighth-longest run in team history, with a 72-yard run in the contest as well.
Besides a great 64-yard reception where Tez Johnson broke the ankles of Daron Bland, the receiver room still didn't get much going. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson tried to get Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin more involved, as they did combine for nine catches, but it still only went for 75 yards on the evening.
Egbuka did have a 14-yard end-around for a touchdown, which was a nice play, however.
Cade Otton finished the night with three catches for 25 yards and Payne Durham even got involved with a five-yard reception of his own. Still, this group is middling and hasn't done much of note this season.
This might have been the best performance of the Bucs offensive line this season. Now, they do get a good number of points off for penalties, as there were plenty from this group in this game.
However, they did do a fantastic job of opening up lanes in the rushing attack and Daniels' scrambling ability kept him to only getting sacked once.
The defensive line continued to be largely ineffective in this matchup, as Dak Prescott was not sacked once in this game and generally didn't face much pressure unless the team sent a blitz against them.
The Cowboys' run game did well in this matchup as well until they had to move away from it since they were down in the game. Also, Yaya Diaby had an interception in this game, which was fun to watch.
Who would've thought that Alex Anzalone would end up with the game-sealing interception for the Bucs, huh? I give a lot of points for that, and overall the unit did some pretty solid work, all things considered.
Jacob Parrish had an up-and-down night for the Buccaneers. He did finish with four passes defended — however, receiver George Pickens ate with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown.
Zyon McCollum was fantastic today in this one, holding CeeDee Lamb to two catches for nine yards in this contest. Also, I thought the safety duo of Tykee Smith and Ifeatu Melifonwu were solid in this game as well.
It was a great day for special teams as Miles Killebrew forced a fumble on Cowboys returner KaVontae Turpin to help the team pull further ahead. Chase McLaughlin made all of his kicks, and Riley Dixon was fine punting the ball as well.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 24-16 Win Over the Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had their backs against the wall heading to Dallas on a short week to take on the Dallas Cowboys for Thursday Night Football.
Unlike every other game this season, there was finally some good things happening on the field for the Buccaneers, who managed to pull out an impressive 24-16 victory in Dallas.
Let's get right into the good, the bad and the ugly.
Daniels' career night started on the opening drive where, despite some mental lapses, Daniels led the longest drive for the Buccaneers' franchise since Jeff Garcia in 2007. He completed 8/8 passes for 49 yards and a TD on 15 plays in almost an entire quarter.
Daniels is 1-of-2 undrafted rookie quarterbacks since 1991 – and the first since 2013 – to earn a 100.0% completion percentage in a single quarter, while completing seven-or-more passes (also Matt McGloin, third quarter, 12/15/13 vs. Kansas City). https://t.co/vWKcc4ifXq
Daniels was excellent throughout this game. Was he perfect? No. But he did more than enough to put his team in a position to win a road game they absolutely had to have.
Although he looked a little too patient in the pocket early on, Daniels seemed to really settle into a nice rhythm in terms of his pocket poise, timing, and decisions about when to look downfield and when to tuck it and run.
Despite possessing a big arm and the speed to be a dual-threat quarterback, Daniels resisted the temptation to play hero ball and instead played like a seasoned game manager tonight, taking care of the football and controlling the clock, which is exactly what his team needed.
Through the first few weeks of the season, Bucky Irving looked like the team's only true weapon on offense. Tonight, Bucky looked like the team's best weapon, but it felt like he was finally getting some help from his offensive line and offensive coordinator.
The Cowboys' defense has struggled mightily this season, but this is still an NFL defense, and the Bucs made them look like they weren't when they handed it off. Irving looked electric in this game and showed just how dangerous he can be when given some half-decent lanes to run through.
The Bucs totaled a whopping 243 yards rushing in this game while averaging over six yards per carry as a team. Bucky Irving himself rushed for 165 yards on just 21 carries.
The Bucs' defense played a really solid game vs. the Cowboys. Most impressive was the performance of their cornerback room, with Jacob Parrish, Zyon McCollum and Tykee Smith all having a significant impact on the Cowboys' production through the air.
Jacob Parrish has recorded three-plus passes defensed in a game for the first time in his NFL career. Parrish's six passes defensed on the season are tied for the fourth-most across the NFL this season (teammate Zyon McCollum is also tied for 4th).
Had it not been for Todd Bowles' atrocious game management decisions, the Bucs would have likely hit the 30-point plateau for the first time this year. Zac Robinson has had a really rough start to his debut as the Bucs' OC, but he was in a tough spot trying to alter his offensive game plan to suit an undrafted rookie quarterback playing the Dallas Cowboys on the road.
Although Daniels executed, it needs to be acknowledged that Robinson put together a game plan that allowed the dynamic but inexperienced rookie quarterback to perform at his peak so early in his career. Robinson mixed the run with the pass really well on Thursday night, and the Bucs dominated the game on the ground throughout.
It's important to note that although Tristan Wirfs did leave the game with some sort of lower-body injury on two different occasions in the second half, he did return to finish the game.
Still, there's little doubt that Wirfs is the best player on the roster, regardless of position, and if the Buccaneers were to lose him for any period of time, it would be a catastrophic hit to a team that is trying to dig their way out of a very deep hole.
Unsure if it was non-contact or not here. Thought at first he got rolled up on but not really the case. pic.twitter.com/8rPNALXTf2
With 3:47 left in the first half and the game tied 7-7, Todd Bowles' indecision cost the Buccaneers three points. The Bucs were facing a third-and-six from around midfield after a Tristan Wirfs false start penalty set them back. Initially, it appeared as though Bowles might be planning to punt the ball away, but then he changed his mind and sent out the field goal unit so McLaughlin could attempt a 61-yarder.
Unfortunately, it took the Bucs too long to get set up for the kick, and Bowles did not use a timeout to buy his team enough time to recalibrate. Bowles' lack of decisiveness — something that has plagued Bowles throughout his tenure in Tampa Bay as a head coach — directly resulted in a delay-of-game penalty, which took the Buccaneers out of field goal range and ultimately cost them points they desperately needed.
Absolutely unbelievable levels of incompetence lol. A high school coach would be embarrassed to mess that up
With 8:36 left in the game and the Buccaneers leading 24-10, Bowles decided to go for it on fourth-and-goal as opposed to kicking the FG to make it a three-score game. The perplexing decision was one that not only reflects Bowles' lack of familiarity with holding a lead this year, but also contradicts his profile as an overly conservative decision-maker on fourth downs.
Throughout the first four weeks of the season, it could be argued that the Buccaneers lost in large part because of Bowles. On Thursday, they won a crucial road victory despite some terrible game management decisions he made,

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Thursday Night Football Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
It took five games, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a win.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys on prime time in AT&T Stadium on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. It wasn't the prettiest win, with problems still present and the Cowboys almost coming back, but the Bucs got it done and outplayed the Cowboys to secure the victory 24-16.
It's a win, but there's still room for some overreactions after the game. Here are three of them as the Bucs get ready for a long week off after their Thursday Night Football matchup:
Walker is playing what is technically his rookie season after he tore his ACL in training camp last year, and boy, has he made the most of it. He pressured quarterback Dak Prescott multiple times on Thursday, disrupting the passing game and helping the defense in a big way. He also tipped a ball in coverage that resulted in a Yaya Diaby interception.
Walker is OLB5 on the depth chart behind Rueben Bain Jr., Yaya Diaby, Al-Quadin Muhammad and Anthony Nelson. So far this year, he's been better than all of them, and he needs the snaps to match.
Yes, this Cowboys defense is awful. But quarterback Jalon Daniels has executed fairly well these last two weeks, and he's played better than most expected him to for an undrafted free agent.
The Bucs took a chance on him after the draft and took an even bigger chance on him by making him QB2. Some were skeptical about what he could do as a UDFA, especially now that the Bucs need him to play, but he's done exactly what he needed to do and played about as well as he can over these past two games to prove the Bucs were right to gamble on him. He wasn't perfect — he almost threw a disastrous pick-six — but he has run the offense and got a win out of it.
Eventually, Mayfield will be back. But the Bucs will feel very comfortable with Daniels behind him.
The Bucs had an absolutely brutal night of penalties in the win, with 13 penalties for 87 yards. A good chunk of those were offensive penalties, with everything from holding to false starts plaguing Tampa Bay throughout the night.
The Bucs have no discipline on the offensive side of the ball. When the play is in motion, wideouts and the quarterback end up in various places the Bucs' line doesn't expect them to, and as a result, the team suffers from a good number of penalties every game.
There doesn't seem to be a fix to these issues in sight, even with this win. The Bucs have to be smoother in their entire operation from the ground up to find a way not to go backwards every week.

title: Buccaneers Matchup Against Cowboys Just Got Tougher
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers already have a tough task on Thursday night. They're set to play a red-hot Dallas Cowboys offense on Thursday Night Football on the road, and at 0-4, the Bucs really need a win to give themselves even a drop of hope for the remainder of the year.
Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, that task got a little bit harder for them once the Dallas Cowboys activated a key starter on the Thursday of the game.
Cowboys guard Tyler Smith was questionable on Dallas' injury report as he's been recovering from thumb surgery before the season. Per the NFL's Ian Rapoport, he's set to make his debut against the Bucs on Thursday night.
The #Cowboys are activating All-Pro G Tyler Smith from Injured Reserve to play tonight against the #Bucs . A big lift. One of the NFL's best, Smith had thumb surgery right before the season with hopes of returning as soon as possible. After a full practice Wednesday, he's back. pic.twitter.com/3XQLuAy8R2
Smith was a Second Team All-Pro in 2023 and is a stalwart on the Cowboys' offensive line. A three-time consecutive Pro Bowler dating back to 2023, Smith has been a crucial part of Dallas' offense and signed a four-year, $96 million contract in 2025.
Now that he's back to protect quarterback Dak Prescott, Tampa Bay's pass rush will have to step up on Thursday to get to him through Smith's efforts. That will include players like Calijah Kancey, Tampa Bay's pass-rushing DT, Vita Vea and A'Shawn Robinson to disrupt the middle and halt both the run and the pass against Dallas.
Tampa Bay is getting a player of its own back with Rueben Bain Jr., who missed the last two games due to a groin issue he suffered against the Cleveland Browns. The Bucs have lost safety Antoine Winfield Jr. for the next few weeks due to a rib injury, though, and they're also starting backup quarterback Jalon Daniels with Baker Mayfield recovering from a thumb injury.
The Bucs will play the Cowboys on Thursday night at 8:15. Head coach Todd Bowles will have to do everything he can to get pressure up the middle, and with Smith's return to the team, his job has gotten a bit harder in that regard.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching Most in Buccaneers Week 5 Matchup Against Cowboys
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are limping into a primetime matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
A 0-4 start hasn't instilled much confidence in this team, and they face yet another tall task in front of them as they search for their first win.
It doesn't seem like the Bucs will have much of a chance in this one, but these are the three storylines we will be watching when they take on the Cowboys in Jerry's World.
This will be Jalon Daniels' second-ever start, and it will come in primetime. The pressure will amp up, and Daniels will not only need to have an excellent game through the air but also on the ground.
Daniels, along with Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker, must all be at their best. They will have ample opportunities to make plays as Dallas is surrendering 150.3 rushing yards per game (31st in the NFL).
Zac Robinson must lean on his running backs and mobile quarterback in this one if they hope to match Dallas score-for-score, and it would also help with controlling the game clock, keeping the Cowboys' offense off the field and keeping themselves out of third-and-long situations.
It's the first 0-4 start in Tampa Bay since 2013, and head coach Todd Bowles' seat couldn't get much warmer.
It's desperation time for Bowles and the Bucs, so not showing up at all would quite literally be the straw that breaks the camel's back.
Getting blown out on national television would put the Bucs' record at 0-5, which would make it one of the worst starts in franchise history — the first since Tony Dungy's inaugural season back in 1996.
If that does indeed happen, the writing will most definitely be on the wall for Bowles and company.
Dallas boasts one of the best offenses in the league, which is headed by an elite passing game with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens leading the charge.
It was already going to be a massive challenge for a young Bucs' secondary, but that hill got even steeper with Antoine Winfield Jr. being ruled out as he deals with a rib fracture.
While Winfield hasn't been his best, the Bucs will now have to rely on backups to try and help slow down the Cowboys' passing attack. How Tampa Bay and Bowles adapt to the absence of Winfield against Dallas' passing game will be a major defining factor in whether they can keep this game close.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Cowboys Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a big game against the Dallas Cowboys on prime time Thursday night. If they can't get the win on Thursday night football, they'll be starting at 0-5 and, despite it just being October, virtually the death knell to their playoff hopes.
As always, our staff is putting in our predictions for the Thursday Night Football — do we think Todd Bowles will get his team back on track, or will the Bucs drop their fifth straight game?
It’s hard to imagine the Buccaneers turning things around in a short week, especially against the Cowboys.
The Cowboys' offense is a high-flying machine and will test the Bucs’ secondary that is now without Antoine Winfield Jr. Their defense has been a work in progress, however, so the Bucs just might be able to exploit it to put points on the board.
With that being said, they haven’t been able to exploit anyone this season.
I expect much of what we have seen through four weeks once again on TNF.
The Buccaneers get another loss here and fall to 0-5. This is a ship without oars, a plane without wings and a team without direction. Just about nothing is going well for this football team, and I believe it will continue with another loss.
Not only are the Buccaneers 0-4 to start this season, but they're a league-worst 2-11 over their last 13 games dating back to last year. For a team that was expected by many to be a potential contender in the NFC this season, the early returns have been incredibly disappointing. Todd Bowles' Bucs don't just look lost, they look lifeless — and his job is at risk because of it.
The Dallas Cowboys have a talented offense and a vulnerable defense. That being said, I don't believe that Jalon Daniels (in his second NFL start) will be able to take advantage of the Cowboys' defense anywhere close to what Dak Prescott could do to Todd Bowles' defense. Especially on the road.
The biggest questions asked of us this week to the Bucs coaching staff and players were whether they think they can keep up with the points against the Cowboys. That's the big question.
Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens showcase the serious power of their offense. But if there's a defense to succeed against, it would be the Cowboys'. Yes, you are still working with an undrafted rookie quarterback, but if you can't show any type of efficiency, it's going to be a long evening on primetime television.
Zac Robinson hasn't shown me that out of nowhere this offense is going to take a big turn, and remember, it is a primetime game — Those don't usually bode well for Todd Bowles and this Bucs team.
The Buccaneers have kept most games "close" so far — they've never actually been in control of any of these close games — but that's going to change on Thursday night. This Cowboys team has the serious means to put up points, and with weapons in the wideout corps and an elite quarterback in Dak Prescott, they certainly will on a Bucs defense that looks better than it is.
Tampa Bay's offense with Jalon Daniels will likely struggle even against a rough Cowboys defense — Joey Porter Jr. will probably add some extra help to a team that really needs it. I think the Bucs get blown out on national television, and it'll be another ember to the fire under Bowles' seat.
